law-of-contract-i-u2-t13.subtitle: Section 29 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: An uncertain agreement is one whose meaning is not certain and cannot be made certain. Section 29 makes such an agreement void . A court cannot enforce a promise when it cannot tell what was promised. The problem is vagueness, not illegality. Nothing wrong is being done; the words simply do not say enough. The key phrase is "capable of being made certain" . If the agreement itself, the nature of the trade, or an agreed method settles the meaning, the agreement stands. In exams this is a short, predictable question built on the Act's six Illustrations. In real life it decides whether a bargain with a missing price, an unclear quantity or two possible figures can be enforced at all.
legalProvision: Section 29. Agreements void for uncertainty. Agreements, the meaning of which is not certain, or capable of being made certain, are void. Illustrations (a) A agrees to sell to B "a hundred tons of oil". There is nothing whatever to show what kind of oil was intended. The agreement is void for uncertainty. (b) A agrees to sell to B one hundred tons of oil of a specified description, known as an article of commerce. There is no uncertainty here to make the agreement void. (c) A, who is a dealer in cocoanut-oil only, agrees to sell to B "one hundred tons of oil". The nature of A's trade affords an indication of the meaning of the words, and A has entered into a contract for the sale of one hundred tons of cocoanut-oil. (d) A agrees to sell to B "all the grain in my granary at Ramnagar". There is no uncertainty here to make the agreement void. (e) A agrees to sell B "one thousand maunds of rice at a price to be fixed by C". As the price is capable of being made certain, there is no uncertainty here to make the agreement void. (f) A agrees to sell to B "my white horse for rupees five hundred or rupees one thousand". There is nothing to show which of the two prices was to be given. The agreement is void.

Sale of Goods Act, 1930, Section 9. Ascertainment of price. (1) The price in a contract of sale may be fixed by the contract or may be left to be fixed in manner thereby agreed or may be determined by the course of dealing between the parties. (2) Where the price is not determined in accordance with the foregoing provisions, the buyer shall pay the seller a reasonable price. What is a reasonable price is a question of fact dependent on the circumstances of each particular case.

Sale of Goods Act, 1930, Section 10. Agreement to sell at valuation. (1) Where there is an agreement to sell goods on the terms that the price is to be fixed by the valuation of a third party and such third party cannot or does not make such valuation, the agreement is thereby avoided: Provided that, if the goods or any part thereof have been delivered to, and appropriated by, the buyer, he shall pay a reasonable price therefor. (2) Where such third party is prevented from making the valuation by the fault of the seller or buyer, the party not in fault may maintain a suit for damages against the party in fault.
In simple words

If the meaning of an agreement is not certain, and nothing can make it certain, the agreement is void. If the meaning can be made certain (by a trade description, the seller's trade, a clear identification, or an agreed method), the agreement is valid. In a sale of goods , a price left open is not fatal: it may be fixed by an agreed method or by the course of dealing, or else a reasonable price is paid.
en.meaning:
The Act does not define "uncertain". Section 29 simply says that an agreement whose meaning is "not certain, or capable of being made certain" is void. An agreement is uncertain when its terms are too vague to give a clear meaning. Section 29 covers two kinds of vagueness alike: Kind What is wrong Illustration A missing or unclear term A term (kind of goods, price, quantity) is not stated and cannot be found (a) "a hundred tons of oil" Two readings with no way to choose The agreement gives alternatives and nothing shows which applies (f) "rupees five hundred or rupees one thousand" The rule rests on a simple point: a court can enforce only what it can identify. The Latin maxim id certum est quod certum reddi potest ("that is certain which can be made certain") states the other side of the rule. A term need not be stated in exact figures, so long as there is a way to fix it. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Start at the top. The agreement is void only if its meaning is unclear and nothing can make it certain. flowchart TD Q1{"Is the meaning of the agreement
clear on its face?"} OK1["Not void for uncertainty
Illustrations (b), (d)"] Q2{"Can it be made certain?
trade description, seller's trade,
clear identification or agreed method"} OK2["Not void: meaning capable
of being made certain
Illustrations (c), (e)"] V["VOID for uncertainty (s.29)
Illustrations (a), (f)
Advance recoverable (s.65)"] Q1 -- "Yes" --> OK1 Q1 -- "No" --> Q2 Q2 -- "Yes" --> OK2 Q2 -- "No" --> V Text description Is the meaning of the agreement clear on its face? If yes, it is not void for uncertainty (Illustrations (b), (d)). If no, can a trade description, the nature of the seller's trade, a clear identification or an agreed method make it certain? If yes, it is not void (Illustrations (c), (e)). If no, the agreement is void for uncertainty (Illustrations (a), (f)); any advance can be recovered under Section 65.
keyPoints: Section 29: an agreement whose meaning is not certain, or capable of being made certain, is void. The agreement stands if a trade description, the seller's trade, a clear identification or an agreed method makes the meaning certain. Illustration (f): two prices with no way to choose make the agreement void. In a sale of goods, a price left open is fixed by the agreed method or course of dealing, or a reasonable price is paid (SoGA Section 9). If a named valuer does not value, the agreement is avoided, but goods taken must be paid for at a reasonable price (SoGA Section 10). Uncertainty is about the words of the agreement. Mistake is about the parties' beliefs. Uncertain agreements are void, not illegal.

caseLaws.name: Mayawanti v
caseLaws.facts: Kaushalya Devi (1990) Facts. By a receipt of 16 September 1971, the defendant agreed to sell a jointly owned factory property in Ludhiana for Rs. 50,000 and took Rs. 5,000 as earnest money. If the co-owner did not sign, she would sell "one of the two shares", otherwise pay back the advance. The buyer sued for specific performance. Principle. "The stipulations and terms of the contract have, therefore, to be certain and the parties must have been consensus ad idem "; with an undefined share at an unstated price, there was no enforceable contract and no specific performance. The High Court's decree for return of the Rs. 5,000 earnest money was upheld. (1990) 3 SCC 1 : [1990] 2 SCR 350. Why it matters. A court will not enforce terms that do not show what was promised; the payer gets back the advance.

selfTest.q: 1. When is an agreement void under Section 29?
selfTest.a: When its meaning is not certain and is not capable of being made certain.

selfTest.q: 2. Is an agreement to sell "one thousand maunds of rice at a price to be fixed by C" void?
selfTest.a: No. The price is capable of being made certain (Illustration (e)).

selfTest.q: 3. What is the effect of an uncertain agreement?
selfTest.a: It is void, and neither party can enforce it. Any advance paid can be recovered under Section 65.

selfTest.q: 4. A agrees to sell B "all the paddy in my barn at Tenali". Is it uncertain?
selfTest.a: No. The goods are clearly identified (compare Illustration (d)).

selfTest.q: 5. The price of goods is to be fixed by Mr. X, who refuses to value. The buyer has already received and used the goods. What must he pay?
selfTest.a: A reasonable price (SoGA Section 10(1), proviso).

selfTest.q: 6. How is uncertainty different from mistake?
selfTest.a: Uncertainty lies in the words of the agreement; mistake lies in the parties' beliefs about facts.

ఒప్పందం అర్థం నిశ్చితంగా లేకపోతే, దాన్ని ఏదీ నిశ్చితం చేయలేకపోతే, ఒప్పందం చెల్లదు. అర్థాన్ని నిశ్చితం చేయగలిగితే (వ్యాపారంలో తెలిసిన వర్ణన, అమ్మేవాడి వ్యాపారం, స్పష్టమైన గుర్తింపు, లేదా అంగీకరించిన పద్ధతి ద్వారా), ఒప్పందం చెల్లుతుంది. వస్తువుల అమ్మకంలో, ధర తెరిచి ఉంచడం ప్రాణాంతకం కాదు: అంగీకరించిన పద్ధతి ద్వారా గానీ, వ్యవహార క్రమం ద్వారా గానీ దాన్ని నిర్ణయించవచ్చు; లేకపోతే సహేతుకమైన ధర చెల్లించాలి.

hi.inOneMinute: An uncertain agreement is one whose meaning is not certain and cannot be made certain. Section 29 makes such an agreement void . A court cannot enforce a promise when it cannot tell what was promised. The problem is vagueness, not illegality. Nothing wrong is being done; the words simply do not say enough. The key phrase is "capable of being made certain" . If the agreement itself, the nature of the trade, or an agreed method settles the meaning, the agreement stands. In exams this is a short, predictable question built on the Act's six Illustrations. In real life it decides whether a bargain with a missing price, an unclear quantity or two possible figures can be enforced at all.
legalProvision: Section 29. Agreements void for uncertainty. Agreements, the meaning of which is not certain, or capable of being made certain, are void. Illustrations (a) A agrees to sell to B "a hundred tons of oil". There is nothing whatever to show what kind of oil was intended. The agreement is void for uncertainty. (b) A agrees to sell to B one hundred tons of oil of a specified description, known as an article of commerce. There is no uncertainty here to make the agreement void. (c) A, who is a dealer in cocoanut-oil only, agrees to sell to B "one hundred tons of oil". The nature of A's trade affords an indication of the meaning of the words, and A has entered into a contract for the sale of one hundred tons of cocoanut-oil. (d) A agrees to sell to B "all the grain in my granary at Ramnagar". There is no uncertainty here to make the agreement void. (e) A agrees to sell B "one thousand maunds of rice at a price to be fixed by C". As the price is capable of being made certain, there is no uncertainty here to make the agreement void. (f) A agrees to sell to B "my white horse for rupees five hundred or rupees one thousand". There is nothing to show which of the two prices was to be given. The agreement is void.

Sale of Goods Act, 1930, Section 9. Ascertainment of price. (1) The price in a contract of sale may be fixed by the contract or may be left to be fixed in manner thereby agreed or may be determined by the course of dealing between the parties. (2) Where the price is not determined in accordance with the foregoing provisions, the buyer shall pay the seller a reasonable price. What is a reasonable price is a question of fact dependent on the circumstances of each particular case.

Sale of Goods Act, 1930, Section 10. Agreement to sell at valuation. (1) Where there is an agreement to sell goods on the terms that the price is to be fixed by the valuation of a third party and such third party cannot or does not make such valuation, the agreement is thereby avoided: Provided that, if the goods or any part thereof have been delivered to, and appropriated by, the buyer, he shall pay a reasonable price therefor. (2) Where such third party is prevented from making the valuation by the fault of the seller or buyer, the party not in fault may maintain a suit for damages against the party in fault.
In simple words

If the meaning of an agreement is not certain, and nothing can make it certain, the agreement is void. If the meaning can be made certain (by a trade description, the seller's trade, a clear identification, or an agreed method), the agreement is valid. In a sale of goods , a price left open is not fatal: it may be fixed by an agreed method or by the course of dealing, or else a reasonable price is paid.
hi.meaning:
The Act does not define "uncertain". Section 29 simply says that an agreement whose meaning is "not certain, or capable of being made certain" is void. An agreement is uncertain when its terms are too vague to give a clear meaning. Section 29 covers two kinds of vagueness alike: Kind What is wrong Illustration A missing or unclear term A term (kind of goods, price, quantity) is not stated and cannot be found (a) "a hundred tons of oil" Two readings with no way to choose The agreement gives alternatives and nothing shows which applies (f) "rupees five hundred or rupees one thousand" The rule rests on a simple point: a court can enforce only what it can identify. The Latin maxim id certum est quod certum reddi potest ("that is certain which can be made certain") states the other side of the rule. A term need not be stated in exact figures, so long as there is a way to fix it. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Start at the top. If yes, it is not void for uncertainty (Illustrations (b), (d)). If no, can a trade description, the nature of the seller's trade, a clear identification or an agreed method make it certain? If yes, it is not void (Illustrations (c), (e)). If no, the agreement is void for uncertainty (Illustrations (a), (f)); any advance can be recovered under Section 65.
keyPoints: Section 29: an agreement whose meaning is not certain, or capable of being made certain, is void. The agreement stands if a trade description, the seller's trade, a clear identification or an agreed method makes the meaning certain. Illustration (f): two prices with no way to choose make the agreement void. In a sale of goods, a price left open is fixed by the agreed method or course of dealing, or a reasonable price is paid (SoGA Section 9). If a named valuer does not value, the agreement is avoided, but goods taken must be paid for at a reasonable price (SoGA Section 10). Uncertainty is about the words of the agreement. Mistake is about the parties' beliefs. Uncertain agreements are void, not illegal.

caseLaws.name: Mayawanti v
caseLaws.facts: Kaushalya Devi (1990) Facts. By a receipt of 16 September 1971, the defendant agreed to sell a jointly owned factory property in Ludhiana for Rs. 50,000 and took Rs. 5,000 as earnest money. If the co-owner did not sign, she would sell "one of the two shares", otherwise pay back the advance. The buyer sued for specific performance. Principle. "The stipulations and terms of the contract have, therefore, to be certain and the parties must have been consensus ad idem "; with an undefined share at an unstated price, there was no enforceable contract and no specific performance. The High Court's decree for return of the Rs. 5,000 earnest money was upheld. (1990) 3 SCC 1 : [1990] 2 SCR 350. Why it matters. A court will not enforce terms that do not show what was promised; the payer gets back the advance.

selfTest.q: 1. When is an agreement void under Section 29?
selfTest.a: When its meaning is not certain and is not capable of being made certain.

selfTest.q: 2. Is an agreement to sell "one thousand maunds of rice at a price to be fixed by C" void?
selfTest.a: No. The price is capable of being made certain (Illustration (e)).

selfTest.q: 3. What is the effect of an uncertain agreement?
selfTest.a: It is void, and neither party can enforce it. Any advance paid can be recovered under Section 65.

selfTest.q: 4. A agrees to sell B "all the paddy in my barn at Tenali". Is it uncertain?
selfTest.a: No. The goods are clearly identified (compare Illustration (d)).

selfTest.q: 5. The price of goods is to be fixed by Mr. X, who refuses to value. The buyer has already received and used the goods. What must he pay?
selfTest.a: A reasonable price (SoGA Section 10(1), proviso).

selfTest.q: 6. How is uncertainty different from mistake?
selfTest.a: Uncertainty lies in the words of the agreement; mistake lies in the parties' beliefs about facts.

en.meaning:
In Chikkam Ammiraju v. Chikkam Seshamma, a threat to commit suicide unless a release deed was executed was held to be:

Explanation. The Madras High Court (1917) held that a threat of suicide amounted to coercion under Section 15, since the Court treated the threatened act as one forbidden by the Indian Penal Code. The release deed was voidable.

Which of the following is a key difference between coercion and undue influence?

Explanation. Undue influence, by its nature, requires a relationship in which one party can dominate the other's will; coercion can come from anyone, including a total stranger to the contract.

On the Raghunath Prasad v. Sarju Prasad approach to Section 16, once a relationship of dominance and an unconscionable transaction are shown, the burden of proof:

Explanation. Raghunath Prasad sets a three-stage approach: dominance, then inducement by undue influence, then the burden of proof. Under Section 16(3), once dominance and an unconscionable bargain are shown, the dominant party must prove the transaction was not induced by undue influence. High interest alone, without proof of dominance, raises no presumption.

en.meaning:
Under Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a person is competent to contract if they are of the age of majority, of sound mind, and:

Explanation. Section 11 lays down exactly three tests: age of majority, sound mind, and not being disqualified from contracting by any law to which the person is subject.

As per the Indian Majority Act, 1875, the general age of majority in India is:

Explanation. Section 3 of the Indian Majority Act, 1875 fixes the general age of majority at 18 years, raised to 21 years only where a court-appointed guardian or the Court of Wards is involved before the person turns 18.

A person of unsound mind who is usually insane but has occasional lucid intervals:

Explanation. Section 12's second paragraph allows a person who is usually of unsound mind, but occasionally of sound mind, to make a contract when they are of sound mind — that is, during a lucid interval.

Which of the following is NOT one of Section 11's three tests of competence?

Explanation. Section 2(j) specifically defines a void contract as one that was valid at formation but later becomes unenforceable — distinct from a void agreement (Section 2(g)), which was never enforceable at all.

A voidable contract, under Section 2(i), remains binding:

Explanation. A voidable contract is fully valid and binding unless and until the party with the option to avoid it actually chooses to do so.

law-of-contract-i-u2-t16.subtitle: Sections 2(g), 2(i), 2(j), 19, 56, 64 and 65 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: The Act uses three similar words for three different things: A void agreement is never enforceable. It never became a contract (Section 2(g)). A voidable contract is valid until the party with the option cancels it (Section 2(i)). A void contract was valid when made, but later stops being enforceable (Section 2(j)). These labels decide who can sue, who can walk away, and what happens to money already paid (Sections 64 and 65). In exams, the three definitions, the comparison table and the sources of each earn the marks. In real life they decide whether you can walk away from a deal and get your money back.
legalProvision: Section 2. In this Act the following words and expressions are used in the following senses, unless a contrary intention appears from the context:— (e) Every promise and every set of promises, forming the consideration for each other, is an agreement; (g) An agreement not enforceable by law is said to be void; (h) An agreement enforceable by law is a contract; (i) An agreement which is enforceable by law at the option of one or more of the parties thereto, but not at the option of the other or others, is a voidable contract; (j) A contract which ceases to be enforceable by law becomes void when it ceases to be enforceable.

Section 19. Voidability of agreements without free consent. When consent to an agreement is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. A party to a contract whose consent was caused by fraud or misrepresentation, may, if he thinks fit, insist that the contract shall be performed, and that he shall be put in the position in which he would have been if the representations made had been true. Exception. —If such consent was caused by misrepresentation or by silence, fraudulent within the meaning of section 17, the contract, nevertheless, is not voidable, if the party whose consent was so caused had the means of discovering the truth with ordinary diligence. Explanation. —A fraud or misrepresentation which did not cause the consent to a contract of the party on whom such fraud was practised, or to whom such misrepresentation was made, does not render a contract voidable. Illustration (b). A, by a misrepresentation, leads B erroneously to believe that, five hundred maunds of indigo are made annually at A's factory. B examines the accounts of the factory, which show that only four hundred maunds of indigo have been made. After this B buys the factory. The contract is not voidable on account of A's misrepresentation. Illustration (c). A fraudulently informs B that A's estate is free from incumbrance. B thereupon buys the estate. The estate is subject to a mortgage. B may either avoid the contract, or may insist on its being carried out and the mortgage debt redeemed.

Section 19A. Power to set aside contract induced by undue influence. When consent to an agreement is caused by undue influence, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. Any such contract may be set aside either absolutely or, if the party who was entitled to avoid it has received any benefit thereunder, upon such terms and conditions as to the Court may seem just. Illustration (b). A, a money-lender, advances Rs. 100 to B, an agriculturist, and, by undue influence, induces B to execute a bond for Rs. 200 with interest at 6 per cent. per month. The Court may set the bond aside, ordering B to repay the Rs. 100 with such interest as may seem just.

Section 53 (first part). When a contract contains reciprocal promises, and one party to the contract prevents the other from performing his promise, the contract becomes voidable at the option of the party so prevented; and he is entitled to compensation from the other party for any loss which he may sustain in consequence of the non-performance of the contract.

Section 55 (first two paragraphs). When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract. Effect of such failure when time is not essential. —If it was not the intention of the parties that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract does not become voidable by the failure to do such thing at or before the specified time; but the promisee is entitled to compensation from the promisor for any loss occasioned to him by such failure.

Section 56 (first two paragraphs). An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. Contract to do an act afterwards becoming impossible or unlawful. —A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Illustrations. (a) A agrees with B to discover treasure by magic. The agreement is void. (b) A and B contract to marry each other. Before the time fixed for the marriage, A goes mad. The contract becomes void. (d) A contracts to take in cargo for B at a foreign port. A's Government afterwards declares war against the country in which the port is situated. The contract becomes void when war is declared.

Section 64. Consequences of rescission of voidable contract. When a person at whose option a contract is voidable rescinds it, the other party thereto need not perform any promise therein contained in which he is promisor. The party rescinding a voidable contract shall, if he have received any benefit thereunder from another party to such contract, restore such benefit, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received.

Section 65. Obligation of person who has received advantage under void agreement, or contract that becomes void. When an agreement is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under such agreement or contract is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it to the person from whom he received it. Illustration (d). A contracts to sing for B at a concert for 1,000 rupees, which are paid in advance. A is too ill to sing. A is not bound to make compensation to B for the loss of the profits which B would have made if A had been able to sing, but must refund to B the 1,000 rupees paid in advance.
In simple words

Agreement + enforceable by law = contract . Agreement + not enforceable = void. Voidable = binding until the wronged party chooses to cancel it. Only he has that choice. A contract that later becomes impossible or unlawful becomes void from that moment. The party who cancels a voidable contract gives back what he received (Section 64). Whoever got an advantage under a void agreement or a contract that becomes void gives it back (Section 65).

The Act builds the three ideas on Section 2: Term Section Meaning Status from the start Agreement 2(e) Promises forming consideration for each other May or may not be enforceable Contract 2(h) Agreement enforceable by law Enforceable Void agreement 2(g) Agreement not enforceable by law Never enforceable Voidable contract 2(i) Enforceable at the option of one or more parties, not the other(s) Enforceable until avoided Void contract 2(j) Contract that ceases to be enforceable Enforceable at first; void later The key questions are always timing and choice : when did it fail, and who decides? See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Start from the agreement. If it is not enforceable, it is a void agreement. If it is enforceable, it is a contract: valid, voidable at one party's option, or later void when it ceases to be enforceable. flowchart TD A["AGREEMENT (s.2(e))"] VA["VOID AGREEMENT (s.2(g))

A contract may be a valid contract (enforceable by both), a voidable contract (Section 2(i): enforceable at one party's option, e.g. coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, prevention, time of essence; on rescission restore under Section 64), or a void contract (Section 2(j): valid when made, later ceases to be enforceable, e.g. impossible or unlawful under Section 56; restore under Section 65).
keyPoints: Void agreement: never enforceable (Section 2(g)). Voidable contract: enforceable until the option-holder avoids it (Section 2(i)). Void contract: valid when made, later ceases to be enforceable (Section 2(j)). The wronged party can avoid, or after fraud or misrepresentation insist on performance (Section 19). No avoidance for misrepresentation or fraudulent silence if the party could have found the truth with ordinary diligence (Section 19, Exception). Voidable contracts also arise under Sections 19A, 53 and 55. Section 64: the party who rescinds restores benefits. Section 65: benefits under a void agreement or contract are restored; not for a minor ( Mohori Bibee ).

caseLaws.name: Mohori Bibee v
caseLaws.facts: Dharmodas Ghose (1903) Facts. A minor mortgaged his houses to a money-lender to secure Rs. 20,000; the lender's agent knew he was a minor. The minor sued to set the mortgage aside, and the lender asked for repayment of the money advanced, relying on Sections 64 and 65. Principle. "There is not any such voidable contract as is dealt with in Section 64"; Section 65, "like Section 64, starts from the basis of there being an agreement or contract between competent parties". (1903) LR 30 IA 114 : ILR 30 Cal 539. Why it matters. It marks the limit of Sections 64 and 65: they do not reach a minor's agreement. Satyabrata Ghose v. Mugneeram Bangur & Co. (1953) Facts. A company agreed to sell a plot in a housing scheme in Greater Calcutta and to build roads. In 1941 much of the land was requisitioned for military purposes, and the company told the buyer to treat the agreement as cancelled and take back his earnest money . Principle. "Impossible" in Section 56 is not "physical or literal impossibility"; but a temporary requisition, with no time fixed for the roads, did not upset the foundation of the contract, so it was not frustrated. [1954] SCR 310. Why it matters. It explains when a contract "becomes void" under Section 56, and when it does not.

selfTest.q: 1. What is a voidable contract?
selfTest.a: An agreement enforceable by law at the option of one or more of the parties, but not at the option of the other or others (Section 2(i)).

selfTest.q: 2. How does a void contract differ from a void agreement?
selfTest.a: A void contract was valid when made and later ceases to be enforceable. A void agreement is not enforceable from the start.

selfTest.q: 3. What must a party do who rescinds a voidable contract?
selfTest.a: Restore any benefit he received under it, so far as may be (Section 64).

selfTest.q: 4. A, induced by B's fraud, buys B's land. Can B avoid the contract?
selfTest.a: No. Only the party whose consent was caused by fraud (A) has the option.

selfTest.q: 5. A contracts to marry B. Before the date, A goes mad. Effect?
selfTest.a: The contract becomes void (Section 56, Illustration (b)).

selfTest.q: 6. A is paid ₹10,000 in advance to sing at a wedding and falls too ill to sing. Must A refund it?
selfTest.a: Yes. The contract becomes void, and A must refund the advance, though not B's lost profits (Section 65, compare Illustration (d)).

ఒప్పందం + చట్టప్రకారం అమలు = కాంట్రాక్టు. ఒప్పందం + అమలు కాదు = చెల్లనిది. రద్దు చేయదగినది = అన్యాయానికి గురైన పక్షం రద్దు చేయాలని ఎంచుకునేవరకు కట్టుబడి ఉండేది. ఆ ఎంపిక అతనికి మాత్రమే. తర్వాత అసాధ్యమైన లేదా చట్టవిరుద్ధమైన కాంట్రాక్టు ఆ క్షణం నుంచి చెల్లనిది అవుతుంది. రద్దు చేయదగిన కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేసే పక్షం తాను పొందినదాన్ని తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలి (సెక్షన్ 64). చెల్లని ఒప్పందం, లేదా చెల్లనిదిగా మారిన కాంట్రాక్టు కింద ప్రయోజనం పొందినవారు దాన్ని తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలి (సెక్షన్ 65).

selfTest.q: 1. రద్దు చేయదగిన కాంట్రాక్టు అంటే ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: ఒకరు లేదా అంతకంటే ఎక్కువ పక్షాల ఆప్షన్ మేరకు చట్టప్రకారం అమలయ్యే, మిగతావారి ఆప్షన్ మేరకు అమలు కాని ఒప్పందం (సెక్షన్ 2(i)).

selfTest.q: 2. చెల్లని కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లని ఒప్పందం నుంచి ఎలా వేరు?
selfTest.a: చెల్లని కాంట్రాక్టు చేసినప్పుడు చెల్లుబాటయ్యేది, తర్వాత అమలు కాకుండా పోతుంది. చెల్లని ఒప్పందం మొదటి నుంచే అమలు కాదు.

selfTest.q: 3. రద్దు చేయదగిన కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేసే పక్షం ఏం చేయాలి?
selfTest.a: దాని కింద పొందిన ప్రయోజనాన్ని వీలైనంత మేరకు తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలి (సెక్షన్ 64).

selfTest.q: 4. B మోసంతో A, B భూమిని కొంటాడు. B కాంట్రాక్టును రద్దు చేయగలడా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. మోసంతో సమ్మతి పొందిన పక్షానికి (A) మాత్రమే ఆప్షన్ ఉంది.

selfTest.q: 5. A, B ని పెళ్లి చేసుకోవడానికి కాంట్రాక్టు చేస్తాడు. తేదీకి ముందే A కి మతిస్థిమితం తప్పుతుంది. ప్రభావం?
selfTest.a: కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లనిది అవుతుంది (సెక్షన్ 56, Illustration (b)).

selfTest.q: 6. ఒక పెళ్లిలో పాడటానికి A కి ₹10,000 ముందుగా ఇచ్చారు; A పాడలేనంత అనారోగ్యం పాలవుతాడు. A దాన్ని తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలా?
selfTest.a: అవును. కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లనిది అవుతుంది; B కోల్పోయిన లాభాలు కాకపోయినా, A అడ్వాన్స్ తిరిగి ఇవ్వాలి (సెక్షన్ 65, Illustration (d) తో పోల్చండి).

hi.inOneMinute: The Act uses three similar words for three different things: A void agreement is never enforceable. It never became a contract (Section 2(g)). A voidable contract is valid until the party with the option cancels it (Section 2(i)). A void contract was valid when made, but later stops being enforceable (Section 2(j)). These labels decide who can sue, who can walk away, and what happens to money already paid (Sections 64 and 65). In exams, the three definitions, the comparison table and the sources of each earn the marks. In real life they decide whether you can walk away from a deal and get your money back.
legalProvision: Section 2. In this Act the following words and expressions are used in the following senses, unless a contrary intention appears from the context:— (e) Every promise and every set of promises, forming the consideration for each other, is an agreement; (g) An agreement not enforceable by law is said to be void; (h) An agreement enforceable by law is a contract; (i) An agreement which is enforceable by law at the option of one or more of the parties thereto, but not at the option of the other or others, is a voidable contract; (j) A contract which ceases to be enforceable by law becomes void when it ceases to be enforceable.

Section 19. Voidability of agreements without free consent. When consent to an agreement is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. A party to a contract whose consent was caused by fraud or misrepresentation, may, if he thinks fit, insist that the contract shall be performed, and that he shall be put in the position in which he would have been if the representations made had been true. Exception. —If such consent was caused by misrepresentation or by silence, fraudulent within the meaning of section 17, the contract, nevertheless, is not voidable, if the party whose consent was so caused had the means of discovering the truth with ordinary diligence. Explanation. —A fraud or misrepresentation which did not cause the consent to a contract of the party on whom such fraud was practised, or to whom such misrepresentation was made, does not render a contract voidable. Illustration (b). A, by a misrepresentation, leads B erroneously to believe that, five hundred maunds of indigo are made annually at A's factory. B examines the accounts of the factory, which show that only four hundred maunds of indigo have been made. After this B buys the factory. The contract is not voidable on account of A's misrepresentation. Illustration (c). A fraudulently informs B that A's estate is free from incumbrance. B thereupon buys the estate. The estate is subject to a mortgage. B may either avoid the contract, or may insist on its being carried out and the mortgage debt redeemed.

Section 19A. Power to set aside contract induced by undue influence. When consent to an agreement is caused by undue influence, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused. Any such contract may be set aside either absolutely or, if the party who was entitled to avoid it has received any benefit thereunder, upon such terms and conditions as to the Court may seem just. Illustration (b). A, a money-lender, advances Rs. 100 to B, an agriculturist, and, by undue influence, induces B to execute a bond for Rs. 200 with interest at 6 per cent. per month. The Court may set the bond aside, ordering B to repay the Rs. 100 with such interest as may seem just.

Section 53 (first part). When a contract contains reciprocal promises, and one party to the contract prevents the other from performing his promise, the contract becomes voidable at the option of the party so prevented; and he is entitled to compensation from the other party for any loss which he may sustain in consequence of the non-performance of the contract.

Section 55 (first two paragraphs). When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract. Effect of such failure when time is not essential. —If it was not the intention of the parties that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract does not become voidable by the failure to do such thing at or before the specified time; but the promisee is entitled to compensation from the promisor for any loss occasioned to him by such failure.

Section 56 (first two paragraphs). An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. Contract to do an act afterwards becoming impossible or unlawful. —A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Illustrations. (a) A agrees with B to discover treasure by magic. The agreement is void. (b) A and B contract to marry each other. Before the time fixed for the marriage, A goes mad. The contract becomes void. (d) A contracts to take in cargo for B at a foreign port. A's Government afterwards declares war against the country in which the port is situated. The contract becomes void when war is declared.

Section 64. Consequences of rescission of voidable contract. When a person at whose option a contract is voidable rescinds it, the other party thereto need not perform any promise therein contained in which he is promisor. The party rescinding a voidable contract shall, if he have received any benefit thereunder from another party to such contract, restore such benefit, so far as may be, to the person from whom it was received.

Section 65. Obligation of person who has received advantage under void agreement, or contract that becomes void. When an agreement is discovered to be void, or when a contract becomes void, any person who has received any advantage under such agreement or contract is bound to restore it, or to make compensation for it to the person from whom he received it. Illustration (d). A contracts to sing for B at a concert for 1,000 rupees, which are paid in advance. A is too ill to sing. A is not bound to make compensation to B for the loss of the profits which B would have made if A had been able to sing, but must refund to B the 1,000 rupees paid in advance.
In simple words

Agreement + enforceable by law = contract . Agreement + not enforceable = void. Voidable = binding until the wronged party chooses to cancel it. Only he has that choice. A contract that later becomes impossible or unlawful becomes void from that moment. The party who cancels a voidable contract gives back what he received (Section 64). Whoever got an advantage under a void agreement or a contract that becomes void gives it back (Section 65).

The Act builds the three ideas on Section 2: Term Section Meaning Status from the start Agreement 2(e) Promises forming consideration for each other May or may not be enforceable Contract 2(h) Agreement enforceable by law Enforceable Void agreement 2(g) Agreement not enforceable by law Never enforceable Voidable contract 2(i) Enforceable at the option of one or more parties, not the other(s) Enforceable until avoided Void contract 2(j) Contract that ceases to be enforceable Enforceable at first; void later The key questions are always timing and choice : when did it fail, and who decides? See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Start from the agreement. If it is not enforceable, it is a void agreement. If it is enforceable, it is a contract: valid, voidable at one party's option, or later void when it ceases to be enforceable. flowchart TD A["AGREEMENT (s.2(e))"] VA["VOID AGREEMENT (s.2(g))

A contract may be a valid contract (enforceable by both), a voidable contract (Section 2(i): enforceable at one party's option, e.g. coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation, prevention, time of essence; on rescission restore under Section 64), or a void contract (Section 2(j): valid when made, later ceases to be enforceable, e.g. impossible or unlawful under Section 56; restore under Section 65).
keyPoints: Void agreement: never enforceable (Section 2(g)). Voidable contract: enforceable until the option-holder avoids it (Section 2(i)). Void contract: valid when made, later ceases to be enforceable (Section 2(j)). The wronged party can avoid, or after fraud or misrepresentation insist on performance (Section 19). No avoidance for misrepresentation or fraudulent silence if the party could have found the truth with ordinary diligence (Section 19, Exception). Voidable contracts also arise under Sections 19A, 53 and 55. Section 64: the party who rescinds restores benefits. Section 65: benefits under a void agreement or contract are restored; not for a minor ( Mohori Bibee ).

caseLaws.name: Mohori Bibee v
caseLaws.facts: Dharmodas Ghose (1903) Facts. A minor mortgaged his houses to a money-lender to secure Rs. 20,000; the lender's agent knew he was a minor. The minor sued to set the mortgage aside, and the lender asked for repayment of the money advanced, relying on Sections 64 and 65. Principle. "There is not any such voidable contract as is dealt with in Section 64"; Section 65, "like Section 64, starts from the basis of there being an agreement or contract between competent parties". (1903) LR 30 IA 114 : ILR 30 Cal 539. Why it matters. It marks the limit of Sections 64 and 65: they do not reach a minor's agreement. Satyabrata Ghose v. Mugneeram Bangur & Co. (1953) Facts. A company agreed to sell a plot in a housing scheme in Greater Calcutta and to build roads. In 1941 much of the land was requisitioned for military purposes, and the company told the buyer to treat the agreement as cancelled and take back his earnest money . Principle. "Impossible" in Section 56 is not "physical or literal impossibility"; but a temporary requisition, with no time fixed for the roads, did not upset the foundation of the contract, so it was not frustrated. [1954] SCR 310. Why it matters. It explains when a contract "becomes void" under Section 56, and when it does not.

selfTest.q: 1. What is a voidable contract?
selfTest.a: An agreement enforceable by law at the option of one or more of the parties, but not at the option of the other or others (Section 2(i)).

selfTest.q: 2. How does a void contract differ from a void agreement?
selfTest.a: A void contract was valid when made and later ceases to be enforceable. A void agreement is not enforceable from the start.

selfTest.q: 3. What must a party do who rescinds a voidable contract?
selfTest.a: Restore any benefit he received under it, so far as may be (Section 64).

selfTest.q: 4. A, induced by B's fraud, buys B's land. Can B avoid the contract?
selfTest.a: No. Only the party whose consent was caused by fraud (A) has the option.

selfTest.q: 5. A contracts to marry B. Before the date, A goes mad. Effect?
selfTest.a: The contract becomes void (Section 56, Illustration (b)).

selfTest.q: 6. A is paid ₹10,000 in advance to sing at a wedding and falls too ill to sing. Must A refund it?
selfTest.a: Yes. The contract becomes void, and A must refund the advance, though not B's lost profits (Section 65, compare Illustration (d)).

law-of-contract-i-u2-t15.subtitle: Sections 31 to 36 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872

en.inOneMinute: A contingent contract is a contract to do or not to do something if some event, collateral to the contract, does or does not happen (Section 31). An insurance policy is the everyday example: the insurer pays only if the insured event (fire, theft, death) happens. Sections 32 to 36 say when such a contract can be enforced and when it becomes void : event must happen: enforce after it happens; void if it becomes impossible (Section 32); event must not happen: enforce when it becomes impossible (Section 33); event is a living person's conduct: impossible once he makes it so (Section 34); event within a fixed time: time limit decides (Section 35); impossible event: void from the start (Section 36). In exams, each section with its Illustration earns the marks. In real life these rules govern insurance, guarantees and conditional sales.
legalProvision: Section 31. "Contingent contract" defined. A "contingent contract" is a contract to do or not to do something, if some event, collateral to such contract, does or does not happen. Illustration. A contracts to pay B Rs. 10,000 if B's house is burnt. This is a contingent contract.

Section 32. Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event happening. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event happens cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened. If the event becomes impossible, such contracts become void. Illustrations. (a) A makes a contract with B to buy B's horse if A survives C. This contract cannot be enforced by law unless and until C dies in A's lifetime. (b) A makes a contract with B to sell a horse to B at a specified price, if C, to whom the horse has been offered, refuses to buy him. The contract cannot be enforced by law unless and until C refuses to buy the horse. (c) A contracts to pay B a sum of money when B marries C. C dies without being married to B. The contract becomes void.

Section 33. Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event not happening. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event does not happen can be enforced when the happening of that event becomes impossible, and not before. Illustration. A agrees to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship does not return. The ship is sunk. The contract can be enforced when the ship sinks.

Section 34. When event on which contract is contingent to be deemed impossible, if it is the future conduct of a living person. If the future event on which a contract is contingent is the way in which a person will act at an unspecified time, the event shall be considered to become impossible when such person does anything which renders it impossible that he should so act within any definite time, or otherwise than under further contingencies. Illustration. A agrees to pay B a sum of money if B marries C. C marries D. The marriage of B to C must now be considered impossible, although it is possible that D may die and that C may afterwards marry B.

Section 35. When contracts become void which are contingent on happening of specified event within fixed time. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if a specified uncertain event happens within a fixed time become void if, at the expiration of the time fixed, such event has not happened, or if, before the time fixed, such event becomes impossible. When contracts may be enforced, which are contingent on specified event not happening within fixed time. —Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything, if a specified uncertain event does not happen within a fixed time may be enforced by law when the time fixed has expired and such event has not happened or, before the time fixed has expired, if it becomes certain that such event will not happen. Illustrations. (a) A promises to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship returns within a year. The contract may be enforced if the ship returns within the year, and becomes void if the ship is burnt within the year. (b) A promises to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship does not return within a year. The contract may be enforced if the ship does not return within the year, or is burnt within the year.

Section 36. Agreement contingent on impossible events void. Contingent agreements to do or not to do anything, if an impossible event happens, are void, whether the impossibility of the event is known or not to the parties to the agreement at the time when it is made. Illustrations. (a) A agrees to pay B 1,000 rupees if two straight lines should enclose a space. The agreement is void. (b) A agrees to pay B 1,000 rupees if B will marry A's daughter C. C was dead at the time of the agreement. The agreement is void.
In simple words

A contingent contract is a real contract from the start; only the duty to perform waits for the event. "If it happens" contracts : wait for the event; void if the event becomes impossible. "If it does not happen" contracts: enforce once the event becomes impossible. A time limit sets a cut-off. An event that is impossible from the start makes the agreement void.
en.meaning:
A contingent contract has a promise whose performance depends on an event. Three things mark the event: Mark Meaning Example 1. Future It has not yet happened A fire next year 2. Uncertain It may or may not happen Fire, theft, a ship's return 3. Collateral It is separate from the promised act itself, not the consideration or the performance The fire is not part of what the insurer promises to do The contract exists from the start. What waits is the duty to perform. Collateral, not part of the bargain. If the "event" is simply one party doing his part of the exchange, it is not a contingent event. "I will pay you ₹1,000 when you deliver the books" is an ordinary contract with reciprocal promises, not a contingent contract. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. First ask whether the event is impossible from the start. Then ask whether the contract depends on the event happening or not happening, and whether there is a fixed time. flowchart TD S["Contingent contract (s.31)

If yes, the agreement is void (Section 36). If no, does the contract depend on the event happening or not happening? If happening: with a fixed time, enforce if it happens in time, void if the time expires or it becomes impossible (Section 35); without a fixed time, enforce only after it happens, void if it becomes impossible (Section 32). If not happening: with a fixed time, enforce when the time expires without it or it becomes certain it will not happen (Section 35); without a fixed time, enforce when it becomes impossible (Section 33). If the event is a living person's conduct, it is impossible once he makes it so (Section 34).
keyPoints: A contingent contract depends on an uncertain event collateral to the contract (Section 31). If the event must happen, the contract is enforceable once it happens and void if it becomes impossible (Section 32). If the event must not happen, the contract is enforceable once the event becomes impossible (Section 33). A living person's own act can make an event impossible (Section 34). A fixed time adds a cut-off (Section 35). An impossible event makes the agreement void, whether known or not (Section 36). The contract is enforceable, and limitation runs, from the event ( Ramzan v. Hussaini ).

caseLaws.name: Ramzan v
caseLaws.facts: Hussaini (1989) Facts. By an agreement of 23 June 1965, a brother agreed to execute a sale deed of a house to his sister once she redeemed its mortgage. She redeemed it in 1970, served a notice in 1984 and sued for specific performance. The courts below held the suit within time. Principle. The agreement "is a typical illustration of a contingent contract" under Section 31; it "became enforceable as soon as the event of redemption" happened, and the date for performance was fixed by that event, so the three-year period under Article 54 ran from it. The appeal was allowed and the suit dismissed. AIR 1990 SC 529 : (1990) 1 SCC 104. Why it matters. A contingent contract becomes enforceable when the event happens, and limitation runs from then.

selfTest.q: 1. What is a contingent contract?
selfTest.a: A contract to do or not to do something if some event, collateral to the contract, does or does not happen (Section 31).

selfTest.q: 2. When can a contract contingent on an event not happening be enforced?
selfTest.a: When the happening of the event becomes impossible, and not before (Section 33).

selfTest.q: 3. What is the effect of a contingent agreement on an impossible event?
selfTest.a: It is void, whether or not the parties knew of the impossibility (Section 36).

selfTest.q: 4. A promises B ₹1,00,000 if B marries C. C marries D. What is the position?
selfTest.a: The marriage of B to C is considered impossible (Section 34), so the contract becomes void (Section 32).

selfTest.q: 5. A promises to pay B if a ship returns within a year. The ship is burnt in the sixth month. Effect?
selfTest.a: The contract becomes void (Section 35, Illustration (a)).

selfTest.q: 6. Is "I will pay you ₹1,000 when you deliver the books" a contingent contract?
selfTest.a: No. Delivery is B's own performance, not a collateral event.

legalProvision: Section 31. "Contingent contract" defined. A "contingent contract" is a contract to do or not to do something, if some event, collateral to such contract, does or does not happen. Illustration. A contracts to pay B Rs. 10,000 if B's house is burnt. This is a contingent contract.

Section 32. Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event happening. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event happens cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened. If the event becomes impossible, such contracts become void. Illustrations. (a) A makes a contract with B to buy B's horse if A survives C. This contract cannot be enforced by law unless and until C dies in A's lifetime. (b) A makes a contract with B to sell a horse to B at a specified price, if C, to whom the horse has been offered, refuses to buy him. The contract cannot be enforced by law unless and until C refuses to buy the horse. (c) A contracts to pay B a sum of money when B marries C. C dies without being married to B. The contract becomes void.

Section 33. Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event not happening. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event does not happen can be enforced when the happening of that event becomes impossible, and not before. Illustration. A agrees to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship does not return. The ship is sunk. The contract can be enforced when the ship sinks.

Section 34. When event on which contract is contingent to be deemed impossible, if it is the future conduct of a living person. If the future event on which a contract is contingent is the way in which a person will act at an unspecified time, the event shall be considered to become impossible when such person does anything which renders it impossible that he should so act within any definite time, or otherwise than under further contingencies. Illustration. A agrees to pay B a sum of money if B marries C. C marries D. The marriage of B to C must now be considered impossible, although it is possible that D may die and that C may afterwards marry B.

Section 35. When contracts become void which are contingent on happening of specified event within fixed time. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if a specified uncertain event happens within a fixed time become void if, at the expiration of the time fixed, such event has not happened, or if, before the time fixed, such event becomes impossible. When contracts may be enforced, which are contingent on specified event not happening within fixed time. —Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything, if a specified uncertain event does not happen within a fixed time may be enforced by law when the time fixed has expired and such event has not happened or, before the time fixed has expired, if it becomes certain that such event will not happen. Illustrations. (a) A promises to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship returns within a year. The contract may be enforced if the ship returns within the year, and becomes void if the ship is burnt within the year. (b) A promises to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship does not return within a year. The contract may be enforced if the ship does not return within the year, or is burnt within the year.

Section 36. Agreement contingent on impossible events void. Contingent agreements to do or not to do anything, if an impossible event happens, are void, whether the impossibility of the event is known or not to the parties to the agreement at the time when it is made. Illustrations. (a) A agrees to pay B 1,000 rupees if two straight lines should enclose a space. The agreement is void. (b) A agrees to pay B 1,000 rupees if B will marry A's daughter C. C was dead at the time of the agreement. The agreement is void.

షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టు మొదటి నుంచే నిజమైన కాంట్రాక్టు; అమలు చేసే బాధ్యత మాత్రమే సంఘటన కోసం ఆగుతుంది. "అది జరిగితే" కాంట్రాక్టులు: సంఘటన కోసం ఆగాలి; సంఘటన అసాధ్యమైతే చెల్లదు. "అది జరగకపోతే" కాంట్రాక్టులు: సంఘటన అసాధ్యమైన వెంటనే అమలు. కాల పరిమితి ఒక గడువు పెడుతుంది. మొదటి నుంచే అసాధ్యమైన సంఘటన ఒప్పందాన్ని చెల్లనిదిగా చేస్తుంది.

షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టులో ఒక వాగ్దానం అమలు ఒక సంఘటనపై ఆధారపడి ఉంటుంది. ఆ సంఘటనకు మూడు లక్షణాలు: లక్షణం అర్థం ఉదాహరణ 1. భవిష్యత్ ఇంకా జరగలేదు వచ్చే ఏడాది అగ్ని ప్రమాదం 2. అనిశ్చితం జరగవచ్చు, జరగకపోవచ్చు అగ్ని, దొంగతనం, ఓడ తిరిగి రావడం 3. అనుబంధం ( collateral ) వాగ్దానం చేసిన పని నుంచి వేరైనది; ప్రతిఫలం గానీ, అమలు గానీ కాదు అగ్ని ప్రమాదం బీమా సంస్థ చేస్తానన్న పనిలో భాగం కాదు కాంట్రాక్టు మొదటి నుంచే ఉంటుంది. ఆగేది అమలు చేసే బాధ్యత మాత్రమే. అనుబంధం, బేరంలో భాగం కాదు. "సంఘటన" అంటే కేవలం ఒక పక్షం తన వంతు బేరాన్ని నెరవేర్చడమే అయితే, అది షరతుతో కూడిన సంఘటన కాదు. "నువ్వు పుస్తకాలు అందించినప్పుడు ₹1,000 ఇస్తాను" అనేది పరస్పర వాగ్దానాలతో కూడిన సాధారణ కాంట్రాక్టు; షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టు కాదు. Diagram 1 చూడండి. selfTest.q: 1. షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టు అంటే ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: కాంట్రాక్టుకు అనుబంధమైన ఏదో సంఘటన జరిగితే లేదా జరగకపోతే, ఏదైనా చేయడానికి లేదా చేయకుండా ఉండడానికి చేసే కాంట్రాక్టు (సెక్షన్ 31).

selfTest.q: 2. సంఘటన జరగకపోవడంపై ఆధారపడిన కాంట్రాక్టు ఎప్పుడు అమలవుతుంది?
selfTest.a: సంఘటన జరగడం అసాధ్యమైనప్పుడు, అంతకు ముందు కాదు (సెక్షన్ 33).

selfTest.q: 3. అసాధ్యమైన సంఘటనపై ఆధారపడిన ఒప్పందం ప్రభావం ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: పక్షాలకు ఆ అసాధ్యత తెలిసినా తెలియకపోయినా అది చెల్లదు (సెక్షన్ 36).

selfTest.q: 4. B, C ని పెళ్లి చేసుకుంటే B కి ₹1,00,000 ఇస్తానని A వాగ్దానం చేస్తాడు. C, D ని పెళ్లి చేసుకుంటుంది. స్థితి ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: B, C ల పెళ్లి అసాధ్యంగా పరిగణించబడుతుంది (సెక్షన్ 34); కాబట్టి కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లనిది అవుతుంది (సెక్షన్ 32).

selfTest.q: 5. ఒక ఓడ ఏడాదిలోపు తిరిగి వస్తే B కి చెల్లిస్తానని A వాగ్దానం చేస్తాడు. ఆరో నెలలో ఓడ కాలిపోతుంది. ప్రభావం?
selfTest.a: కాంట్రాక్టు చెల్లనిది అవుతుంది (సెక్షన్ 35, Illustration (a)).

selfTest.q: 6. "నువ్వు పుస్తకాలు అందించినప్పుడు ₹1,000 ఇస్తాను" అనేది షరతులతో కూడిన కాంట్రాక్టా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. పుస్తకాలు అందించడం B సొంత అమలు; అనుబంధ సంఘటన కాదు.

hi.inOneMinute: A contingent contract is a contract to do or not to do something if some event, collateral to the contract, does or does not happen (Section 31). An insurance policy is the everyday example: the insurer pays only if the insured event (fire, theft, death) happens. Sections 32 to 36 say when such a contract can be enforced and when it becomes void : event must happen: enforce after it happens; void if it becomes impossible (Section 32); event must not happen: enforce when it becomes impossible (Section 33); event is a living person's conduct: impossible once he makes it so (Section 34); event within a fixed time: time limit decides (Section 35); impossible event: void from the start (Section 36). In exams, each section with its Illustration earns the marks. In real life these rules govern insurance, guarantees and conditional sales.
legalProvision: Section 31. "Contingent contract" defined. A "contingent contract" is a contract to do or not to do something, if some event, collateral to such contract, does or does not happen. Illustration. A contracts to pay B Rs. 10,000 if B's house is burnt. This is a contingent contract.

Section 32. Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event happening. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event happens cannot be enforced by law unless and until that event has happened. If the event becomes impossible, such contracts become void. Illustrations. (a) A makes a contract with B to buy B's horse if A survives C. This contract cannot be enforced by law unless and until C dies in A's lifetime. (b) A makes a contract with B to sell a horse to B at a specified price, if C, to whom the horse has been offered, refuses to buy him. The contract cannot be enforced by law unless and until C refuses to buy the horse. (c) A contracts to pay B a sum of money when B marries C. C dies without being married to B. The contract becomes void.

Section 33. Enforcement of contracts contingent on an event not happening. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if an uncertain future event does not happen can be enforced when the happening of that event becomes impossible, and not before. Illustration. A agrees to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship does not return. The ship is sunk. The contract can be enforced when the ship sinks.

Section 34. When event on which contract is contingent to be deemed impossible, if it is the future conduct of a living person. If the future event on which a contract is contingent is the way in which a person will act at an unspecified time, the event shall be considered to become impossible when such person does anything which renders it impossible that he should so act within any definite time, or otherwise than under further contingencies. Illustration. A agrees to pay B a sum of money if B marries C. C marries D. The marriage of B to C must now be considered impossible, although it is possible that D may die and that C may afterwards marry B.

Section 35. When contracts become void which are contingent on happening of specified event within fixed time. Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything if a specified uncertain event happens within a fixed time become void if, at the expiration of the time fixed, such event has not happened, or if, before the time fixed, such event becomes impossible. When contracts may be enforced, which are contingent on specified event not happening within fixed time. —Contingent contracts to do or not to do anything, if a specified uncertain event does not happen within a fixed time may be enforced by law when the time fixed has expired and such event has not happened or, before the time fixed has expired, if it becomes certain that such event will not happen. Illustrations. (a) A promises to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship returns within a year. The contract may be enforced if the ship returns within the year, and becomes void if the ship is burnt within the year. (b) A promises to pay B a sum of money if a certain ship does not return within a year. The contract may be enforced if the ship does not return within the year, or is burnt within the year.

Section 36. Agreement contingent on impossible events void. Contingent agreements to do or not to do anything, if an impossible event happens, are void, whether the impossibility of the event is known or not to the parties to the agreement at the time when it is made. Illustrations. (a) A agrees to pay B 1,000 rupees if two straight lines should enclose a space. The agreement is void. (b) A agrees to pay B 1,000 rupees if B will marry A's daughter C. C was dead at the time of the agreement. The agreement is void.
In simple words

A contingent contract is a real contract from the start; only the duty to perform waits for the event. "If it happens" contracts : wait for the event; void if the event becomes impossible. "If it does not happen" contracts: enforce once the event becomes impossible. A time limit sets a cut-off. An event that is impossible from the start makes the agreement void.
hi.meaning:
A contingent contract has a promise whose performance depends on an event. Three things mark the event: Mark Meaning Example 1. Future It has not yet happened A fire next year 2. Uncertain It may or may not happen Fire, theft, a ship's return 3. Collateral It is separate from the promised act itself, not the consideration or the performance The fire is not part of what the insurer promises to do The contract exists from the start. What waits is the duty to perform. Collateral, not part of the bargain. If the "event" is simply one party doing his part of the exchange, it is not a contingent event. "I will pay you ₹1,000 when you deliver the books" is an ordinary contract with reciprocal promises, not a contingent contract. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. First ask whether the event is impossible from the start. Then ask whether the contract depends on the event happening or not happening, and whether there is a fixed time. flowchart TD S["Contingent contract (s.31)

VOID if it becomes impossible (s.32)"] N35["Enforce when time expires without it,

impossible, not before (s.33)"] L34["Living person's conduct: impossible

If yes, the agreement is void (Section 36). If no, does the contract depend on the event happening or not happening? If happening: with a fixed time, enforce if it happens in time, void if the time expires or it becomes impossible (Section 35); without a fixed time, enforce only after it happens, void if it becomes impossible (Section 32). If not happening: with a fixed time, enforce when the time expires without it or it becomes certain it will not happen (Section 35); without a fixed time, enforce when it becomes impossible (Section 33). If the event is a living person's conduct, it is impossible once he makes it so (Section 34).
keyPoints: A contingent contract depends on an uncertain event collateral to the contract (Section 31). If the event must happen, the contract is enforceable once it happens and void if it becomes impossible (Section 32). If the event must not happen, the contract is enforceable once the event becomes impossible (Section 33). A living person's own act can make an event impossible (Section 34). A fixed time adds a cut-off (Section 35). An impossible event makes the agreement void, whether known or not (Section 36). The contract is enforceable, and limitation runs, from the event ( Ramzan v. Hussaini ).

caseLaws.name: Ramzan v
caseLaws.facts: Hussaini (1989) Facts. By an agreement of 23 June 1965, a brother agreed to execute a sale deed of a house to his sister once she redeemed its mortgage. She redeemed it in 1970, served a notice in 1984 and sued for specific performance. The courts below held the suit within time. Principle. The agreement "is a typical illustration of a contingent contract" under Section 31; it "became enforceable as soon as the event of redemption" happened, and the date for performance was fixed by that event, so the three-year period under Article 54 ran from it. The appeal was allowed and the suit dismissed. AIR 1990 SC 529 : (1990) 1 SCC 104. Why it matters. A contingent contract becomes enforceable when the event happens, and limitation runs from then.

selfTest.q: 1. What is a contingent contract?
selfTest.a: A contract to do or not to do something if some event, collateral to the contract, does or does not happen (Section 31).

selfTest.q: 2. When can a contract contingent on an event not happening be enforced?
selfTest.a: When the happening of the event becomes impossible, and not before (Section 33).

selfTest.q: 3. What is the effect of a contingent agreement on an impossible event?
selfTest.a: It is void, whether or not the parties knew of the impossibility (Section 36).

selfTest.q: 4. A promises B ₹1,00,000 if B marries C. C marries D. What is the position?
selfTest.a: The marriage of B to C is considered impossible (Section 34), so the contract becomes void (Section 32).

selfTest.q: 5. A promises to pay B if a ship returns within a year. The ship is burnt in the sixth month. Effect?
selfTest.a: The contract becomes void (Section 35, Illustration (a)).

selfTest.q: 6. Is "I will pay you ₹1,000 when you deliver the books" a contingent contract?
selfTest.a: No. Delivery is B's own performance, not a collateral event.

en.meaning:
X agrees to sell his car to B for ₹50,000 or ₹1,00,000, with nothing in the agreement showing which price was meant. This agreement is:

Explanation. Since the price term has no fixed, ascertainable meaning and nothing in the agreement resolves which figure applies, it is void for uncertainty under Section 29.

In Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya, the Supreme Court held that a partnership formed to carry on wagering transactions is:

Explanation. The Court held that wagering agreements are void under Section 30 but are not 'immoral' or otherwise unlawful under Section 23 — so a partnership formed to conduct a wagering business is not itself illegal.

A collateral agreement connected to a main agreement that is merely VOID (but not illegal):

Explanation. A collateral deal made to further an illegal purpose is tainted. If the main agreement is merely void, such as a wager, a collateral deal is not automatically tainted (Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya). This is the key practical difference between void and illegal.

Section 29 makes an agreement void when:

The Court held that wagering agreements are void under Section 30 but are not 'immoral' or otherwise unlawful under Section 23 — so a partnership formed to conduct a wagering business is not itself illegal. A collateral agreement connected to a main agreement that is merely VOID (but not illegal): Explanation. A collateral deal made to further an illegal purpose is tainted. If the main agreement is merely void, such as a wager, a collateral deal is not automatically tainted (Gherulal Parakh v. Mahadeodas Maiya). en.meaning:
Under Section 27, an agreement in restraint of trade is:

Explanation. Section 27 voids agreements restraining a lawful trade, profession, or business, with the sole statutory exception being a reasonable restriction on the seller in a sale of goodwill.

In Madhub Chander v. Raj Coomar Doss, the Calcutta High Court held that even a PARTIAL restraint of trade (limited to one locality) is:

Explanation. Indian courts read Section 27 strictly — unlike English law's 'reasonableness' approach, even a partial restraint of trade is void unless it falls within the statutory goodwill exception.

In Superintendence Company of India v. Krishan Murgai, the majority held that a clause barring the employee from competing for two years after he 'left' the company:

Explanation. Tulzapurkar and Untwalia, JJ. read 'leave' as voluntary departure, so the clause never applied to an employee dismissed by the company. They did not decide the Section 27 question. Sen, J., concurring in the result, held that a post-service restraint is void under Section 27.

Which of the following is NOT a ground of unlawfulness under Section 23?
