The mediator, a neutral person, helps them talk and reach their own terms. If they agree, they sign a mediated settlement agreement, which the mediator authenticates (Section 19). It is final and binding and enforceable as a decree (Section 27), and can be challenged only on the grounds in Section 28. The mediator does not decide the dispute and cannot impose a settlement.
keyPoints: A mediation agreement is a written contract to mediate present or future disputes (Section 4). The mediator helps. The parties decide. Pre-litigation mediation is voluntary under Section 5. It is mandatory for commercial suits under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act ( Patil Automation ). A mediated settlement agreement is binding and enforceable as a decree (Section 27). Challenge only on fraud, corruption, impersonation or unfit subject matter, within 90 days, plus 90 for sufficient cause (Section 28). Sections 4, 5, 6, 19, 27 and 28 await commencement; only some sections came into force on 9 October 2023.

caseLaws.name: Patil Automation Pvt
caseLaws.facts: Ltd. v. Rakheja Engineers Pvt. Ltd. (2022) Facts. The Supreme Court considered whether pre-institution mediation under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 is mandatory, in commercial suits that did not contemplate urgent interim relief. Principle. It is mandatory: "the language used in Section 12A is plainly imperative in nature" (para 53). A commercial suit filed in breach, where no urgent interim relief is sought, must be rejected, and the court may do so on its own (para 68). Supreme Court, 17 August 2022, K.M. Joseph and Hrishikesh Roy JJ. Why it matters. It is the rule that makes mediation compulsory for commercial suits. Afcons Infrastructure Ltd. v. Cherian Varkey Construction Co. (P) Ltd. (2010) Facts. Afcons sub-contracted part of a Cochin Port Trust bridge and road contract to Cherian Varkey, under a sub-contract with no arbitration clause. The sub-contractor sued for ₹2,10,70,881 with interest, and the trial court referred the suit to arbitration under Section 89. Principle. A court must consider ADR after the pleadings, but it cannot refer a suit to arbitration under Section 89 "unless all the parties to the suit agree" (para 35). A mediation settlement is placed before the court for recording (para 28). The appeal was allowed and the reference set aside. (2010) 8 SCC 24 (26 July 2010, R.V. Raveendran and J.M. Panchal JJ.). Why it matters. It explains court-annexed mediation.

selfTest.q: 1. Must a mediation agreement be in writing?
selfTest.a: Yes. Section 4 of the Mediation Act, 2023 says so.

selfTest.q: 2. How is a mediated settlement agreement enforced?
selfTest.a: As if it were a judgment or decree of a court (Section 27).

selfTest.q: 3. On what grounds can it be challenged?
selfTest.a: Fraud, corruption, impersonation, or because the dispute was not fit for mediation (Section 28).

selfTest.q: 4. Is pre-litigation mediation compulsory under the Mediation Act?
selfTest.a: No. It is voluntary under Section 5. It is compulsory only for commercial suits of Specified Value under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, unless urgent interim relief is contemplated.

selfTest.q: 5. Can a void settlement be a mediated settlement agreement?
selfTest.a: No. The Explanation to Section 19(1) says a settlement void under the Indian Contract Act is not a lawful mediated settlement agreement.

Commercial Courts Act, 2015, Section 12A ( Patil Automation , para 24 లో సుప్రీంకోర్టు ఉదహరించినట్లు; దగ్గరగా చెప్పినది, ఉదహరించిన మాటలు కొటేషన్లలో). (1) "A suit, which does not contemplate any urgent interim relief under this Act, shall not be instituted" "unless the plaintiff exhausts the remedy of pre- institution mediation" "in accordance with such manner and procedure as may be prescribed by rules made by the Central Government." (3) అధికారం పొందిన Authority "shall complete the process of mediation within a period of three months" "from the date of application made by the plaintiff under sub-section (1)"; "the period of mediation may be extended for a further period of two months with the consent of the parties"; "the period during which the parties remained occupied with the pre-institution mediation," "such period shall not be computed for the purpose of limitation under the Limitation Act, 1963". (4) "If the parties to the commercial dispute arrive at a settlement, the same shall be" "reduced into writing and shall be signed by the parties to the dispute and the mediator." (5) "The settlement arrived at under this section shall have the same status and effect" "as if it is an arbitral award on agreed terms under sub-section (4) of section 30" "of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996".
సరళమైన మాటల్లో

సెక్షన్ 4, Mediation Act: మీడియేషన్ ఒప్పందం లిఖితంగా ఉండాలి. వచ్చిన లేదా రాబోయే అన్ని లేదా కొన్ని వివాదాలను మీడియేషన్‌కు అప్పగిస్తామని పక్షాల మధ్య, వారి ద్వారా హక్కు కోరేవారితో సహా, చేసుకునే ఒప్పందం అది. అది కాంట్రాక్టులో ఒక క్లాజుగా గానీ, విడి ఒప్పందంగా గానీ ఉండవచ్చు. సంతకం చేసిన పత్రం, లేఖలు లేదా ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ సమాచార మార్పిడి, లేదా ఒక పక్షం ఒప్పందం ఉందని చెప్పి మరో పక్షం కాదనని pleadings లిఖితమే. వివాదం రాకముందు గానీ, వచ్చిన తర్వాత గానీ మీడియేషన్‌కు అంగీకరించవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 5: మీడియేషన్ ఒప్పందం ఉన్నా లేకపోయినా, సివిల్ లేదా వాణిజ్య దావా వేసే ముందు, పక్షాలు స్వచ్ఛందంగా, పరస్పర అంగీకారంతో pre-litigation మీడియేషన్ ప్రయత్నించవచ్చు. Specified Value ఉన్న వాణిజ్య వివాదాల్లో, pre-litigation మీడియేషన్ Commercial Courts Act, 2015 సెక్షన్ 12A ప్రకారం జరగాలి. సెక్షన్ 6: First Schedule లోని సూచనాత్మక జాబితాలోని వివాదాలు మీడియేషన్‌కు తగినవి కావు. వాటిలో నేర విచారణతో కూడిన వివాదాలు, మైనర్లపై క్లెయిములు, మూడో పక్షాల హక్కులను ప్రభావితం చేసే వివాదాలు ఉన్నాయి. రాజీ చేయదగిన నేరాలను, రాజీ చేయదగిన వైవాహిక నేరాలతో సహా, కోర్టు ఇంకా మీడియేషన్‌కు పంపవచ్చు, కానీ ఫలితం సెక్షన్ 27(2) కింది డిక్రీ కాదు. కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వం First Schedule ను సవరించవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 19: మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం అంటే, మీడియేషన్ ఫలితంగా, కొన్ని లేదా అన్ని వివాదాలను పరిష్కరిస్తూ, కొందరు లేదా అందరు పక్షాల మధ్య, మీడియేటర్ ధృవీకరించిన (authenticated) లిఖిత ఒప్పందం. దాని నిబంధనలు అప్పగించిన వివాదాలను మించి వెళ్లవచ్చు. Indian Contract Act, 1872 కింద శూన్యమైన సెటిల్‌మెంట్ చట్టబద్ధమైన మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం కాదు. సెక్షన్ 27: పక్షాలు సంతకం చేసి, మీడియేటర్ ధృవీకరించిన మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం పక్షాలపై, వారి కింద హక్కు కోరేవారిపై అంతిమమైనది, కట్టుబడి ఉండాల్సినది. కోర్టు తీర్పు లేదా డిక్రీ లాగే Code of Civil Procedure కింద దాన్ని అమలు చేస్తారు; defence లేదా set-off గా కూడా వాడుకోవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 28: మోసం, అవినీతి, ఇతరుడిగా నటించడం (impersonation), లేదా సెక్షన్ 6 కింద వివాదం మీడియేషన్‌కు తగినది కాకపోవడం అనే కారణాలపై మాత్రమే దాన్ని సవాలు చేయవచ్చు. ప్రతి అందిన 90 రోజుల్లో దరఖాస్తు చేయాలి; తగిన కారణం ఉంటే మరో 90 రోజులు పొడిగించవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 12A, Commercial Courts Act: అత్యవసర మధ్యంతర ఉపశమనం కోరని వాణిజ్య దావాను, వాది pre-institution మీడియేషన్ ప్రయత్నించే వరకు వేయకూడదు. మీడియేషన్ మూడు నెలల్లో పూర్తి కావాలి, అంగీకారంతో రెండు నెలలు పొడిగించవచ్చు, ఆ సమయాన్ని limitation కు లెక్కించరు. సెటిల్‌మెంట్‌ను లిఖితంగా రాసి పక్షాలు, మీడియేటర్ సంతకం చేస్తారు; దానికి అంగీకరించిన నిబంధనలపై arbitral award హోదా ఉంటుంది. సెక్షన్ 89, CPC: పక్షాలకు ఆమోదయోగ్యమైన సెటిల్‌మెంట్ అంశాలు ఉన్నచోట, కోర్టు వివాదాన్ని arbitration, conciliation, judicial settlement (Lok Adalat తో సహా) లేదా మీడియేషన్‌కు పంపవచ్చు. మీడియేషన్‌లో, నిర్దేశిత విధానం ప్రకారం కోర్టు పక్షాల మధ్య రాజీ కుదురుస్తుంది.
te.meaning:
మీడియేషన్ ఒప్పందం అంటే, ఒక మీడియేటర్ సహాయంతో వివాదాలను పరిష్కరించుకోవడానికి ప్రయత్నిస్తామని పక్షాలు అంగీకరించే కాంట్రాక్టు. మీడియేటర్ తటస్థ (ఏ వైపూ మొగ్గని) వ్యక్తి; పక్షాలు తమ సొంత సెటిల్‌మెంట్‌కు చేరడానికి సహాయం చేస్తారు. ఆయన నిర్ణయించరు. పక్షాలు అంగీకరిస్తే ఫలితం మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం. కాంట్రాక్టు కాబట్టి, మీడియేషన్ ఒప్పందం Indian Contract Act, 1872 లోని సాధారణ షరతులను నెరవేర్చాలి: స్వేచ్ఛాయుత సమ్మతి , చట్టబద్ధమైన లక్ష్యం, ప్రతిఫలం ; ఇక్కడ ప్రతిఫలం మీడియేషన్ చేస్తామని పక్షాలు ఒకరికొకరు ఇచ్చుకునే వాగ్దానాలు. సెక్షన్ 19 మరో చివర కూడా ఇదే పరీక్ష పెడుతుంది: Contract Act కింద శూన్యమైన సెటిల్‌మెంట్ చట్టబద్ధమైన మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందం కాదు. ఈ అంశం జవాబిచ్చే ప్రశ్న. మీడియేషన్ ప్రయత్నిస్తామని పక్షాలు వాగ్దానం చేస్తే, ఆ వాగ్దానం ఎలా ఉండాలి, ఏ వివాదాలు మీడియేషన్‌కు వెళ్లవచ్చు, వారు చేరిన సెటిల్‌మెంట్‌కు ఎంత బలం ఉంటుంది? చట్టం ఈ నియమం ఎందుకు పెట్టింది. తమ వివాదాన్ని తామే పరిష్కరించుకున్న పక్షాలు ఆ సెటిల్‌మెంట్‌ను, వ్యాపార సంబంధాన్ని నిలుపుకునే అవకాశం ఎక్కువ. ఆ శ్రమ వృథా కాకుండా చట్టం సెటిల్‌మెంట్‌కు డిక్రీ బలాన్ని ఇస్తుంది. పక్షాల చిత్రం ఎవరు ఏం చేస్తారో చూపిస్తుంది. selfTest.q: 1. మీడియేషన్ ఒప్పందం లిఖితంగా ఉండాలా?
selfTest.a: అవును. Mediation Act, 2023 సెక్షన్ 4 అలా చెబుతుంది.

selfTest.q: 2. మీడియేటెడ్ సెటిల్‌మెంట్ ఒప్పందాన్ని ఎలా అమలు చేస్తారు?
selfTest.a: కోర్టు తీర్పు లేదా డిక్రీ లాగా (సెక్షన్ 27).

selfTest.q: 3. దాన్ని ఏ కారణాలపై సవాలు చేయవచ్చు?
selfTest.a: మోసం, అవినీతి, impersonation, లేదా వివాదం మీడియేషన్‌కు తగినది కాకపోవడం (సెక్షన్ 28).

selfTest.q: 4. Mediation Act కింద pre-litigation మీడియేషన్ తప్పనిసరా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. సెక్షన్ 5 కింద అది స్వచ్ఛందం. అత్యవసర మధ్యంతర ఉపశమనం కోరితే తప్ప, Commercial Courts Act సెక్షన్ 12A కింద Specified Value వాణిజ్య దావాలకు మాత్రమే తప్పనిసరి.

hi.inOneMinute: Court cases about contracts take years and often end the business relationship. Arbitration is faster, but an outsider still decides who wins. A mediation agreement lets the parties promise to try a third route first: settling the dispute themselves with the help of a neutral mediator. The Mediation Act, 2023 governs it. In exams, you must define a mediation agreement, say what the mediator does, explain the legal force of a mediated settlement agreement , and compare mediation with arbitration.
legalProvision: Mediation Act, 2023, Section 4. Mediation agreement. (1) A mediation agreement shall be in writing, by or between parties and anyone claiming through them, to submit to mediation all or certain disputes which have arisen or which may arise between the parties. (2) A mediation agreement may be in the form of a mediation clause in a contract or in the form of a separate agreement. (3) A mediation agreement is in writing, if it is contained in or recorded as— (a) any document signed by the parties; (b) an exchange of communications or letters including through electronic form as provided under the Information Technology Act, 2000 (21 of 2000); (c) any pleadings in a suit or any other proceedings in which existence of mediation agreement is alleged by one party and not denied by the other. (4) A reference in any agreement containing a mediation clause shall constitute a mediation agreement if the agreement is in writing and the reference is such as to make the mediation clause as part of the agreement. (5) The parties may agree to submit to mediation any dispute arising between them under an agreement, whether entered prior to arising of the dispute or subsequent thereto. (6) A mediation agreement in case of international mediation shall refer to an agreement for resolution in matters of commercial disputes referred to in clause (a) of section 3.

Mediation Act, 2023, Section 5. Pre-litigation mediation. (1) Subject to other provisions of this Act, whether any mediation agreement exists or not, the parties before filing any suit or proceedings of civil or commercial nature in any court, may voluntarily and with mutual consent take steps to settle the disputes by pre-litigation mediation in accordance with the provisions of this Act: Provided that pre-litigation mediation in matters of commercial disputes of Specified Value shall be undertaken in accordance with the provisions of section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 (4 of 2016), and the rules made thereunder.

Mediation Act, 2023, Section 6. Disputes or matters not fit for mediation. (1) A mediation under this Act shall not be conducted for resolution of any dispute or matter contained in the indicative list under the First Schedule: Provided that nothing contained herein shall prevent any court, if deemed appropriate, from referring any dispute relating to compoundable offences including the matrimonial offences which are compoundable and pending between the parties, to mediation: Provided further that the outcome of such mediation shall not be deemed to be a judgment or decree of court referred to in sub-section (2) of section 27, and shall be further considered by the court in accordance with the law for the time being in force. (2) If the Central Government is satisfied that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, by notification, amend the First Schedule.

Mediation Act, 2023, Section 19. Mediated settlement agreement. (1) A mediated settlement agreement includes an agreement in writing between some or all of the parties resulting from mediation, settling some or all of the disputes between such parties, and authenticated by the mediator: Provided that the terms of the mediated settlement agreement may extend beyond the disputes referred to mediation. Explanation.— A mediated settlement agreement which is void under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (9 of 1872), shall not be deemed to be lawful settlement agreement within the meaning of mediated settlement agreement. (2) Where a mediated settlement agreement is reached between the parties with regard to all or some of the disputes, the same shall be reduced in to writing and signed by the parties.

Mediation Act, 2023, Section 27. Enforcement of mediated settlement agreement. (1) A mediated settlement agreement resulting from a mediation signed by the parties and authenticated by the mediator shall be final and binding on the parties and persons claiming under them respectively and enforceable as per the provisions of sub-section (2). (2) Subject to the provisions of section 28, the mediated settlement agreement shall be enforced in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908), in the same manner as if it were a judgment or decree passed by a court, and may, accordingly, be relied on by any of the parties or persons claiming through them, by way of defence, set off or otherwise in any legal proceeding.

Mediation Act, 2023, Section 28. Challenge to mediated settlement agreement. (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, in any case in which the mediated settlement agreement is arrived at between the parties and is sought to be challenged by either of the parties, such party may file an application before the court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction. (2) A mediated settlement agreement may be challenged only on all or any of the following grounds, namely:— (i) fraud; (ii) corruption; (iii) impersonation; (iv) where the mediation was conducted in disputes or matters not fit for mediation under section 6. (3) An application for challenging the mediated settlement agreement shall not be made after ninety days have elapsed from the date on which the party making that application has received the copy of mediated settlement agreement under sub-section (3) of section 19: Provided that if the court or tribunal, as the case may be, is satisfied that the applicant was prevented by sufficient cause from making the application within the said period of ninety days, it may entertain the application within a further period of ninety days.

Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Section 89. Settlement of disputes outside the Court. (1) Where it appears to the Court that there exist elements of a settlement which may be acceptable to the parties, the Court shall formulate the terms of settlement and give them to the parties for their observations and after receiving the observations of the parties, the Court may reformulate the terms of a possible settlement and refer the same for:— (a) arbitration; (b) conciliation; (c) judicial settlement including settlement through Lok Adalat; or (d) mediation. . . . (2) Were a dispute has been referred— . . . (d) for mediation, the Court shall effect a compromise between the parties and shall follow such procedure as may be prescribed.

Commercial Courts Act, 2015, Section 12A (as quoted by the Supreme Court in Patil Automation , para 24; stated closely, with the quoted words in inverted commas). (1) "A suit, which does not contemplate any urgent interim relief under this Act, shall not be instituted" "unless the plaintiff exhausts the remedy of pre- institution mediation" "in accordance with such manner and procedure as may be prescribed by rules made by the Central Government." (3) The authorised Authority "shall complete the process of mediation within a period of three months" "from the date of application made by the plaintiff under sub-section (1)"; "the period of mediation may be extended for a further period of two months with the consent of the parties"; and "the period during which the parties remained occupied with the pre-institution mediation," "such period shall not be computed for the purpose of limitation under the Limitation Act, 1963". (4) "If the parties to the commercial dispute arrive at a settlement, the same shall be" "reduced into writing and shall be signed by the parties to the dispute and the mediator." (5) "The settlement arrived at under this section shall have the same status and effect" "as if it is an arbitral award on agreed terms under sub-section (4) of section 30" "of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996".
In simple words

Section 4, Mediation Act: a mediation agreement shall be in writing. It is an agreement by or between parties, and anyone claiming through them, to submit to mediation all or certain disputes that have arisen or may arise. It may be a clause in a contract or a separate agreement. Writing includes a signed document, an exchange of letters or electronic communications, or pleadings in which one party alleges the agreement and the other does not deny it. The parties may agree to mediate before or after the dispute arises. Section 5: whether or not a mediation agreement exists, parties may voluntarily and with mutual consent try pre-litigation mediation before filing a civil or commercial suit or proceeding. For commercial disputes of Specified Value, pre-litigation mediation is to be undertaken in accordance with Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015. Section 6: disputes on the indicative list in the First Schedule are not fit for mediation. Items include disputes involving prosecution for criminal offences, claims against minors, and disputes that affect the rights of third parties. A court may still refer compoundable offences, including compoundable matrimonial offences, to mediation, but the outcome is not a decree under Section 27(2). The Central Government may amend the First Schedule. Section 19: a mediated settlement agreement is a written agreement between some or all of the parties, resulting from mediation, settling some or all of the disputes, and authenticated (confirmed as genuine) by the mediator. Its terms may go beyond the disputes referred. A settlement that is void under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 is not a lawful mediated settlement agreement. Section 27: a mediated settlement agreement, signed by the parties and authenticated by the mediator, is final and binding on the parties and those claiming under them. It is enforced under the Code of Civil Procedure as if it were a judgment or decree of a court, and may be relied on as a defence or set-off . Section 28: it may be challenged only on grounds of fraud, corruption, impersonation (pretending to be another person), or because the dispute was not fit for mediation under Section 6. The application must be made within 90 days of receiving the copy, extendable by 90 more days for sufficient cause. Section 12A, Commercial Courts Act: a commercial suit that does not contemplate urgent interim relief shall not be instituted until the plaintiff has tried pre-institution mediation. The mediation is to be completed in three months, extendable by two months with consent, and that time is not counted for limitation. A settlement is put in writing and signed by the parties and the mediator, and has the status of an arbitral award on agreed terms. Section 89, CPC: where there are elements of a settlement acceptable to the parties, the court may refer the dispute to arbitration, conciliation, judicial settlement (including Lok Adalat) or mediation. In a mediation, the court effects a compromise between the parties by the prescribed procedure.
hi.meaning:
A mediation agreement is a contract in which parties agree to try to settle disputes with the help of a mediator. The mediator is a neutral (not taking either side) person who helps the parties reach their own settlement. He does not decide. The result, if the parties agree, is a mediated settlement agreement. As a contract, a mediation agreement must meet the usual conditions of the Indian Contract Act, 1872: free consent , a lawful object, and consideration , which here is the parties' mutual promises to mediate. Section 19 adds the same check at the other end: a settlement that is void under the Contract Act is not a lawful mediated settlement agreement. The question this topic answers. If parties promise to try mediation, what must the promise look like, which disputes can go to mediation, and what is the force of the settlement they reach? Why the law has this rule. Parties who settle their own dispute are more likely to keep the settlement and the business relationship. The law gives the settlement the force of a decree so that the effort is not wasted. The mediator, a neutral person, helps them talk and reach their own terms. If they agree, they sign a mediated settlement agreement, which the mediator authenticates (Section 19). It is final and binding and enforceable as a decree (Section 27), and can be challenged only on the grounds in Section 28. The mediator does not decide the dispute and cannot impose a settlement.
keyPoints: A mediation agreement is a written contract to mediate present or future disputes (Section 4). The mediator helps. The parties decide. Pre-litigation mediation is voluntary under Section 5. It is mandatory for commercial suits under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act ( Patil Automation ). A mediated settlement agreement is binding and enforceable as a decree (Section 27). Challenge only on fraud, corruption, impersonation or unfit subject matter, within 90 days, plus 90 for sufficient cause (Section 28). Sections 4, 5, 6, 19, 27 and 28 await commencement; only some sections came into force on 9 October 2023.

caseLaws.name: Patil Automation Pvt
caseLaws.facts: Ltd. v. Rakheja Engineers Pvt. Ltd. (2022) Facts. The Supreme Court considered whether pre-institution mediation under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015 is mandatory, in commercial suits that did not contemplate urgent interim relief. Principle. It is mandatory: "the language used in Section 12A is plainly imperative in nature" (para 53). A commercial suit filed in breach, where no urgent interim relief is sought, must be rejected, and the court may do so on its own (para 68). Supreme Court, 17 August 2022, K.M. Joseph and Hrishikesh Roy JJ. Why it matters. It is the rule that makes mediation compulsory for commercial suits. Afcons Infrastructure Ltd. v. Cherian Varkey Construction Co. (P) Ltd. (2010) Facts. Afcons sub-contracted part of a Cochin Port Trust bridge and road contract to Cherian Varkey, under a sub-contract with no arbitration clause. The sub-contractor sued for ₹2,10,70,881 with interest, and the trial court referred the suit to arbitration under Section 89. Principle. A court must consider ADR after the pleadings, but it cannot refer a suit to arbitration under Section 89 "unless all the parties to the suit agree" (para 35). A mediation settlement is placed before the court for recording (para 28). The appeal was allowed and the reference set aside. (2010) 8 SCC 24 (26 July 2010, R.V. Raveendran and J.M. Panchal JJ.). Why it matters. It explains court-annexed mediation.

selfTest.q: 1. Must a mediation agreement be in writing?
selfTest.a: Yes. Section 4 of the Mediation Act, 2023 says so.

selfTest.q: 2. How is a mediated settlement agreement enforced?
selfTest.a: As if it were a judgment or decree of a court (Section 27).

selfTest.q: 3. On what grounds can it be challenged?
selfTest.a: Fraud, corruption, impersonation, or because the dispute was not fit for mediation (Section 28).

selfTest.q: 4. Is pre-litigation mediation compulsory under the Mediation Act?
selfTest.a: No. It is voluntary under Section 5. It is compulsory only for commercial suits of Specified Value under Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, unless urgent interim relief is contemplated.

selfTest.q: 5. Can a void settlement be a mediated settlement agreement?
selfTest.a: No. The Explanation to Section 19(1) says a settlement void under the Indian Contract Act is not a lawful mediated settlement agreement.

law-of-contract-i-u5-t16.subtitle: Works contracts under the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and the Specific Relief Act, 1963

en.inOneMinute: Building a house, a road or a bridge takes months or years and depends on weather, materials, labour and approvals. Delay, cost overruns and defective work are common, and each leads to a dispute about who pays. Construction contracts therefore carry many detailed clauses. The general rules of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and the Specific Relief Act, 1963 apply to them. In exams, you must know the kinds of construction contract, the key clauses, how delay is compensated under Sections 73 and 74, and what the 2018 amendments changed for specific relief.
legalProvision: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 55. Effect of failure to perform at fixed time, in contract in which time is essential. When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract. Effect of such failure when time is not essential.—If it was not the intention of the parties that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract does not become voidable by the failure to do such thing at or before the specified time; but the promisee is entitled to compensation from the promisor for any loss occasioned to him by such failure. Effect of acceptance of performance at time other than that agreed upon.—If, in case of a contract voidable on account of the promisor’s failure to perform his promise at the time agreed, the promisee accepts performance of such promise at any time other than that agreed, the promisee cannot claim compensation for any loss occasioned by the non-performance of the promise at the time agreed, unless, at the time of such acceptance, he gives notice to the promisor of his intention to do so.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 56. Agreement to do impossible act. An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. Contract to do an act afterwards becoming impossible or unlawful.—A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Compensation for loss through non-performance of act known to be impossible or unlawful.— Where one person has promised to do something which he knew, or, with reasonable diligence, might have known, and which the promisee did not know, to be impossible or unlawful, such promisor must make compensation to such promisee for any loss which such promisee sustains through the non- performance of the promise.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 73. Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract. When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from the breach of it. Such compensation is not to be given for any remote and indirect loss or damage sustained by reason of the breach. Compensation for failure to discharge obligation resembling those created by contract.—When an obligation resembling those created by contract has been incurred and has not been discharged, any person injured by the failure to discharge it is entitled to receive the same compensation from the party in default, as if such person had contracted to discharge it and had broken his contract. Explanation.—In estimating the loss or damage arising from a breach of contract, the means which existed of remedying the inconvenience caused by the non-performance of the contract must be taken into account. Illustration (l). A, a builder, contracts to erect and finish a house by the first of January, in order that B may give possession of it at that time to C, to whom B has contracted to let it. A is informed of the contract between B and C. A builds the house so badly that, before the first of January, it falls down and has to be re-built by B, who, in consequence, loses the rent which he was to have received from C, and is obliged to make compensation to C for the breach of his contract. A must make compensation to B for the cost of rebuilding the house, for the rent lost, and for the compensation made to C.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 74. Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for. When a contract has been broken, if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of such breach, or if the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused thereby, to receive from the party who has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or, as the case may be, the penalty stipulated for. Explanation.—A stipulation for increased interest from the date of default may be a stipulation by way of penalty.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 10. Specific performance in respect of contracts. The specific performance of a contract shall be enforced by the court subject to the provisions contained in sub-section (2) of section 11, section 14 and section 16.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 14. Contracts not specifically enforceable. The following contracts cannot be specifically enforced, namely:— (a) where a party to the contract has obtained substituted performance of contract in accordance with the provisions of section 20; (b) a contract, the performance of which involves the performance of a continuous duty which the court cannot supervise; (c) a contract which is so dependent on the personal qualifications of the parties that the court cannot enforce specific performance of its material terms; and (d) a contract which is in its nature determinable.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 20. Substituted performance of contract. (1) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions contained in the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (9 of 1872), and, except as otherwise agreed upon by the parties, where the contract is broken due to non-performance of promise by any party, the party who suffers by such breach shall have the option of substituted performance through a third party or by his own agency, and, recover the expenses and other costs actually incurred, spent or suffered by him, from the party committing such breach. (2) No substituted performance of contract under sub-section (1) shall be undertaken unless the party who suffers such breach has given a notice in writing, of not less than thirty days, to the party in breach calling upon him to perform the contract within such time as specified in the notice, and on his refusal or failure to do so, he may get the same performed by a third party or by his own agency: Provided that the party who suffers such breach shall not be entitled to recover the expenses and costs under sub-section (1) unless he has got the contract performed through a third party or by his own agency. (3) Where the party suffering breach of contract has got the contract performed through a third party or by his own agency after giving notice under sub-section (1), he shall not be entitled to claim relief of specific performance against the party in breach. (4) Nothing in this section shall prevent the party who has suffered breach of contract from claiming compensation from the party in breach.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 20A. Special provisions for contract relating to infrastructure project. (1) No injunction shall be granted by a court in a suit under this Act involving a contract relating to an infrastructure project specified in the Schedule, where granting injunction would cause impediment or delay in the progress or completion of such infrastructure project.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 41. Injunction when refused. An injunction cannot be granted— . . . (ha) if it would impede or delay the progress or completion of any infrastructure project or interfere with the continued provision of relevant facility related thereto or services being the subject matter of such project.
In simple words

Section 55, Contract Act: if a party fails to perform by the agreed time, the contract (or the part not performed) is voidable at the promisee's option when the parties intended time to be of the essence. If time was not of the essence, the contract is not voidable, but the promisee gets compensation for the loss. If the promisee accepts late performance of a voidable contract, he cannot claim compensation for the delay unless he gives notice of his intention to do so when accepting. Section 56: an agreement to do an impossible act is void. A contract to do an act that later becomes impossible, or unlawful because of an event the promisor could not prevent, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Section 73: the party who suffers by a breach gets compensation for loss which naturally arose in the usual course of things, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, was likely to result. Remote and indirect loss is not compensated. The means that existed of remedying the inconvenience must be taken into account. Illustration (l) is a builder's case. Section 74: where the contract names a sum to be paid on breach, or contains any other stipulation by way of penalty , the injured party gets reasonable compensation not exceeding the sum named, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved. Section 10, Specific Relief Act (after 2018): specific performance shall be enforced, subject to Sections 11(2), 14 and 16. Section 14: four kinds of contract cannot be specifically enforced. Clause (b) covers a contract that involves a continuous duty which the court cannot supervise (watch over and direct). Section 20: unless the parties agreed otherwise, the injured party may have the work done through a third party or his own agency, and recover the expenses and costs actually incurred, after at least 30 days' written notice. He then cannot claim specific performance, but he can still claim compensation. Sections 20A and 41(ha): no injunction that would impede or delay a Schedule infrastructure project.

A construction contract is an agreement in which a contractor builds, repairs or alters a structure for an owner for a price. In law, it is usually a works contract , which is a contract to carry out work as against a contract to sell goods. The tree shows the common types. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. By how the price is fixed: a lump-sum contract, with a fixed total price for the whole work; an item-rate or unit-price contract, with payment by measured quantities at agreed rates; and a cost-plus contract, with actual cost plus an agreed fee or percentage. By how much the contractor does: a turnkey or EPC contract, in which one contractor designs, procures and builds, then hands over a ready project; and a build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract, in which the contractor builds and runs the project for a period and then hands it over. By how the price is fixed: a lump-sum contract (a fixed total price for the whole work); an item-rate or unit-price contract (payment by measured quantities at agreed rates); a cost-plus contract (actual cost plus an agreed fee or percentage). By how much the contractor does: a turnkey or EPC (engineering, procurement and construction) contract, in which one contractor designs, procures and builds, then hands over a ready project; a build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract, in which the contractor builds and runs the project for a period and then hands it over. The question this topic answers. How do the general rules of contract and specific relief apply when a building job is late, abandoned or defective? Why the law has this rule. A construction contract runs for a long time and many things can go wrong. The law lets the owner get compensation, get the work finished by someone else, or in some cases have the contract specifically enforced, while protecting public projects from being stopped by injunction.
keyPoints: An entire building contract is a works contract, not a sale of goods ( Gannon Dunkerley ). Time is of the essence only if the parties intended it (Section 55). Delay: compensation under Sections 73 and 74. Reasonable compensation up to the named sum. After 2018: specific performance is the rule (Section 10), but a continuous duty is a bar (Section 14(b)). Substituted performance after 30 days' notice (Section 20). Infrastructure projects are shielded from delaying injunctions (Sections 20A, 41(ha)).

caseLaws.name: State of Madras v
caseLaws.facts: Gannon Dunkerley (1958) Facts. The State sought to levy sales tax under the Madras General Sales Tax Act, 1939 on the value of materials used by a contractor in building contracts. Principle. In an entire, indivisible building contract "there is no sale as such of materials used in a building contract". It is a works contract. The State's appeal "fails, and is dismissed with costs". AIR 1958 SC 560 : 1959 SCR 379 (1 April 1958). Why it matters. It places construction contracts in the law of contract and not in the law of sale. Fateh Chand v. Balkishan Dass (1963) Facts. A buyer paid ₹1,000 as earnest money and ₹24,000 towards the price of land and a building in Delhi, and the sale was not completed. The seller claimed to forfeit the whole ₹25,000 under the contract. Principle. Section 74 covers every stipulation by way of penalty, including forfeiture of money paid. The seller keeps only reasonable compensation; here, only the ₹1,000. [1964] 1 SCR 515 : AIR 1963 SC 1405 (Constitution Bench, 15 January 1963). Why it matters. It governs liquidated damages for delay. Kailash Nath Associates v. DDA (2015) Facts. A bidder paid ₹78 lakh, 25 per cent of a ₹3.12 crore bid, as earnest money for a DDA plot. DDA forfeited it "without putting the appellant on notice" and without any loss being shown. Principle. "Damage or loss caused is a sine qua non" for Section 74 (para 43). The Single Judge's order refunding the money with 9 per cent interest was restored. (2015) 4 SCC 136 (9 January 2015, R.F. Nariman and Ranjan Gogoi JJ.). In K.R. Suresh v. R. Poornima (2025), another two-judge Bench noted that "A different view was taken by this Court in Kailash Nath" and held that a clause forfeiting earnest money "is not penal in the ordinary sense", so Section 74 is "inapplicable" to it (paras 48, 51). Why it matters. It limits sums fixed in advance. ONGC v. Saw Pipes (2003) Facts. ONGC deducted liquidated damages from a supplier's bills for late supply of casing pipes. The tribunal ordered a refund. Principle. The Supreme Court set aside the refund direction as patently illegal. Where the sum is a genuine pre-estimate, actual loss need not be proved. (2003) 5 SCC 705 : AIR 2003 SC 2629. Later changes to Section 34 narrowed the " patent illegality " ground. Why it matters. It shows how an award on liquidated damages can be tested. State of Rajasthan v. Ferro Concrete Construction (2009) Facts. A contract for a 37.41 km water pipeline in Ajmer district was treated as abandoned on 22 August 1990. The award of 21 September 1994 was challenged. Principle. The Court set aside two awards and cut pre-reference interest from 18 to 9 per cent, holding that "Courts can not sit in judgment over the award of the arbitrator , nor re-appreciate the evidence" (para 37). The appeals were allowed in part. (2009) 12 SCC 1 (22 April 2009, R.V. Raveendran and Lokeshwar Singh Panta JJ.). Why it matters. It shows the limits of court review of a construction award. Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta (1994) Facts. Allottees of flats under a development authority's housing schemes paid deposits, but the flats were not delivered on time; in one appeal ₹6,132 and ₹1,09,975 were deposited in July 1988 and the flat was not delivered "as the construction work was not complete". Principle. "Housing activity is a service", and delay in delivering possession "is denial of service" under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (para 6). The authority's appeals were dismissed with costs. AIR 1994 SC 787 : (1994) 1 SCC 243 (5 November 1993). Why it matters. It protects home buyers.

selfTest.q: 1. Is an entire building contract a sale of the materials used?
selfTest.a: No. It is a works contract ( State of Madras v. Gannon Dunkerley , 1958).

selfTest.q: 2. What does Section 74 allow for delay under a liquidated damages clause?
selfTest.a: Reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount named ( Fateh Chand ).

selfTest.q: 3. What notice does Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act require?
selfTest.a: Written notice of at least 30 days.

selfTest.q: 4. Can an owner who has got the work finished under Section 20 also sue for specific performance?
selfTest.a: No. Section 20(3) bars it, but Section 20(4) keeps his claim for compensation.

selfTest.q: 5. Does a sharp rise in the cost of materials frustrate a construction contract?
selfTest.a: No. It is commercial hardship, not impossibility under Section 56.

legalProvision: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 55. Effect of failure to perform at fixed time, in contract in which time is essential. When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract. Effect of such failure when time is not essential.—If it was not the intention of the parties that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract does not become voidable by the failure to do such thing at or before the specified time; but the promisee is entitled to compensation from the promisor for any loss occasioned to him by such failure. Effect of acceptance of performance at time other than that agreed upon.—If, in case of a contract voidable on account of the promisor’s failure to perform his promise at the time agreed, the promisee accepts performance of such promise at any time other than that agreed, the promisee cannot claim compensation for any loss occasioned by the non-performance of the promise at the time agreed, unless, at the time of such acceptance, he gives notice to the promisor of his intention to do so.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 56. Agreement to do impossible act. An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. Contract to do an act afterwards becoming impossible or unlawful.—A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Compensation for loss through non-performance of act known to be impossible or unlawful.— Where one person has promised to do something which he knew, or, with reasonable diligence, might have known, and which the promisee did not know, to be impossible or unlawful, such promisor must make compensation to such promisee for any loss which such promisee sustains through the non- performance of the promise.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 73. Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract. When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from the breach of it. Such compensation is not to be given for any remote and indirect loss or damage sustained by reason of the breach. Compensation for failure to discharge obligation resembling those created by contract.—When an obligation resembling those created by contract has been incurred and has not been discharged, any person injured by the failure to discharge it is entitled to receive the same compensation from the party in default, as if such person had contracted to discharge it and had broken his contract. Explanation.—In estimating the loss or damage arising from a breach of contract, the means which existed of remedying the inconvenience caused by the non-performance of the contract must be taken into account. Illustration (l). A, a builder, contracts to erect and finish a house by the first of January, in order that B may give possession of it at that time to C, to whom B has contracted to let it. A is informed of the contract between B and C. A builds the house so badly that, before the first of January, it falls down and has to be re-built by B, who, in consequence, loses the rent which he was to have received from C, and is obliged to make compensation to C for the breach of his contract. A must make compensation to B for the cost of rebuilding the house, for the rent lost, and for the compensation made to C.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 74. Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for. When a contract has been broken, if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of such breach, or if the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused thereby, to receive from the party who has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or, as the case may be, the penalty stipulated for. Explanation.—A stipulation for increased interest from the date of default may be a stipulation by way of penalty.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 10. Specific performance in respect of contracts. The specific performance of a contract shall be enforced by the court subject to the provisions contained in sub-section (2) of section 11, section 14 and section 16.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 14. Contracts not specifically enforceable. The following contracts cannot be specifically enforced, namely:— (a) where a party to the contract has obtained substituted performance of contract in accordance with the provisions of section 20; (b) a contract, the performance of which involves the performance of a continuous duty which the court cannot supervise; (c) a contract which is so dependent on the personal qualifications of the parties that the court cannot enforce specific performance of its material terms; and (d) a contract which is in its nature determinable.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 20. Substituted performance of contract. (1) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions contained in the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (9 of 1872), and, except as otherwise agreed upon by the parties, where the contract is broken due to non-performance of promise by any party, the party who suffers by such breach shall have the option of substituted performance through a third party or by his own agency, and, recover the expenses and other costs actually incurred, spent or suffered by him, from the party committing such breach. (2) No substituted performance of contract under sub-section (1) shall be undertaken unless the party who suffers such breach has given a notice in writing, of not less than thirty days, to the party in breach calling upon him to perform the contract within such time as specified in the notice, and on his refusal or failure to do so, he may get the same performed by a third party or by his own agency: Provided that the party who suffers such breach shall not be entitled to recover the expenses and costs under sub-section (1) unless he has got the contract performed through a third party or by his own agency. (3) Where the party suffering breach of contract has got the contract performed through a third party or by his own agency after giving notice under sub-section (1), he shall not be entitled to claim relief of specific performance against the party in breach. (4) Nothing in this section shall prevent the party who has suffered breach of contract from claiming compensation from the party in breach.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 20A. Special provisions for contract relating to infrastructure project. (1) No injunction shall be granted by a court in a suit under this Act involving a contract relating to an infrastructure project specified in the Schedule, where granting injunction would cause impediment or delay in the progress or completion of such infrastructure project.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 41. Injunction when refused. An injunction cannot be granted— . . . (ha) if it would impede or delay the progress or completion of any infrastructure project or interfere with the continued provision of relevant facility related thereto or services being the subject matter of such project.

సెక్షన్ 55, కాంట్రాక్టు చట్టం: ఒక పక్షం అంగీకరించిన సమయానికి నెరవేర్చకపోతే, సమయమే ప్రధానమని పక్షాలు ఉద్దేశించి ఉంటే, కాంట్రాక్టు (లేదా నెరవేర్చని భాగం) వాగ్దాన గ్రహీత ఇష్టం మేరకు రద్దు చేయదగినది (voidable) అవుతుంది. సమయం ప్రధానం కాకపోతే కాంట్రాక్టు రద్దు చేయదగినది కాదు, కానీ వాగ్దాన గ్రహీతకు నష్టానికి పరిహారం వస్తుంది. రద్దు చేయదగిన కాంట్రాక్టులో ఆలస్యంగా నెరవేర్పును అంగీకరిస్తే, అంగీకరించే సమయంలోనే తన ఉద్దేశం గురించి నోటీసు ఇస్తే తప్ప, ఆలస్యానికి పరిహారం కోరలేడు. సెక్షన్ 56: అసాధ్యమైన పని చేసే ఒప్పందం శూన్యం. తర్వాత అసాధ్యమైన, లేదా వాగ్దానకర్త ఆపలేని సంఘటన వల్ల చట్టవిరుద్ధమైన పనిని చేసే కాంట్రాక్టు, ఆ పని అసాధ్యం లేదా చట్టవిరుద్ధం అయినప్పుడు శూన్యమవుతుంది. సెక్షన్ 73: ఉల్లంఘన వల్ల నష్టపోయిన పక్షానికి, సాధారణ క్రమంలో సహజంగా వచ్చిన నష్టానికి, లేదా కాంట్రాక్టు చేసేటప్పుడు వస్తుందని పక్షాలకు తెలిసిన నష్టానికి పరిహారం వస్తుంది. దూరపు, పరోక్ష నష్టానికి పరిహారం లేదు. అసౌకర్యాన్ని సరిచేయడానికి అందుబాటులో ఉన్న మార్గాలను లెక్కలోకి తీసుకోవాలి. Illustration (l) ఒక బిల్డర్ కేసు. సెక్షన్ 74: ఉల్లంఘనకు చెల్లించాల్సిన మొత్తాన్ని కాంట్రాక్టు పేర్కొంటే, లేదా జరిమానా రూపంలో మరేదైనా నిబంధన ఉంటే, నష్టపోయిన పక్షానికి, అసలు నష్టం నిరూపించినా నిరూపించకపోయినా, పేర్కొన్న మొత్తానికి మించని సహేతుక పరిహారం వస్తుంది. సెక్షన్ 10, నిర్దిష్ట ఉపశమన చట్టం (2018 తర్వాత): సెక్షన్లు 11(2), 14, 16 కు లోబడి నిర్దిష్ట అమలు జరిపించాలి. సెక్షన్ 14: నాలుగు రకాల కాంట్రాక్టులను నిర్దిష్టంగా అమలు చేయలేరు. క్లాజు (b), కోర్టు పర్యవేక్షించలేని (చూసుకుంటూ నడిపించలేని) నిరంతర బాధ్యత ఉన్న కాంట్రాక్టును కవర్ చేస్తుంది. సెక్షన్ 20: పక్షాలు వేరేలా అంగీకరించకపోతే, నష్టపోయిన పక్షం కనీసం 30 రోజుల లిఖిత నోటీసు తర్వాత, మూడో వ్యక్తి ద్వారా లేదా సొంతంగా పని చేయించి, నిజంగా అయిన ఖర్చులను వసూలు చేసుకోవచ్చు. అప్పుడు నిర్దిష్ట అమలు కోరలేడు, కానీ పరిహారం ఇంకా కోరవచ్చు. సెక్షన్లు 20A, 41(ha): షెడ్యూల్ మౌలిక సదుపాయాల ప్రాజెక్టును అడ్డుకునే లేదా ఆలస్యం చేసే నిషేధాజ్ఞ లేదు.

నిర్మాణ కాంట్రాక్టు అంటే, ఒక కాంట్రాక్టరు యజమాని కోసం ధరకు ఒక నిర్మాణాన్ని కట్టే, మరమ్మతు చేసే లేదా మార్చే ఒప్పందం. చట్టంలో అది సాధారణంగా ఒక works contract , అంటే సరుకులు అమ్మే కాంట్రాక్టు కాకుండా పని చేసే కాంట్రాక్టు. చెట్టు చిత్రం సాధారణ రకాలను చూపిస్తుంది. selfTest.q: 1. సంపూర్ణ భవన నిర్మాణ కాంట్రాక్టు అందులో వాడిన సామగ్రి అమ్మకమా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. అది works contract ( State of Madras v. Gannon Dunkerley , 1958).

selfTest.q: 2. ముందే నిర్ణయించిన నష్టపరిహార క్లాజు కింద ఆలస్యానికి సెక్షన్ 74 ఏమి అనుమతిస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: పేర్కొన్న మొత్తానికి మించని సహేతుక పరిహారం ( Fateh Chand ).

selfTest.q: 3. నిర్దిష్ట ఉపశమన చట్టం సెక్షన్ 20 ఏ నోటీసు కోరుతుంది?
selfTest.a: కనీసం 30 రోజుల లిఖిత నోటీసు.

selfTest.q: 4. సెక్షన్ 20 కింద పని పూర్తి చేయించుకున్న యజమాని నిర్దిష్ట అమలు కోసం కూడా దావా వేయగలడా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. సెక్షన్ 20(3) దాన్ని అడ్డుకుంటుంది, కానీ సెక్షన్ 20(4) అతని పరిహారం క్లెయిమును నిలుపుతుంది.

selfTest.q: 5. సామగ్రి ధర బాగా పెరిగితే నిర్మాణ కాంట్రాక్టు ఫ్రస్ట్రేట్ అవుతుందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. అది వాణిజ్య కష్టం, సెక్షన్ 56 కింది అసాధ్యత కాదు.

hi.inOneMinute: Building a house, a road or a bridge takes months or years and depends on weather, materials, labour and approvals. Delay, cost overruns and defective work are common, and each leads to a dispute about who pays. Construction contracts therefore carry many detailed clauses. The general rules of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 and the Specific Relief Act, 1963 apply to them. In exams, you must know the kinds of construction contract, the key clauses, how delay is compensated under Sections 73 and 74, and what the 2018 amendments changed for specific relief.
legalProvision: Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 55. Effect of failure to perform at fixed time, in contract in which time is essential. When a party to a contract promises to do a certain thing at or before a specified time, or certain things at or before specified times, and fails to do any such thing at or before the specified time, the contract, or so much of it as has not been performed, becomes voidable at the option of the promisee, if the intention of the parties was that time should be of the essence of the contract. Effect of such failure when time is not essential.—If it was not the intention of the parties that time should be of the essence of the contract, the contract does not become voidable by the failure to do such thing at or before the specified time; but the promisee is entitled to compensation from the promisor for any loss occasioned to him by such failure. Effect of acceptance of performance at time other than that agreed upon.—If, in case of a contract voidable on account of the promisor’s failure to perform his promise at the time agreed, the promisee accepts performance of such promise at any time other than that agreed, the promisee cannot claim compensation for any loss occasioned by the non-performance of the promise at the time agreed, unless, at the time of such acceptance, he gives notice to the promisor of his intention to do so.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 56. Agreement to do impossible act. An agreement to do an act impossible in itself is void. Contract to do an act afterwards becoming impossible or unlawful.—A contract to do an act which, after the contract is made, becomes impossible, or, by reason of some event which the promisor could not prevent, unlawful, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Compensation for loss through non-performance of act known to be impossible or unlawful.— Where one person has promised to do something which he knew, or, with reasonable diligence, might have known, and which the promisee did not know, to be impossible or unlawful, such promisor must make compensation to such promisee for any loss which such promisee sustains through the non- performance of the promise.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 73. Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract. When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby, which naturally arose in the usual course of things from such breach, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, to be likely to result from the breach of it. Such compensation is not to be given for any remote and indirect loss or damage sustained by reason of the breach. Compensation for failure to discharge obligation resembling those created by contract.—When an obligation resembling those created by contract has been incurred and has not been discharged, any person injured by the failure to discharge it is entitled to receive the same compensation from the party in default, as if such person had contracted to discharge it and had broken his contract. Explanation.—In estimating the loss or damage arising from a breach of contract, the means which existed of remedying the inconvenience caused by the non-performance of the contract must be taken into account. Illustration (l). A, a builder, contracts to erect and finish a house by the first of January, in order that B may give possession of it at that time to C, to whom B has contracted to let it. A is informed of the contract between B and C. A builds the house so badly that, before the first of January, it falls down and has to be re-built by B, who, in consequence, loses the rent which he was to have received from C, and is obliged to make compensation to C for the breach of his contract. A must make compensation to B for the cost of rebuilding the house, for the rent lost, and for the compensation made to C.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, Section 74. Compensation for breach of contract where penalty stipulated for. When a contract has been broken, if a sum is named in the contract as the amount to be paid in case of such breach, or if the contract contains any other stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused thereby, to receive from the party who has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or, as the case may be, the penalty stipulated for. Explanation.—A stipulation for increased interest from the date of default may be a stipulation by way of penalty.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 10. Specific performance in respect of contracts. The specific performance of a contract shall be enforced by the court subject to the provisions contained in sub-section (2) of section 11, section 14 and section 16.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 14. Contracts not specifically enforceable. The following contracts cannot be specifically enforced, namely:— (a) where a party to the contract has obtained substituted performance of contract in accordance with the provisions of section 20; (b) a contract, the performance of which involves the performance of a continuous duty which the court cannot supervise; (c) a contract which is so dependent on the personal qualifications of the parties that the court cannot enforce specific performance of its material terms; and (d) a contract which is in its nature determinable.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 20. Substituted performance of contract. (1) Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions contained in the Indian Contract Act, 1872 (9 of 1872), and, except as otherwise agreed upon by the parties, where the contract is broken due to non-performance of promise by any party, the party who suffers by such breach shall have the option of substituted performance through a third party or by his own agency, and, recover the expenses and other costs actually incurred, spent or suffered by him, from the party committing such breach. (2) No substituted performance of contract under sub-section (1) shall be undertaken unless the party who suffers such breach has given a notice in writing, of not less than thirty days, to the party in breach calling upon him to perform the contract within such time as specified in the notice, and on his refusal or failure to do so, he may get the same performed by a third party or by his own agency: Provided that the party who suffers such breach shall not be entitled to recover the expenses and costs under sub-section (1) unless he has got the contract performed through a third party or by his own agency. (3) Where the party suffering breach of contract has got the contract performed through a third party or by his own agency after giving notice under sub-section (1), he shall not be entitled to claim relief of specific performance against the party in breach. (4) Nothing in this section shall prevent the party who has suffered breach of contract from claiming compensation from the party in breach.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 20A. Special provisions for contract relating to infrastructure project. (1) No injunction shall be granted by a court in a suit under this Act involving a contract relating to an infrastructure project specified in the Schedule, where granting injunction would cause impediment or delay in the progress or completion of such infrastructure project.

Specific Relief Act, 1963, Section 41. Injunction when refused. An injunction cannot be granted— . . . (ha) if it would impede or delay the progress or completion of any infrastructure project or interfere with the continued provision of relevant facility related thereto or services being the subject matter of such project.
In simple words

Section 55, Contract Act: if a party fails to perform by the agreed time, the contract (or the part not performed) is voidable at the promisee's option when the parties intended time to be of the essence. If time was not of the essence, the contract is not voidable, but the promisee gets compensation for the loss. If the promisee accepts late performance of a voidable contract, he cannot claim compensation for the delay unless he gives notice of his intention to do so when accepting. Section 56: an agreement to do an impossible act is void. A contract to do an act that later becomes impossible, or unlawful because of an event the promisor could not prevent, becomes void when the act becomes impossible or unlawful. Section 73: the party who suffers by a breach gets compensation for loss which naturally arose in the usual course of things, or which the parties knew, when they made the contract, was likely to result. Remote and indirect loss is not compensated. The means that existed of remedying the inconvenience must be taken into account. Illustration (l) is a builder's case. Section 74: where the contract names a sum to be paid on breach, or contains any other stipulation by way of penalty , the injured party gets reasonable compensation not exceeding the sum named, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved. Section 10, Specific Relief Act (after 2018): specific performance shall be enforced, subject to Sections 11(2), 14 and 16. Section 14: four kinds of contract cannot be specifically enforced. Clause (b) covers a contract that involves a continuous duty which the court cannot supervise (watch over and direct). Section 20: unless the parties agreed otherwise, the injured party may have the work done through a third party or his own agency, and recover the expenses and costs actually incurred, after at least 30 days' written notice. He then cannot claim specific performance, but he can still claim compensation. Sections 20A and 41(ha): no injunction that would impede or delay a Schedule infrastructure project.
hi.meaning:
A construction contract is an agreement in which a contractor builds, repairs or alters a structure for an owner for a price. In law, it is usually a works contract , which is a contract to carry out work as against a contract to sell goods. The tree shows the common types. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. By how the price is fixed: a lump-sum contract, with a fixed total price for the whole work; an item-rate or unit-price contract, with payment by measured quantities at agreed rates; and a cost-plus contract, with actual cost plus an agreed fee or percentage. By how much the contractor does: a turnkey or EPC contract, in which one contractor designs, procures and builds, then hands over a ready project; and a build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract, in which the contractor builds and runs the project for a period and then hands it over. By how the price is fixed: a lump-sum contract (a fixed total price for the whole work); an item-rate or unit-price contract (payment by measured quantities at agreed rates); a cost-plus contract (actual cost plus an agreed fee or percentage). By how much the contractor does: a turnkey or EPC (engineering, procurement and construction) contract, in which one contractor designs, procures and builds, then hands over a ready project; a build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract, in which the contractor builds and runs the project for a period and then hands it over. The question this topic answers. How do the general rules of contract and specific relief apply when a building job is late, abandoned or defective? Why the law has this rule. A construction contract runs for a long time and many things can go wrong. The law lets the owner get compensation, get the work finished by someone else, or in some cases have the contract specifically enforced, while protecting public projects from being stopped by injunction.
keyPoints: An entire building contract is a works contract, not a sale of goods ( Gannon Dunkerley ). Time is of the essence only if the parties intended it (Section 55). Delay: compensation under Sections 73 and 74. Reasonable compensation up to the named sum. After 2018: specific performance is the rule (Section 10), but a continuous duty is a bar (Section 14(b)). Substituted performance after 30 days' notice (Section 20). Infrastructure projects are shielded from delaying injunctions (Sections 20A, 41(ha)).

caseLaws.name: State of Madras v
caseLaws.facts: Gannon Dunkerley (1958) Facts. The State sought to levy sales tax under the Madras General Sales Tax Act, 1939 on the value of materials used by a contractor in building contracts. Principle. In an entire, indivisible building contract "there is no sale as such of materials used in a building contract". It is a works contract. The State's appeal "fails, and is dismissed with costs". AIR 1958 SC 560 : 1959 SCR 379 (1 April 1958). Why it matters. It places construction contracts in the law of contract and not in the law of sale. Fateh Chand v. Balkishan Dass (1963) Facts. A buyer paid ₹1,000 as earnest money and ₹24,000 towards the price of land and a building in Delhi, and the sale was not completed. The seller claimed to forfeit the whole ₹25,000 under the contract. Principle. Section 74 covers every stipulation by way of penalty, including forfeiture of money paid. The seller keeps only reasonable compensation; here, only the ₹1,000. [1964] 1 SCR 515 : AIR 1963 SC 1405 (Constitution Bench, 15 January 1963). Why it matters. It governs liquidated damages for delay. Kailash Nath Associates v. DDA (2015) Facts. A bidder paid ₹78 lakh, 25 per cent of a ₹3.12 crore bid, as earnest money for a DDA plot. DDA forfeited it "without putting the appellant on notice" and without any loss being shown. Principle. "Damage or loss caused is a sine qua non" for Section 74 (para 43). The Single Judge's order refunding the money with 9 per cent interest was restored. (2015) 4 SCC 136 (9 January 2015, R.F. Nariman and Ranjan Gogoi JJ.). In K.R. Suresh v. R. Poornima (2025), another two-judge Bench noted that "A different view was taken by this Court in Kailash Nath" and held that a clause forfeiting earnest money "is not penal in the ordinary sense", so Section 74 is "inapplicable" to it (paras 48, 51). Why it matters. It limits sums fixed in advance. ONGC v. Saw Pipes (2003) Facts. ONGC deducted liquidated damages from a supplier's bills for late supply of casing pipes. The tribunal ordered a refund. Principle. The Supreme Court set aside the refund direction as patently illegal. Where the sum is a genuine pre-estimate, actual loss need not be proved. (2003) 5 SCC 705 : AIR 2003 SC 2629. Later changes to Section 34 narrowed the " patent illegality " ground. Why it matters. It shows how an award on liquidated damages can be tested. State of Rajasthan v. Ferro Concrete Construction (2009) Facts. A contract for a 37.41 km water pipeline in Ajmer district was treated as abandoned on 22 August 1990. The award of 21 September 1994 was challenged. Principle. The Court set aside two awards and cut pre-reference interest from 18 to 9 per cent, holding that "Courts can not sit in judgment over the award of the arbitrator , nor re-appreciate the evidence" (para 37). The appeals were allowed in part. (2009) 12 SCC 1 (22 April 2009, R.V. Raveendran and Lokeshwar Singh Panta JJ.). Why it matters. It shows the limits of court review of a construction award. Lucknow Development Authority v. M.K. Gupta (1994) Facts. Allottees of flats under a development authority's housing schemes paid deposits, but the flats were not delivered on time; in one appeal ₹6,132 and ₹1,09,975 were deposited in July 1988 and the flat was not delivered "as the construction work was not complete". Principle. "Housing activity is a service", and delay in delivering possession "is denial of service" under the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (para 6). The authority's appeals were dismissed with costs. AIR 1994 SC 787 : (1994) 1 SCC 243 (5 November 1993). Why it matters. It protects home buyers.

selfTest.q: 1. Is an entire building contract a sale of the materials used?
selfTest.a: No. It is a works contract ( State of Madras v. Gannon Dunkerley , 1958).

selfTest.q: 2. What does Section 74 allow for delay under a liquidated damages clause?
selfTest.a: Reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount named ( Fateh Chand ).

selfTest.q: 3. What notice does Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act require?
selfTest.a: Written notice of at least 30 days.

selfTest.q: 4. Can an owner who has got the work finished under Section 20 also sue for specific performance?
selfTest.a: No. Section 20(3) bars it, but Section 20(4) keeps his claim for compensation.

selfTest.q: 5. Does a sharp rise in the cost of materials frustrate a construction contract?
selfTest.a: No. It is commercial hardship, not impossibility under Section 56.
