te.inOneMinute: సంపూర్ణ బాధ్యత అనేది M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987), అంటే Oleum Gas Leak కేసు లో రాజ్యాంగ ధర్మాసనం నిర్ణయించిన భారత నియమం. ప్రమాదకర లేదా స్వతహాగా ప్రమాదకరమైన కార్యకలాపం నిర్వహించే సంస్థ "an absolute and nondelegable duty to the community to ensure that no harm results to anyone" (అర్థం: ఎవరికీ హాని జరగకుండా చూసే సంపూర్ణ, అప్పగించలేని విధి సమాజం పట్ల) కలిగి ఉంటుంది. హాని జరిగితే, సంస్థ "strictly and absolutely liable" (అర్థం: కఠినంగా, సంపూర్ణంగా బాధ్యత వహిస్తుంది), ఆ బాధ్యత Rylands v. Fletcher యొక్క "is not subject to any of the exceptions" (అర్థం: ఏ మినహాయింపులకూ లోబడదు). సహేతుక జాగ్రత్త జవాబు కాదు. పరిహార మొత్తం "co-related to the magnitude and capacity of the enterprise" (అర్థం: సంస్థ పరిమాణం, సామర్థ్యంతో సంబంధం ఉండాలి), తద్వారా అది నిరోధక ప్రభావం కలిగి ఉంటుంది. అలాంటి కేసులకు Rylands ను తిరస్కరించారు, ఎందుకంటే అది "evolved in the 19th Century" (అర్థం: 19వ శతాబ్దంలో రూపొందింది), ఆధునిక పారిశ్రామిక ఆర్థిక వ్యవస్థకు "cannot afford any guidance" (అర్థం: ఏ మార్గదర్శకత్వమూ ఇవ్వలేదు). ఈ నియమాన్ని Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India (1996) ధృవీకరించింది. పార్లమెంట్ దీనిపై Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 , National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 (s. 17(3): "principle of no fault" (అర్థం: తప్పు-రహిత సూత్రం)) ను నిర్మించింది.
te.meaning: సంపూర్ణ బాధ్యత – ప్రమాదకర లేదా స్వతహాగా ప్రమాదకరమైన కార్యకలాపం నిర్వహించే సంస్థ, ఆ కార్యకలాపంలో ప్రమాదం వల్ల హాని పొందిన ప్రతి ఒక్కరికీ, నిర్లక్ష్యం రుజువు లేకుండా, Rylands మినహాయింపులు ఏవీ లేకుండా పరిహారం చెల్లించే బాధ్యత. ప్రమాదకర లేదా స్వతహాగా ప్రమాదకరమైన కార్యకలాపం – "which poses a potential threat to the health and safety of the persons working in the factory and residing in the surrounding areas" (అర్థం: ఫ్యాక్టరీలో పనిచేసే, చుట్టుపక్కల నివసించే వ్యక్తుల ఆరోగ్యానికి, భద్రతకు సంభావ్య ముప్పు కలిగించే) కార్యకలాపం ( M.C. Mehta ), ఉదా. విషపూరిత రసాయనాలు లేదా వాయువుల తయారీ. అప్పగించలేని విధి – సంస్థ మరెవరికీ (కాంట్రాక్టర్, సరఫరాదారు) అప్పగించలేని విధి. విధి ఉల్లంఘించబడితే, పనిని మరొకరు చేసినా సంస్థే బాధ్యత వహిస్తుంది.
keyPoints: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987): Oleum Gas Leak; రాజ్యాంగ ధర్మాసనం; 20 Dec 1986. ప్రమాదకర సంస్థ "absolute and nondelegable duty" (అర్థం: సంపూర్ణ, అప్పగించలేని విధి) కలిగి ఉంటుంది. Rylands మినహాయింపులు లేవు; సహేతుక జాగ్రత్త రక్షణ కాదు. పరిహారం "magnitude and capacity of the enterprise" (అర్థం: సంస్థ పరిమాణం, సామర్థ్యం) తో అనుసంధానం. Rylands "evolved in the 19th Century" (అర్థం: 19వ శతాబ్దంలో రూపొందింది), ఆధునిక పరిశ్రమకు మార్గదర్శకత్వం ఇవ్వదు. Union Carbide (1991) దానిని obiter అంది; Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action (1996) విభేదించి అన్వయించింది. PLI Act 1991 s. 3: తప్పు-రహిత ఉపశమనం; s. 4: తప్పనిసరి బీమా. hi.inOneMinute: Absolute liability is an Indian rule laid down by a Constitution Bench in M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987), the Oleum Gas Leak case . An enterprise engaged in a hazardous or inherently dangerous activity owes "an absolute and nondelegable duty to the community to ensure that no harm results to anyone". If harm results, the enterprise is "strictly and absolutely liable", and the liability "is not subject to any of the exceptions" of Rylands v. Fletcher . Reasonable care is no answer. The amount of compensation must be "co-related to the magnitude and capacity of the enterprise" so that it has a deterrent effect. Rylands was rejected for such cases because it "evolved in the 19th Century" and "cannot afford any guidance" for a modern industrial economy. The rule was confirmed in Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v. Union of India (1996). Parliament built on it in the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 and the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 (s. 17(3): "principle of no fault").
legalProvision: Absolute liability is a judge-made rule of the Supreme Court. It was laid down in proceedings under Art. 32 for enforcement of Art. 21. Statutes now carry the same idea:

Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, s. 3(1) – "Where death or injury to any person (other than a workman) or damage to any property has resulted from an accident, the owner shall be liable to reimburse such amount, or provide such other relief as may be prescribed, for— (a) death due to fatal accident; (b) medical expenses incurred due to total or partial disability; (c) loss of wages due to partial disability; (d) other injury or sickness; (e) damage to private property; or (f) such other loss or damage, as may be prescribed."

PLI Act, s. 3(2) – "the claimant shall not be required to plead and establish that the death, injury or damage in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act, neglect or default of any person."
PLI Act, s. 4(1) – "Every owner of any undertaking shall take out, before he starts handling any hazardous substance, one or more insurance policies" against this liability.

National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, s. 17(1) – where death, injury or damage to property or environment "has resulted from an accident or the adverse impact of an activity or operation or process, under any enactment specified in Schedule I, the person responsible shall be liable to pay such relief or compensation".
NGT Act, s. 17(3) – "The Tribunal shall, in case of an accident, apply the principle of no fault."
hi.meaning: Absolute liability – the liability of an enterprise carrying on a hazardous or inherently dangerous activity to compensate everyone harmed by an accident in that activity, without proof of negligence and without any of the Rylands exceptions. Hazardous or inherently dangerous activity – an activity "which poses a potential threat to the health and safety of the persons working in the factory and residing in the surrounding areas" ( M.C. Mehta ), e.g. manufacture of toxic chemicals or gases. Non-delegable duty – a duty that the enterprise cannot pass on to anyone else (a contractor, a supplier). If the duty is broken, the enterprise is liable even if someone else did the work.
keyPoints: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1987): Oleum Gas Leak; Constitution Bench; 20 Dec 1986. Hazardous enterprise owes an "absolute and nondelegable duty". No Rylands exceptions; reasonable care is no defence. Compensation linked to "magnitude and capacity of the enterprise". Rylands "evolved in the 19th Century" and gives no guidance for modern industry. Union Carbide (1991) called it obiter; Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action (1996) disagreed and applied it. PLI Act 1991 s. 3: no-fault relief; s. 4: compulsory insurance. NGT Act 2010 s. 17(3): "principle of no fault" in accidents.

selfTest.a: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak case). When did the oleum gas leak happen? 4 and 6 December 1985. What duty does a hazardous enterprise owe? An absolute and nondelegable duty to the community. Which Rylands exceptions apply? None. Is reasonable care a defence? No. How is compensation measured? Co-related to the magnitude and capacity of the enterprise, to deter. Why was Rylands rejected? It evolved in the 19th century and cannot guide modern industrial liability. Which case confirmed the rule and rejected the obiter view? Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action (1996). Under the PLI Act, must the claimant prove negligence? No (s. 3(2)). What principle does NGT Act s. 17(3) apply in accidents? The principle of no fault.

law-of-torts-u2-t4.subtitle: Joint and several liability, composite negligence, suing the wrongdoers, release and the right of contribution

en.inOneMinute: When two or more persons are responsible for the same damage to the plaintiff, they are joint tortfeasors (or concurrent wrongdoers causing one damage). Persons become joint tortfeasors in three main ways: (1) agency or authorisation (one does it, another authorised it), (2) vicarious liability (employer and employee), (3) concerted action for a common purpose. Their liability is joint and several : each is liable for the whole damage; the plaintiff may sue all or any of them; but he can recover the total only once. Where two wrongdoers' negligence combines to injure a third person, it is composite negligence . The injured need not prove each one's share ( T.O. Antony v. Karvarnan , 2008). Composite negligence is different from contributory negligence , where the injured person himself is partly at fault and his damages are reduced. A wrongdoer who pays more than his share may claim contribution from the others. In India there is no general statute on this; courts decide on justice, equity and good conscience. Procedure: all such defendants may be joined in one suit (CPC Order I r. 3).
legalProvision: There is no single Indian statute on joint tortfeasors. The rules come from common law principles applied by Indian courts. The provisions that matter are:

Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order I r. 3 – "All persons may be joined in one suit as defendants where— (a) any right to relief in respect of, or arising out of, the same act or transaction or series of acts or transactions is alleged to exist against such persons, whether jointly, severally or in the alternative; and (b) if separate suits were brought against such persons, any common question of law or fact would arise."

Indian Partnership Act, 1932, s. 25 – every partner is liable "jointly with all the other partners and also severally" for all acts of the firm done while he is a partner. Read with s. 26 , this makes partners joint tortfeasors for a partner's wrongful act in the ordinary course of business.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, s. 43 (by analogy only) – "Each of two or more joint promisors may compel every other joint promisor to contribute equally with himself to the performance of the promise, unless a contrary intention appears from the contract." This is a contract rule; it shows the idea of contribution that courts also apply to wrongdoers.
en.meaning: Joint tortfeasors – two or more persons who are liable for the same tort , causing the same damage to the plaintiff, because of a common link: agency, employment, or concerted action. Independent (several) tortfeasors causing the same damage – persons acting separately, without common design, whose separate wrongs combine to cause one indivisible damage. They too are each liable for the whole, but they are not "joint" in the strict sense. Indian motor accident law calls this composite negligence . Joint and several liability – liability in which each wrongdoer can be made to pay the whole amount, and all can also be sued together; the plaintiff cannot recover more than the total damage. Composite negligence – T.O. Antony : "Where a person is injured as a result of negligence on the part of two or more wrong doers, it is said that the person was injured on account of the composite negligence of those wrong-doers." Contribution – the right of a wrongdoer who has paid the plaintiff to recover a fair share from the other wrongdoers liable for the same damage.
keyPoints: Joint tortfeasors: same tort, same damage, linked by agency, employment or common design. Liability is joint and several: each liable for the whole. Plaintiff may sue all or any, but recovers only once. Plaintiff need not prove each wrongdoer's share ( T.O. Antony ). Composite negligence (third party injured) ≠ contributory negligence (claimant at fault). No automatic 50:50 split ( T.O. Antony ). Contribution among wrongdoers is allowed in India on equity; no general statute. CPC Order I r. 3 allows joinder of all wrongdoers in one suit.

His fault was fixed at 25%. Why it matters: the leading Indian explanation of joint and several liability and its difference from contributory negligence.

Why it matters: shows employer and employees as joint tortfeasors liable together.

Why it matters: the servant and the employer were sued together as wrongdoers for the same death.

selfTest.q: Name the three ways persons become joint tortfeasors. Agency/authorisation, vicarious liability, concerted action. What does "joint and several" mean?
selfTest.a: Each is liable for the whole; all can be sued together. Can the plaintiff sue only one wrongdoer? Yes, he may proceed against all or any. Can he recover the full amount twice? No, only once. Define composite negligence. Injury to a person caused by the negligence of two or more wrongdoers. How is contributory negligence different? The claimant is himself partly at fault; his damages are reduced. What error did T.O. Antony correct? Automatic 50:50 split and treating composite and contributory negligence as the same. In T.O. Antony , what share of fault was fixed on the claimant? 25%. Is there an Indian statute on contribution between tortfeasors? No; courts apply justice, equity and good conscience. Which CPC provision allows joining all wrongdoers? Order I r. 3.

te.inOneMinute: వాదికి కలిగిన ఒకే నష్టానికి ఇద్దరు లేదా అంతకంటే ఎక్కువ మంది బాధ్యులైతే, వారు ఉమ్మడి టార్ట్ కర్తలు (లేదా ఒకే నష్టం కలిగించిన సమకాలీన తప్పిదారులు). వ్యక్తులు మూడు ప్రధాన విధాలుగా ఉమ్మడి టార్ట్ కర్తలు అవుతారు: (1) ఏజెన్సీ లేదా అనుమతి (ఒకరు చేస్తారు, మరొకరు అనుమతిస్తారు), (2) ప్రాతినిధ్య బాధ్యత (యజమాని మరియు ఉద్యోగి), (3) ఉమ్మడి ఉద్దేశ్యం కోసం సమన్వయ చర్య . వారి బాధ్యత ఉమ్మడి మరియు వేర్వేరు : ప్రతి ఒక్కరూ మొత్తం నష్టానికి బాధ్యులు; వాది అందరిపై లేదా ఎవరిపైనైనా దావా వేయవచ్చు; కానీ మొత్తాన్ని ఒక్కసారి మాత్రమే వసూలు చేయగలడు. ఇద్దరు తప్పిదారుల నిర్లక్ష్యం కలిసి మూడో వ్యక్తికి గాయం చేస్తే, అది సమ్మిళిత నిర్లక్ష్యం . గాయపడినవాడు ఒక్కొక్కరి వాటాను నిరూపించాల్సిన అవసరం లేదు ( T.O. Antony v. Karvarnan , 2008). సమ్మిళిత నిర్లక్ష్యం సహకార నిర్లక్ష్యం (contributory negligence) నుండి వేరు; అందులో గాయపడినవాడే పాక్షికంగా తప్పు చేశాడు, అతని నష్టపరిహారం తగ్గుతుంది. తన వాటా కంటే ఎక్కువ చెల్లించిన తప్పిదారుడు మిగతావారి నుండి వాటా చెల్లింపు కోరవచ్చు. భారతదేశంలో దీనిపై సాధారణ చట్టం లేదు; కోర్టులు న్యాయం, సమానత్వం, మంచి మనస్సాక్షి ఆధారంగా నిర్ణయిస్తాయి. ప్రక్రియ: అలాంటి ప్రతివాదులందరినీ ఒకే దావాలో చేర్చవచ్చు (CPC Order I r. 3).
te.meaning: ఉమ్మడి టార్ట్ కర్తలు – ఏజెన్సీ, ఉద్యోగం లేదా సమన్వయ చర్య అనే ఉమ్మడి లింక్ వల్ల, వాదికి ఒకే నష్టం కలిగించిన ఒకే టార్ట్‌కు బాధ్యులైన ఇద్దరు లేదా ఎక్కువ వ్యక్తులు. ఒకే నష్టం కలిగించిన స్వతంత్ర (వేర్వేరు) టార్ట్ కర్తలు – ఉమ్మడి ఉద్దేశ్యం లేకుండా వేర్వేరుగా పనిచేసి, వారి వేర్వేరు తప్పులు కలిసి ఒకే విభజించలేని నష్టాన్ని కలిగించిన వ్యక్తులు. వీరు కూడా ప్రతి ఒక్కరూ మొత్తానికి బాధ్యులు, కానీ కచ్చితమైన అర్థంలో "ఉమ్మడి" కాదు. భారత మోటార్ ప్రమాద చట్టం దీనిని సమ్మిళిత నిర్లక్ష్యం అంటుంది. ఉమ్మడి మరియు వేర్వేరు బాధ్యత – ప్రతి తప్పిదారుడితో మొత్తం చెల్లింపు చేయించవచ్చు, అందరిపై కలిపి కూడా దావా వేయవచ్చు; వాది మొత్తం నష్టం కంటే ఎక్కువ వసూలు చేయలేడు. సమ్మిళిత నిర్లక్ష్యం – T.O. Antony : "Where a person is injured as a result of negligence on the part of two or more wrong doers, it is said that the person was injured on account of the composite negligence of those wrong-doers." (అర్థం: ఇద్దరు లేదా ఎక్కువ తప్పిదారుల నిర్లక్ష్యం ఫలితంగా ఒక వ్యక్తి గాయపడితే, ఆ తప్పిదారుల సమ్మిళిత నిర్లక్ష్యం వల్ల గాయపడ్డాడని అంటారు.) వాటా చెల్లింపు – వాదికి చెల్లించిన తప్పిదారుడు, అదే నష్టానికి బాధ్యులైన ఇతర తప్పిదారుల నుండి న్యాయమైన వాటాను వసూలు చేసుకునే హక్కు.
keyPoints: ఉమ్మడి టార్ట్ కర్తలు: ఒకే టార్ట్, ఒకే నష్టం, ఏజెన్సీ, ఉద్యోగం లేదా ఉమ్మడి రూపకల్పన ద్వారా లింక్. బాధ్యత ఉమ్మడి మరియు వేర్వేరు: ప్రతి ఒక్కరూ మొత్తానికి బాధ్యులు. వాది అందరిపై లేదా ఎవరిపైనైనా దావా వేయవచ్చు, కానీ ఒక్కసారి మాత్రమే వసూలు చేస్తాడు. ఒక్కొక్క తప్పిదారుడి వాటాను వాది నిరూపించనక్కరలేదు ( T.O. Antony ). సమ్మిళిత నిర్లక్ష్యం (మూడో వ్యక్తి గాయపడటం) ≠ సహకార నిర్లక్ష్యం (వాది తప్పు). స్వయంచాలక 50:50 విభజన లేదు ( T.O. Antony ). భారతదేశంలో తప్పిదారుల మధ్య వాటా చెల్లింపు సమానత్వం ఆధారంగా అనుమతించబడుతుంది; సాధారణ చట్టం లేదు. CPC Order I r. 3 తప్పిదారులందరినీ ఒకే దావాలో చేర్చడానికి అనుమతిస్తుంది.

selfTest.q: వ్యక్తులు ఉమ్మడి టార్ట్ కర్తలు అయ్యే మూడు మార్గాలు చెప్పండి. ఏజెన్సీ/అనుమతి, ప్రాతినిధ్య బాధ్యత, సమన్వయ చర్య. "ఉమ్మడి మరియు వేర్వేరు" అంటే ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: ప్రతి ఒక్కరూ మొత్తానికి బాధ్యులు; అందరిపై కలిపి దావా వేయవచ్చు. వాది ఒక్క తప్పిదారుడిపై మాత్రమే దావా వేయవచ్చా? అవును, అందరిపై లేదా ఎవరిపైనైనా చర్య తీసుకోవచ్చు. అతను మొత్తాన్ని రెండుసార్లు వసూలు చేయగలడా? లేదు, ఒక్కసారి మాత్రమే. సమ్మిళిత నిర్లక్ష్యాన్ని నిర్వచించండి. ఇద్దరు లేదా ఎక్కువ తప్పిదారుల నిర్లక్ష్యం వల్ల ఒక వ్యక్తికి గాయం. సహకార నిర్లక్ష్యం ఎలా వేరు? వాదే పాక్షికంగా తప్పు చేశాడు; అతని నష్టపరిహారం తగ్గుతుంది. T.O. Antony ఏ పొరపాటును సరిచేసింది? స్వయంచాలక 50:50 విభజన, సమ్మిళిత-సహకార నిర్లక్ష్యాలను ఒకటిగా చూడటం. T.O. Antony లో వాదిపై ఎంత తప్పు నిర్ణయించారు? 25%. టార్ట్ కర్తల మధ్య వాటా చెల్లింపుపై భారత చట్టం ఉందా? లేదు; కోర్టులు న్యాయం, సమానత్వం, మంచి మనస్సాక్షిని అన్వయిస్తాయి. తప్పిదారులందరినీ చేర్చడానికి ఏ CPC నిబంధన అనుమతిస్తుంది? Order I r. 3.

hi.inOneMinute: When two or more persons are responsible for the same damage to the plaintiff, they are joint tortfeasors (or concurrent wrongdoers causing one damage). Persons become joint tortfeasors in three main ways: (1) agency or authorisation (one does it, another authorised it), (2) vicarious liability (employer and employee), (3) concerted action for a common purpose. Their liability is joint and several : each is liable for the whole damage; the plaintiff may sue all or any of them; but he can recover the total only once. Where two wrongdoers' negligence combines to injure a third person, it is composite negligence . The injured need not prove each one's share ( T.O. Antony v. Karvarnan , 2008). Composite negligence is different from contributory negligence , where the injured person himself is partly at fault and his damages are reduced. A wrongdoer who pays more than his share may claim contribution from the others. In India there is no general statute on this; courts decide on justice, equity and good conscience. Procedure: all such defendants may be joined in one suit (CPC Order I r. 3).
legalProvision: There is no single Indian statute on joint tortfeasors. The rules come from common law principles applied by Indian courts. The provisions that matter are:

Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, Order I r. 3 – "All persons may be joined in one suit as defendants where— (a) any right to relief in respect of, or arising out of, the same act or transaction or series of acts or transactions is alleged to exist against such persons, whether jointly, severally or in the alternative; and (b) if separate suits were brought against such persons, any common question of law or fact would arise."

Indian Partnership Act, 1932, s. 25 – every partner is liable "jointly with all the other partners and also severally" for all acts of the firm done while he is a partner. Read with s. 26 , this makes partners joint tortfeasors for a partner's wrongful act in the ordinary course of business.

Indian Contract Act, 1872, s. 43 (by analogy only) – "Each of two or more joint promisors may compel every other joint promisor to contribute equally with himself to the performance of the promise, unless a contrary intention appears from the contract." This is a contract rule; it shows the idea of contribution that courts also apply to wrongdoers.
hi.meaning: Joint tortfeasors – two or more persons who are liable for the same tort , causing the same damage to the plaintiff, because of a common link: agency, employment, or concerted action. Independent (several) tortfeasors causing the same damage – persons acting separately, without common design, whose separate wrongs combine to cause one indivisible damage. They too are each liable for the whole, but they are not "joint" in the strict sense. Indian motor accident law calls this composite negligence . Joint and several liability – liability in which each wrongdoer can be made to pay the whole amount, and all can also be sued together; the plaintiff cannot recover more than the total damage. Composite negligence – T.O. Antony : "Where a person is injured as a result of negligence on the part of two or more wrong doers, it is said that the person was injured on account of the composite negligence of those wrong-doers." Contribution – the right of a wrongdoer who has paid the plaintiff to recover a fair share from the other wrongdoers liable for the same damage.
keyPoints: Joint tortfeasors: same tort, same damage, linked by agency, employment or common design. Liability is joint and several: each liable for the whole. Plaintiff may sue all or any, but recovers only once. Plaintiff need not prove each wrongdoer's share ( T.O. Antony ). Composite negligence (third party injured) ≠ contributory negligence (claimant at fault). No automatic 50:50 split ( T.O. Antony ). Contribution among wrongdoers is allowed in India on equity; no general statute. CPC Order I r. 3 allows joinder of all wrongdoers in one suit.

Principle: In composite negligence "each wrong doer, is jointly and severally liable to the injured for payment of the entire damages and the injured person has the choice of proceeding against all or any of them"; where the claimant himself is negligent, it is contributory negligence and there is no "automatic inference that the negligence was 50:50". His fault was fixed at 25%. Why it matters: the leading Indian explanation of joint and several liability and its difference from contributory negligence.
State of Maharashtra v. Kanchanmala Vijaysing Shirke [1995] Supp. 3 SCR (22 Aug 1995)

caseLaws.name: Facts: A State jeep, driven by a clerk with the authorised driver's permission, hit a scooter and ki
caseLaws.facts: The High Court held the State, the driver and the clerk jointly and severally liable for ₹2,06,000 with interest. Principle: Once the negligent act of the driver and the clerk was "in the course of employment", the State was vicariously liable; appeal dismissed. Why it matters: shows employer and employees as joint tortfeasors liable together.

Why it matters: the servant and the employer were sued together as wrongdoers for the same death.

selfTest.q: Name the three ways persons become joint tortfeasors. Agency/authorisation, vicarious liability, concerted action. What does "joint and several" mean?
selfTest.a: Each is liable for the whole; all can be sued together. Can the plaintiff sue only one wrongdoer? Yes, he may proceed against all or any. Can he recover the full amount twice? No, only once. Define composite negligence. Injury to a person caused by the negligence of two or more wrongdoers. How is contributory negligence different? The claimant is himself partly at fault; his damages are reduced. What error did T.O. Antony correct? Automatic 50:50 split and treating composite and contributory negligence as the same. In T.O. Antony , what share of fault was fixed on the claimant? 25%. Is there an Indian statute on contribution between tortfeasors? No; courts apply justice, equity and good conscience. Which CPC provision allows joining all wrongdoers? Order I r. 3.

law-of-torts-u2-t9.subtitle: Giving up a right of action knowingly, and losing it by standing by in silence

en.inOneMinute: Waiver and acquiescence are ways in which a person who has a right of action in tort may lose it, or lose some remedy, by his own choice or conduct. Waiver is "an intentional relinquishment of a known right" (S.K. Das J., Basheshar Nath v. CIT , 1958). It may be express or shown by conduct. Election of remedies is a form of waiver: where a person has two inconsistent remedies and clearly chooses one, he may be unable to go back to the other. Acquiescence means standing by, with knowledge, while one's right is being infringed, so that it would be unjust to allow him to complain later. It mainly defeats equitable relief : an injunction cannot be granted "to prevent a continuing breach in which the plaintiff has acquiesced" (Specific Relief Act, 1963 s. 41(g)). Long acquiescence can even let the other side acquire a right , e.g. an easement by prescription after twenty years (Easements Act, 1882 s. 15). But a person cannot acquiesce in what he does not know of or cannot prevent ( Sturges v. Bridgman , 1879). Limits: fundamental rights cannot be waived ( Basheshar Nath ); an excess of statutory power "could not be validated by acquiescence" ( K. Ramadas Shenoy , 1974).
legalProvision: Specific Relief Act, 1963, s. 41 – "An injunction cannot be granted— ... (g) to prevent a continuing breach in which the plaintiff has acquiesced; ... (i) when the conduct of the plaintiff or his agents has been such as to disentitle him to the assistance of the court".

Indian Easements Act, 1882, s. 15 – where "the access and use of light or air to and for any building have been peaceably enjoyed therewith, as an easement, without interruption, and for twenty years", and where "a right of way or any other easement has been peaceably and openly enjoyed" as of right, without interruption, for twenty years, the right to it becomes absolute (prescription). The period is thirty years where the property belongs to Government. Explanation II links this to acquiescence: an obstruction counts as an "interruption" only if it "is submitted to or acquiesced in for one year after the claimant has notice thereof".

Limitation Act, 1963, s. 22 – "In the case of a continuing breach of contract or in the case of a continuing tort, a fresh period of limitation begins to run at every moment of the time during which the breach or the tort, as the case may be, continues." (So delay alone does not end a continuing tort; acquiescence is different from limitation.)
en.meaning: Waiver – S.K. Das J. in Basheshar Nath : "to constitute 'waiver', there must be an intentional relinquishment of a known right or the voluntary relinquishment or abandonment of a known existing legal right, or conduct such as warrants an inference of the relinquishment of a known right or privilege." Waiver and estoppel – S.K. Das J.: "Waiver differs from estoppel in the sense that it is contractual and is an agreement to release or not to assert a right; estoppel is a rule of evidence." Election of remedies – the choice, by a person entitled to two inconsistent remedies for the same wrong, of one of them, made with knowledge and shown clearly, after which he cannot pursue the other. Acquiescence – knowing of the infringement of one's right and standing by without objection, in circumstances that lead the wrongdoer to act on the belief that no objection will be taken. Thesiger L.J. in Sturges : "Consent or acquiescence of the owner of the servient tenement lies at the root of prescription".
keyPoints: Waiver = intentional relinquishment of a known right ( Basheshar Nath , S.K. Das J.). Waiver may be express, implied by conduct, or by election of remedies. Waiver is contractual; estoppel is a rule of evidence (S.K. Das J.). Acquiescence = knowing, standing by, other side acting on it. SRA s. 41(g): no injunction for a continuing breach the plaintiff acquiesced in. Prescription: twenty years' peaceable, uninterrupted use (Easements Act s. 15). No acquiescence without knowledge or power to prevent ( Sturges ). Fundamental rights cannot be waived; statutory excess not cured by acquiescence.

caseLaws.facts: Basheshar Nath v. Commissioner of Income-Tax AIR 1959 SC 149; 1959 Supp (1) SCR 528 (Constitution Bench, 19 Nov 1958)

caseLaws.name: Facts: An assessee whose case had been referred under s
caseLaws.facts: 5(1) of the Taxation on Income (Investigation Commission) Act, 1947 agreed to a settlement under s. 8-A. The Supreme Court later held the procedure under that Act discriminatory and violative of Art. 14 (in Suraj Mall Mohta and Shree Meenakshi Mills ). The Revenue argued that he had waived his fundamental right by agreeing to the settlement. Principle: Waiver means "an intentional relinquishment of a known right" (S.K. Das J.); and "it is not open to a citizen to waive the fundamental rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution" (majority view). Why it matters: gives the accepted meaning of waiver and its limits.
Sturges v. Bridgman (1879) 11 Ch D 852 (Court of Appeal)

caseLaws.name: Facts: A confectioner had for over twenty years used a pestle and mortar in his back premises next t
caseLaws.facts: Principle: "Consent or acquiescence ... lies at the root of prescription"; a man cannot acquiesce in an enjoyment "of which he has no knowledge" or which he could not have stopped. No prescriptive right; injunction granted. Why it matters: sets the knowledge and power-to-prevent limits on acquiescence.
K. Ramadas Shenoy v. Chief Officers, Town Municipal Council, Udipi [1975] 1 SCR 680 (9 Aug 1974; A.N. Ray CJ and K.K. Mathew J)

caseLaws.name: Facts: A municipal council, against the Town Planning Scheme, allowed a Kalyan Mantap-cum-Lecture Ha
caseLaws.facts: The High Court refused to quash it because the builder had spent a large sum. Principle: "The excess of statutory power could not be validated by acquiescence in or by the operation of estoppel." Why it matters: acquiescence cannot make an illegal act lawful.

selfTest.q: Define waiver. An intentional relinquishment of a known right. Which case gives this definition?
selfTest.a: Basheshar Nath v. CIT (S.K. Das J.). How does waiver differ from estoppel? Waiver is contractual; estoppel is a rule of evidence. What is election of remedies? Choosing one of two inconsistent remedies, after which the other is lost. What are the elements of acquiescence? Knowledge, standing by, the other side acting on it, inequity. Which provision bars an injunction for acquiesced breach? Specific Relief Act s. 41(g). How long for an easement by prescription? Twenty years (Easements Act s. 15). Why did the defence fail in Sturges v. Bridgman ? The noise was not a nuisance until the consulting room was built, so there was no acquiescence. Can a fundamental right be waived? No (Basheshar Nath). Can acquiescence validate an excess of statutory power? No (K. Ramadas Shenoy).

te.inOneMinute: మాఫీ (waiver) , అంగీకార మౌనం (acquiescence) అనేవి టార్ట్‌లో దావా హక్కు ఉన్న వ్యక్తి తన స్వంత ఎంపిక లేదా ప్రవర్తన ద్వారా ఆ హక్కును, లేదా ఏదైనా పరిహారాన్ని కోల్పోయే మార్గాలు. మాఫీ అంటే "an intentional relinquishment of a known right" (అర్థం: తెలిసిన హక్కును ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా వదులుకోవడం) (S.K. Das J., Basheshar Nath v. CIT , 1958). ఇది స్పష్టంగా లేదా ప్రవర్తన ద్వారా ఉండవచ్చు. పరిహారాల ఎంపిక మాఫీ యొక్క ఒక రూపం: ఒక వ్యక్తికి పరస్పర విరుద్ధమైన రెండు పరిహారాలు ఉండి, స్పష్టంగా ఒకదాన్ని ఎంచుకుంటే, మరొకదానికి తిరిగి వెళ్లలేకపోవచ్చు. అంగీకార మౌనం అంటే తన హక్కు ఉల్లంఘించబడుతుండగా తెలిసి చూస్తూ ఊరుకోవడం, తద్వారా తర్వాత ఫిర్యాదు చేయడానికి అనుమతించడం అన్యాయం అవుతుంది. ఇది ముఖ్యంగా సమానత్వ ఉపశమనాన్ని ఓడిస్తుంది: "to prevent a continuing breach in which the plaintiff has acquiesced" (అర్థం: వాది అంగీకార మౌనం వహించిన కొనసాగుతున్న ఉల్లంఘనను నివారించడానికి) నిషేధాజ్ఞ ఇవ్వలేరు (Specific Relief Act, 1963 s. 41(g)). దీర్ఘ అంగీకార మౌనం అవతలి పక్షానికి ఒక హక్కును కూడా సంపాదించి పెట్టవచ్చు, ఉదా. ఇరవై సంవత్సరాల తర్వాత prescription ద్వారా easement (Easements Act, 1882 s. 15). కానీ తనకు తెలియని లేదా నివారించలేని దానిలో ఎవరూ అంగీకార మౌనం వహించలేరు ( Sturges v. Bridgman , 1879). పరిమితులు: ప్రాథమిక హక్కులను మాఫీ చేయలేరు ( Basheshar Nath ); చట్టబద్ధ అధికారాన్ని మించిన చర్య "could not be validated by acquiescence" (అర్థం: అంగీకార మౌనం ద్వారా చెల్లుబాటు కాదు) ( K. Ramadas Shenoy , 1974).
te.meaning: మాఫీ – Basheshar Nath లో S.K. Das J.: "to constitute 'waiver', there must be an intentional relinquishment of a known right or the voluntary relinquishment or abandonment of a known existing legal right, or conduct such as warrants an inference of the relinquishment of a known right or privilege." (అర్థం: 'మాఫీ' కావాలంటే, తెలిసిన హక్కును ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా వదులుకోవడం, లేదా తెలిసిన, ఉన్న చట్టపరమైన హక్కును స్వచ్ఛందంగా వదులుకోవడం లేదా విడిచిపెట్టడం, లేదా తెలిసిన హక్కు లేదా సౌకర్యాన్ని వదులుకున్నట్లు భావించడానికి వీలిచ్చే ప్రవర్తన ఉండాలి.) మాఫీ మరియు estoppel – S.K. Das J.: "Waiver differs from estoppel in the sense that it is contractual and is an agreement to release or not to assert a right; estoppel is a rule of evidence." (అర్థం: మాఫీ ఒప్పంద స్వభావం కలది, ఒక హక్కును విడుదల చేయడానికి లేదా దానిని నొక్కి చెప్పకుండా ఉండడానికి ఒప్పందం; estoppel ఒక సాక్ష్య నియమం – అదే తేడా.) పరిహారాల ఎంపిక – ఒకే తప్పుకు పరస్పర విరుద్ధమైన రెండు పరిహారాలకు అర్హుడైన వ్యక్తి, తెలిసి, స్పష్టంగా వాటిలో ఒకదాన్ని ఎంచుకోవడం; ఆ తర్వాత మరొకదాన్ని కొనసాగించలేడు. అంగీకార మౌనం – తన హక్కు ఉల్లంఘన తెలిసి, అభ్యంతరం చెప్పకుండా చూస్తూ ఊరుకోవడం; అభ్యంతరం రాదనే నమ్మకంతో తప్పిదారుడు చర్య తీసుకునే పరిస్థితుల్లో. Sturges లో Thesiger L.J.: "Consent or acquiescence of the owner of the servient tenement lies at the root of prescription" (అర్థం: servient tenement యజమాని సమ్మతి లేదా అంగీకార మౌనం prescription కు మూలం).
keyPoints: మాఫీ = తెలిసిన హక్కును ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా వదులుకోవడం ( Basheshar Nath , S.K. Das J.). మాఫీ స్పష్టంగా, ప్రవర్తన ద్వారా సూచితంగా, లేదా పరిహారాల ఎంపిక ద్వారా ఉండవచ్చు. మాఫీ ఒప్పంద స్వభావం; estoppel సాక్ష్య నియమం (S.K. Das J.). అంగీకార మౌనం = తెలిసి, చూస్తూ ఊరుకోవడం, అవతలి పక్షం దానిపై చర్య తీసుకోవడం. SRA s. 41(g): వాది అంగీకార మౌనం వహించిన కొనసాగుతున్న ఉల్లంఘనకు నిషేధాజ్ఞ లేదు. Prescription: ఇరవై సంవత్సరాల శాంతియుత, అంతరాయం లేని వినియోగం (Easements Act s. 15). జ్ఞానం లేదా నివారించే శక్తి లేకుండా అంగీకార మౌనం లేదు ( Sturges ). ప్రాథమిక హక్కులు మాఫీ కావు; చట్టబద్ధ అధికార అతిక్రమణ అంగీకార మౌనంతో సరిదిద్దబడదు.

hi.inOneMinute: Waiver and acquiescence are ways in which a person who has a right of action in tort may lose it, or lose some remedy, by his own choice or conduct. Waiver is "an intentional relinquishment of a known right" (S.K. Das J., Basheshar Nath v. CIT , 1958). It may be express or shown by conduct. Election of remedies is a form of waiver: where a person has two inconsistent remedies and clearly chooses one, he may be unable to go back to the other. Acquiescence means standing by, with knowledge, while one's right is being infringed, so that it would be unjust to allow him to complain later. It mainly defeats equitable relief : an injunction cannot be granted "to prevent a continuing breach in which the plaintiff has acquiesced" (Specific Relief Act, 1963 s. 41(g)). Long acquiescence can even let the other side acquire a right , e.g. an easement by prescription after twenty years (Easements Act, 1882 s. 15). But a person cannot acquiesce in what he does not know of or cannot prevent ( Sturges v. Bridgman , 1879). Limits: fundamental rights cannot be waived ( Basheshar Nath ); an excess of statutory power "could not be validated by acquiescence" ( K. Ramadas Shenoy , 1974).
legalProvision: Specific Relief Act, 1963, s. 41 – "An injunction cannot be granted— ... (g) to prevent a continuing breach in which the plaintiff has acquiesced; ... (i) when the conduct of the plaintiff or his agents has been such as to disentitle him to the assistance of the court".

Indian Easements Act, 1882, s. 15 – where "the access and use of light or air to and for any building have been peaceably enjoyed therewith, as an easement, without interruption, and for twenty years", and where "a right of way or any other easement has been peaceably and openly enjoyed" as of right, without interruption, for twenty years, the right to it becomes absolute (prescription). The period is thirty years where the property belongs to Government. Explanation II links this to acquiescence: an obstruction counts as an "interruption" only if it "is submitted to or acquiesced in for one year after the claimant has notice thereof".

Limitation Act, 1963, s. 22 – "In the case of a continuing breach of contract or in the case of a continuing tort, a fresh period of limitation begins to run at every moment of the time during which the breach or the tort, as the case may be, continues." (So delay alone does not end a continuing tort; acquiescence is different from limitation.)
hi.meaning: Waiver – S.K. Das J. in Basheshar Nath : "to constitute 'waiver', there must be an intentional relinquishment of a known right or the voluntary relinquishment or abandonment of a known existing legal right, or conduct such as warrants an inference of the relinquishment of a known right or privilege." Waiver and estoppel – S.K. Das J.: "Waiver differs from estoppel in the sense that it is contractual and is an agreement to release or not to assert a right; estoppel is a rule of evidence." Election of remedies – the choice, by a person entitled to two inconsistent remedies for the same wrong, of one of them, made with knowledge and shown clearly, after which he cannot pursue the other. Acquiescence – knowing of the infringement of one's right and standing by without objection, in circumstances that lead the wrongdoer to act on the belief that no objection will be taken. Thesiger L.J. in Sturges : "Consent or acquiescence of the owner of the servient tenement lies at the root of prescription".
keyPoints: Waiver = intentional relinquishment of a known right ( Basheshar Nath , S.K. Das J.). Waiver may be express, implied by conduct, or by election of remedies. Waiver is contractual; estoppel is a rule of evidence (S.K. Das J.). Acquiescence = knowing, standing by, other side acting on it. SRA s. 41(g): no injunction for a continuing breach the plaintiff acquiesced in. Prescription: twenty years' peaceable, uninterrupted use (Easements Act s. 15). No acquiescence without knowledge or power to prevent ( Sturges ). Fundamental rights cannot be waived; statutory excess not cured by acquiescence.

selfTest.q: Define waiver. An intentional relinquishment of a known right. Which case gives this definition?
selfTest.a: Basheshar Nath v. CIT (S.K. Das J.). How does waiver differ from estoppel? Waiver is contractual; estoppel is a rule of evidence. What is election of remedies? Choosing one of two inconsistent remedies, after which the other is lost. What are the elements of acquiescence? Knowledge, standing by, the other side acting on it, inequity. Which provision bars an injunction for acquiesced breach? Specific Relief Act s. 41(g). How long for an easement by prescription? Twenty years (Easements Act s. 15). Why did the defence fail in Sturges v. Bridgman ? The noise was not a nuisance until the consulting room was built, so there was no acquiescence. Can a fundamental right be waived? No (Basheshar Nath). Can acquiescence validate an excess of statutory power? No (K. Ramadas Shenoy).

law-of-torts-u2-t11.subtitle: How an agreement to take something in place of a claim, once performed, ends the claim

en.inOneMinute: Accord and satisfaction is a way a tort liability ends by agreement and payment. Accord – the injured person and the wrongdoer agree that the injured person will take something (usually money) in place of his claim. Satisfaction – that agreed thing is actually given and accepted. When both are present, the right of action is discharged. The injured person cannot sue on the original tort. In India the basis is s. 63, Indian Contract Act, 1872: the promisee "may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit". Its Illustrations show that a smaller sum, a sum from a third person, or a sum for an unascertained amount can discharge the whole claim if accepted in satisfaction. Inside a suit for damages, the defendant may deposit in court a sum as "a satisfaction in full of the claim" (Order XXIV, CPC). The plaintiff may accept it in full or only in part. Because it rests on agreement, the injured person's consent must be free (s. 14); otherwise the arrangement is voidable (ss. 19, 19A).
legalProvision: No statute deals with "accord and satisfaction" in tort as such. It works through the following:
Indian Contract Act, 1872

Section 63: "Every promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, the performance of the promise made to him, or may extend the time for such performance, or may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit." Illustration (b): "A owes B 5,000 rupees. A pays to B, and B accepts, in satisfaction of the whole debt, 2,000 rupees paid at the time and place at which the 5,000 rupees were payable. The whole debt is discharged." Illustration (c): "A owes B 5,000 rupees. C pays to B 1,000 rupees, and B accepts them, in satisfaction of his claim on A. This payment is a discharge of the whole claim." Illustration (d): A owes B a sum "the amount of which has not been ascertained". A gives and B accepts 2,000 rupees in satisfaction. "This is a discharge of the whole debt, whatever may be its amount." Illustration (e): a composition of eight annas in the rupee agreed with all creditors; payment to B of 1,000 rupees on a 2,000 rupee debt "is a discharge of B's demand". Section 41: "When a promisee accepts performance of the promise from a third person, he cannot afterwards enforce it against the promisor." Sections 14, 19, 19A: consent must be free; consent caused by coercion, fraud, misrepresentation or undue influence makes the agreement voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.
Code of Civil Procedure, 1908

Order XXIII, rule 3: where "the defendant satisfied the plaintiff in respect to the whole or any part of the subject-matter of the suit", the Court shall order the satisfaction "to be recorded, and shall pass a decree in accordance therewith". Order XXIV, rule 1: "The defendant in any suit to recover a debt or damages may, at any stage of the suit, deposit in Court such sum of money as he considers a satisfaction in full of the claim." Order XXIV, rule 4(1): if the plaintiff accepts it "as satisfaction in part only of his claim, he may prosecute his suit for the balance". Order XXIV, rule 4(2): if the plaintiff accepts it "as satisfaction in full of his claim", he files a statement and "the Court shall pronounce judgment accordingly".
en.meaning: Accord – the agreement by which the injured person agrees to accept something in place of his claim against the wrongdoer. Satisfaction – the actual giving and acceptance of what was agreed under the accord. Accord and satisfaction – the two together; they discharge the right of action. Unliquidated claim – a claim whose amount is not yet fixed, like most claims for tort damages. Section 63 Illustration (d) shows such a claim can be discharged by an agreed sum. Payment into court – the defendant's deposit in court of a sum offered as satisfaction in full of a claim for debt or damages (O. XXIV r. 1 CPC).
keyPoints: Accord = agreement to take a substitute. Satisfaction = substitute given and accepted. Together they discharge the right of action. s. 63: "accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit". Illus. (b) smaller sum; (c) third person; (d) unliquidated claim; (e) composition. s. 41: performance accepted from a third person cannot be enforced again against the promisor. O. XXIV: payment into court as full satisfaction; accept in full or in part. Consent must be free; otherwise voidable.

te.inOneMinute: అకార్డ్ అండ్ శాటిస్‌ఫాక్షన్ (Accord and satisfaction) అనేది ఒప్పందం, చెల్లింపు ద్వారా టార్ట్ బాధ్యత ముగిసే ఒక మార్గం. అకార్డ్ (ఒప్పందం) – బాధితుడు తన దావాకు బదులుగా ఏదైనా (సాధారణంగా డబ్బు) తీసుకుంటానని బాధితుడు, తప్పు చేసిన వ్యక్తి అంగీకరించడం. శాటిస్‌ఫాక్షన్ (సంతృప్తి) – అంగీకరించినది వాస్తవంగా ఇవ్వబడి స్వీకరించబడడం. రెండూ ఉన్నప్పుడు దావా హక్కు తీరిపోతుంది. బాధితుడు అసలు టార్ట్‌పై దావా వేయలేడు. భారతదేశంలో ఆధారం భారతీయ ఒప్పంద చట్టం, 1872 సెక్షన్ 63: వాగ్దాన గ్రహీత "may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit" (అర్థం: దానికి బదులుగా తనకు సరైనదనిపించే ఏ సంతృప్తినైనా స్వీకరించవచ్చు). తక్కువ మొత్తం, మూడో వ్యక్తి ఇచ్చిన మొత్తం, లేదా నిర్ధారించని మొత్తానికి ఇచ్చిన మొత్తం సంతృప్తిగా స్వీకరిస్తే మొత్తం దావా తీరిపోతుందని దాని ఉదాహరణలు చూపిస్తాయి. నష్టపరిహార దావాలో, ప్రతివాది "a satisfaction in full of the claim" (అర్థం: దావాకు పూర్తి సంతృప్తి)గా ఒక మొత్తాన్ని కోర్టులో జమ చేయవచ్చు (ఆర్డర్ XXIV, CPC). వాది దాన్ని పూర్తిగా లేదా పాక్షికంగా మాత్రమే స్వీకరించవచ్చు. ఇది ఒప్పందంపై ఆధారపడినందున బాధితుడి సమ్మతి స్వేచ్ఛగా ఉండాలి (సెక్షన్ 14); లేకపోతే ఆ ఏర్పాటు రద్దు చేయదగినది (సెక్షన్లు 19, 19A).
te.meaning: అకార్డ్ (Accord) – తప్పు చేసిన వ్యక్తిపై తన దావాకు బదులుగా ఏదైనా స్వీకరిస్తానని బాధితుడు అంగీకరించే ఒప్పందం . శాటిస్‌ఫాక్షన్ (Satisfaction) – అకార్డ్ కింద అంగీకరించినదాన్ని వాస్తవంగా ఇవ్వడం, స్వీకరించడం. అకార్డ్ అండ్ శాటిస్‌ఫాక్షన్ – రెండూ కలిసి; అవి దావా హక్కును తీర్చివేస్తాయి. నిర్ధారించని దావా ( Unliquidated claim) – ఇంకా మొత్తం నిర్ణయించని దావా, చాలా టార్ట్ నష్టపరిహార దావాల వలె. అంగీకరించిన మొత్తంతో అలాంటి దావా తీరిపోవచ్చని సెక్షన్ 63 ఉదాహరణ (d) చూపిస్తుంది. కోర్టులో జమ (Payment into court) – బాకీ లేదా నష్టపరిహార దావాకు పూర్తి సంతృప్తిగా ప్రతివాది కోర్టులో జమ చేసే సొమ్ము (ఆర్డర్ XXIV రూల్ 1 CPC).
keyPoints: అకార్డ్ = ప్రత్యామ్నాయం తీసుకునే ఒప్పందం. శాటిస్‌ఫాక్షన్ = ప్రత్యామ్నాయం ఇవ్వడం, స్వీకరించడం. రెండూ కలిసి దావా హక్కును తీరుస్తాయి. సెక్షన్ 63: "accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit" (అర్థం: దానికి బదులుగా తనకు సరైనదనిపించే ఏ సంతృప్తినైనా స్వీకరించడం). ఉదా. (b) తక్కువ మొత్తం; (c) మూడో వ్యక్తి; (d) నిర్ధారించని దావా; (e) రాజీ. సెక్షన్ 41: మూడో వ్యక్తి నుంచి స్వీకరించిన నెరవేర్పును మళ్లీ వాగ్దానకర్తపై అమలు చేయలేరు. ఆర్డర్ XXIV: పూర్తి సంతృప్తిగా కోర్టులో జమ; పూర్తిగా లేదా పాక్షికంగా స్వీకరించవచ్చు. సమ్మతి స్వేచ్ఛగా ఉండాలి; లేకపోతే రద్దు చేయదగినది.

hi.inOneMinute: Accord and satisfaction is a way a tort liability ends by agreement and payment. Accord – the injured person and the wrongdoer agree that the injured person will take something (usually money) in place of his claim. Satisfaction – that agreed thing is actually given and accepted. When both are present, the right of action is discharged. The injured person cannot sue on the original tort. In India the basis is s. 63, Indian Contract Act, 1872: the promisee "may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit". Its Illustrations show that a smaller sum, a sum from a third person, or a sum for an unascertained amount can discharge the whole claim if accepted in satisfaction. Inside a suit for damages, the defendant may deposit in court a sum as "a satisfaction in full of the claim" (Order XXIV, CPC). The plaintiff may accept it in full or only in part. Because it rests on agreement, the injured person's consent must be free (s. 14); otherwise the arrangement is voidable (ss. 19, 19A).
legalProvision: No statute deals with "accord and satisfaction" in tort as such. It works through the following:
Indian Contract Act, 1872

Section 63: "Every promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, the performance of the promise made to him, or may extend the time for such performance, or may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit." Illustration (b): "A owes B 5,000 rupees. A pays to B, and B accepts, in satisfaction of the whole debt, 2,000 rupees paid at the time and place at which the 5,000 rupees were payable. The whole debt is discharged." Illustration (c): "A owes B 5,000 rupees. C pays to B 1,000 rupees, and B accepts them, in satisfaction of his claim on A. This payment is a discharge of the whole claim." Illustration (d): A owes B a sum "the amount of which has not been ascertained". A gives and B accepts 2,000 rupees in satisfaction. "This is a discharge of the whole debt, whatever may be its amount." Illustration (e): a composition of eight annas in the rupee agreed with all creditors; payment to B of 1,000 rupees on a 2,000 rupee debt "is a discharge of B's demand". Section 41: "When a promisee accepts performance of the promise from a third person, he cannot afterwards enforce it against the promisor." Sections 14, 19, 19A: consent must be free; consent caused by coercion, fraud, misrepresentation or undue influence makes the agreement voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused.
Code of Civil Procedure, 1908

Order XXIII, rule 3: where "the defendant satisfied the plaintiff in respect to the whole or any part of the subject-matter of the suit", the Court shall order the satisfaction "to be recorded, and shall pass a decree in accordance therewith". Order XXIV, rule 1: "The defendant in any suit to recover a debt or damages may, at any stage of the suit, deposit in Court such sum of money as he considers a satisfaction in full of the claim." Order XXIV, rule 4(1): if the plaintiff accepts it "as satisfaction in part only of his claim, he may prosecute his suit for the balance". Order XXIV, rule 4(2): if the plaintiff accepts it "as satisfaction in full of his claim", he files a statement and "the Court shall pronounce judgment accordingly".
hi.meaning: Accord – the agreement by which the injured person agrees to accept something in place of his claim against the wrongdoer. Satisfaction – the actual giving and acceptance of what was agreed under the accord. Accord and satisfaction – the two together; they discharge the right of action. Unliquidated claim – a claim whose amount is not yet fixed, like most claims for tort damages. Section 63 Illustration (d) shows such a claim can be discharged by an agreed sum. Payment into court – the defendant's deposit in court of a sum offered as satisfaction in full of a claim for debt or damages (O. XXIV r. 1 CPC).
keyPoints: Accord = agreement to take a substitute. Satisfaction = substitute given and accepted. Together they discharge the right of action. s. 63: "accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit". Illus. (b) smaller sum; (c) third person; (d) unliquidated claim; (e) composition. s. 41: performance accepted from a third person cannot be enforced again against the promisor. O. XXIV: payment into court as full satisfaction; accept in full or in part. Consent must be free; otherwise voidable.

law-of-torts-u2-t8.subtitle: How liability in tort comes to an end: death, waiver, release, accord and satisfaction, judgment and lapse of time

en.inOneMinute: Extinction of liability means the ways in which a liability in tort, once it has arisen, comes to an end, so that the injured person can no longer enforce it. A defence (like volenti or act of God) stops liability from arising. Extinction works on a liability that has already arisen . The main modes are: Waiver and acquiescence – the injured person gives up the right or stands by. Release – the injured person gives up the claim, usually in writing. Accord and satisfaction – a new agreement (accord) and its performance (satisfaction) replace the claim. Judgment and satisfaction – once a court decides the claim, it cannot be tried again ( res judicata , CPC s. 11); payment of the decree ends it. Limitation – a suit after the period of limitation "shall be dismissed" (Limitation Act, 1963 s. 3). Death – under the old maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona a personal action died with the person; in India this is largely changed by statute (Indian Succession Act, 1925 s. 306; Fatal Accidents Act, 1855). Each mode has its own syllabus topic. This note gives the full map and the rules on limitation and judgment.
legalProvision: Limitation Act, 1963, s. 3(1) – "Subject to the provisions contained in sections 4 to 24 (inclusive), every suit instituted, appeal preferred, and application made after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence."

Limitation Act, s. 22 – "In the case of a continuing breach of contract or in the case of a continuing tort, a fresh period of limitation begins to run at every moment of the time during which the breach or the tort, as the case may be, continues."

Limitation Act, s. 23 – "In the case of a suit for compensation for an act which does not give rise to a cause of action unless some specific injury actually results therefrom, the period of limitation shall be computed from the time when the injury results."
Limitation Act, Schedule, Part VII ("Suits relating to tort") – some periods:

Article Suit Period Time begins 72 Act done in pursuance of an enactment One year When the act or omission takes place 73 False imprisonment One year When the imprisonment ends 74 Malicious prosecution One year When the plaintiff is acquitted or the prosecution is otherwise terminated 75 Libel One year When the libel is published 76 Slander One year When the words are spoken (or when special damage results) 82 Under the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855 Two years The date of the death of the person killed 87 Trespass upon immovable property Three years The date of the trespass 91 Wrongful taking or injuring of movable property Three years As stated in the Article 113 Any suit with no other period (residuary) Three years When the right to sue accrues

Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, s. 11 – "No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties, or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, litigating under the same title, in a Court competent to try such subsequent suit or the suit in which such issue has been subsequently raised, and has been heard and finally decided by such Court."

Indian Succession Act, 1925, s. 306 (as quoted in Kumud Lall v. Suresh Chandra Roy , 2026) – "All demands whatsoever and all rights to prosecute or defend any action or special proceeding existing in favour of or against a person at the time of his decease, survive to and against his executors or administrators; except causes of action for defamation, assault, as defined in the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (45 of 1860) or other personal injuries not causing the death of the party; and except also cases where, after the death of the party, the relief sought could not be enjoyed or granting it would be nugatory."

Special periods: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 s. 166(3) – a claim must be made "within six months of the occurrence of the accident", extendable by up to twelve months for sufficient cause. Consumer Protection Act, 2019 s. 69(1) – a complaint must be filed "within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen".
en.meaning: Extinction of liability – the ending of an existing liability in tort by the act of the parties ( waiver , release, accord and satisfaction ), by the court process (judgment and satisfaction), by lapse of time (limitation), or by death of a party. Waiver – giving up a known right, expressly or by conduct. Acquiescence – standing by while one's right is infringed, so that it would be unjust to sue later. Release – giving up a cause of action by the injured person in favour of the wrongdoer, usually by a written instrument. Accord and satisfaction – an agreement to accept something in place of the claim (accord), and the carrying out of that agreement (satisfaction). Res judicata – a matter finally decided by a competent court cannot be tried again between the same parties (CPC s. 11). Limitation – the fixed time within which a suit must be filed; after it, the court must dismiss the suit. Actio personalis moritur cum persona – "a personal action dies with the person" (as translated in Kumud Lall ).
keyPoints: Extinction ends an existing liability; a defence prevents liability. Six modes: waiver/acquiescence, release, accord and satisfaction, judgment and satisfaction, limitation, death. Limitation Act s. 3: late suit dismissed even if not pleaded. One year for false imprisonment, malicious prosecution, libel, slander (Arts. 73–76). Three years for trespass to land (Art. 87) and residuary cases (Art. 113). Continuing tort: fresh period every moment (s. 22). Res judicata (CPC s. 11) bars a second trial of the same matter. ISA s. 306: most claims survive death; defamation, assault and personal injuries not causing death abate ( Kumud Lall , 2026).

caseLaws.facts: Kumud Lall v. Suresh Chandra Roy 2026 INSC 443 (Supreme Court, 4 May 2026; J.K. Maheshwari and Atul S. Chandurkar JJ)

caseLaws.name: Facts: A consumer complaint alleged medical negligence by a doctor
caseLaws.facts: The doctor died on 4 August 2009 while the revision was pending before the NCDRC, which allowed the doctor's legal heirs to be substituted. The heirs appealed. Principle: The maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona "in India has been statutorily modified"; under s. 306 of the Indian Succession Act, "personal injury claims abate, while claims for or against the estate of the deceased survive"; the heirs could be brought on record and the NCDRC must decide the surviving claims. Why it matters: the latest Supreme Court statement on how death extinguishes , or does not extinguish, tort liability in India.
Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Subhagwanti AIR 1966 SC 1750 (24 Feb 1966)

caseLaws.name: Facts: Heirs of persons killed when the Clock Tower in Chandni Chowk collapsed sued the Corporation
caseLaws.facts: Principle: The Corporation, as owner of a structure beside the highway, was liable even for a latent defect; damages were assessed for the dependants. Why it matters: shows that where a wrong causes death, the claim does not die with the victim: the dependants sue under the Fatal Accidents Act (period two years, Art. 82).

selfTest.q: How does extinction differ from a defence?
selfTest.a: Extinction ends a liability that has already arisen. Name the six modes. Waiver/acquiescence, release, accord and satisfaction, judgment and satisfaction, limitation, death. Must the defendant plead limitation? No; s. 3 requires dismissal even if not pleaded. What is the period for libel? One year from publication (Art. 75). What is the period for false imprisonment? One year from when the imprisonment ends (Art. 73). What does s. 22 say about continuing torts? A fresh period begins every moment the tort continues. What is res judicata? A matter finally decided between the same parties cannot be tried again (CPC s. 11). What does actio personalis moritur cum persona mean? A personal action dies with the person. Which claims abate on death under s. 306? Defamation, assault, and other personal injuries not causing death. What is the limitation for a consumer complaint? Two years from the cause of action (CPA 2019 s. 69).

te.inOneMinute: బాధ్యత అంతరించడం అంటే ఒకసారి ఏర్పడిన టార్ట్ బాధ్యత ముగిసిపోయి, గాయపడిన వ్యక్తి దానిని ఇక అమలు చేయలేని మార్గాలు. ఒక రక్షణ (volenti లేదా దైవ చర్య వంటిది) బాధ్యత ఏర్పడకుండా ఆపుతుంది. అంతరించడం అనేది ఇప్పటికే ఏర్పడిన బాధ్యతపై పనిచేస్తుంది. ప్రధాన మార్గాలు: మాఫీ (waiver) మరియు అంగీకార మౌనం ( acquiescence ) – గాయపడిన వ్యక్తి హక్కును వదులుకుంటాడు లేదా చూస్తూ ఊరుకుంటాడు. విడుదల (release) – గాయపడిన వ్యక్తి దావాను వదులుకుంటాడు, సాధారణంగా లిఖితపూర్వకంగా. ఒప్పందం మరియు తృప్తి (accord and satisfaction) – కొత్త ఒప్పందం (accord), దాని అమలు (satisfaction) దావాను భర్తీ చేస్తాయి. తీర్పు మరియు తృప్తి – కోర్టు దావాను నిర్ణయించిన తర్వాత మళ్లీ విచారించలేరు ( res judicata , CPC s. 11); డిక్రీ చెల్లింపు దానిని ముగిస్తుంది. కాలపరిమితి – కాలపరిమితి గడువు తర్వాత వేసిన దావా "shall be dismissed" (అర్థం: కొట్టివేయబడాలి) (Limitation Act, 1963 s. 3). మరణం – పాత సూక్తి actio personalis moritur cum persona ప్రకారం వ్యక్తిగత చర్య వ్యక్తితోనే చనిపోయేది; భారతదేశంలో చట్టం ద్వారా ఇది చాలావరకు మారింది (Indian Succession Act, 1925 s. 306; Fatal Accidents Act, 1855). ప్రతి మార్గానికి దాని స్వంత సిలబస్ అంశం ఉంది. ఈ నోట్ పూర్తి పటాన్ని, కాలపరిమితి, తీర్పుపై నియమాలను ఇస్తుంది.
te.meaning: బాధ్యత అంతరించడం – పక్షాల చర్య ( మాఫీ , విడుదల, ఒప్పందం మరియు తృప్తి), కోర్టు ప్రక్రియ (తీర్పు మరియు తృప్తి), కాలం గడవడం ( కాలపరిమితి ), లేదా పక్షం మరణం ద్వారా ఉన్న టార్ట్ బాధ్యత ముగియడం. మాఫీ (waiver) – తెలిసిన హక్కును స్పష్టంగా లేదా ప్రవర్తన ద్వారా వదులుకోవడం. అంగీకార మౌనం ( acquiescence ) – తన హక్కు ఉల్లంఘించబడుతుండగా చూస్తూ ఊరుకోవడం, తద్వారా తర్వాత దావా వేయడం అన్యాయం అవుతుంది. విడుదల (release) – గాయపడిన వ్యక్తి తప్పిదారుడికి అనుకూలంగా దావా కారణాన్ని వదులుకోవడం, సాధారణంగా లిఖిత పత్రం ద్వారా. ఒప్పందం మరియు తృప్తి – దావాకు బదులుగా ఏదైనా అంగీకరించే ఒప్పందం (accord), ఆ ఒప్పందాన్ని అమలు చేయడం (satisfaction). Res judicata – సమర్థ కోర్టు తుది నిర్ణయం తీసుకున్న విషయాన్ని అవే పక్షాల మధ్య మళ్లీ విచారించలేరు (CPC s. 11). కాలపరిమితి – దావా దాఖలు చేయాల్సిన నిర్ణీత సమయం; దాని తర్వాత కోర్టు దావాను కొట్టివేయాలి. Actio personalis moritur cum persona – "a personal action dies with the person" (అర్థం: వ్యక్తిగత చర్య వ్యక్తితోనే చనిపోతుంది) ( Kumud Lall లో అనువాదం).
keyPoints: అంతరించడం ఉన్న బాధ్యతను ముగిస్తుంది; రక్షణ బాధ్యతను నివారిస్తుంది. ఆరు మార్గాలు: మాఫీ/అంగీకార మౌనం, విడుదల, ఒప్పందం మరియు తృప్తి, తీర్పు మరియు తృప్తి, కాలపరిమితి, మరణం. Limitation Act s. 3: వాదించకపోయినా ఆలస్య దావా కొట్టివేత. తప్పుడు నిర్బంధం, దురుద్దేశ ప్రాసిక్యూషన్, libel, slander కు ఒక సంవత్సరం (Arts. 73–76). భూమిపై అతిక్రమణ (Art. 87), అవశేష సందర్భాలకు (Art. 113) మూడు సంవత్సరాలు. కొనసాగుతున్న టార్ట్: ప్రతి క్షణం కొత్త గడువు (s. 22). Res judicata (CPC s. 11) అదే విషయాన్ని రెండోసారి విచారించడాన్ని నిషేధిస్తుంది. ISA s. 306: చాలా దావాలు మరణం తర్వాత కొనసాగుతాయి; పరువు నష్టం, దాడి, మరణానికి దారితీయని వ్యక్తిగత గాయాలు రద్దవుతాయి ( Kumud Lall , 2026).

selfTest.q: అంతరించడం రక్షణ నుండి ఎలా వేరు?

hi.inOneMinute: Extinction of liability means the ways in which a liability in tort, once it has arisen, comes to an end, so that the injured person can no longer enforce it. A defence (like volenti or act of God) stops liability from arising. Extinction works on a liability that has already arisen . The main modes are: Waiver and acquiescence – the injured person gives up the right or stands by. Release – the injured person gives up the claim, usually in writing. Accord and satisfaction – a new agreement (accord) and its performance (satisfaction) replace the claim. Judgment and satisfaction – once a court decides the claim, it cannot be tried again ( res judicata , CPC s. 11); payment of the decree ends it. Limitation – a suit after the period of limitation "shall be dismissed" (Limitation Act, 1963 s. 3). Death – under the old maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona a personal action died with the person; in India this is largely changed by statute (Indian Succession Act, 1925 s. 306; Fatal Accidents Act, 1855). Each mode has its own syllabus topic. This note gives the full map and the rules on limitation and judgment.
legalProvision: Limitation Act, 1963, s. 3(1) – "Subject to the provisions contained in sections 4 to 24 (inclusive), every suit instituted, appeal preferred, and application made after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence."

Limitation Act, s. 22 – "In the case of a continuing breach of contract or in the case of a continuing tort, a fresh period of limitation begins to run at every moment of the time during which the breach or the tort, as the case may be, continues."

Limitation Act, s. 23 – "In the case of a suit for compensation for an act which does not give rise to a cause of action unless some specific injury actually results therefrom, the period of limitation shall be computed from the time when the injury results."
Limitation Act, Schedule, Part VII ("Suits relating to tort") – some periods:

Article Suit Period Time begins 72 Act done in pursuance of an enactment One year When the act or omission takes place 73 False imprisonment One year When the imprisonment ends 74 Malicious prosecution One year When the plaintiff is acquitted or the prosecution is otherwise terminated 75 Libel One year When the libel is published 76 Slander One year When the words are spoken (or when special damage results) 82 Under the Fatal Accidents Act, 1855 Two years The date of the death of the person killed 87 Trespass upon immovable property Three years The date of the trespass 91 Wrongful taking or injuring of movable property Three years As stated in the Article 113 Any suit with no other period (residuary) Three years When the right to sue accrues

Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, s. 11 – "No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties, or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, litigating under the same title, in a Court competent to try such subsequent suit or the suit in which such issue has been subsequently raised, and has been heard and finally decided by such Court."

Indian Succession Act, 1925, s. 306 (as quoted in Kumud Lall v. Suresh Chandra Roy , 2026) – "All demands whatsoever and all rights to prosecute or defend any action or special proceeding existing in favour of or against a person at the time of his decease, survive to and against his executors or administrators; except causes of action for defamation, assault, as defined in the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (45 of 1860) or other personal injuries not causing the death of the party; and except also cases where, after the death of the party, the relief sought could not be enjoyed or granting it would be nugatory."

Special periods: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 s. 166(3) – a claim must be made "within six months of the occurrence of the accident", extendable by up to twelve months for sufficient cause. Consumer Protection Act, 2019 s. 69(1) – a complaint must be filed "within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen".
hi.meaning: Extinction of liability – the ending of an existing liability in tort by the act of the parties ( waiver , release, accord and satisfaction ), by the court process (judgment and satisfaction), by lapse of time (limitation), or by death of a party. Waiver – giving up a known right, expressly or by conduct. Acquiescence – standing by while one's right is infringed, so that it would be unjust to sue later. Release – giving up a cause of action by the injured person in favour of the wrongdoer, usually by a written instrument. Accord and satisfaction – an agreement to accept something in place of the claim (accord), and the carrying out of that agreement (satisfaction). Res judicata – a matter finally decided by a competent court cannot be tried again between the same parties (CPC s. 11). Limitation – the fixed time within which a suit must be filed; after it, the court must dismiss the suit. Actio personalis moritur cum persona – "a personal action dies with the person" (as translated in Kumud Lall ).
keyPoints: Extinction ends an existing liability; a defence prevents liability. Six modes: waiver/acquiescence, release, accord and satisfaction, judgment and satisfaction, limitation, death. Limitation Act s. 3: late suit dismissed even if not pleaded. One year for false imprisonment, malicious prosecution, libel, slander (Arts. 73–76). Three years for trespass to land (Art. 87) and residuary cases (Art. 113). Continuing tort: fresh period every moment (s. 22). Res judicata (CPC s. 11) bars a second trial of the same matter. ISA s. 306: most claims survive death; defamation, assault and personal injuries not causing death abate ( Kumud Lall , 2026).

caseLaws.facts: Kumud Lall v. Suresh Chandra Roy 2026 INSC 443 (Supreme Court, 4 May 2026; J.K. Maheshwari and Atul S. Chandurkar JJ)

caseLaws.name: Facts: A consumer complaint alleged medical negligence by a doctor
caseLaws.facts: The doctor died on 4 August 2009 while the revision was pending before the NCDRC, which allowed the doctor's legal heirs to be substituted. The heirs appealed. Principle: The maxim actio personalis moritur cum persona "in India has been statutorily modified"; under s. 306 of the Indian Succession Act, "personal injury claims abate, while claims for or against the estate of the deceased survive"; the heirs could be brought on record and the NCDRC must decide the surviving claims. Why it matters: the latest Supreme Court statement on how death extinguishes , or does not extinguish, tort liability in India.
Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Subhagwanti AIR 1966 SC 1750 (24 Feb 1966)

caseLaws.name: Facts: Heirs of persons killed when the Clock Tower in Chandni Chowk collapsed sued the Corporation
caseLaws.facts: Principle: The Corporation, as owner of a structure beside the highway, was liable even for a latent defect; damages were assessed for the dependants. Why it matters: shows that where a wrong causes death, the claim does not die with the victim: the dependants sue under the Fatal Accidents Act (period two years, Art. 82).

selfTest.q: How does extinction differ from a defence?
selfTest.a: Extinction ends a liability that has already arisen. Name the six modes. Waiver/acquiescence, release, accord and satisfaction, judgment and satisfaction, limitation, death. Must the defendant plead limitation? No; s. 3 requires dismissal even if not pleaded. What is the period for libel? One year from publication (Art. 75). What is the period for false imprisonment? One year from when the imprisonment ends (Art. 73). What does s. 22 say about continuing torts? A fresh period begins every moment the tort continues. What is res judicata? A matter finally decided between the same parties cannot be tried again (CPC s. 11). What does actio personalis moritur cum persona mean? A personal action dies with the person. Which claims abate on death under s. 306? Defamation, assault, and other personal injuries not causing death. What is the limitation for a consumer complaint? Two years from the cause of action (CPA 2019 s. 69).

law-of-torts-u2-t10.subtitle: How a release ends a claim in tort, when it is valid, and how it can be set aside

en.inOneMinute: Release is one way a tort liability comes to an end. The injured person, the only one entitled to sue, gives up his right of action against the wrongdoer, wholly or in part. Once validly released, the claim cannot be sued on. (See Diagram 1 .) A release is a matter of agreement and consent . In India, the Indian Contract Act, 1872 supplies the rules: a person entitled to performance "may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part" what is due to him (s. 63); the consent must be free , that is, not caused by coercion, undue influence, fraud, misrepresentation or mistake (s. 14); a release obtained without free consent is voidable at the option of the injured person (ss. 19, 19A); the person releasing must be competent : of majority and sound mind (s. 11). Once a suit is filed, an adjustment or satisfaction of the claim, in writing and signed by the parties, is recorded and a decree passed on it (Order XXIII, rule 3, Code of Civil Procedure). For a minor , the next friend or guardian cannot compromise without the court's leave (Order XXXII, rule 7). Release gives up the claim. Accord and satisfaction replaces the claim with something else that is actually given and accepted.
legalProvision: No statute deals with "release" of a tort claim as such. It works through the general law of agreement:
Indian Contract Act, 1872

Section 63: "Every promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, the performance of the promise made to him, or may extend the time for such performance, or may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit." Illustration (a): "A promises to paint a picture for B. B afterwards forbids him to do so. A is no longer bound to perform the promise." Section 11: "Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind, and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject." Section 14: consent is free when it is not caused by coercion (s. 15), undue influence (s. 16), fraud (s. 17), misrepresentation (s. 18) or mistake (ss. 20–22). Section 19: "When consent to an agreement is caused by coercion, fraud or misrepresentation, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused." Section 19A: "When consent to an agreement is caused by undue influence, the agreement is a contract voidable at the option of the party whose consent was so caused."
Code of Civil Procedure, 1908

Order XXIII, rule 3: "Where it is proved to the satisfaction of the Court that a suit has been adjusted wholly or in part by any lawful agreement or compromise in writing and signed by the parties, or where the defendant satisfied the plaintiff in respect to the whole or any part of the subject-matter of the suit, the Court shall order such agreement, compromise or satisfaction to be recorded, and shall pass a decree in accordance therewith". Order XXXII, rule 7(1): "No next friend or guardian for the suit shall, without the leave of the Court, expressly recorded in the proceedings, enter into any agreement or compromise on behalf of a minor with reference to the suit in which he acts as next friend or guardian."
en.meaning: Release – the injured person's giving up of his right of action in tort , wholly or in part, so that the wrongdoer's liability ends to that extent. Right of action – the injured person's right to sue the wrongdoer for the tort. Release extinguishes it. Free consent – consent not caused by coercion , undue influence , fraud, misrepresentation or mistake (s. 14, Contract Act). A release must rest on free consent. Voidable – valid until the person whose consent was not free chooses to avoid it (ss. 19, 19A). A release obtained by fraud or pressure is voidable, not automatically void. Remission – giving up, wholly or in part, what is due (s. 63). A release of a tort claim is a remission of the right to compensation.
keyPoints: Release: the injured person gives up his right of action. s. 63: "dispense with or remit, wholly or in part" – remission. Total or partial. Needs competence (s. 11) and free consent (s. 14). Without free consent: voidable (ss. 19, 19A). Pending suit: written, signed compromise recorded; decree (O. XXIII r. 3). Minor's suit: court leave (O. XXXII r. 7). Release needs no substitute; accord and satisfaction does.

te.inOneMinute: విడుదల (Release) అనేది టార్ట్ బాధ్యత ముగిసే ఒక మార్గం. దావా వేయడానికి అర్హత ఉన్న ఏకైక వ్యక్తి అయిన బాధితుడు, తప్పు చేసిన వ్యక్తిపై తన దావా హక్కును పూర్తిగా లేదా పాక్షికంగా వదులుకుంటాడు. చెల్లుబాటుగా విడుదల చేసిన తర్వాత ఆ దావాపై కేసు వేయలేరు. ( చిత్రం 1 చూడండి.) విడుదల అనేది ఒప్పందం మరియు సమ్మతి విషయం. భారతదేశంలో భారతీయ ఒప్పంద చట్టం, 1872 నియమాలను ఇస్తుంది: తనకు రావలసిన నెరవేర్పును పొందే హక్కు ఉన్న వ్యక్తి "may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part" (అర్థం: పూర్తిగా లేదా పాక్షికంగా మినహాయించవచ్చు లేదా వదులుకోవచ్చు) (సెక్షన్ 63); సమ్మతి స్వేచ్ఛగా ఉండాలి, అంటే బలవంతం, అనుచిత ప్రభావం, మోసం, తప్పుడు ప్రాతినిధ్యం లేదా పొరపాటు వల్ల కలగకూడదు (సెక్షన్ 14); స్వేచ్ఛా సమ్మతి లేకుండా పొందిన విడుదల, బాధితుడి ఇష్టానుసారం రద్దు చేయదగినది (సెక్షన్లు 19, 19A); విడుదల ఇచ్చే వ్యక్తి అర్హుడు కావాలి: మేజర్ వయస్సు, స్థిరమైన మనస్సు (సెక్షన్ 11). దావా వేసిన తర్వాత, లిఖితంగా ఉండి పక్షాలు సంతకం చేసిన సర్దుబాటు లేదా సంతృప్తిని కోర్టు నమోదు చేసి దాని ప్రకారం డిక్రీ ఇస్తుంది (ఆర్డర్ XXIII, రూల్ 3, సివిల్ ప్రొసీజర్ కోడ్). మైనర్ విషయంలో, నెక్స్ట్ ఫ్రెండ్ లేదా సంరక్షకుడు కోర్టు అనుమతి లేకుండా రాజీ చేయలేరు (ఆర్డర్ XXXII, రూల్ 7). విడుదల దావాను వదులుకుంటుంది. అకార్డ్ అండ్ శాటిస్‌ఫాక్షన్ దావా స్థానంలో వాస్తవంగా ఇచ్చి స్వీకరించిన మరొకదాన్ని ఉంచుతుంది.
te.meaning: విడుదల (Release) – బాధితుడు టార్ట్‌లో తన దావా హక్కును పూర్తిగా లేదా పాక్షికంగా వదులుకోవడం; దాంతో ఆ మేరకు తప్పు చేసిన వ్యక్తి బాధ్యత ముగుస్తుంది. దావా హక్కు (Right of action) – టార్ట్ కోసం తప్పు చేసిన వ్యక్తిపై దావా వేసే బాధితుడి హక్కు. విడుదల దీన్ని అంతం చేస్తుంది. స్వేచ్ఛా సమ్మతి (Free consent) – బలవంతం , అనుచిత ప్రభావం , మోసం, తప్పుడు ప్రాతినిధ్యం లేదా పొరపాటు వల్ల కలగని సమ్మతి (సెక్షన్ 14, ఒప్పంద చట్టం). విడుదల స్వేచ్ఛా సమ్మతిపై ఆధారపడాలి. రద్దు చేయదగినది (Voidable) – సమ్మతి స్వేచ్ఛగా లేని వ్యక్తి దాన్ని రద్దు చేయాలని ఎంచుకునే వరకు చెల్లుబాటు అవుతుంది (సెక్షన్లు 19, 19A). మోసం లేదా ఒత్తిడితో పొందిన విడుదల రద్దు చేయదగినది, అది స్వయంగా శూన్యం కాదు. మినహాయింపు (Remission) – రావలసినదాన్ని పూర్తిగా లేదా పాక్షికంగా వదులుకోవడం (సెక్షన్ 63). టార్ట్ దావా విడుదల అనేది నష్టపరిహార హక్కు మినహాయింపు.
keyPoints: విడుదల: బాధితుడు తన దావా హక్కును వదులుకుంటాడు. సెక్షన్ 63: "dispense with or remit, wholly or in part" (అర్థం: పూర్తిగా లేదా పాక్షికంగా మినహాయించడం లేదా వదులుకోవడం) – మినహాయింపు. పూర్తి లేదా పాక్షిక. అర్హత (సెక్షన్ 11), స్వేచ్ఛా సమ్మతి (సెక్షన్ 14) అవసరం. స్వేచ్ఛా సమ్మతి లేకపోతే: రద్దు చేయదగినది (సెక్షన్లు 19, 19A). పెండింగ్ దావా: లిఖిత, సంతకం చేసిన రాజీ నమోదు; డిక్రీ (ఆర్డర్ XXIII రూల్ 3). మైనర్ దావా: కోర్టు అనుమతి (ఆర్డర్ XXXII రూల్ 7). విడుదలకు ప్రత్యామ్నాయం అవసరం లేదు; అకార్డ్ అండ్ శాటిస్‌ఫాక్షన్‌కు అవసరం.

selfTest.q: టార్ట్ చట్టంలో విడుదల అంటే ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: దావాను పూర్తిగా లేదా పాక్షికంగా వదులుకోవడానికి ఒప్పంద చట్టంలోని ఏ సెక్షన్ అనుమతిస్తుంది? మోసంతో పొందిన విడుదల శూన్యమా లేదా రద్దు చేయదగినదా? ఆర్డర్ XXIII రూల్ 3 CPC ఏం కోరుతుంది? కోర్టు అనుమతి లేకుండా సంరక్షకుడు మైనర్ పెండింగ్ దావాను పరిష్కరించవచ్చా? విడుదల అకార్డ్ అండ్ శాటిస్‌ఫాక్షన్ నుంచి ఎలా భిన్నం?
