hi.inOneMinute: A consumer who has a grievance under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (CPA 2019) gets these remedies (See Diagram 1 ): Final reliefs – the Commission's order under s. 39(1)(a) to (n): remove the defect, replace, refund with interest, compensation (with punitive damages), product liability compensation, stop unfair or restrictive trade practices, withdraw or stop making hazardous goods, a sum of at least 25% of value for unidentified consumers, corrective advertisement, costs, and stop misleading advertisement. Interim order – while the case is pending, "such interim order as is just and proper" (s. 38(8)). Mediation – a settlement through the consumer mediation cell (s. 37; Chapter V). Challenge to an order (See Diagram 2 ) – review by the same Commission for an "error apparent on the face of the record" within 30 days (ss. 40, 50, 60); appeal to the next level (s. 41: 45 days; ss. 51, 67: 30 days), after a pre-deposit of 50% of the amount ordered; revision by the State or National Commission (ss. 47(1)(b), 58(1)(b)); setting aside an ex parte order of the National Commission (s. 61). Enforcement – the order is executed as a decree (s. 71), and non-compliance is punishable (s. 72). Other remedies remain: a civil suit in tort, or criminal law, because the Act is "in addition to and not in derogation of" other laws (s. 100). Nizam's Institute (2009) shows how compensation is measured; Kumud Lall v. Suresh Chandra Roy (2026) shows what happens to the remedy when the opposite party dies (See Diagram 3 ).
legalProvision: Consumer Protection Act, 2019

s. 39(1) – where the District Commission is satisfied that the goods suffer from defects, or that allegations about the services or any unfair trade practices, "or claims for compensation under product liability are proved, it shall issue an order to the opposite party directing him to do one or more of the following, namely:— (a) to remove the defect pointed out by the appropriate laboratory from the goods in question; (b) to replace the goods with new goods of similar description which shall be free from any defect; (c) to return to the complainant the price, or, as the case may be, the charges paid by the complainant along with such interest on such price or charges as may be decided; (d) to pay such amount as may be awarded by it as compensation to the consumer for any loss or injury suffered by the consumer due to the negligence of the opposite party: Provided that the District Commission shall have the power to grant punitive damages in such circumstances as it deems fit; (e) to pay such amount as may be awarded by it as compensation in a product liability action under Chapter VI; (f) to remove the defects in goods or deficiencies in the services in question; (g) to discontinue the unfair trade practice or restrictive trade practice and not to repeat them; (h) not to offer the hazardous or unsafe goods for sale; (i) to withdraw the hazardous goods from being offered for sale; (j) to cease manufacture of hazardous goods and to desist from offering services which are hazardous in nature; (k) to pay such sum as may be determined by it, if it is of the opinion that loss or injury has been suffered by a large number of consumers who are not identifiable conveniently: Provided that the minimum amount of sum so payable shall not be less than twenty-five per cent. of the value of such defective goods sold or service provided, as the case may be, to such consumers; (l) to issue corrective advertisement to neutralise the effect of misleading advertisement at the cost of the opposite party responsible for issuing such misleading advertisement; (m) to provide for adequate costs to parties; and (n) to cease and desist from issuing any misleading advertisement." s. 39(2) – "Any amount obtained under sub-section (1) shall be credited to such fund and utilised in such manner as may be prescribed." ss. 49(1), 59(1) – the same provisions apply to complaints before the State Commission and the National Commission. s. 38(8) – "Where during the pendency of any proceeding before the District Commission, if it appears necessary, it may pass such interim order as is just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case." s. 38(12) – on the death of a complainant who is a consumer, or of the opposite party, "the provisions of Order XXII of the First Schedule to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908) shall apply". s. 37 – reference of the dispute to mediation where there are elements of a settlement which may be acceptable to the parties. s. 40 (District), s. 50 (State), s. 60 (National) – each Commission "shall have the power to review any of the order passed by it if there is an error apparent on the face of the record, either of its own motion or on an application made by any of the parties within thirty days of such order". s. 41 – "Any person aggrieved by an order made by the District Commission may prefer an appeal against such order to the State Commission on the grounds of facts or law within a period of forty-five days from the date of the order". Provisos: delay may be condoned for "sufficient cause"; no appeal by a person required to pay an amount "unless the appellant has deposited fifty per cent. of that amount"; "no appeal shall lie from any order passed under sub-section (1) of section 81 by the District Commission pursuant to a settlement by mediation under section 80". s. 51(1) – appeal against an order of the State Commission in its original jurisdiction to the National Commission "within a period of thirty days", with the same 50% deposit. s. 51(2) – an appeal lies to the National Commission from an order passed in appeal by a State Commission only "if the National Commission is satisfied that the case involves a substantial question of law". s. 67 – appeal against an order of the National Commission in its original jurisdiction "to the Supreme Court within a period of thirty days", with the same 50% deposit. s. 47(1)(b) and s. 58(1)(b) – the State Commission (over District Commissions) and the National Commission (over State Commissions) may "call for the records and pass appropriate orders" where the lower Commission "has exercised a jurisdiction not vested in it by law, or has failed to exercise a jurisdiction so vested or has acted in exercise of its jurisdiction illegally or with material irregularity". s. 61 – "Where an order is passed by the National Commission ex parte, the aggrieved party may make an application to the Commission for setting aside such order." s. 68 – an order "shall, if no appeal has been preferred against such order under the provisions of this Act, be final". s. 69(1) – a complaint must be "filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen"; s. 69(2) – delay may be condoned for sufficient cause, with reasons recorded. s. 71 – every order "shall be enforced by it in the same manner as if it were a decree made by a Court in a suit before it and the provisions of Order XXI of the First Schedule to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908) shall, as far as may be, applicable". s. 72(1) – whoever fails to comply with an order of a Commission is punishable with imprisonment from one month to three years, or fine from ₹25,000 to ₹1 lakh, or both. s. 100 – "The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to and not in derogation of the provisions of any other law for the time being in force."

Consumer Protection Act, 1986 (for comparison) – s. 14(1) listed the reliefs of the District Forum: (a) remove defect; (b) replace; (c) return the price or charges; (d) compensation for negligence, with punitive damages (proviso inserted in 2003); (e) remove defects or deficiencies; (f) discontinue unfair or restrictive trade practice; (g), (h) not offer, and withdraw, hazardous goods; (ha) cease manufacture of hazardous goods; (hb) a sum for unidentified consumers, "not be less than five per cent." of the value; (hc) corrective advertisement; (i) costs. Appeals: s. 15 (to the State Commission within thirty days; deposit of "fifty per cent. of that amount or twenty-five thousand rupees, whichever is less"), s. 19 and s. 23 (thirty days; deposit of 50% or ₹35,000 and 50% or ₹50,000, whichever is less).
hi.meaning: Remedy – the relief that the law gives to a person whose right has been violated. Under CPA 2019 it is mainly an order of a Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. Interim order – a temporary order passed while the case is pending, to protect the complainant until the final decision (s. 38(8)). Review – re-examination of an order by the same Commission that passed it, only where there is "an error apparent on the face of the record" (ss. 40, 50, 60). Appeal – a challenge to a higher Commission or the Supreme Court, on facts and law (ss. 41, 51, 67). Revision – supervisory power of the State or National Commission to call for records and correct a lower Commission's jurisdictional error, illegality or material irregularity (ss. 47(1)(b), 58(1)(b)). Pre-deposit – the condition that a person ordered to pay must first deposit fifty per cent. of that amount before an appeal is entertained (provisos to ss. 41, 51(1), 67).
keyPoints: s. 39(1): 14 reliefs; "one or more". Punitive damages: proviso to s. 39(1)(d). Unidentified consumers: at least 25% (1986: 5%). Interim order: s. 38(8). Review: ss. 40, 50, 60; 30 days; error apparent. Appeals: s. 41 (45 days), s. 51 (30 days), s. 67 (30 days); 50% pre-deposit. Second appeal to National Commission only on a substantial question of law (s. 51(2)). Revision: ss. 47(1)(b), 58(1)(b). No appeal from mediated settlement order. Finality s. 68; limitation s. 69 (two years). Enforcement: ss. 71, 72. Death of party: s. 38(12); Kumud Lall . (See Diagram 3 .)

caseLaws.facts: Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences v. Prasanth S. Dhananka, [2009] 9 SCR 313 (14 May 2009) Facts: A twenty-year-old engineering student became paraplegic after surgery to remove a tumour at the appellant hospital. The National Commission found negligence before, during and after the operation and awarded ₹14 lakh (and ₹1.5 lakh to the parents). Both sides appealed to the Supreme Court (B.N. Agrawal, Harjit Singh Bedi and G.S. Singhvi JJ.). Principle: The Court must "strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable"; "if a case is made out, the Court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation". It awarded ₹1 crore with interest at 6% from 1 March 1999. Why it matters: It is the leading guide on how a Consumer Commission should measure the compensation remedy – adequate and realistic, not token. 2. Kumud Lall v. Suresh Chandra Roy, 2026 INSC 443 (4 May 2026) Facts: A patient's husband complained (1997) that an eye surgeon's wrong operation had cost her the sight of one eye. The District Forum awarded ₹2.6 lakh; the State Commission set the award aside. While the complainant's revision was pending before the National Commission, the doctor died (2009), and the National Commission brought his wife and son on record. They appealed to the Supreme Court (J.K. Maheshwari and Atul S. Chandurkar JJ.). Principle: "upon the death of the alleged medically negligent doctor, his/her legal heirs can be impleaded and brought on record"; under s. 306 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, "personal injury claims abate, while claims for or against the estate of the deceased survive". The matter was remitted to the National Commission to decide negligence and the surviving claims against the estate within six months. Why it matters: The consumer's remedy does not end with the opposite party's death; it continues against the estate, but only for claims that survive.

law-of-torts-u5-t11.subtitle: The regulator created by sections 10 to 27 to protect consumers as a class: its structure, functions and powers

en.inOneMinute: The Central Consumer Protection Authority ("Central Authority", s. 2(4)) is a regulator created by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (CPA 2019), Chapter III, ss. 10 to 27. It did not exist under the 1986 Act. Establishment (s. 10(1)): by Central Government notification , "to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of public and consumers and to promote, protect and enforce the rights of consumers as a class ". Chapter III came into force on 24 July 2020. Composition (s. 10(2)): a Chief Commissioner and such number of other Commissioners as may be prescribed, appointed by the Central Government. Headquarters in the National Capital Region of Delhi, with regional and other offices (s. 10(3)). It has an Investigation Wing headed by a Director-General (s. 15) (See Diagram 1 ). Main powers: inquiry and investigation, suo motu , on complaint or on Central Government direction (ss. 18(2)(a), 19); search and seizure (s. 22); recall of goods , withdrawal of services, refund of prices and discontinuation of unfair practices (s. 20); directions and penalties against false or misleading advertisements, up to ₹10 lakh (₹50 lakh for later contraventions ), and a ban on an endorser for up to one year (three years for later contraventions) (s. 21); filing complaints before, and intervening in, the Consumer Commissions (s. 18(2)(b), (c)); safety notices, guidelines and advice to Ministries (s. 18(2)(j), (k), (l)). Checks: hearing before orders under ss. 20 and 21; appeal to the National Commission within 30 days (s. 24); policy directions of the Central Government bind it (s. 99) (See Diagram 2 ). Not a court: it does not award compensation to an individual consumer; that is the work of the Commissions.
legalProvision: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Chapter III – "Central Consumer Protection Authority" (ss. 10 to 27 in force from 24 July 2020, by Notification S.O. 2421(E) dated 23 July 2020).

s. 2(4) – "Central Authority" means "the Central Consumer Protection Authority established under section 10". s. 10(1) – "The Central Government shall, by notification, establish with effect from such date as it may specify in that notification, a Central Consumer Protection Authority to be known as the Central Authority to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of public and consumers and to promote, protect and enforce the rights of consumers as a class." s. 10(2) – "The Central Authority shall consist of a Chief Commissioner and such number of other Commissioners as may be prescribed, to be appointed by the Central Government to exercise the powers and discharge the functions under this Act." s. 10(3) – headquarters "at such place in the National Capital Region of Delhi", with "regional and other offices in any other place in India as the Central Government may decide". s. 11 – the Central Government may, by notification, make rules for the qualifications, method of recruitment, procedure for appointment, term of office, salaries and allowances, resignation, removal and other conditions of service of the Chief Commissioner and Commissioners. s. 12 – no act or proceeding is invalid merely because of a vacancy or defect in constitution, a defect in appointment, or "any irregularity in the procedure of the Central Authority not affecting the merits of the case". s. 13 – the Central Government provides officers and employees; the Authority "may engage ... experts and professionals of integrity and ability" in fields such as "consumer rights and welfare, consumer policy, law, medicine, food safety, health, engineering, product safety, commerce, economics, public affairs or administration". s. 14 – procedure by regulations; the Chief Commissioner has "the powers of general superintendence, direction and control in respect of all administrative matters" and may delegate them. s. 15(1) – "The Central Authority shall have an Investigation Wing headed by a Director-General for the purpose of conducting inquiry or investigation under this Act as may be directed by the Central Authority." s. 15(2) – the Central Government may appoint a Director-General and Additional Director-General, Director, Joint Director, Deputy Director and Assistant Director. s. 15(5) – reports go to the Central Authority as specified by regulations. s. 16 – the District Collector "may, on a complaint or on a reference made to him by the Central Authority or the Commissioner of a regional office, inquire into or investigate complaints regarding violation of rights of consumers as a class ... within his jurisdiction and submit his report". s. 17 – a complaint about violation of consumer rights, unfair trade practices or false or misleading advertisements "prejudicial to the interests of consumers as a class" may be forwarded "in writing or in electronic mode" to the District Collector, the Commissioner of a regional office or the Central Authority. s. 18(1) – "The Central Authority shall— (a) protect, promote and enforce the rights of consumers as a class, and prevent violation of consumers rights under this Act; (b) prevent unfair trade practices and ensure that no person engages himself in unfair trade practices; (c) ensure that no false or misleading advertisement is made of any goods or services which contravenes the provisions of this Act or the rules or regulations made thereunder; (d) ensure that no person takes part in the publication of any advertisement which is false or misleading." s. 18(2) – for these purposes it may: (a) "inquire or cause an inquiry or investigation to be made into violations of consumer rights or unfair trade practices, either suo motu or on a complaint received or on the directions from the Central Government"; (b) "file complaints before the District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission"; (c) "intervene in any proceedings" before them; (d) review factors "inhibiting enjoyment of, consumer rights" and recommend remedial measures; (e) recommend adoption of "international covenants and best international practices"; (f) "undertake and promote research"; (g) "spread and promote awareness on consumer rights"; (h) encourage NGOs; (i) "mandate the use of unique and universal goods identifiers"; (j) "issue safety notices to alert consumers against dangerous or hazardous or unsafe goods or services"; (k) "advise the Ministries and Departments of the Central and State Governments on consumer welfare measures"; (l) "issue necessary guidelines to prevent unfair trade practices and protect consumers' interest". s. 19(1) – on information, complaint, Central Government direction or of its own motion, a preliminary inquiry into whether "there exists a prima facie case"; if satisfied, "it shall cause investigation to be made by the Director-General or by the District Collector". s. 19(2) – may refer the matter to another Regulator. s. 19(3) – may call upon a person to produce documents. s. 20 – on sufficient evidence of violation of consumer rights or unfair trade practice, orders including "(a) recalling of goods or withdrawal of services which are dangerous, hazardous or unsafe; (b) reimbursement of the prices of goods or services so recalled to purchasers ...; and (c) discontinuation of practices which are unfair and prejudicial to consumers' interest". Proviso: "an opportunity of being heard before passing an order". s. 21(1) – directions to "the concerned trader or manufacturer or endorser or advertiser or publisher" to discontinue or modify a false or misleading advertisement. s. 21(2) – penalty on a manufacturer or endorser "which may extend to ten lakh rupees"; for every subsequent contravention, "which may extend to fifty lakh rupees". s. 21(3) – may "prohibit the endorser ... from making endorsement of any product or service for a period which may extend to one year"; for every subsequent contravention, "three years". s. 21(4) – a person who publishes, or is a party to publishing, a misleading advertisement: penalty "which may extend to ten lakh rupees". s. 21(5) – no penalty on an endorser under sub-ss. (2) and (3) "if he has exercised due diligence to verify the veracity of the claims". s. 21(6) – no penalty on a person who proves publication "in the ordinary course of his business", unless he had previous knowledge of the Authority's order. s. 21(7) – factors for penalty: (a) "the population and the area impacted"; (b) "the frequency and duration"; (c) "the vulnerability of the class of persons likely to be adversely affected"; (d) "the gross revenue from the sales effected". s. 21(8) – hearing before the order. s. 22 – the Director-General or an authorised officer, or the District Collector, may enter premises, search and seize documents, records, articles or other evidence; the search and seizure provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure apply "as far as may be"; seized documents must be returned within twenty days after copies are taken. s. 23 – the Central Government may designate "any statutory authority or body" to exercise the Authority's powers. s. 24 – "A person aggrieved by any order passed by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 may file an appeal to the National Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such order." ss. 25 to 27 – grants from the Central Government; accounts audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General and laid before Parliament; an annual report laid before each House. Related: s. 2(5)(iv) (the Central Authority is a "complainant"); s. 2(28) ("misleading advertisement"); s. 88 (non-compliance with directions under ss. 20 and 21: imprisonment up to six months or fine up to twenty lakh rupees, or both); s. 89 (false or misleading advertisement: up to two years and fine up to ten lakh rupees; subsequent offence up to five years and fine up to fifty lakh rupees); s. 92 (no cognizance of offences under ss. 88 and 89 "except on a complaint filed by the Central Authority or any officer authorised by it"); s. 95 (its officers are public servants); s. 96 (compounding); s. 98 (good-faith protection); s. 99 (policy directions of the Central Government); s. 104 (regulations by the Central Authority).
en.meaning: Central Authority – the Central Consumer Protection Authority established under s. 10 (s. 2(4)): a regulator for consumer rights at the national level. Consumers as a class – consumers taken together as a group, not one consumer in one transaction. The Central Authority's duty is to "protect, promote and enforce the rights of consumers as a class" (s. 18(1)(a)). Suo motu – "of its own motion"; acting without waiting for a complaint (s. 18(2)(a); s. 19(1) "of its own motion"). Preliminary inquiry – a first look to see whether "there exists a prima facie case" (s. 19(1)) before a full investigation. Recall of goods – an order calling back from the market goods "which are dangerous, hazardous or unsafe", with reimbursement of their price to purchasers (s. 20(a), (b)). Endorser – a person who endorses (promotes) a product or service in an advertisement; s. 21 allows penalties on, and a temporary ban against, an endorser of a false or misleading advertisement. Misleading advertisement – an advertisement which falsely describes a product or service, gives a false guarantee or is likely to mislead about its nature, substance, quantity or quality, conveys a representation that would be an unfair trade practice , or "deliberately conceals important information" (s. 2(28)).
keyPoints: Chapter III, ss. 10–27; in force 24 July 2020. Purpose: regulate violations of consumer rights, unfair trade practices, false or misleading ads; enforce rights of consumers as a class. Chief Commissioner + Commissioners; HQ in NCR of Delhi; regional offices. Investigation Wing under a Director-General (s. 15); District Collector (s. 16). Complaints to Collector, regional Commissioner or the Authority (s. 17). s. 20: recall, refund, discontinuation. s. 21: ad directions; ₹10 lakh / ₹50 lakh; endorser ban 1 / 3 years; due diligence defence. s. 22: search and seizure. s. 24: appeal to National Commission within 30 days. s. 88: non-compliance offence; s. 92: cognizance only on Authority's complaint.

te.inOneMinute: కేంద్ర వినియోగదారుల రక్షణ ప్రాధికార సంస్థ ("Central Authority" (అర్థం: కేంద్ర ప్రాధికార సంస్థ), సెక్షన్ 2(4)) వినియోగదారుల రక్షణ చట్టం, 2019 (CPA 2019), అధ్యాయం III, సెక్షన్లు 10 నుండి 27 ద్వారా సృష్టించబడిన నియంత్రణ సంస్థ. 1986 చట్టం కింద ఇది లేదు. ఏర్పాటు (సెక్షన్ 10(1)): కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వ నోటిఫికేషన్ ద్వారా, "to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of public and consumers and to promote, protect and enforce the rights of consumers as a class" (అర్థం: ప్రజలు, వినియోగదారుల ప్రయోజనాలకు హానికరమైన వినియోగదారుల హక్కుల ఉల్లంఘన, అన్యాయ వ్యాపార పద్ధతులు, తప్పుడు లేదా తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటనలకు సంబంధించిన విషయాలను నియంత్రించడానికి, వినియోగదారుల సమూహం (తరగతిగా వినియోగదారులు) హక్కులను ప్రోత్సహించి, రక్షించి, అమలు చేయడానికి). అధ్యాయం III 24 జూలై 2020 నుండి అమలులోకి వచ్చింది. కూర్పు (సెక్షన్ 10(2)): ఒక చీఫ్ కమిషనర్ , నియమాల ద్వారా నిర్ణయించిన సంఖ్యలో ఇతర కమిషనర్లు ; వీరిని కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వం నియమిస్తుంది. ప్రధాన కార్యాలయం ఢిల్లీ జాతీయ రాజధాని ప్రాంతంలో; ప్రాంతీయ, ఇతర కార్యాలయాలు ఉంటాయి (సెక్షన్ 10(3)). డైరెక్టర్ జనరల్ నేతృత్వంలో ఒక దర్యాప్తు విభాగం ఉంటుంది (సెక్షన్ 15) ( చిత్రం 1 చూడండి). ముఖ్య అధికారాలు: స్వయంగా (suo motu) , ఫిర్యాదుపై లేదా కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వ ఆదేశంపై విచారణ, దర్యాప్తు (సెక్షన్లు 18(2)(a), 19); సోదా, జప్తు (సెక్షన్ 22); వస్తువులను వెనక్కి రప్పించడం , సేవల ఉపసంహరణ, ధరల వాపసు, అన్యాయ పద్ధతుల నిలిపివేత (సెక్షన్ 20); తప్పుడు లేదా తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటనలపై ఆదేశాలు, జరిమానాలు: ₹10 లక్షల వరకు (తర్వాతి ఉల్లంఘనలకు ₹50 లక్షల వరకు); ఎండార్సర్‌ పై ఒక సంవత్సరం వరకు (తర్వాతి ఉల్లంఘనలకు మూడు సంవత్సరాల వరకు) నిషేధం (సెక్షన్ 21); వినియోగదారుల కమిషన్ల ముందు ఫిర్యాదులు దాఖలు చేయడం, జోక్యం చేసుకోవడం (సెక్షన్ 18(2)(b), (c)); భద్రతా నోటీసులు, మార్గదర్శకాలు, మంత్రిత్వ శాఖలకు సలహా (సెక్షన్ 18(2)(j), (k), (l)). నియంత్రణలు: సెక్షన్లు 20, 21 కింద ఉత్తర్వులకు ముందు విచారణ అవకాశం; 30 రోజుల్లో జాతీయ కమిషన్‌కు అప్పీల్ (సెక్షన్ 24); కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వ విధాన ఆదేశాలు దానిని కట్టుబడేలా చేస్తాయి (సెక్షన్ 99) ( చిత్రం 2 చూడండి). కోర్టు కాదు: ఒక్కొక్క వినియోగదారుకు అది నష్టపరిహారం ఇప్పించదు; అది కమిషన్ల పని.
te.meaning: కేంద్ర ప్రాధికార సంస్థ – సెక్షన్ 10 కింద ఏర్పాటైన కేంద్ర వినియోగదారుల రక్షణ ప్రాధికార సంస్థ (సెక్షన్ 2(4)): జాతీయ స్థాయిలో వినియోగదారుల హక్కుల నియంత్రణ సంస్థ. వినియోగదారుల సమూహం – ఒక లావాదేవీలోని ఒక్క వినియోగదారు కాకుండా, వినియోగదారులందరినీ ఒక సమూహంగా తీసుకోవడం. కేంద్ర ప్రాధికార సంస్థ విధి "protect, promote and enforce the rights of consumers as a class" (అర్థం: వినియోగదారుల సమూహం హక్కులను రక్షించి, ప్రోత్సహించి, అమలు చేయడం) (సెక్షన్ 18(1)(a)). స్వయంగా (suo motu) – "of its own motion" (అర్థం: తనంతట తానుగా); ఫిర్యాదు కోసం వేచి చూడకుండా చర్య తీసుకోవడం (సెక్షన్ 18(2)(a); సెక్షన్ 19(1) "of its own motion"). ప్రాథమిక విచారణ – పూర్తి దర్యాప్తుకు ముందు "there exists a prima facie case" (అర్థం: ప్రాథమికంగా కేసు ఉందా) అని చూసే మొదటి పరిశీలన (సెక్షన్ 19(1)). వస్తువులను వెనక్కి రప్పించడం – "which are dangerous, hazardous or unsafe" (అర్థం: ప్రమాదకరమైన, హానికరమైన లేదా అసురక్షితమైన) వస్తువులను మార్కెట్ నుండి వెనక్కి పిలిచే ఉత్తర్వు; కొనుగోలుదారులకు వాటి ధర తిరిగి చెల్లింపుతో (సెక్షన్ 20(a), (b)). ఎండార్సర్ – ఒక ప్రకటనలో ఉత్పత్తి లేదా సేవను సమర్థించే (ప్రచారం చేసే) వ్యక్తి; తప్పుడు లేదా తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటన ఎండార్సర్‌పై జరిమానాలు, తాత్కాలిక నిషేధానికి సెక్షన్ 21 అనుమతిస్తుంది. తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటన – ఉత్పత్తి లేదా సేవను తప్పుగా వర్ణించే, తప్పుడు హామీ ఇచ్చే లేదా దాని స్వభావం, సారం, పరిమాణం లేదా నాణ్యత గురించి తప్పుదారి పట్టించే అవకాశం ఉన్న, అన్యాయ వ్యాపార పద్ధతి అయ్యే ప్రాతినిధ్యాన్ని తెలిపే, లేదా "deliberately conceals important information" (అర్థం: ముఖ్యమైన సమాచారాన్ని ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా దాచే) ప్రకటన (సెక్షన్ 2(28)).
keyPoints: అధ్యాయం III, సెక్షన్లు 10–27; 24 జూలై 2020 నుండి అమలు. ప్రయోజనం: వినియోగదారుల హక్కుల ఉల్లంఘనలు, అన్యాయ వ్యాపార పద్ధతులు, తప్పుడు లేదా తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటనల నియంత్రణ; వినియోగదారుల సమూహం హక్కుల అమలు. చీఫ్ కమిషనర్ + కమిషనర్లు; ఢిల్లీ NCRలో ప్రధాన కార్యాలయం; ప్రాంతీయ కార్యాలయాలు. డైరెక్టర్ జనరల్ నేతృత్వంలో దర్యాప్తు విభాగం (సెక్షన్ 15); జిల్లా కలెక్టర్ (సెక్షన్ 16). ఫిర్యాదులు కలెక్టర్, ప్రాంతీయ కమిషనర్ లేదా ప్రాధికార సంస్థకు (సెక్షన్ 17). సెక్షన్ 20: వెనక్కి రప్పించడం, వాపసు, నిలిపివేత. సెక్షన్ 21: ప్రకటనలపై ఆదేశాలు; ₹10 లక్షలు / ₹50 లక్షలు; ఎండార్సర్‌పై 1 / 3 సంవత్సరాల నిషేధం; తగిన శ్రద్ధ రక్షణ. సెక్షన్ 22: సోదా, జప్తు. సెక్షన్ 24: 30 రోజుల్లో జాతీయ కమిషన్‌కు అప్పీల్. సెక్షన్ 88: పాటించకపోవడం నేరం; సెక్షన్ 92: ప్రాధికార సంస్థ ఫిర్యాదుపై మాత్రమే కోర్టు స్వీకరణ.

selfTest.q: సెక్షన్ 10(1) నుండి కేంద్ర ప్రాధికార సంస్థ ప్రయోజనాన్ని ఉదహరించండి. కేంద్ర ప్రాధికార సంస్థకు, దాని దర్యాప్తు విభాగానికి అధిపతులు ఎవరు?
selfTest.a: సెక్షన్ 17 కింద సమూహ ఫిర్యాదును ఎవరికి పంపవచ్చు? సెక్షన్ 20 కింద జారీ చేయగల మూడు ఉత్తర్వులు రాయండి. మొదటి తప్పుడు లేదా తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటనకు ఎండార్సర్‌పై గరిష్ఠ జరిమానా ఎంత, అతన్ని ఎంత కాలం నిషేధించవచ్చు? సెక్షన్ 21(5) ఎండార్సర్‌కు ఏ రక్షణ ఇస్తుంది? సెక్షన్ 20 లేదా 21 కింద ఉత్తర్వుపై అప్పీల్ ఎక్కడ, ఎంత సమయంలో చేయాలి? సెక్షన్ 20 కింద ఆదేశాన్ని పాటించకపోతే శిక్ష ఏమిటి?

hi.inOneMinute: The Central Consumer Protection Authority ("Central Authority", s. 2(4)) is a regulator created by the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (CPA 2019), Chapter III, ss. 10 to 27. It did not exist under the 1986 Act. Establishment (s. 10(1)): by Central Government notification , "to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of public and consumers and to promote, protect and enforce the rights of consumers as a class ". Chapter III came into force on 24 July 2020. Composition (s. 10(2)): a Chief Commissioner and such number of other Commissioners as may be prescribed, appointed by the Central Government. Headquarters in the National Capital Region of Delhi, with regional and other offices (s. 10(3)). It has an Investigation Wing headed by a Director-General (s. 15) (See Diagram 1 ). Main powers: inquiry and investigation, suo motu , on complaint or on Central Government direction (ss. 18(2)(a), 19); search and seizure (s. 22); recall of goods , withdrawal of services, refund of prices and discontinuation of unfair practices (s. 20); directions and penalties against false or misleading advertisements, up to ₹10 lakh (₹50 lakh for later contraventions ), and a ban on an endorser for up to one year (three years for later contraventions) (s. 21); filing complaints before, and intervening in, the Consumer Commissions (s. 18(2)(b), (c)); safety notices, guidelines and advice to Ministries (s. 18(2)(j), (k), (l)). Checks: hearing before orders under ss. 20 and 21; appeal to the National Commission within 30 days (s. 24); policy directions of the Central Government bind it (s. 99) (See Diagram 2 ). Not a court: it does not award compensation to an individual consumer; that is the work of the Commissions.
legalProvision: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Chapter III – "Central Consumer Protection Authority" (ss. 10 to 27 in force from 24 July 2020, by Notification S.O. 2421(E) dated 23 July 2020).

s. 2(4) – "Central Authority" means "the Central Consumer Protection Authority established under section 10". s. 10(1) – "The Central Government shall, by notification, establish with effect from such date as it may specify in that notification, a Central Consumer Protection Authority to be known as the Central Authority to regulate matters relating to violation of rights of consumers, unfair trade practices and false or misleading advertisements which are prejudicial to the interests of public and consumers and to promote, protect and enforce the rights of consumers as a class." s. 10(2) – "The Central Authority shall consist of a Chief Commissioner and such number of other Commissioners as may be prescribed, to be appointed by the Central Government to exercise the powers and discharge the functions under this Act." s. 10(3) – headquarters "at such place in the National Capital Region of Delhi", with "regional and other offices in any other place in India as the Central Government may decide". s. 11 – the Central Government may, by notification, make rules for the qualifications, method of recruitment, procedure for appointment, term of office, salaries and allowances, resignation, removal and other conditions of service of the Chief Commissioner and Commissioners. s. 12 – no act or proceeding is invalid merely because of a vacancy or defect in constitution, a defect in appointment, or "any irregularity in the procedure of the Central Authority not affecting the merits of the case". s. 13 – the Central Government provides officers and employees; the Authority "may engage ... experts and professionals of integrity and ability" in fields such as "consumer rights and welfare, consumer policy, law, medicine, food safety, health, engineering, product safety, commerce, economics, public affairs or administration". s. 14 – procedure by regulations; the Chief Commissioner has "the powers of general superintendence, direction and control in respect of all administrative matters" and may delegate them. s. 15(1) – "The Central Authority shall have an Investigation Wing headed by a Director-General for the purpose of conducting inquiry or investigation under this Act as may be directed by the Central Authority." s. 15(2) – the Central Government may appoint a Director-General and Additional Director-General, Director, Joint Director, Deputy Director and Assistant Director. s. 15(5) – reports go to the Central Authority as specified by regulations. s. 16 – the District Collector "may, on a complaint or on a reference made to him by the Central Authority or the Commissioner of a regional office, inquire into or investigate complaints regarding violation of rights of consumers as a class ... within his jurisdiction and submit his report". s. 17 – a complaint about violation of consumer rights, unfair trade practices or false or misleading advertisements "prejudicial to the interests of consumers as a class" may be forwarded "in writing or in electronic mode" to the District Collector, the Commissioner of a regional office or the Central Authority. s. 18(1) – "The Central Authority shall— (a) protect, promote and enforce the rights of consumers as a class, and prevent violation of consumers rights under this Act; (b) prevent unfair trade practices and ensure that no person engages himself in unfair trade practices; (c) ensure that no false or misleading advertisement is made of any goods or services which contravenes the provisions of this Act or the rules or regulations made thereunder; (d) ensure that no person takes part in the publication of any advertisement which is false or misleading." s. 18(2) – for these purposes it may: (a) "inquire or cause an inquiry or investigation to be made into violations of consumer rights or unfair trade practices, either suo motu or on a complaint received or on the directions from the Central Government"; (b) "file complaints before the District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission"; (c) "intervene in any proceedings" before them; (d) review factors "inhibiting enjoyment of, consumer rights" and recommend remedial measures; (e) recommend adoption of "international covenants and best international practices"; (f) "undertake and promote research"; (g) "spread and promote awareness on consumer rights"; (h) encourage NGOs; (i) "mandate the use of unique and universal goods identifiers"; (j) "issue safety notices to alert consumers against dangerous or hazardous or unsafe goods or services"; (k) "advise the Ministries and Departments of the Central and State Governments on consumer welfare measures"; (l) "issue necessary guidelines to prevent unfair trade practices and protect consumers' interest". s. 19(1) – on information, complaint, Central Government direction or of its own motion, a preliminary inquiry into whether "there exists a prima facie case"; if satisfied, "it shall cause investigation to be made by the Director-General or by the District Collector". s. 19(2) – may refer the matter to another Regulator. s. 19(3) – may call upon a person to produce documents. s. 20 – on sufficient evidence of violation of consumer rights or unfair trade practice, orders including "(a) recalling of goods or withdrawal of services which are dangerous, hazardous or unsafe; (b) reimbursement of the prices of goods or services so recalled to purchasers ...; and (c) discontinuation of practices which are unfair and prejudicial to consumers' interest". Proviso: "an opportunity of being heard before passing an order". s. 21(1) – directions to "the concerned trader or manufacturer or endorser or advertiser or publisher" to discontinue or modify a false or misleading advertisement. s. 21(2) – penalty on a manufacturer or endorser "which may extend to ten lakh rupees"; for every subsequent contravention, "which may extend to fifty lakh rupees". s. 21(3) – may "prohibit the endorser ... from making endorsement of any product or service for a period which may extend to one year"; for every subsequent contravention, "three years". s. 21(4) – a person who publishes, or is a party to publishing, a misleading advertisement: penalty "which may extend to ten lakh rupees". s. 21(5) – no penalty on an endorser under sub-ss. (2) and (3) "if he has exercised due diligence to verify the veracity of the claims". s. 21(6) – no penalty on a person who proves publication "in the ordinary course of his business", unless he had previous knowledge of the Authority's order. s. 21(7) – factors for penalty: (a) "the population and the area impacted"; (b) "the frequency and duration"; (c) "the vulnerability of the class of persons likely to be adversely affected"; (d) "the gross revenue from the sales effected". s. 21(8) – hearing before the order. s. 22 – the Director-General or an authorised officer, or the District Collector, may enter premises, search and seize documents, records, articles or other evidence; the search and seizure provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure apply "as far as may be"; seized documents must be returned within twenty days after copies are taken. s. 23 – the Central Government may designate "any statutory authority or body" to exercise the Authority's powers. s. 24 – "A person aggrieved by any order passed by the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21 may file an appeal to the National Commission within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of such order." ss. 25 to 27 – grants from the Central Government; accounts audited by the Comptroller and Auditor-General and laid before Parliament; an annual report laid before each House. Related: s. 2(5)(iv) (the Central Authority is a "complainant"); s. 2(28) ("misleading advertisement"); s. 88 (non-compliance with directions under ss. 20 and 21: imprisonment up to six months or fine up to twenty lakh rupees, or both); s. 89 (false or misleading advertisement: up to two years and fine up to ten lakh rupees; subsequent offence up to five years and fine up to fifty lakh rupees); s. 92 (no cognizance of offences under ss. 88 and 89 "except on a complaint filed by the Central Authority or any officer authorised by it"); s. 95 (its officers are public servants); s. 96 (compounding); s. 98 (good-faith protection); s. 99 (policy directions of the Central Government); s. 104 (regulations by the Central Authority).
hi.meaning: Central Authority – the Central Consumer Protection Authority established under s. 10 (s. 2(4)): a regulator for consumer rights at the national level. Consumers as a class – consumers taken together as a group, not one consumer in one transaction. The Central Authority's duty is to "protect, promote and enforce the rights of consumers as a class" (s. 18(1)(a)). Suo motu – "of its own motion"; acting without waiting for a complaint (s. 18(2)(a); s. 19(1) "of its own motion"). Preliminary inquiry – a first look to see whether "there exists a prima facie case" (s. 19(1)) before a full investigation. Recall of goods – an order calling back from the market goods "which are dangerous, hazardous or unsafe", with reimbursement of their price to purchasers (s. 20(a), (b)). Endorser – a person who endorses (promotes) a product or service in an advertisement; s. 21 allows penalties on, and a temporary ban against, an endorser of a false or misleading advertisement. Misleading advertisement – an advertisement which falsely describes a product or service, gives a false guarantee or is likely to mislead about its nature, substance, quantity or quality, conveys a representation that would be an unfair trade practice , or "deliberately conceals important information" (s. 2(28)).
keyPoints: Chapter III, ss. 10–27; in force 24 July 2020. Purpose: regulate violations of consumer rights, unfair trade practices, false or misleading ads; enforce rights of consumers as a class. Chief Commissioner + Commissioners; HQ in NCR of Delhi; regional offices. Investigation Wing under a Director-General (s. 15); District Collector (s. 16). Complaints to Collector, regional Commissioner or the Authority (s. 17). s. 20: recall, refund, discontinuation. s. 21: ad directions; ₹10 lakh / ₹50 lakh; endorser ban 1 / 3 years; due diligence defence. s. 22: search and seizure. s. 24: appeal to National Commission within 30 days. s. 88: non-compliance offence; s. 92: cognizance only on Authority's complaint.

law-of-torts-u5-t12.subtitle: Chapter VI of the 2019 Act: when a manufacturer, a service provider or a seller must pay for harm from a defective product

en.inOneMinute: Product liability is "the responsibility of a product manufacturer or product seller, of any product or service, to compensate for any harm caused to a consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services relating thereto" (CPA 2019, s. 2(34)). Chapter VI (ss. 82 to 87) is new in the 2019 Act. A product liability action is a complaint before a District, State or National Commission "for claiming compensation for the harm caused to him" (s. 2(35)). It may be brought against three persons (s. 83) (See Diagram 1 ): Product manufacturer (s. 84): liable for a manufacturing defect, a design defect, deviation from manufacturing specifications, non-conformity with an express warranty , or lack of adequate instructions or warnings. Liable "even if he proves that he was not negligent or fraudulent in making the express warranty" (s. 84(2)). Product service provider (s. 85): liable for faulty or deficient service, act of omission or commission or negligence or conscious withholding of information causing harm, inadequate instructions or warnings, or non-conformity with express warranty or contract. Product seller (s. 86): a seller who is not the manufacturer is liable only in five situations – substantial control over design or manufacture, alteration that substantially caused the harm, his own express warranty, manufacturer unknown or beyond reach, or failure of reasonable care or to pass on warnings (See Diagram 2 ). Harm (s. 2(22)) covers damage to other property, personal injury, illness or death, mental agony attendant on these, and loss of consortium or services – but not harm to the product itself, breach of warranty damage, or "any commercial or economic loss". Exceptions (s. 87): no action against a seller if the product was misused, altered or modified; four situations where the manufacturer is not liable for failure to warn; no duty to warn about an obvious or commonly known danger (See Diagram 3 ). Common law background: Donoghue v. Stevenson [1932] AC 562 – a manufacturer owes a duty of reasonable care to the ultimate consumer. The 2019 Act goes further by not requiring proof of negligence for the listed defects.
legalProvision: Consumer Protection Act, 2019

s. 2(34) – "product liability" means "the responsibility of a product manufacturer or product seller, of any product or service, to compensate for any harm caused to a consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services relating thereto". s. 2(35) – "product liability action" means "a complaint filed by a person before a District Commission or State Commission or National Commission, as the case may be, for claiming compensation for the harm caused to him". s. 2(33) – "product" means "any article or goods or substance or raw material or any extended cycle of such product, which may be in gaseous, liquid, or solid state possessing intrinsic value which is capable of delivery either as wholly assembled or as a component part and is produced for introduction to trade or commerce, but does not include human tissues, blood, blood products and organs". s. 2(36) – "product manufacturer" means a person who "(i) makes any product or parts thereof; or (ii) assembles parts thereof made by others; or (iii) puts or causes to be put his own mark on any products made by any other person; or (iv) makes a product and sells, distributes, leases, installs, prepares, packages, labels, markets, repairs, maintains such product or is otherwise involved in placing such product for commercial purpose; or (v) designs, produces, fabricates, constructs or re-manufactures any product before its sale; or (vi) being a product seller of a product, is also a manufacturer of such product". s. 2(37) – "product seller" means a person who, "in the course of business, imports, sells, distributes, leases, installs, prepares, packages, labels, markets, repairs, maintains, or otherwise is involved in placing such product for commercial purpose", and includes a manufacturer who is also a seller and a service provider; but does not include (a) a seller of immovable property, "unless such person is engaged in the sale of constructed house or in the construction of homes or flats"; (b) a provider of professional services where the sale or use of a product "is only incidental thereto, but furnishing of opinion, skill or services being the essence of such transaction"; (c) a person who acts only in a financial capacity, is not a manufacturer, wholesaler, distributor, retailer, direct seller or electronic service provider, or leases a product without a reasonable opportunity to inspect it, where selection, possession, maintenance and operation are controlled by someone other than the lessor. s. 2(38) – "product service provider", in relation to a product, means "a person who provides any service in respect of such product". s. 2(10) – "defect" means "any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, express or implied or as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods or product". s. 2(12) – "design", in relation to a product, means "the intended or known physical and material characteristics of such product and includes any intended or known formulation or content of such product and the usual result of the intended manufacturing or other process used to produce such product". s. 2(22) – "harm", in relation to a product liability, includes "(i) damage to any property, other than the product itself; (ii) personal injury, illness or death; (iii) mental agony or emotional distress attendant to personal injury or illness or damage to property; or (iv) any loss of consortium or services or other loss resulting from a harm referred to in sub-clause (i) or sub-clause (ii) or sub-clause (iii), but shall not include any harm caused to a product itself or any damage to the property on account of breach of warranty conditions or any commercial or economic loss, including any direct, incidental or consequential loss relating thereto". s. 2(6)(vii) – a "complaint" includes an allegation that "a claim for product liability action lies against the product manufacturer, product seller or product service provider, as the case may be". s. 82 – "This Chapter shall apply to every claim for compensation under a product liability action by a complainant for any harm caused by a defective product manufactured by a product manufacturer or serviced by a product service provider or sold by a product seller." s. 83 – "A product liability action may be brought by a complainant against a product manufacturer or a product service provider or a product seller, as the case may be, for any harm caused to him on account of a defective product." s. 84(1) – "A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) the product contains a manufacturing defect; or (b) the product is defective in design; or (c) there is a deviation from manufacturing specifications; or (d) the product does not conform to the express warranty; or (e) the product fails to contain adequate instructions of correct usage to prevent any harm or any warning regarding improper or incorrect usage." s. 84(2) – "A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action even if he proves that he was not negligent or fraudulent in making the express warranty of a product." s. 85 – "A product service provider shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) the service provided by him was faulty or imperfect or deficient or inadequate in quality, nature or manner of performance which is required to be provided by or under any law for the time being in force, or pursuant to any contract or otherwise; or (b) there was an act of omission or commission or negligence or conscious withholding any information which caused harm; or (c) the service provider did not issue adequate instructions or warnings to prevent any harm; or (d) the service did not conform to express warranty or the terms and conditions of the contract." s. 86 – "A product seller who is not a product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) he has exercised substantial control over the designing, testing, manufacturing, packaging or labelling of a product that caused harm; or (b) he has altered or modified the product and such alteration or modification was the substantial factor in causing the harm; or (c) he has made an express warranty of a product independent of any express warranty made by a manufacturer and such product failed to conform to the express warranty made by the product seller which caused the harm; or (d) the product has been sold by him and the identity of product manufacturer of such product is not known, or if known, the service of notice or process or warrant cannot be effected on him or he is not subject to the law which is in force in India or the order, if any, passed or to be passed cannot be enforced against him; or (e) he failed to exercise reasonable care in assembling, inspecting or maintaining such product or he did not pass on the warnings or instructions of the product manufacturer regarding the dangers involved or proper usage of the product while selling such product and such failure was the proximate cause of the harm." s. 87(1) – "A product liability action cannot be brought against the product seller if, at the time of harm, the product was misused, altered, or modified." s. 87(2) – in an action based on failure to provide adequate warnings or instructions, the manufacturer is not liable if "(a) the product was purchased by an employer for use at the workplace and the product manufacturer had provided warnings or instructions to such employer; (b) the product was sold as a component or material to be used in another product and necessary warnings or instructions were given by the product manufacturer to the purchaser of such component or material, but the harm was caused to the complainant by use of the end product in which such component or material was used; (c) the product was one which was legally meant to be used or dispensed only by or under the supervision of an expert or a class of experts and the product manufacturer had employed reasonable means to give the warnings or instructions for usage of such product to such expert or class of experts; or (d) the complainant, while using such product, was under the influence of alcohol or any prescription drug which had not been prescribed by a medical practitioner". s. 87(3) – "A product manufacturer shall not be liable for failure to instruct or warn about a danger which is obvious or commonly known to the user or consumer of such product or which, such user or consumer, ought to have known, taking into account the characteristics of such product." s. 39(1)(e) – the Commission may order the opposite party "to pay such amount as may be awarded by it as compensation in a product liability action under Chapter VI". s. 90 – separate criminal liability for manufacturing, selling or importing products containing an adulterant (see the topic "Civil & Criminal liability").
en.meaning: Product liability – the duty of a manufacturer, service provider or seller to compensate for harm caused by a defective product or by deficient service relating to it (s. 2(34)). Product liability action – the complaint by which that compensation is claimed before a Consumer Commission (s. 2(35)). Product – any article, goods, substance or raw material with intrinsic value, produced for trade, whole or as a component; excludes human tissues, blood, blood products and organs (s. 2(33)). Manufacturing defect – the particular item departs from what the manufacturer intended (for example, a crack in one bottle). Compare design defect – the intended "physical and material characteristics" (s. 2(12)) are themselves unsafe, so every item is defective. Express warranty – a definite promise made about the product's quality, performance or condition (for example, "waterproof up to 50 metres"). The Act does not define the term; this is its ordinary meaning. Harm – the losses listed in s. 2(22). Pure economic loss and loss of the product itself are excluded.
keyPoints: s. 2(34): product liability; s. 2(35): action before a Commission. s. 83: action against manufacturer, service provider, seller. s. 84(1): five grounds; s. 84(2): no negligence defence. s. 85: four grounds for service provider. s. 86: seller liable only in five cases. s. 2(22): harm – injury, death, other property, mental agony, consortium; not product itself or economic loss. s. 2(33): blood, tissues, organs excluded. s. 87(1): misuse/alteration protects seller; s. 87(2): four warning exceptions; s. 87(3): obvious danger. Donoghue v. Stevenson [1932] AC 562: manufacturer's duty of care to the ultimate consumer.

caseLaws.facts: Donoghue v. Stevenson [1932] AC 562 (HL, 26 May 1932) Facts: The appellant drank ginger-beer bought for her by a friend. The opaque bottle contained the decomposed remains of a snail, which could not be seen until most of the contents had been drunk. She claimed shock and severe gastro-enteritis and sued the manufacturer, with whom she had no contract. Principle: Lord Atkin (with Lords Thankerton and Macmillan; Lords Buckmaster and Tomlin dissenting): "a manufacturer of products, which he sells in such a form as to show that he intends them to reach the ultimate consumer in the form in which they left him with no reasonable possibility of intermediate examination, and with the knowledge that the absence of reasonable care in the preparation or putting up of the products will result in an injury to the consumer's life or property, owes a duty to the consumer to take that reasonable care." Lord Macmillan added that the injured party must prove the defect and the carelessness: "Negligence must be both averred and proved." Why it matters: It is the root of manufacturers' liability to consumers without contract. The 2019 Act builds on it and removes the need to prove negligence for the manufacturer's statutory grounds (s. 84(2)). Note: No judgment interpreting Chapter VI of CPA 2019 was found among the judgments available for this note.

te.inOneMinute: ఉత్పత్తి బాధ్యత అంటే "the responsibility of a product manufacturer or product seller, of any product or service, to compensate for any harm caused to a consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services relating thereto" (అర్థం: తయారు చేసిన లేదా అమ్మిన లోపభూయిష్ట ఉత్పత్తి వల్ల, లేదా దానికి సంబంధించిన సేవల్లో లోపం వల్ల వినియోగదారుకు కలిగిన ఏ హానికైనా నష్టపరిహారం చెల్లించే, ఏ ఉత్పత్తి లేదా సేవకైనా సంబంధించిన ఉత్పత్తి తయారీదారు లేదా ఉత్పత్తి విక్రేత బాధ్యత) (CPA 2019, సెక్షన్ 2(34)). అధ్యాయం VI (సెక్షన్లు 82 నుండి 87) 2019 చట్టంలో కొత్తది. ఉత్పత్తి బాధ్యత దావా అంటే జిల్లా, రాష్ట్ర లేదా జాతీయ కమిషన్ ముందు "for claiming compensation for the harm caused to him" (అర్థం: తనకు కలిగిన హానికి నష్టపరిహారం కోరుతూ) దాఖలు చేసే ఫిర్యాదు (సెక్షన్ 2(35)). దీనిని ముగ్గురిపై వేయవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 83) ( చిత్రం 1 చూడండి): ఉత్పత్తి తయారీదారు (సెక్షన్ 84): తయారీ లోపం, డిజైన్ లోపం, తయారీ నిర్దేశాల నుండి విచలనం, స్పష్టమైన వారంటీ కి అనుగుణంగా లేకపోవడం, లేదా సరిపడని సూచనలు లేదా హెచ్చరికలకు బాధ్యుడు. "even if he proves that he was not negligent or fraudulent in making the express warranty" (అర్థం: స్పష్టమైన వారంటీ ఇవ్వడంలో తాను నిర్లక్ష్యంగా లేదా మోసపూరితంగా వ్యవహరించలేదని నిరూపించినా) బాధ్యుడే (సెక్షన్ 84(2)). ఉత్పత్తి సేవా ప్రదాత (సెక్షన్ 85): లోపభూయిష్ట సేవ, హాని కలిగించిన చర్య లేదా లోపం లేదా నిర్లక్ష్యం లేదా ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా సమాచారం దాచడం, సరిపడని సూచనలు లేదా హెచ్చరికలు, లేదా స్పష్టమైన వారంటీ లేదా ఒప్పందానికి అనుగుణంగా లేకపోవడానికి బాధ్యుడు. ఉత్పత్తి విక్రేత (సెక్షన్ 86): తయారీదారు కాని విక్రేత ఐదు సందర్భాల్లో మాత్రమే బాధ్యుడు – డిజైన్ లేదా తయారీపై గణనీయమైన నియంత్రణ, హానికి ప్రధాన కారణమైన మార్పు, తన స్వంత స్పష్టమైన వారంటీ, తయారీదారు తెలియకపోవడం లేదా అందుబాటులో లేకపోవడం, లేదా సహేతుక శ్రద్ధ లేదా హెచ్చరికలు అందించడంలో వైఫల్యం ( చిత్రం 2 చూడండి). హాని (సెక్షన్ 2(22)) లో ఇతర ఆస్తికి నష్టం, వ్యక్తిగత గాయం, అనారోగ్యం లేదా మరణం, వీటితో పాటు వచ్చే మానసిక వేదన, సాహచర్యం లేదా సేవల నష్టం ఉంటాయి – కానీ ఉత్పత్తికే కలిగిన హాని, వారంటీ ఉల్లంఘన నష్టం, లేదా "any commercial or economic loss" (అర్థం: ఏదైనా వాణిజ్య లేదా ఆర్థిక నష్టం) ఉండవు. మినహాయింపులు (సెక్షన్ 87): ఉత్పత్తిని దుర్వినియోగం చేసినా, మార్చినా విక్రేతపై దావా లేదు; హెచ్చరిక ఇవ్వకపోవడానికి తయారీదారు బాధ్యుడు కాని నాలుగు సందర్భాలు; స్పష్టమైన లేదా అందరికీ తెలిసిన ప్రమాదం గురించి హెచ్చరించే బాధ్యత లేదు ( చిత్రం 3 చూడండి). కామన్ లా నేపథ్యం: Donoghue v. Stevenson [1932] AC 562 – తయారీదారు తుది వినియోగదారుకు సహేతుక శ్రద్ధ వహించే బాధ్యత కలిగి ఉంటాడు. జాబితాలోని లోపాలకు నిర్లక్ష్యం నిరూపించాల్సిన అవసరం లేకుండా 2019 చట్టం మరింత ముందుకు వెళ్తుంది.
te.meaning: ఉత్పత్తి బాధ్యత – లోపభూయిష్ట ఉత్పత్తి వల్ల లేదా దానికి సంబంధించిన లోపభూయిష్ట సేవ వల్ల కలిగిన హానికి నష్టపరిహారం చెల్లించే తయారీదారు, సేవా ప్రదాత లేదా విక్రేత బాధ్యత (సెక్షన్ 2(34)). ఉత్పత్తి బాధ్యత దావా – ఆ నష్టపరిహారాన్ని వినియోగదారుల కమిషన్ ముందు కోరే ఫిర్యాదు (సెక్షన్ 2(35)). ఉత్పత్తి – వ్యాపారం కోసం ఉత్పత్తి చేసిన, పూర్తి రూపంలో లేదా భాగంగా ఉండే, స్వతహా విలువ ఉన్న ఏదైనా వస్తువు, సరుకు, పదార్థం లేదా ముడి పదార్థం; మానవ కణజాలాలు, రక్తం, రక్త ఉత్పత్తులు, అవయవాలు మినహా (సెక్షన్ 2(33)). తయారీ లోపం – ఒక నిర్దిష్ట వస్తువు తయారీదారు ఉద్దేశించిన దానికి భిన్నంగా ఉండటం (ఉదాహరణకు, ఒక సీసాలో పగులు). దీనితో పోల్చండి డిజైన్ లోపం – ఉద్దేశించిన "physical and material characteristics" (అర్థం: భౌతిక, పదార్థ లక్షణాలు) (సెక్షన్ 2(12)) స్వయంగా అసురక్షితమైనవి, కాబట్టి ప్రతి వస్తువూ లోపభూయిష్టమే. స్పష్టమైన వారంటీ – ఉత్పత్తి నాణ్యత, పనితీరు లేదా స్థితి గురించి ఇచ్చిన నిర్దిష్ట వాగ్దానం (ఉదాహరణకు, "waterproof up to 50 metres" (అర్థం: 50 మీటర్ల వరకు నీటి నిరోధకం)). చట్టం ఈ పదాన్ని నిర్వచించలేదు; ఇది దాని సాధారణ అర్థం. హాని – సెక్షన్ 2(22)లో పేర్కొన్న నష్టాలు. కేవలం ఆర్థిక నష్టం, ఉత్పత్తికే కలిగిన నష్టం మినహాయించబడ్డాయి.
keyPoints: సెక్షన్ 2(34): ఉత్పత్తి బాధ్యత; సెక్షన్ 2(35): కమిషన్ ముందు దావా. సెక్షన్ 83: తయారీదారు, సేవా ప్రదాత, విక్రేతపై దావా. సెక్షన్ 84(1): ఐదు కారణాలు; సెక్షన్ 84(2): నిర్లక్ష్యం లేదనే రక్షణ లేదు. సెక్షన్ 85: సేవా ప్రదాతకు నాలుగు కారణాలు. సెక్షన్ 86: విక్రేత ఐదు సందర్భాల్లో మాత్రమే బాధ్యుడు. సెక్షన్ 2(22): హాని – గాయం, మరణం, ఇతర ఆస్తి, మానసిక వేదన, సాహచర్యం; ఉత్పత్తి స్వయంగా లేదా ఆర్థిక నష్టం కాదు. సెక్షన్ 2(33): రక్తం, కణజాలాలు, అవయవాలు మినహాయింపు. సెక్షన్ 87(1): దుర్వినియోగం/మార్పు విక్రేతను రక్షిస్తుంది; సెక్షన్ 87(2): నాలుగు హెచ్చరిక మినహాయింపులు; సెక్షన్ 87(3): స్పష్టమైన ప్రమాదం. Donoghue v. Stevenson [1932] AC 562: తుది వినియోగదారు పట్ల తయారీదారు శ్రద్ధ బాధ్యత.

selfTest.q: ఉత్పత్తి బాధ్యతను నిర్వచించండి. ఉత్పత్తి బాధ్యత దావాను ఎవరిపై వేయవచ్చు?
selfTest.a: తయారీదారు బాధ్యతకు ఐదు కారణాలు రాయండి. తాను నిర్లక్ష్యంగా లేనని నిరూపించి తయారీదారు బాధ్యత నుండి తప్పించుకోగలడా? తయారీదారు కాని ఉత్పత్తి విక్రేత ఎప్పుడు బాధ్యుడు? "హాని" నుండి ఏ నష్టాలు మినహాయించబడ్డాయి? హెచ్చరిక కేసుల్లో తయారీదారుకు ఉన్న నాలుగు మినహాయింపులు చెప్పండి. Donoghue v. Stevenson ఏమి నిర్ణయించింది?

(b) డిజైన్ లోపం డిజైనే అసురక్షితం కేసింగ్ ఎప్పుడూ ప్రమాదకరంగా వేడెక్కే హీటర్ మోడల్
(c) తయారీ నిర్దేశాల నుండి విచలనం చెప్పిన నిర్దేశం ప్రకారం తయారు కాలేదు నిర్దేశం కంటే సన్నని హెల్మెట్ షెల్

hi.inOneMinute: Product liability is "the responsibility of a product manufacturer or product seller, of any product or service, to compensate for any harm caused to a consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services relating thereto" (CPA 2019, s. 2(34)). Chapter VI (ss. 82 to 87) is new in the 2019 Act. A product liability action is a complaint before a District, State or National Commission "for claiming compensation for the harm caused to him" (s. 2(35)). It may be brought against three persons (s. 83) (See Diagram 1 ): Product manufacturer (s. 84): liable for a manufacturing defect, a design defect, deviation from manufacturing specifications, non-conformity with an express warranty , or lack of adequate instructions or warnings. Liable "even if he proves that he was not negligent or fraudulent in making the express warranty" (s. 84(2)). Product service provider (s. 85): liable for faulty or deficient service, act of omission or commission or negligence or conscious withholding of information causing harm, inadequate instructions or warnings, or non-conformity with express warranty or contract. Product seller (s. 86): a seller who is not the manufacturer is liable only in five situations – substantial control over design or manufacture, alteration that substantially caused the harm, his own express warranty, manufacturer unknown or beyond reach, or failure of reasonable care or to pass on warnings (See Diagram 2 ). Harm (s. 2(22)) covers damage to other property, personal injury, illness or death, mental agony attendant on these, and loss of consortium or services – but not harm to the product itself, breach of warranty damage, or "any commercial or economic loss". Exceptions (s. 87): no action against a seller if the product was misused, altered or modified; four situations where the manufacturer is not liable for failure to warn; no duty to warn about an obvious or commonly known danger (See Diagram 3 ). Common law background: Donoghue v. Stevenson [1932] AC 562 – a manufacturer owes a duty of reasonable care to the ultimate consumer. The 2019 Act goes further by not requiring proof of negligence for the listed defects.
legalProvision: Consumer Protection Act, 2019

s. 2(34) – "product liability" means "the responsibility of a product manufacturer or product seller, of any product or service, to compensate for any harm caused to a consumer by such defective product manufactured or sold or by deficiency in services relating thereto". s. 2(35) – "product liability action" means "a complaint filed by a person before a District Commission or State Commission or National Commission, as the case may be, for claiming compensation for the harm caused to him". s. 2(33) – "product" means "any article or goods or substance or raw material or any extended cycle of such product, which may be in gaseous, liquid, or solid state possessing intrinsic value which is capable of delivery either as wholly assembled or as a component part and is produced for introduction to trade or commerce, but does not include human tissues, blood, blood products and organs". s. 2(36) – "product manufacturer" means a person who "(i) makes any product or parts thereof; or (ii) assembles parts thereof made by others; or (iii) puts or causes to be put his own mark on any products made by any other person; or (iv) makes a product and sells, distributes, leases, installs, prepares, packages, labels, markets, repairs, maintains such product or is otherwise involved in placing such product for commercial purpose; or (v) designs, produces, fabricates, constructs or re-manufactures any product before its sale; or (vi) being a product seller of a product, is also a manufacturer of such product". s. 2(37) – "product seller" means a person who, "in the course of business, imports, sells, distributes, leases, installs, prepares, packages, labels, markets, repairs, maintains, or otherwise is involved in placing such product for commercial purpose", and includes a manufacturer who is also a seller and a service provider; but does not include (a) a seller of immovable property, "unless such person is engaged in the sale of constructed house or in the construction of homes or flats"; (b) a provider of professional services where the sale or use of a product "is only incidental thereto, but furnishing of opinion, skill or services being the essence of such transaction"; (c) a person who acts only in a financial capacity, is not a manufacturer, wholesaler, distributor, retailer, direct seller or electronic service provider, or leases a product without a reasonable opportunity to inspect it, where selection, possession, maintenance and operation are controlled by someone other than the lessor. s. 2(38) – "product service provider", in relation to a product, means "a person who provides any service in respect of such product". s. 2(10) – "defect" means "any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard which is required to be maintained by or under any law for the time being in force or under any contract, express or implied or as is claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever in relation to any goods or product". s. 2(12) – "design", in relation to a product, means "the intended or known physical and material characteristics of such product and includes any intended or known formulation or content of such product and the usual result of the intended manufacturing or other process used to produce such product". s. 2(22) – "harm", in relation to a product liability, includes "(i) damage to any property, other than the product itself; (ii) personal injury, illness or death; (iii) mental agony or emotional distress attendant to personal injury or illness or damage to property; or (iv) any loss of consortium or services or other loss resulting from a harm referred to in sub-clause (i) or sub-clause (ii) or sub-clause (iii), but shall not include any harm caused to a product itself or any damage to the property on account of breach of warranty conditions or any commercial or economic loss, including any direct, incidental or consequential loss relating thereto". s. 2(6)(vii) – a "complaint" includes an allegation that "a claim for product liability action lies against the product manufacturer, product seller or product service provider, as the case may be". s. 82 – "This Chapter shall apply to every claim for compensation under a product liability action by a complainant for any harm caused by a defective product manufactured by a product manufacturer or serviced by a product service provider or sold by a product seller." s. 83 – "A product liability action may be brought by a complainant against a product manufacturer or a product service provider or a product seller, as the case may be, for any harm caused to him on account of a defective product." s. 84(1) – "A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) the product contains a manufacturing defect; or (b) the product is defective in design; or (c) there is a deviation from manufacturing specifications; or (d) the product does not conform to the express warranty; or (e) the product fails to contain adequate instructions of correct usage to prevent any harm or any warning regarding improper or incorrect usage." s. 84(2) – "A product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action even if he proves that he was not negligent or fraudulent in making the express warranty of a product." s. 85 – "A product service provider shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) the service provided by him was faulty or imperfect or deficient or inadequate in quality, nature or manner of performance which is required to be provided by or under any law for the time being in force, or pursuant to any contract or otherwise; or (b) there was an act of omission or commission or negligence or conscious withholding any information which caused harm; or (c) the service provider did not issue adequate instructions or warnings to prevent any harm; or (d) the service did not conform to express warranty or the terms and conditions of the contract." s. 86 – "A product seller who is not a product manufacturer shall be liable in a product liability action, if— (a) he has exercised substantial control over the designing, testing, manufacturing, packaging or labelling of a product that caused harm; or (b) he has altered or modified the product and such alteration or modification was the substantial factor in causing the harm; or (c) he has made an express warranty of a product independent of any express warranty made by a manufacturer and such product failed to conform to the express warranty made by the product seller which caused the harm; or (d) the product has been sold by him and the identity of product manufacturer of such product is not known, or if known, the service of notice or process or warrant cannot be effected on him or he is not subject to the law which is in force in India or the order, if any, passed or to be passed cannot be enforced against him; or (e) he failed to exercise reasonable care in assembling, inspecting or maintaining such product or he did not pass on the warnings or instructions of the product manufacturer regarding the dangers involved or proper usage of the product while selling such product and such failure was the proximate cause of the harm." s. 87(1) – "A product liability action cannot be brought against the product seller if, at the time of harm, the product was misused, altered, or modified." s. 87(2) – in an action based on failure to provide adequate warnings or instructions, the manufacturer is not liable if "(a) the product was purchased by an employer for use at the workplace and the product manufacturer had provided warnings or instructions to such employer; (b) the product was sold as a component or material to be used in another product and necessary warnings or instructions were given by the product manufacturer to the purchaser of such component or material, but the harm was caused to the complainant by use of the end product in which such component or material was used; (c) the product was one which was legally meant to be used or dispensed only by or under the supervision of an expert or a class of experts and the product manufacturer had employed reasonable means to give the warnings or instructions for usage of such product to such expert or class of experts; or (d) the complainant, while using such product, was under the influence of alcohol or any prescription drug which had not been prescribed by a medical practitioner". s. 87(3) – "A product manufacturer shall not be liable for failure to instruct or warn about a danger which is obvious or commonly known to the user or consumer of such product or which, such user or consumer, ought to have known, taking into account the characteristics of such product." s. 39(1)(e) – the Commission may order the opposite party "to pay such amount as may be awarded by it as compensation in a product liability action under Chapter VI". s. 90 – separate criminal liability for manufacturing, selling or importing products containing an adulterant (see the topic "Civil & Criminal liability").
hi.meaning: Product liability – the duty of a manufacturer, service provider or seller to compensate for harm caused by a defective product or by deficient service relating to it (s. 2(34)). Product liability action – the complaint by which that compensation is claimed before a Consumer Commission (s. 2(35)). Product – any article, goods, substance or raw material with intrinsic value, produced for trade, whole or as a component; excludes human tissues, blood, blood products and organs (s. 2(33)). Manufacturing defect – the particular item departs from what the manufacturer intended (for example, a crack in one bottle). Compare design defect – the intended "physical and material characteristics" (s. 2(12)) are themselves unsafe, so every item is defective. Express warranty – a definite promise made about the product's quality, performance or condition (for example, "waterproof up to 50 metres"). The Act does not define the term; this is its ordinary meaning. Harm – the losses listed in s. 2(22). Pure economic loss and loss of the product itself are excluded.
keyPoints: s. 2(34): product liability; s. 2(35): action before a Commission. s. 83: action against manufacturer, service provider, seller. s. 84(1): five grounds; s. 84(2): no negligence defence. s. 85: four grounds for service provider. s. 86: seller liable only in five cases. s. 2(22): harm – injury, death, other property, mental agony, consortium; not product itself or economic loss. s. 2(33): blood, tissues, organs excluded. s. 87(1): misuse/alteration protects seller; s. 87(2): four warning exceptions; s. 87(3): obvious danger. Donoghue v. Stevenson [1932] AC 562: manufacturer's duty of care to the ultimate consumer.

caseLaws.facts: Donoghue v. Stevenson [1932] AC 562 (HL, 26 May 1932) Facts: The appellant drank ginger-beer bought for her by a friend. The opaque bottle contained the decomposed remains of a snail, which could not be seen until most of the contents had been drunk. She claimed shock and severe gastro-enteritis and sued the manufacturer, with whom she had no contract. Principle: Lord Atkin (with Lords Thankerton and Macmillan; Lords Buckmaster and Tomlin dissenting): "a manufacturer of products, which he sells in such a form as to show that he intends them to reach the ultimate consumer in the form in which they left him with no reasonable possibility of intermediate examination, and with the knowledge that the absence of reasonable care in the preparation or putting up of the products will result in an injury to the consumer's life or property, owes a duty to the consumer to take that reasonable care." Lord Macmillan added that the injured party must prove the defect and the carelessness: "Negligence must be both averred and proved." Why it matters: It is the root of manufacturers' liability to consumers without contract. The 2019 Act builds on it and removes the need to prove negligence for the manufacturer's statutory grounds (s. 84(2)). Note: No judgment interpreting Chapter VI of CPA 2019 was found among the judgments available for this note.
