law-of-torts-u5-t16.subtitle: Electronic filing of consumer complaints and the other places where the 2019 Act allows electronic means

en.inOneMinute: E-filing means filing a consumer complaint before a Consumer Commission online, by electronic means, instead of handing in a paper complaint. The legal basis (See Diagram 1 ): Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (CPA 2019), s. 35(1) proviso: "the complaint under this sub-section may be filed electronically in such manner as may be prescribed." s. 35(2): the fee is payable "in such manner, including electronic form, as may be prescribed". Information Technology Act, 2000 (IT Act): an electronic record satisfies a legal need for writing (s. 4); an electronic signature satisfies a need for signature (s. 5); filing with a Government body and payment of money may be done electronically (s. 6). Other electronic features of CPA 2019: hearing by video conferencing (s. 38(6) proviso); notices by electronic means (s. 65(1)); notice to an electronic service provider through its nodal officer (s. 65(2)); and orders to an electronic service provider to give information (s. 38(4)). The portal: According to the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, the e-Daakhil portal "was first launched on 7th September 2020 by the National Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission"; a consumer or advocate signs up with an OTP or email link, files the complaint, pays the fee and tracks the case online. In 2025 the Ministry reported the launch of e-Jagriti to "further streamline case filing, tracking, and management". E-filing is an option , not a duty ("may be filed electronically"). It does not change who may file, the limitation period, the Commission's jurisdiction or the fee.
legalProvision: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Act 35 of 2019)

s. 35(1), proviso: "Provided that the complaint under this sub-section may be filed electronically in such manner as may be prescribed." s. 35(2): "Every complaint filed under sub-section (1) shall be accompanied with such fee and payable in such manner, including electronic form, as may be prescribed." ss. 49(1), 59(1): the provisions on complaints in ss. 35 to 39 apply, with necessary modifications, to the State Commission and the National Commission. So e-filing is available at all three levels. s. 38(4): "For the purposes of sub-sections (2) and (3), the District Commission may, by order, require an electronic service provider to provide such information, documents or records, as may be specified in that order." s. 38(6): "Every complaint shall be heard by the District Commission on the basis of affidavit and documentary evidence placed on record: Provided that where an application is made for hearing or for examination of parties in person or through video conferencing, the District Commission may, on sufficient cause being shown, and after recording its reasons in writing, allow the same." s. 65(1): notices are served by registered post acknowledgment due, speed post, approved courier, "or by any other mode of transmission of documents including electronic means". s. 65(2): "the notice required by this Act may be served on an electronic service provider at the address provided by it on the electronic platform from where it provides its services as such and for this purpose, the electronic service provider shall designate a nodal officer to accept and process such notices." s. 2(17): "electronic service provider" means "a person who provides technologies or processes to enable a product seller to engage in advertising or selling goods or services to a consumer and includes any online market place or online auction sites". s. 2(7), Explanation (b): "buys any goods" and "hires or avails any services" include "offline or online transactions through electronic means or by teleshopping or direct selling or multi-level marketing".
Information Technology Act, 2000 (Act 21 of 2000)

s. 2(1)(t): "electronic record" means "data, record or data generated, image or sound stored, received or sent in an electronic form or micro film or computer generated micro fiche". s. 2(1)(ta): "electronic signature" means "authentication of any electronic record by a subscriber by means of the electronic technique specified in the Second Schedule and includes digital signature". s. 4: "Where any law provides that information or any other matter shall be in writing or in the typewritten or printed form, then, notwithstanding anything contained in such law, such requirement shall be deemed to have been satisfied if such information or matter is– (a) rendered or made available in an electronic form; and (b) accessible so as to be usable for a subsequent reference." s. 5: where a law requires a signature, the requirement is satisfied "if such information or matter is authenticated by means of electronic signature affixed in such manner as may be prescribed by the Central Government". s. 6(1): where a law provides for "(a) the filing of any form, application or any other document with any office, authority, body or agency owned or controlled by the appropriate Government in a particular manner; … (c) the receipt or payment of money in a particular manner", the requirement is satisfied if done "by means of such electronic form as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government". s. 6(2): the Government may prescribe the manner and format of electronic filing and the method of paying fees.

Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020 , rule 7(2) Table (as substituted by G.S.R. 606(E), 17 August 2023) – the fee slabs apply equally to a complaint filed electronically: "Upto Rupees Five Lakh Nil", rising to ₹7,500 "Above Rupees Ten Crore".
Consumer Protection Act, 1986 – no provision for electronic filing of complaints was found in the Act.
en.meaning: E-filing – filing of a complaint "electronically" under the proviso to s. 35(1), with the fee paid in "electronic form" (s. 35(2)). Electronic record – data, record, image or sound stored, received or sent in an electronic form (IT Act s. 2(1)(t)). An e-filed complaint and its scanned documents are electronic records. Electronic signature – authentication of an electronic record by the technique in the Second Schedule to the IT Act, including a digital signature (s. 2(1)(ta)). Video conferencing – hearing or examining parties through a live audio-video link, which the Commission may allow for sufficient cause, with reasons (s. 38(6) proviso). Electronic service provider – the online platform that enables a seller to advertise or sell, including an online marketplace (s. 2(17)); it has duties in the e-filing system because notices can be served on it (s. 65(2)) and it can be ordered to give information (s. 38(4)).
keyPoints: s. 35(1) proviso: "may be filed electronically". s. 35(2): fee "including electronic form". All three Commissions (ss. 49(1), 59(1)). IT Act s. 4 (writing), s. 5 (signature), s. 6 (filing and payment with Government bodies). Video conferencing: s. 38(6) proviso – discretionary . Electronic notices: s. 65(1); nodal officer of electronic service provider: s. 65(2). Information from electronic service provider: s. 38(4). e-Daakhil: launched 7 September 2020 by the NCDRC; OTP or email sign-up; file, pay, track. e-Jagriti: reported in 2025 to streamline filing, tracking and management. Same fee, limitation and jurisdiction as paper filing.

caseLaws.facts: This note relies on the bare text of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the Information Technology Act, 2000, the 2020 Rules (as amended in 2023) and the Ministry of Consumer Affairs' official releases.

te.inOneMinute: ఇ-ఫైలింగ్ అంటే వినియోగదారుల కమిషన్ ముందు కాగితపు ఫిర్యాదు ఇవ్వడానికి బదులు, ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ పద్ధతిలో ఆన్‌లైన్‌లో ఫిర్యాదు దాఖలు చేయడం. చట్టపరమైన ఆధారం ( చిత్రం 1 చూడండి): వినియోగదారుల రక్షణ చట్టం, 2019 (CPA 2019), సెక్షన్ 35(1) నిబంధన: "the complaint under this sub-section may be filed electronically in such manner as may be prescribed." (అర్థం: ఈ ఉప-సెక్షన్ కింద ఫిర్యాదును నిర్దేశించిన పద్ధతిలో ఎలక్ట్రానిక్‌గా దాఖలు చేయవచ్చు). సెక్షన్ 35(2): రుసుము "in such manner, including electronic form, as may be prescribed" (అర్థం: ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ రూపంతో సహా నిర్దేశించిన పద్ధతిలో) చెల్లించాలి. సమాచార సాంకేతిక చట్టం, 2000 (IT చట్టం): ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ రికార్డు లిఖిత అవసరాన్ని తీరుస్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 4); ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ సంతకం సంతకం అవసరాన్ని తీరుస్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 5); ప్రభుత్వ సంస్థతో దాఖలు, డబ్బు చెల్లింపు ఎలక్ట్రానిక్‌గా చేయవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 6). CPA 2019లో ఇతర ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ అంశాలు: వీడియో కాన్ఫరెన్సింగ్ ద్వారా విచారణ (సెక్షన్ 38(6) నిబంధన); ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ పద్ధతుల్లో నోటీసులు (సెక్షన్ 65(1)); ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ సేవా ప్రదాతకు దాని నోడల్ అధికారి ద్వారా నోటీసు (సెక్షన్ 65(2)); సమాచారం ఇవ్వమని ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ సేవా ప్రదాతకు ఆదేశాలు (సెక్షన్ 38(4)). పోర్టల్: వినియోగదారుల వ్యవహారాల మంత్రిత్వ శాఖ ప్రకారం, e-Daakhil పోర్టల్ "was first launched on 7th September 2020 by the National Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission" (అర్థం: 7 సెప్టెంబర్ 2020న జాతీయ వినియోగదారుల వివాదాల పరిష్కార కమిషన్ మొదట ప్రారంభించింది); వినియోగదారుడు లేదా న్యాయవాది OTP లేదా ఇమెయిల్ లింక్‌తో నమోదు చేసుకుని, ఫిర్యాదు దాఖలు చేసి, రుసుము చెల్లించి, కేసును ఆన్‌లైన్‌లో ట్రాక్ చేయవచ్చు. 2025లో మంత్రిత్వ శాఖ e-Jagriti ప్రారంభాన్ని తెలిపింది, అది "further streamline case filing, tracking, and management" (అర్థం: కేసు దాఖలు, ట్రాకింగ్, నిర్వహణను మరింత సులభతరం చేస్తుంది). ఇ-ఫైలింగ్ ఒక ఐచ్ఛికం , బాధ్యత కాదు ("may be filed electronically" (అర్థం: ఎలక్ట్రానిక్‌గా దాఖలు చేయవచ్చు)). ఎవరు దాఖలు చేయవచ్చు, కాల పరిమితి, కమిషన్ అధికార పరిధి, రుసుము – వీటిలో ఏదీ మారదు.
te.meaning: ఇ-ఫైలింగ్ – సెక్షన్ 35(1) నిబంధన కింద ఫిర్యాదును "electronically" (అర్థం: ఎలక్ట్రానిక్‌గా) దాఖలు చేయడం, రుసుమును "electronic form" (అర్థం: ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ రూపం)లో చెల్లించడం (సెక్షన్ 35(2)). ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ రికార్డు – ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ రూపంలో నిల్వ చేసిన, స్వీకరించిన లేదా పంపిన డేటా, రికార్డు, చిత్రం లేదా శబ్దం (IT చట్టం సెక్షన్ 2(1)(t)). ఇ-ఫైల్ చేసిన ఫిర్యాదు, దాని స్కాన్ చేసిన పత్రాలు ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ రికార్డులు. ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ సంతకం – IT చట్టం రెండో షెడ్యూల్‌లోని పద్ధతి ద్వారా ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ రికార్డును ప్రామాణీకరించడం, డిజిటల్ సంతకంతో సహా (సెక్షన్ 2(1)(ta)). వీడియో కాన్ఫరెన్సింగ్ – ప్రత్యక్ష ఆడియో-వీడియో లింక్ ద్వారా పక్షాలను విచారించడం లేదా పరిశీలించడం; తగిన కారణంతో, కారణాలు నమోదు చేసి కమిషన్ అనుమతించవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 38(6) నిబంధన). ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ సేవా ప్రదాత – అమ్మకందారు ప్రకటించడానికి లేదా అమ్మడానికి వీలు కల్పించే ఆన్‌లైన్ ప్లాట్‌ఫామ్, ఆన్‌లైన్ మార్కెట్ ప్లేస్‌తో సహా (సెక్షన్ 2(17)); దానిపై నోటీసులు జారీ చేయవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 65(2)), సమాచారం ఇవ్వమని ఆదేశించవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 38(4)) కాబట్టి ఇ-ఫైలింగ్ వ్యవస్థలో దానికి బాధ్యతలు ఉన్నాయి.
keyPoints: సెక్షన్ 35(1) నిబంధన: "may be filed electronically" (అర్థం: ఎలక్ట్రానిక్‌గా దాఖలు చేయవచ్చు). సెక్షన్ 35(2): రుసుము "including electronic form" (అర్థం: ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ రూపంతో సహా). మూడు కమిషన్లూ (సెక్షన్లు 49(1), 59(1)). IT చట్టం సెక్షన్ 4 (లిఖితం), సెక్షన్ 5 (సంతకం), సెక్షన్ 6 (ప్రభుత్వ సంస్థలతో దాఖలు, చెల్లింపు). వీడియో కాన్ఫరెన్సింగ్: సెక్షన్ 38(6) నిబంధన – విచక్షణాధికారం. ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ నోటీసులు: సెక్షన్ 65(1); ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ సేవా ప్రదాత నోడల్ అధికారి: సెక్షన్ 65(2). ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ సేవా ప్రదాత నుండి సమాచారం: సెక్షన్ 38(4). e-Daakhil: 7 సెప్టెంబర్ 2020న NCDRC ప్రారంభించింది; OTP లేదా ఇమెయిల్ నమోదు; దాఖలు, చెల్లింపు, ట్రాకింగ్. e-Jagriti: దాఖలు, ట్రాకింగ్, నిర్వహణను సులభతరం చేయడానికి 2025లో తెలియజేయబడింది. కాగితపు దాఖలు లాగే రుసుము, కాల పరిమితి, అధికార పరిధి.

selfTest.q: వినియోగదారుల ఫిర్యాదును ఎలక్ట్రానిక్‌గా దాఖలు చేయడానికి ఏ నిబంధన అనుమతిస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: ఇ-ఫైలింగ్ తప్పనిసరా? ఎలక్ట్రానిక్ ఫిర్యాదును "లిఖిత" ఫిర్యాదుగా చేసే IT చట్టం నిబంధన ఏది? e-Daakhil పోర్టల్‌ను మొదట ఎప్పుడు, ఎవరు ప్రారంభించారు? చెల్లించిన విలువ ₹4 లక్షలు ఉన్న ఇ-ఫైల్ ఫిర్యాదుకు రుసుము ఎంత? వీడియో కాన్ఫరెన్సింగ్ విచారణను పక్షం హక్కుగా కోరగలదా? ఆన్‌లైన్ మార్కెట్ ప్లేస్‌కు నోటీసు ఎలా జారీ చేయవచ్చు?

hi.inOneMinute: E-filing means filing a consumer complaint before a Consumer Commission online, by electronic means, instead of handing in a paper complaint. The legal basis (See Diagram 1 ): Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (CPA 2019), s. 35(1) proviso: "the complaint under this sub-section may be filed electronically in such manner as may be prescribed." s. 35(2): the fee is payable "in such manner, including electronic form, as may be prescribed". Information Technology Act, 2000 (IT Act): an electronic record satisfies a legal need for writing (s. 4); an electronic signature satisfies a need for signature (s. 5); filing with a Government body and payment of money may be done electronically (s. 6). Other electronic features of CPA 2019: hearing by video conferencing (s. 38(6) proviso); notices by electronic means (s. 65(1)); notice to an electronic service provider through its nodal officer (s. 65(2)); and orders to an electronic service provider to give information (s. 38(4)). The portal: According to the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, the e-Daakhil portal "was first launched on 7th September 2020 by the National Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission"; a consumer or advocate signs up with an OTP or email link, files the complaint, pays the fee and tracks the case online. In 2025 the Ministry reported the launch of e-Jagriti to "further streamline case filing, tracking, and management". E-filing is an option , not a duty ("may be filed electronically"). It does not change who may file, the limitation period, the Commission's jurisdiction or the fee.
legalProvision: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Act 35 of 2019)

s. 35(1), proviso: "Provided that the complaint under this sub-section may be filed electronically in such manner as may be prescribed." s. 35(2): "Every complaint filed under sub-section (1) shall be accompanied with such fee and payable in such manner, including electronic form, as may be prescribed." ss. 49(1), 59(1): the provisions on complaints in ss. 35 to 39 apply, with necessary modifications, to the State Commission and the National Commission. So e-filing is available at all three levels. s. 38(4): "For the purposes of sub-sections (2) and (3), the District Commission may, by order, require an electronic service provider to provide such information, documents or records, as may be specified in that order." s. 38(6): "Every complaint shall be heard by the District Commission on the basis of affidavit and documentary evidence placed on record: Provided that where an application is made for hearing or for examination of parties in person or through video conferencing, the District Commission may, on sufficient cause being shown, and after recording its reasons in writing, allow the same." s. 65(1): notices are served by registered post acknowledgment due, speed post, approved courier, "or by any other mode of transmission of documents including electronic means". s. 65(2): "the notice required by this Act may be served on an electronic service provider at the address provided by it on the electronic platform from where it provides its services as such and for this purpose, the electronic service provider shall designate a nodal officer to accept and process such notices." s. 2(17): "electronic service provider" means "a person who provides technologies or processes to enable a product seller to engage in advertising or selling goods or services to a consumer and includes any online market place or online auction sites". s. 2(7), Explanation (b): "buys any goods" and "hires or avails any services" include "offline or online transactions through electronic means or by teleshopping or direct selling or multi-level marketing".
Information Technology Act, 2000 (Act 21 of 2000)

s. 2(1)(t): "electronic record" means "data, record or data generated, image or sound stored, received or sent in an electronic form or micro film or computer generated micro fiche". s. 2(1)(ta): "electronic signature" means "authentication of any electronic record by a subscriber by means of the electronic technique specified in the Second Schedule and includes digital signature". s. 4: "Where any law provides that information or any other matter shall be in writing or in the typewritten or printed form, then, notwithstanding anything contained in such law, such requirement shall be deemed to have been satisfied if such information or matter is– (a) rendered or made available in an electronic form; and (b) accessible so as to be usable for a subsequent reference." s. 5: where a law requires a signature, the requirement is satisfied "if such information or matter is authenticated by means of electronic signature affixed in such manner as may be prescribed by the Central Government". s. 6(1): where a law provides for "(a) the filing of any form, application or any other document with any office, authority, body or agency owned or controlled by the appropriate Government in a particular manner; … (c) the receipt or payment of money in a particular manner", the requirement is satisfied if done "by means of such electronic form as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government". s. 6(2): the Government may prescribe the manner and format of electronic filing and the method of paying fees.

Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) Rules, 2020 , rule 7(2) Table (as substituted by G.S.R. 606(E), 17 August 2023) – the fee slabs apply equally to a complaint filed electronically: "Upto Rupees Five Lakh Nil", rising to ₹7,500 "Above Rupees Ten Crore".
Consumer Protection Act, 1986 – no provision for electronic filing of complaints was found in the Act.
hi.meaning: E-filing – filing of a complaint "electronically" under the proviso to s. 35(1), with the fee paid in "electronic form" (s. 35(2)). Electronic record – data, record, image or sound stored, received or sent in an electronic form (IT Act s. 2(1)(t)). An e-filed complaint and its scanned documents are electronic records. Electronic signature – authentication of an electronic record by the technique in the Second Schedule to the IT Act, including a digital signature (s. 2(1)(ta)). Video conferencing – hearing or examining parties through a live audio-video link, which the Commission may allow for sufficient cause, with reasons (s. 38(6) proviso). Electronic service provider – the online platform that enables a seller to advertise or sell, including an online marketplace (s. 2(17)); it has duties in the e-filing system because notices can be served on it (s. 65(2)) and it can be ordered to give information (s. 38(4)).
keyPoints: s. 35(1) proviso: "may be filed electronically". s. 35(2): fee "including electronic form". All three Commissions (ss. 49(1), 59(1)). IT Act s. 4 (writing), s. 5 (signature), s. 6 (filing and payment with Government bodies). Video conferencing: s. 38(6) proviso – discretionary . Electronic notices: s. 65(1); nodal officer of electronic service provider: s. 65(2). Information from electronic service provider: s. 38(4). e-Daakhil: launched 7 September 2020 by the NCDRC; OTP or email sign-up; file, pay, track. e-Jagriti: reported in 2025 to streamline filing, tracking and management. Same fee, limitation and jurisdiction as paper filing.

law-of-torts-u5-t21.subtitle: Chapter V of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019: the mediation cell, the panel of mediators, their duties and how a settlement becomes an order

en.inOneMinute: Mediation is "the process by which a mediator mediates the consumer disputes" (CPA 2019, s. 2(25)). The Act provides for it in s. 37 (reference) and Chapter V, ss. 74 to 81. Reference (s. 37): at the first hearing after admission, or later, if the District Commission sees "elements of a settlement", it may ask the parties to consent in writing within five days; on consent, it refers the matter within five days. The State and National Commissions follow the same provisions (ss. 49(1), 59(1)). Certain cases cannot be referred (Mediation Rules 2020, r. 4) (See Diagram 1 ). Consumer mediation cell (s. 74): attached to every District and State Commission (set up by the State Government) and to the National Commission and its regional Benches (set up by the Central Government). Empanelment (s. 75): each Commission prepares a panel of mediators on the recommendation of a selection committee of "the President and a member of that Commission"; the panel is valid for five years , with re-empanelment possible. Eligibility, disqualifications, fee, training and code of conduct are in the Mediation Regulations 2020 (See Diagram 2 ). Appointment (s. 76): the Commission nominates a mediator from the panel, considering "his suitability for resolving the consumer dispute involved"; it replaces him if needed (s. 78). Duties (ss. 77, 79): disclose any interest or circumstance that may raise "a justifiable doubt as to his independence or impartiality"; be guided by "the principles of natural justice"; have regard to the parties' rights and obligations and usages of trade; keep confidentiality; never impose a settlement (Regulations 10 to 13). Settlement (ss. 80, 81): agreement in writing signed by the parties; mediator's settlement report to the Commission; the Commission records the settlement by order within seven days ; partial settlement – the rest is heard; no settlement – the whole is heard. No appeal lies from an order recording a settlement (s. 41, third proviso) (See Diagram 3 ).
legalProvision: Consumer Protection Act, 2019

s. 2(25) – "mediation" means "the process by which a mediator mediates the consumer disputes"; s. 2(26) – "mediator" means "a mediator referred to in section 75". s. 37(1) – "At the first hearing of the complaint after its admission, or at any later stage, if it appears to the District Commission that there exists elements of a settlement which may be acceptable to the parties, except in such cases as may be prescribed, it may direct the parties to give in writing, within five days, consent to have their dispute settled by mediation in accordance with the provisions of Chapter V." s. 37(2) – "Where the parties agree for settlement by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission shall, within five days of receipt of such consent, refer the matter for mediation, and in such case, the provisions of Chapter V, relating to mediation, shall apply." s. 38(1) – the District Commission proceeds with the complaint on admission, "or in respect of cases referred for mediation on failure of settlement by mediation". ss. 49(1), 59(1) – the provisions relating to complaints under ss. 35 to 39 apply, with necessary modifications, to the State Commission and the National Commission. s. 74(1) – "The State Government shall establish, by notification, a consumer mediation cell to be attached to each of the District Commissions and the State Commissions of that State." s. 74(2) – "The Central Government shall establish, by notification, a consumer mediation cell to be attached to the National Commission and each of the regional Benches." s. 74(3) – it "shall consist of such persons as may be prescribed". s. 74(4) – every cell shall maintain "(a) a list of empanelled mediators; (b) a list of cases handled by the cell; (c) record of proceeding; and (d) any other information as may be specified by regulations". s. 74(5) – a "quarterly report" to the Commission to which it is attached. s. 75(1) – "For the purpose of mediation, the National Commission or the State Commission or the District Commission, as the case may be, shall prepare a panel of the mediators to be maintained by the consumer mediation cell attached to it, on the recommendation of a selection committee consisting of the President and a member of that Commission." s. 75(2) – qualifications and experience, procedure for empanelment, training, fee, terms and conditions, code of conduct, and grounds and manner of removal "shall be such as may be specified by regulations". s. 75(3) – "The panel of mediators prepared under sub-section (1) shall be valid for a period of five years, and the empanelled mediators shall be eligible to be considered for re-empanelment for another term, subject to such conditions as may be specified by regulations." s. 76 – "The District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission shall, while nominating any person from the panel of mediators referred to in section 75, consider his suitability for resolving the consumer dispute involved." s. 77 – "It shall be the duty of the mediator to disclose— (a) any personal, professional or financial interest in the outcome of the consumer dispute; (b) the circumstances which may give rise to a justifiable doubt as to his independence or impartiality; and (c) such other facts as may be specified by regulations." s. 78 – where the Commission "is satisfied, on the information furnished by the mediator or on the information received from any other person including parties to the complaint and after hearing the mediator, it shall replace such mediator by another mediator". s. 79(1) – mediation "shall be held in the consumer mediation cell attached to" the Commission. s. 79(2) – the mediator "shall have regard to the rights and obligations of the parties, the usages of trade, if any, the circumstances giving rise to the consumer dispute and such other relevant factors, as he may deem necessary and shall be guided by the principles of natural justice while carrying out mediation". s. 79(3) – time and manner as specified by regulations. s. 80(1) – "Pursuant to mediation, if an agreement is reached between the parties with respect to all of the issues involved in the consumer dispute or with respect to only some of the issues, the terms of such agreement shall be reduced to writing accordingly, and signed by the parties to such dispute or their authorised representatives." s. 80(2) – "The mediator shall prepare a settlement report of the settlement and forward the signed agreement along with such report to the concerned Commission." s. 80(3) – if no agreement is reached "within the specified time" or settlement is not possible, the mediator reports accordingly. s. 81(1) – the Commission "shall, within seven days of the receipt of the settlement report, pass suitable order recording such settlement of consumer dispute and dispose of the matter accordingly". s. 81(2) – partial settlement: record the settled issues and "continue to hear other issues". s. 81(3) – no settlement: "continue to hear all the issues". s. 41, third proviso – "no appeal shall lie from any order passed under sub-section (1) of section 81 by the District Commission pursuant to a settlement by mediation under section 80".
Consumer Protection (Mediation) Rules, 2020 (G.S.R. 450(E), 15 July 2020; in force 20 July 2020)

r. 3 – each mediation cell has a panel recommended by the selection committee (President and a member); support staff as decided by the President in consultation with the Government. r. 4 – matters not to be referred: "(a) the matters relating to proceedings in respect of medical negligence resulting in grievous injury or death; (b) matters which relate to defaults or offences for which applications for compounding of offences have been made by one or more parties; (c) cases involving serious and specific allegations of fraud, fabrication of documents, forgery, impersonation, coercion; (d) cases relating to prosecution for criminal and non-compoundable offences; (e) cases which involve public interest or the interest of numerous persons who are not parties before the Commission". Proviso: in other cases the Commission "may choose not to refer" if no elements of settlement exist or mediation is otherwise not appropriate. r. 5 – if a settlement is reached, "the complainant shall be entitled to receive full amount of application fee paid". r. 6 – the parties "shall not initiate any arbitral or judicial proceedings in respect of a matter which is the subject-matter of the mediation". r. 7 – "A settlement agreement shall not be discharged by the death of any party thereto and shall be enforceable by or against the legal representative of the deceased party."
Consumer Protection (Mediation) Regulations, 2020 (made by the National Commission under s. 103; published 24 July 2020)

reg. 3 – eligible for empanelment: retired Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts; retired Members of a Consumer Commission; retired District and Sessions Judges, Additional District and Sessions Judges or other retired Members of the Higher Judicial Services; retired judicial officers with not less than ten years' experience; "an advocate with a minimum experience of ten years at Bar"; mediators empanelled with the Mediation Cell of the Supreme Court, a High Court or a District Court; "a person having experience of at least five years in mediation or conciliation"; "experts or other professionals with at least fifteen years' experience or retired senior bureaucrats or retired executives". reg. 4(1) – disqualified: an adjudged insolvent; a person facing pending criminal charges involving moral turpitude; a person convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude; a person against whom disciplinary proceedings are pending or have resulted in punishment. reg. 4(2) – a person interested in or connected with the subject-matter, or connected with any party, is disqualified from being nominated in that case. reg. 5 – applications invited by notice in at least one English and one vernacular newspaper; scrutiny; selection committee recommends a panel on "suitability, integrity as well as relevant experience"; size of panel fixed by the President; consent of the person needed; "The Mediation Cell shall be headed by the President of the Consumer Commission." reg. 6 – removal from panel for disqualification, misconduct or unsuitability, "after giving an opportunity of hearing". reg. 7 – re-empanelment only of those who "successfully and efficiently discharged their functions", on the selection committee's recommendation. reg. 8 – consolidated fee fixed case-wise by the President; half the fee in an unsuccessful mediation; "shared equally by the two sets of parties"; deposited in advance; if a party defaults, the Commission may let the other party deposit and recover it like a money decree, or terminate the mediation. reg. 9 – training is "obligatory". reg. 10 – no private communication with parties or counsel; no gifts or hospitality; disclosure, before commencement, of any past or present relationship with the parties and any circumstance raising "reasonable doubt as to his independence and impartiality". reg. 11 – mediation in the presence of the parties or their representatives; terminates on expiry of three months from the first appearance before the mediator, unless extended by the Commission; mediator guided by "the principles of natural justice and fair play" but not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure or the Indian Evidence Act; the Commission may direct a non-participating party to participate; record signed on every date; agreement sent to the Commission "in a sealed cover"; if no agreement, the mediator informs the Commission "without in any manner disclosing" what happened. reg. 12 – the mediator "shall attempt to facilitate a voluntary resolution ... but shall not impose any term or any settlement upon the parties"; must explain the terms before signatures. reg. 13 – confidentiality; "There shall be no audio or video recording of the mediation proceedings." reg. 14 – the mediator communicates with the Commission only by his report, with copies to all parties. reg. 15 – immunity for acts done bona fide; the mediator "shall not be summoned by a party to appear in a Court or other forum, to testify". reg. 16 – quarterly report of the cell, within one month of the end of each quarter.

Mediation Act, 2023 – Tenth Schedule (s. 65): omits clauses (25) and (26) of s. 2 and Chapter V of CPA 2019, and substitutes s. 37 by new ss. 37, 37A and 37B, under which a Commission "may at any stage of proceedings refer the disputes for settlement by mediation under the Mediation Act, 2023". The commencement note in the Act text used for this note shows only ss. 1, 3, 26, 31 to 38, 45 to 47, 50 to 54 and 56 to 57 brought into force (9 October 2023); s. 65 is not among them. The CPA text used still contains Chapter V.
en.meaning: Mediation – a process in which a neutral person, the mediator, helps the parties to a consumer dispute reach their own settlement (s. 2(25); reg. 12). Mediator – a person on the panel prepared under s. 75 (s. 2(26)). Consumer mediation cell – the unit attached to a Commission where mediation is held and the panel and records are kept (ss. 74, 79(1)). It is headed by the President of that Commission (reg. 5(6)). Empanelment – inclusion of a person in the panel of mediators of a Commission, on the selection committee's recommendation (s. 75(1)). Nomination – the Commission's choice of a particular empanelled mediator for a particular dispute (s. 76). Settlement report – the mediator's report of the settlement, sent with the signed agreement to the Commission (s. 80(2)). Settlement – "a settlement arrived at in the course of a mediation proceeding in respect of all or some of the issues involved in a consumer dispute pending before a Consumer Commission" (reg. 2(1)(g)).
keyPoints: s. 2(25): mediation; s. 2(26): mediator. s. 37: reference at first hearing or later; consent in five days; reference in five days. r. 4: five classes not to be referred. s. 74: cells – State Govt for District and State; Central Govt for National and regional Benches. s. 75: panel by Commission on recommendation of President + member; five years. reg. 3: nine eligible classes; reg. 4: disqualifications. s. 76: nomination by suitability; s. 78: replacement after hearing. s. 77: disclosure; s. 79: natural justice, usages of trade. reg. 11(2): three months; reg. 12: no imposed settlement; reg. 13: confidentiality. s. 80: written, signed agreement and settlement report; s. 81: order in seven days. s. 41: no appeal from settlement order; r. 5: full fee refund.

te.inOneMinute: మధ్యవర్తిత్వం అంటే "the process by which a mediator mediates the consumer disputes" (అర్థం: మధ్యవర్తి వినియోగదారుల వివాదాలలో మధ్యవర్తిత్వం చేసే ప్రక్రియ) (CPA 2019, సెక్షన్ 2(25)). చట్టం దీనిని సెక్షన్ 37 (పంపడం), అధ్యాయం V, సెక్షన్లు 74 నుండి 81లో అందిస్తుంది. పంపడం (సెక్షన్ 37): స్వీకరణ తర్వాత మొదటి విచారణలో, లేదా తర్వాత, జిల్లా కమిషన్‌కు "elements of a settlement" (అర్థం: పరిష్కార అంశాలు) కనిపిస్తే, ఐదు రోజుల్లో రాతపూర్వక అంగీకారం ఇవ్వమని పక్షాలను కోరవచ్చు; అంగీకారం వస్తే ఐదు రోజుల్లో పంపుతుంది. రాష్ట్ర, జాతీయ కమిషన్లు కూడా ఇవే నిబంధనలు పాటిస్తాయి (సెక్షన్లు 49(1), 59(1)). కొన్ని కేసులను పంపలేరు (మధ్యవర్తిత్వ నియమాలు 2020, నియమం 4) ( చిత్రం 1 చూడండి). వినియోగదారుల మధ్యవర్తిత్వ విభాగం (సెక్షన్ 74): ప్రతి జిల్లా, రాష్ట్ర కమిషన్‌కు (రాష్ట్ర ప్రభుత్వం ఏర్పాటు చేస్తుంది), జాతీయ కమిషన్‌కు, దాని ప్రాంతీయ బెంచ్‌లకు (కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వం ఏర్పాటు చేస్తుంది) జతచేయబడి ఉంటుంది. ప్యానెల్‌లో చేర్పు (సెక్షన్ 75): "the President and a member of that Commission" (అర్థం: ఆ కమిషన్ ప్రెసిడెంట్, ఒక సభ్యుడు) తో కూడిన ఎంపిక కమిటీ సిఫార్సుపై ప్రతి కమిషన్ మధ్యవర్తుల ప్యానెల్ తయారు చేస్తుంది; ప్యానెల్ ఐదు సంవత్సరాలు చెల్లుతుంది, మళ్లీ చేర్పు సాధ్యం. అర్హత, అనర్హతలు, ఫీజు, శిక్షణ, ప్రవర్తనా నియమావళి మధ్యవర్తిత్వ నిబంధనలు 2020లో ఉన్నాయి ( చిత్రం 2 చూడండి). నియామకం (సెక్షన్ 76): "his suitability for resolving the consumer dispute involved" (అర్థం: సంబంధిత వినియోగదారుల వివాదాన్ని పరిష్కరించడానికి అతని అనుకూలత) పరిగణించి కమిషన్ ప్యానెల్ నుండి మధ్యవర్తిని నియమిస్తుంది; అవసరమైతే మారుస్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 78). విధులు (సెక్షన్లు 77, 79): "a justifiable doubt as to his independence or impartiality" (అర్థం: అతని స్వతంత్రత లేదా నిష్పక్షపాతంపై సహేతుకమైన సందేహం) కలిగించే ఏ ప్రయోజనాన్నైనా లేదా పరిస్థితినైనా వెల్లడించాలి; "the principles of natural justice" (అర్థం: సహజ న్యాయ సూత్రాలు) పాటించాలి; పక్షాల హక్కులు, బాధ్యతలు, వ్యాపార ఆచారాలను పరిగణించాలి; రహస్యం పాటించాలి; పరిష్కారాన్ని ఎప్పుడూ బలవంతంగా రుద్దకూడదు (నిబంధనలు 10 నుండి 13). పరిష్కారం (సెక్షన్లు 80, 81): పక్షాలు సంతకం చేసిన రాతపూర్వక ఒప్పందం; కమిషన్‌కు మధ్యవర్తి పరిష్కార నివేదిక ; కమిషన్ ఏడు రోజుల్లో ఉత్తర్వు ద్వారా పరిష్కారాన్ని నమోదు చేస్తుంది; పాక్షిక పరిష్కారం – మిగిలినది విచారిస్తారు; పరిష్కారం లేకపోతే – మొత్తం విచారిస్తారు. పరిష్కారాన్ని నమోదు చేసే ఉత్తర్వుపై అప్పీల్ లేదు (సెక్షన్ 41, మూడవ నిబంధన) ( చిత్రం 3 చూడండి).
te.meaning: మధ్యవర్తిత్వం – తటస్థ వ్యక్తి అయిన మధ్యవర్తి, వినియోగదారుల వివాద పక్షాలు తమ స్వంత పరిష్కారానికి రావడానికి సహాయం చేసే ప్రక్రియ (సెక్షన్ 2(25); నిబంధన 12). మధ్యవర్తి – సెక్షన్ 75 కింద తయారైన ప్యానెల్‌లోని వ్యక్తి (సెక్షన్ 2(26)). వినియోగదారుల మధ్యవర్తిత్వ విభాగం – మధ్యవర్తిత్వం జరిగే, ప్యానెల్, రికార్డులు నిర్వహించే, కమిషన్‌కు జతచేయబడిన విభాగం (సెక్షన్లు 74, 79(1)). దానికి ఆ కమిషన్ ప్రెసిడెంట్ అధిపతి (నిబంధన 5(6)). ప్యానెల్‌లో చేర్పు – ఎంపిక కమిటీ సిఫార్సుపై ఒక వ్యక్తిని కమిషన్ మధ్యవర్తుల ప్యానెల్‌లో చేర్చడం (సెక్షన్ 75(1)). నియామకం (Nomination) – ఒక నిర్దిష్ట వివాదానికి ప్యానెల్‌లోని ఒక నిర్దిష్ట మధ్యవర్తిని కమిషన్ ఎంచుకోవడం (సెక్షన్ 76). పరిష్కార నివేదిక – సంతకం చేసిన ఒప్పందంతో పాటు కమిషన్‌కు పంపే పరిష్కారంపై మధ్యవర్తి నివేదిక (సెక్షన్ 80(2)). పరిష్కారం (Settlement) – "a settlement arrived at in the course of a mediation proceeding in respect of all or some of the issues involved in a consumer dispute pending before a Consumer Commission" (అర్థం: వినియోగదారుల కమిషన్ ముందు పెండింగ్‌లో ఉన్న వినియోగదారుల వివాదంలోని అన్ని లేదా కొన్ని అంశాలపై మధ్యవర్తిత్వ ప్రొసీడింగ్ సమయంలో కుదిరిన పరిష్కారం) (నిబంధన 2(1)(g)).
keyPoints: సెక్షన్ 2(25): మధ్యవర్తిత్వం; సెక్షన్ 2(26): మధ్యవర్తి. సెక్షన్ 37: మొదటి విచారణలో లేదా తర్వాత పంపడం; ఐదు రోజుల్లో అంగీకారం; ఐదు రోజుల్లో పంపడం. నియమం 4: పంపకూడని ఐదు తరగతులు. సెక్షన్ 74: విభాగాలు – జిల్లా, రాష్ట్రాలకు రాష్ట్ర ప్రభుత్వం; జాతీయ, ప్రాంతీయ బెంచ్‌లకు కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వం. సెక్షన్ 75: ప్రెసిడెంట్ + సభ్యుడి సిఫార్సుపై కమిషన్ ప్యానెల్; ఐదు సంవత్సరాలు. నిబంధన 3: తొమ్మిది అర్హ తరగతులు; నిబంధన 4: అనర్హతలు. సెక్షన్ 76: అనుకూలత ఆధారంగా నియామకం; సెక్షన్ 78: విచారణ తర్వాత మార్పు. సెక్షన్ 77: వెల్లడి; సెక్షన్ 79: సహజ న్యాయం, వ్యాపార ఆచారాలు. నిబంధన 11(2): మూడు నెలలు; నిబంధన 12: బలవంతపు పరిష్కారం లేదు; నిబంధన 13: రహస్యం. సెక్షన్ 80: రాతపూర్వక, సంతకం చేసిన ఒప్పందం, పరిష్కార నివేదిక; సెక్షన్ 81: ఏడు రోజుల్లో ఉత్తర్వు. సెక్షన్ 41: పరిష్కార ఉత్తర్వుపై అప్పీల్ లేదు; నియమం 5: ఫీజు మొత్తం వాపసు.

selfTest.q: CPA 2019 కింద మధ్యవర్తిత్వాన్ని నిర్వచించండి. పక్షాలు ఎన్ని రోజుల్లో అంగీకరించాలి, కమిషన్ ఎన్ని రోజుల్లో పంపాలి?
selfTest.a: మధ్యవర్తిత్వానికి పంపలేని ఏవైనా మూడు విషయాలు చెప్పండి. ప్యానెల్ కోసం ఎంపిక కమిటీలో ఎవరు ఉంటారు, ప్యానెల్ ఎంత కాలం చెల్లుతుంది? సెక్షన్ 77 కింద మధ్యవర్తి ఏమి వెల్లడించాలి? మధ్యవర్తిత్వం ఎంత సమయంలో పూర్తి కావాలి? పరిష్కార నివేదిక అందిన ఏడు రోజుల్లో కమిషన్ ఏమి చేయాలి? మధ్యవర్తిత్వ పరిష్కారాన్ని నమోదు చేసే ఉత్తర్వుపై అప్పీల్ ఉంటుందా?

hi.inOneMinute: Mediation is "the process by which a mediator mediates the consumer disputes" (CPA 2019, s. 2(25)). The Act provides for it in s. 37 (reference) and Chapter V, ss. 74 to 81. Reference (s. 37): at the first hearing after admission, or later, if the District Commission sees "elements of a settlement", it may ask the parties to consent in writing within five days; on consent, it refers the matter within five days. The State and National Commissions follow the same provisions (ss. 49(1), 59(1)). Certain cases cannot be referred (Mediation Rules 2020, r. 4) (See Diagram 1 ). Consumer mediation cell (s. 74): attached to every District and State Commission (set up by the State Government) and to the National Commission and its regional Benches (set up by the Central Government). Empanelment (s. 75): each Commission prepares a panel of mediators on the recommendation of a selection committee of "the President and a member of that Commission"; the panel is valid for five years , with re-empanelment possible. Eligibility, disqualifications, fee, training and code of conduct are in the Mediation Regulations 2020 (See Diagram 2 ). Appointment (s. 76): the Commission nominates a mediator from the panel, considering "his suitability for resolving the consumer dispute involved"; it replaces him if needed (s. 78). Duties (ss. 77, 79): disclose any interest or circumstance that may raise "a justifiable doubt as to his independence or impartiality"; be guided by "the principles of natural justice"; have regard to the parties' rights and obligations and usages of trade; keep confidentiality; never impose a settlement (Regulations 10 to 13). Settlement (ss. 80, 81): agreement in writing signed by the parties; mediator's settlement report to the Commission; the Commission records the settlement by order within seven days ; partial settlement – the rest is heard; no settlement – the whole is heard. No appeal lies from an order recording a settlement (s. 41, third proviso) (See Diagram 3 ).
legalProvision: Consumer Protection Act, 2019

s. 2(25) – "mediation" means "the process by which a mediator mediates the consumer disputes"; s. 2(26) – "mediator" means "a mediator referred to in section 75". s. 37(1) – "At the first hearing of the complaint after its admission, or at any later stage, if it appears to the District Commission that there exists elements of a settlement which may be acceptable to the parties, except in such cases as may be prescribed, it may direct the parties to give in writing, within five days, consent to have their dispute settled by mediation in accordance with the provisions of Chapter V." s. 37(2) – "Where the parties agree for settlement by mediation and give their consent in writing, the District Commission shall, within five days of receipt of such consent, refer the matter for mediation, and in such case, the provisions of Chapter V, relating to mediation, shall apply." s. 38(1) – the District Commission proceeds with the complaint on admission, "or in respect of cases referred for mediation on failure of settlement by mediation". ss. 49(1), 59(1) – the provisions relating to complaints under ss. 35 to 39 apply, with necessary modifications, to the State Commission and the National Commission. s. 74(1) – "The State Government shall establish, by notification, a consumer mediation cell to be attached to each of the District Commissions and the State Commissions of that State." s. 74(2) – "The Central Government shall establish, by notification, a consumer mediation cell to be attached to the National Commission and each of the regional Benches." s. 74(3) – it "shall consist of such persons as may be prescribed". s. 74(4) – every cell shall maintain "(a) a list of empanelled mediators; (b) a list of cases handled by the cell; (c) record of proceeding; and (d) any other information as may be specified by regulations". s. 74(5) – a "quarterly report" to the Commission to which it is attached. s. 75(1) – "For the purpose of mediation, the National Commission or the State Commission or the District Commission, as the case may be, shall prepare a panel of the mediators to be maintained by the consumer mediation cell attached to it, on the recommendation of a selection committee consisting of the President and a member of that Commission." s. 75(2) – qualifications and experience, procedure for empanelment, training, fee, terms and conditions, code of conduct, and grounds and manner of removal "shall be such as may be specified by regulations". s. 75(3) – "The panel of mediators prepared under sub-section (1) shall be valid for a period of five years, and the empanelled mediators shall be eligible to be considered for re-empanelment for another term, subject to such conditions as may be specified by regulations." s. 76 – "The District Commission, the State Commission or the National Commission shall, while nominating any person from the panel of mediators referred to in section 75, consider his suitability for resolving the consumer dispute involved." s. 77 – "It shall be the duty of the mediator to disclose— (a) any personal, professional or financial interest in the outcome of the consumer dispute; (b) the circumstances which may give rise to a justifiable doubt as to his independence or impartiality; and (c) such other facts as may be specified by regulations." s. 78 – where the Commission "is satisfied, on the information furnished by the mediator or on the information received from any other person including parties to the complaint and after hearing the mediator, it shall replace such mediator by another mediator". s. 79(1) – mediation "shall be held in the consumer mediation cell attached to" the Commission. s. 79(2) – the mediator "shall have regard to the rights and obligations of the parties, the usages of trade, if any, the circumstances giving rise to the consumer dispute and such other relevant factors, as he may deem necessary and shall be guided by the principles of natural justice while carrying out mediation". s. 79(3) – time and manner as specified by regulations. s. 80(1) – "Pursuant to mediation, if an agreement is reached between the parties with respect to all of the issues involved in the consumer dispute or with respect to only some of the issues, the terms of such agreement shall be reduced to writing accordingly, and signed by the parties to such dispute or their authorised representatives." s. 80(2) – "The mediator shall prepare a settlement report of the settlement and forward the signed agreement along with such report to the concerned Commission." s. 80(3) – if no agreement is reached "within the specified time" or settlement is not possible, the mediator reports accordingly. s. 81(1) – the Commission "shall, within seven days of the receipt of the settlement report, pass suitable order recording such settlement of consumer dispute and dispose of the matter accordingly". s. 81(2) – partial settlement: record the settled issues and "continue to hear other issues". s. 81(3) – no settlement: "continue to hear all the issues". s. 41, third proviso – "no appeal shall lie from any order passed under sub-section (1) of section 81 by the District Commission pursuant to a settlement by mediation under section 80".
Consumer Protection (Mediation) Rules, 2020 (G.S.R. 450(E), 15 July 2020; in force 20 July 2020)

r. 3 – each mediation cell has a panel recommended by the selection committee (President and a member); support staff as decided by the President in consultation with the Government. r. 4 – matters not to be referred: "(a) the matters relating to proceedings in respect of medical negligence resulting in grievous injury or death; (b) matters which relate to defaults or offences for which applications for compounding of offences have been made by one or more parties; (c) cases involving serious and specific allegations of fraud, fabrication of documents, forgery, impersonation, coercion; (d) cases relating to prosecution for criminal and non-compoundable offences; (e) cases which involve public interest or the interest of numerous persons who are not parties before the Commission". Proviso: in other cases the Commission "may choose not to refer" if no elements of settlement exist or mediation is otherwise not appropriate. r. 5 – if a settlement is reached, "the complainant shall be entitled to receive full amount of application fee paid". r. 6 – the parties "shall not initiate any arbitral or judicial proceedings in respect of a matter which is the subject-matter of the mediation". r. 7 – "A settlement agreement shall not be discharged by the death of any party thereto and shall be enforceable by or against the legal representative of the deceased party."
Consumer Protection (Mediation) Regulations, 2020 (made by the National Commission under s. 103; published 24 July 2020)

reg. 3 – eligible for empanelment: retired Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts; retired Members of a Consumer Commission; retired District and Sessions Judges, Additional District and Sessions Judges or other retired Members of the Higher Judicial Services; retired judicial officers with not less than ten years' experience; "an advocate with a minimum experience of ten years at Bar"; mediators empanelled with the Mediation Cell of the Supreme Court, a High Court or a District Court; "a person having experience of at least five years in mediation or conciliation"; "experts or other professionals with at least fifteen years' experience or retired senior bureaucrats or retired executives". reg. 4(1) – disqualified: an adjudged insolvent; a person facing pending criminal charges involving moral turpitude; a person convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude; a person against whom disciplinary proceedings are pending or have resulted in punishment. reg. 4(2) – a person interested in or connected with the subject-matter, or connected with any party, is disqualified from being nominated in that case. reg. 5 – applications invited by notice in at least one English and one vernacular newspaper; scrutiny; selection committee recommends a panel on "suitability, integrity as well as relevant experience"; size of panel fixed by the President; consent of the person needed; "The Mediation Cell shall be headed by the President of the Consumer Commission." reg. 6 – removal from panel for disqualification, misconduct or unsuitability, "after giving an opportunity of hearing". reg. 7 – re-empanelment only of those who "successfully and efficiently discharged their functions", on the selection committee's recommendation. reg. 8 – consolidated fee fixed case-wise by the President; half the fee in an unsuccessful mediation; "shared equally by the two sets of parties"; deposited in advance; if a party defaults, the Commission may let the other party deposit and recover it like a money decree, or terminate the mediation. reg. 9 – training is "obligatory". reg. 10 – no private communication with parties or counsel; no gifts or hospitality; disclosure, before commencement, of any past or present relationship with the parties and any circumstance raising "reasonable doubt as to his independence and impartiality". reg. 11 – mediation in the presence of the parties or their representatives; terminates on expiry of three months from the first appearance before the mediator, unless extended by the Commission; mediator guided by "the principles of natural justice and fair play" but not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure or the Indian Evidence Act; the Commission may direct a non-participating party to participate; record signed on every date; agreement sent to the Commission "in a sealed cover"; if no agreement, the mediator informs the Commission "without in any manner disclosing" what happened. reg. 12 – the mediator "shall attempt to facilitate a voluntary resolution ... but shall not impose any term or any settlement upon the parties"; must explain the terms before signatures. reg. 13 – confidentiality; "There shall be no audio or video recording of the mediation proceedings." reg. 14 – the mediator communicates with the Commission only by his report, with copies to all parties. reg. 15 – immunity for acts done bona fide; the mediator "shall not be summoned by a party to appear in a Court or other forum, to testify". reg. 16 – quarterly report of the cell, within one month of the end of each quarter.

Mediation Act, 2023 – Tenth Schedule (s. 65): omits clauses (25) and (26) of s. 2 and Chapter V of CPA 2019, and substitutes s. 37 by new ss. 37, 37A and 37B, under which a Commission "may at any stage of proceedings refer the disputes for settlement by mediation under the Mediation Act, 2023". The commencement note in the Act text used for this note shows only ss. 1, 3, 26, 31 to 38, 45 to 47, 50 to 54 and 56 to 57 brought into force (9 October 2023); s. 65 is not among them. The CPA text used still contains Chapter V.
hi.meaning: Mediation – a process in which a neutral person, the mediator, helps the parties to a consumer dispute reach their own settlement (s. 2(25); reg. 12). Mediator – a person on the panel prepared under s. 75 (s. 2(26)). Consumer mediation cell – the unit attached to a Commission where mediation is held and the panel and records are kept (ss. 74, 79(1)). It is headed by the President of that Commission (reg. 5(6)). Empanelment – inclusion of a person in the panel of mediators of a Commission, on the selection committee's recommendation (s. 75(1)). Nomination – the Commission's choice of a particular empanelled mediator for a particular dispute (s. 76). Settlement report – the mediator's report of the settlement, sent with the signed agreement to the Commission (s. 80(2)). Settlement – "a settlement arrived at in the course of a mediation proceeding in respect of all or some of the issues involved in a consumer dispute pending before a Consumer Commission" (reg. 2(1)(g)).
keyPoints: s. 2(25): mediation; s. 2(26): mediator. s. 37: reference at first hearing or later; consent in five days; reference in five days. r. 4: five classes not to be referred. s. 74: cells – State Govt for District and State; Central Govt for National and regional Benches. s. 75: panel by Commission on recommendation of President + member; five years. reg. 3: nine eligible classes; reg. 4: disqualifications. s. 76: nomination by suitability; s. 78: replacement after hearing. s. 77: disclosure; s. 79: natural justice, usages of trade. reg. 11(2): three months; reg. 12: no imposed settlement; reg. 13: confidentiality. s. 80: written, signed agreement and settlement report; s. 81: order in seven days. s. 41: no appeal from settlement order; r. 5: full fee refund.

en.meaning:
Before any consumer-specific statute existed, which tort was the primary remedy available to a consumer injured by a defective product or careless service?

Explanation. Before consumer-specific legislation, an injured consumer's only real remedy was the tort of negligence — proving a duty of care, breach, and resulting damage.

What barrier did the doctrine of privity of contract traditionally create for an injured consumer?

Explanation. Privity of contract meant a buyer generally had no claim against a manufacturer or other party they had no direct contract with, even if that party's carelessness caused the harm.

In Donoghue v. Stevenson, what did the House of Lords hold about a manufacturer's duty of care?

Explanation. The House of Lords held that a manufacturer's duty of care to the ultimate consumer exists independently of contract, removing privity as a bar to a negligence claim.

In Cassidy v. Ministry of Health, the Ministry relied on an older, narrower view of hospital liability. Which test did the Court of Appeal move away from?

law-of-torts-u5-t18.subtitle: How the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 gives civil remedies for consumers and creates criminal offences for serious wrongs

en.inOneMinute: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (CPA 2019) makes a wrongdoer answerable in two ways (See Diagram 1 ): Civil liability – an order of a Consumer Commission to remove a defect, replace goods, refund the price with interest, pay compensation (including punitive damages ), pay product liability compensation, stop unfair practices, withdraw hazardous goods, pay a sum for unidentified consumers, issue a corrective advertisement and pay costs (s. 39(1)(a)–(n)). Orders are enforced like a civil court decree (s. 71). Criminal liability – offences tried by a court (or, for s. 72, by the Commission itself) and punished with imprisonment and fine: s. 72 – non-compliance with a Commission's order: imprisonment 1 month to 3 years, or fine ₹25,000 to ₹1 lakh, or both; s. 88 – non-compliance with the Central Authority's directions: up to 6 months, or fine up to ₹20 lakh, or both; s. 89 – false or misleading advertisement: up to 2 years and fine up to ₹10 lakh (later: 5 years and ₹50 lakh); s. 90 – product containing an adulterant : from 6 months and ₹1 lakh (no injury) to not less than 7 years up to life and fine not less than ₹10 lakh (death); s. 91 – spurious goods : from 1 year and ₹3 lakh (simple injury) to not less than 7 years up to life and fine not less than ₹10 lakh (death); s. 93 – vexatious search by an officer: up to 1 year, or fine up to ₹10,000, or both. Both can run together: s. 100 says the Act is "in addition to and not in derogation of" other laws, so the general criminal law (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023) and the tort action also remain. Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences v. Prasanth S. Dhananka (2009): on civil liability, the Supreme Court raised a Consumer Commission award from ₹14 lakh to ₹1 crore with interest, saying a court "must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation".
legalProvision: Civil liability – Consumer Protection Act, 2019

s. 39(1) – where the District Commission is satisfied that goods suffer from defects, or allegations about services or unfair trade practices, "or claims for compensation under product liability are proved", it "shall issue an order to the opposite party directing him to do one or more of the following": "(a) to remove the defect pointed out by the appropriate laboratory from the goods in question; (b) to replace the goods with new goods of similar description which shall be free from any defect; (c) to return to the complainant the price, or, as the case may be, the charges paid by the complainant along with such interest on such price or charges as may be decided; (d) to pay such amount as may be awarded by it as compensation to the consumer for any loss or injury suffered by the consumer due to the negligence of the opposite party: Provided that the District Commission shall have the power to grant punitive damages in such circumstances as it deems fit; (e) to pay such amount as may be awarded by it as compensation in a product liability action under Chapter VI; (f) to remove the defects in goods or deficiencies in the services in question; (g) to discontinue the unfair trade practice or restrictive trade practice and not to repeat them; (h) not to offer the hazardous or unsafe goods for sale; (i) to withdraw the hazardous goods from being offered for sale; (j) to cease manufacture of hazardous goods and to desist from offering services which are hazardous in nature; (k) to pay such sum as may be determined by it, if it is of the opinion that loss or injury has been suffered by a large number of consumers who are not identifiable conveniently: Provided that the minimum amount of sum so payable shall not be less than twenty-five per cent. of the value of such defective goods sold or service provided, as the case may be, to such consumers; (l) to issue corrective advertisement to neutralise the effect of misleading advertisement at the cost of the opposite party responsible for issuing such misleading advertisement; (m) to provide for adequate costs to parties; and (n) to cease and desist from issuing any misleading advertisement." s. 39(2) – "Any amount obtained under sub-section (1) shall be credited to such fund and utilised in such manner as may be prescribed." ss. 49(1), 59(1) – these provisions apply to complaints before the State and National Commissions. s. 71 – "Every order made by a District Commission, State Commission or the National Commission shall be enforced by it in the same manner as if it were a decree made by a Court in a suit before it and the provisions of Order XXI of the First Schedule to the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (5 of 1908) shall, as far as may be, applicable". ss. 82 to 87 – product liability of manufacturers, service providers and sellers (see that topic).
Criminal liability – Consumer Protection Act, 2019

s. 72(1) – "Whoever fails to comply with any order made by the District Commission or the State Commission or the National Commission, as the case may be, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than one month, but which may extend to three years, or with fine, which shall not be less than twenty-five thousand rupees, but which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both." s. 72(2) – the Commission "shall have the power of a Judicial Magistrate of first class for the trial of offences under sub-section (1)". s. 72(3) – such offences "shall be tried summarily". s. 73 – appeal against an order under s. 72(1), "both on facts and on law", from the District Commission to the State Commission, from the State Commission to the National Commission, and from the National Commission to the Supreme Court, within thirty days (delay may be condoned for sufficient cause). s. 88 – "Whoever, fails to comply with any direction of the Central Authority under sections 20 and 21, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months or with fine which may extend to twenty lakh rupees, or with both." s. 89 – "Any manufacturer or service provider who causes a false or misleading advertisement to be made which is prejudicial to the interest of consumers shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years and with fine which may extend to ten lakh rupees; and for every subsequent offence, be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to fifty lakh rupees." s. 90(1) – "Whoever, by himself or by any other person on his behalf, manufactures for sale or stores or sells or distributes or imports any product containing an adulterant shall be punished, if such act— (a) does not result in any injury to the consumer, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months and with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees; (b) causing injury not amounting to grievous hurt to the consumer, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and with fine which may extend to three lakh rupees; (c) causing injury resulting in grievous hurt to the consumer, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees; and (d) results in the death of a consumer, with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life and with fine which shall not be less than ten lakh rupees." s. 90(2) – offences under clauses (c) and (d) "shall be cognizable and non-bailable". s. 90(3) – the court may, on first conviction, "suspend any licence ... for a period up to two years, and in case of second or subsequent conviction, cancel the licence". Explanation – "adulterant" means "any material including extraneous matter which is employed or used for making a product unsafe"; "grievous hurt" has the meaning in s. 320 of the Indian Penal Code. s. 91(1) – whoever manufactures for sale, stores, sells, distributes or imports any spurious goods: "(a) causing injury not amounting to grievous hurt to the consumer, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year and with fine which may extend to three lakh rupees; (b) causing injury resulting in grievous hurt to the consumer, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to seven years and with fine which may extend to five lakh rupees; (c) results in the death of a consumer, with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years, but may extend to imprisonment for life and with fine which shall not be less than ten lakh rupees". s. 91(2) – clauses (b) and (c) are cognizable and non-bailable. s. 91(3) – licence suspension (first conviction, up to two years) or cancellation (second or subsequent). s. 2(43) – "spurious goods" means "such goods which are falsely claimed to be genuine". s. 92 – no cognizance of offences under ss. 88 and 89 "except on a complaint filed by the Central Authority or any officer authorised by it in this behalf". s. 93 – an officer exercising s. 22 powers who, knowing there are no reasonable grounds, searches premises or seizes records: "imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both". s. 96 – offences under ss. 88 and 89 may be compounded. s. 100 – "The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to and not in derogation of the provisions of any other law for the time being in force."

Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (general criminal law, for comparison): s. 274 – adulteration of food or drink intended for sale, making it noxious: imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to five thousand rupees, or both; ss. 275 to 278 – sale of noxious food or drink, adulteration and sale of adulterated drugs, and sale of a drug as a different drug.
en.meaning: Civil liability – liability to repair the wrong to the consumer : to put right, replace, refund or pay compensation. Its aim is redress . Criminal liability – liability to punishment (imprisonment, fine, licence suspension) for an offence. Its aim is punishment and deterrence . Compensation – money to make good the "loss or injury suffered by the consumer due to the negligence of the opposite party" (s. 39(1)(d)), or for "harm" in a product liability action (s. 39(1)(e)). Punitive damages – damages beyond actual loss, to punish and deter; the Commission may grant them "in such circumstances as it deems fit" (proviso to s. 39(1)(d)). Adulterant – "any material including extraneous matter which is employed or used for making a product unsafe" (s. 90, Explanation (a)). Spurious goods – "goods which are falsely claimed to be genuine" (s. 2(43)). Cognizable and non-bailable – the police may arrest without warrant, and bail is not a matter of right (used for the serious clauses of ss. 90 and 91).
keyPoints: s. 39(1): 14 civil reliefs; punitive damages in proviso to (d); 25% minimum in (k). s. 71: orders enforced as decrees. s. 72: non-compliance – 1 month–3 years, or ₹25,000–₹1 lakh; Commission as JMFC; summary trial. s. 73: appeal in 30 days; NCDRC to Supreme Court. (See Diagram 3 .) s. 88: 6 months / ₹20 lakh; s. 89: 2 years + ₹10 lakh (5 years + ₹50 lakh). s. 90: adulterant – four grades; death: 7 years–life + ≥ ₹10 lakh. s. 91: spurious goods – three grades. ss. 90(2), 91(2): serious grades cognizable and non-bailable; licence suspension or cancellation. s. 92: ss. 88, 89 only on Authority's complaint; s. 96: compounding of ss. 88, 89 only, not for a repeat within three years. s. 100: Act is in addition to other laws.

caseLaws.facts: Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences v. Prasanth S. Dhananka, [2009] 9 SCR 313 (14 May 2009) Facts: A twenty-year-old engineering student underwent surgery at the appellant hospital to remove a tumour. Immediately after the operation he developed acute paraplegia. The National Commission found negligence and deficiency of service before, during and after the operation and awarded ₹14 lakh (plus ₹1.5 lakh to his parents). Both sides appealed (B.N. Agrawal, Harjit Singh Bedi and G.S. Singhvi JJ.). Principle: The Court must "strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable"; "if a case is made out, the Court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation". It rejected the multiplier method as unsuitable for this kind of damage and awarded ₹1 crore with interest at 6% from 1 March 1999, refusing a "hypothetical" claim of ₹2 crore for future treatment. Why it matters: It shows how civil liability under consumer law is measured – full, realistic compensation for actual and future loss, not a token sum. Note: No judgment applying the offence provisions of CPA 2019 (ss. 72, 88 to 93) was found among the judgments available for this note.

te.inOneMinute: వినియోగదారుల రక్షణ చట్టం, 2019 (CPA 2019) తప్పు చేసిన వ్యక్తిని రెండు విధాలుగా బాధ్యుడిని చేస్తుంది ( చిత్రం 1 చూడండి): సివిల్ బాధ్యత – వినియోగదారుల కమిషన్ ఇచ్చే ఉత్తర్వు: లోపం తొలగించడం, వస్తువులు మార్చడం, ధరను వడ్డీతో తిరిగి ఇవ్వడం, నష్టపరిహారం ( శిక్షాత్మక నష్టపరిహారం సహా) చెల్లించడం, ఉత్పత్తి బాధ్యత నష్టపరిహారం, అన్యాయ వ్యాపార పద్ధతులు ఆపడం, ప్రమాదకర వస్తువులు ఉపసంహరించడం, గుర్తించలేని వినియోగదారుల కోసం మొత్తం చెల్లించడం, సరిదిద్దే ప్రకటన ఇవ్వడం, ఖర్చులు చెల్లించడం (సెక్షన్ 39(1)(a)–(n)). ఈ ఉత్తర్వులు సివిల్ కోర్టు డిక్రీలాగా అమలవుతాయి (సెక్షన్ 71). క్రిమినల్ బాధ్యత – కోర్టు (సెక్షన్ 72 విషయంలో కమిషనే) విచారించి జైలు శిక్ష, జరిమానా విధించే నేరాలు: సెక్షన్ 72 – కమిషన్ ఉత్తర్వు పాటించకపోవడం: 1 నెల నుండి 3 సంవత్సరాల జైలు, లేదా ₹25,000 నుండి ₹1 లక్ష జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ; సెక్షన్ 88 – కేంద్ర అథారిటీ ఆదేశాలు పాటించకపోవడం: 6 నెలల వరకు, లేదా ₹20 లక్షల వరకు జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ; సెక్షన్ 89 – తప్పుడు లేదా తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటన: 2 సంవత్సరాల వరకు మరియు ₹10 లక్షల వరకు జరిమానా (తర్వాతి నేరానికి: 5 సంవత్సరాలు, ₹50 లక్షలు); సెక్షన్ 90 – కల్తీ పదార్థం ఉన్న ఉత్పత్తి: గాయం లేకపోతే 6 నెలలు, ₹1 లక్ష నుండి, మరణం జరిగితే కనీసం 7 సంవత్సరాలు నుండి యావజ్జీవం వరకు, కనీసం ₹10 లక్షల జరిమానా వరకు; సెక్షన్ 91 – నకిలీ వస్తువులు : సాధారణ గాయానికి 1 సంవత్సరం, ₹3 లక్షల నుండి, మరణానికి కనీసం 7 సంవత్సరాలు నుండి యావజ్జీవం, కనీసం ₹10 లక్షల జరిమానా వరకు; సెక్షన్ 93 – అధికారి చేసే వేధింపు సోదా: 1 సంవత్సరం వరకు, లేదా ₹10,000 వరకు జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ. రెండూ కలిసి నడవవచ్చు: సెక్షన్ 100 ప్రకారం ఈ చట్టం ఇతర చట్టాలకు "in addition to and not in derogation of" (అర్థం: అదనంగా ఉంటుంది, వాటిని తగ్గించదు). కాబట్టి సాధారణ నేర చట్టం (భారతీయ న్యాయ సంహిత, 2023), టార్ట్ దావా కూడా అందుబాటులో ఉంటాయి. Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences v. Prasanth S. Dhananka (2009): సివిల్ బాధ్యత విషయంలో, సుప్రీంకోర్టు వినియోగదారుల కమిషన్ ఇచ్చిన ₹14 లక్షల పరిహారాన్ని వడ్డీతో ₹1 కోటికి పెంచింది. కోర్టు "must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation" (అర్థం: తగిన నష్టపరిహారం ఇవ్వడానికి వెనుకాడకూడదు) అని చెప్పింది.
te.meaning: సివిల్ బాధ్యత – వినియోగదారుడికి జరిగిన తప్పును సరిదిద్దే బాధ్యత: సరిచేయడం, మార్చడం, డబ్బు తిరిగి ఇవ్వడం లేదా నష్టపరిహారం చెల్లించడం. దీని లక్ష్యం పరిహారం. క్రిమినల్ బాధ్యత – ఒక నేరానికి శిక్ష (జైలు, జరిమానా, లైసెన్స్ నిలిపివేత) అనుభవించే బాధ్యత. దీని లక్ష్యం శిక్షించడం, ఇతరులను నిరోధించడం. నష్టపరిహారం – "loss or injury suffered by the consumer due to the negligence of the opposite party" (అర్థం: ఎదుటి పక్షం నిర్లక్ష్యం వల్ల వినియోగదారుడికి కలిగిన నష్టం లేదా గాయం) పూడ్చే డబ్బు (సెక్షన్ 39(1)(d)), లేదా ఉత్పత్తి బాధ్యత దావాలో "harm" (హాని) కోసం (సెక్షన్ 39(1)(e)). శిక్షాత్మక నష్టపరిహారం – అసలు నష్టం కంటే ఎక్కువగా, శిక్షించడానికి, నిరోధించడానికి ఇచ్చే నష్టపరిహారం; కమిషన్ దీనిని "in such circumstances as it deems fit" (అర్థం: తగినదని భావించే సందర్భాల్లో) ఇవ్వవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 39(1)(d) నిబంధన). కల్తీ పదార్థం ( Adulterant ) – "any material including extraneous matter which is employed or used for making a product unsafe" (అర్థం: ఉత్పత్తిని సురక్షితం కానిదిగా చేయడానికి వాడే బయటి పదార్థం సహా ఏ పదార్థమైనా) (సెక్షన్ 90, వివరణ (a)). నకిలీ వస్తువులు – "goods which are falsely claimed to be genuine" (అర్థం: అసలైనవని తప్పుగా చెప్పుకునే వస్తువులు) (సెక్షన్ 2(43)). కాగ్నిజబుల్ మరియు బెయిల్ రాని – పోలీసులు వారంట్ లేకుండా అరెస్ట్ చేయవచ్చు, బెయిల్ హక్కుగా రాదు (సెక్షన్లు 90, 91లోని తీవ్రమైన క్లాజులకు వర్తిస్తుంది).
keyPoints: సెక్షన్ 39(1): 14 సివిల్ పరిష్కారాలు; (d) నిబంధనలో శిక్షాత్మక నష్టపరిహారం; (k)లో కనీసం 25%. సెక్షన్ 71: ఉత్తర్వులు డిక్రీలాగా అమలు. సెక్షన్ 72: పాటించకపోవడం – 1 నెల–3 సంవత్సరాలు, లేదా ₹25,000–₹1 లక్ష; కమిషన్ JMFCగా; సంక్షిప్త విచారణ. సెక్షన్ 73: 30 రోజుల్లో అప్పీలు; NCDRC నుండి సుప్రీంకోర్టు. ( చిత్రం 3 చూడండి.) సెక్షన్ 88: 6 నెలలు / ₹20 లక్షలు; సెక్షన్ 89: 2 సంవత్సరాలు + ₹10 లక్షలు (5 సంవత్సరాలు + ₹50 లక్షలు). సెక్షన్ 90: కల్తీ – నాలుగు దశలు; మరణం: 7 సంవత్సరాలు–యావజ్జీవం + కనీసం ₹10 లక్షలు. సెక్షన్ 91: నకిలీ వస్తువులు – మూడు దశలు. సెక్షన్లు 90(2), 91(2): తీవ్ర దశలు కాగ్నిజబుల్, బెయిల్ రానివి; లైసెన్స్ నిలిపివేత లేదా రద్దు. సెక్షన్ 92: సెక్షన్లు 88, 89 అథారిటీ ఫిర్యాదుపై మాత్రమే; సెక్షన్ 96: సెక్షన్లు 88, 89 మాత్రమే రాజీ, మూడు సంవత్సరాల్లో పునరావృతానికి కాదు. సెక్షన్ 100: చట్టం ఇతర చట్టాలకు అదనం.

selfTest.q: సెక్షన్ 39(1) కింద ఏవైనా ఆరు పరిష్కారాలు రాయండి. కమిషన్ శిక్షాత్మక నష్టపరిహారం ఎప్పుడు ఇవ్వవచ్చు?
selfTest.a: కమిషన్ ఉత్తర్వు ఎలా అమలవుతుంది? కమిషన్ ఉత్తర్వు పాటించకపోతే శిక్ష ఏమిటి? కల్తీ ఉత్పత్తి మరణానికి కారణమైతే సెక్షన్ 90 కింద శిక్ష చెప్పండి. "నకిలీ వస్తువులు" నిర్వచించండి. CPA 2019 కింద ఏ నేరాలు కాగ్నిజబుల్, బెయిల్ రానివి? ఏ నేరాలను రాజీ చేయవచ్చు?
