te.inOneMinute: భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 లోని సెక్షన్లు 14, 15 — సంస్థ ఆస్తి
te.meaning:
భాగస్వాముల మధ్య ఒప్పందానికి లోబడి, సంస్థ ఆస్తిలో అసలు సంస్థ స్టాక్‌లోకి తెచ్చిన, లేదా కొనుగోలు ద్వారా లేదా ఇతర విధంగా సంస్థ ద్వారా లేదా దాని కోసం, లేదా సంస్థ వ్యాపార ప్రయోజనాల కోసం వ్యాపార క్రమంలో సంపాదించిన అన్ని ఆస్తి, ఆస్తిలో హక్కులు, ఆసక్తులు ఉంటాయి. వ్యాపారం గుడ్‌విల్ కూడా దానిలో ఉంటుంది (సెక్షన్ 14).

వేరే ఉద్దేశం కనిపిస్తే తప్ప, సంస్థకు చెందిన డబ్బుతో సంపాదించిన ఆస్తిని సంస్థ కోసం సంపాదించినట్లు భావిస్తారు (సెక్షన్ 14). ఒప్పందానికి లోబడి, సంస్థ ఆస్తిని భాగస్వాములు వ్యాపార ప్రయోజనాల కోసం మాత్రమే ఉంచి, వాడాలి (సెక్షన్ 15). సమాధానంలో ముఖ్యమైనవి: ఏమి ఉంటాయి, సంస్థ డబ్బుతో కొన్న ఆస్తిపై భావన, ప్రత్యేక వాడకం విధి.

ముందు ఈ పదాలు చదవండి. ఈ అంశంలో ప్రతి పదం పదే పదే వస్తుంది.

నియమం. భాగస్వాముల ఒప్పందానికి లోబడి, సంస్థ ఆస్తిలో మూడు సమూహాలు ఉంటాయి.

ఉదాహరణ. అనిల్, బీనా ఒక బేకరీ మొదలుపెట్టారు. అనిల్ సంస్థ స్టాక్‌లోకి ఒక ఓవెన్ తెచ్చాడు, సంస్థ తర్వాత ఒక డెలివరీ వ్యాన్ కొన్నది. ఓవెన్, వ్యాన్ రెండూ సంస్థ ఆస్తి, బేకరీ గుడ్‌విల్ కూడా (సెక్షన్ 14).

నియమం. వేరే ఉద్దేశం కనిపిస్తే తప్ప, సంస్థకు చెందిన డబ్బుతో సంపాదించిన ఆస్తి, ఆస్తిలో హక్కులు, ఆసక్తులను సంస్థ కోసం సంపాదించినట్లు భావిస్తారు.

ఉదాహరణ. సంస్థ ఖాతాలోని డబ్బుతో చందన్ తన సొంత పేరుతో ఒక స్థలం కొన్నాడు. వేరే ఉద్దేశం కనిపిస్తే తప్ప, ఆ స్థలాన్ని సంస్థ కోసం సంపాదించినట్లు భావిస్తారు.

selfTest.q: 1. గుడ్‌విల్ సంస్థ ఆస్తిలో భాగమా?
selfTest.a: అవును. సంస్థ ఆస్తిలో వ్యాపార గుడ్‌విల్ కూడా ఉంటుందని సెక్షన్ 14 చెబుతుంది. 2. సంస్థ డబ్బుతో భాగస్వామి పేరుతో కొన్న ఆస్తి ఎవరిది? వేరే ఉద్దేశం కనిపిస్తే తప్ప, సంస్థ కోసం సంపాదించినట్లు భావిస్తారు (సెక్షన్ 14). 3. సంస్థ ఆస్తిని ఎలా వాడాలి? ఒప్పందానికి లోబడి, భాగస్వాములు వ్యాపార ప్రయోజనాల కోసం మాత్రమే ఉంచి, వాడాలి (సెక్షన్ 15).

hi.meaning: What is the firm's property (section 14) Rule. Subject to the partners' contract, the firm's property includes three groups. Property and rights and interests in property originally brought into the stock of the firm. Property and rights and interests acquired, by purchase or otherwise, by or for the firm, or for the purposes and in the course of its business. The goodwill of the business. Example. Anil and Bina start a bakery. Anil brings an oven into the firm's stock, and the firm later buys a delivery van. Both the oven and the van are property of the firm, and so is the goodwill of the bakery (section 14). Property bought with the firm's money (section 14) Rule. Unless the contrary intention appears, property and rights and interests in property acquired with money belonging to the firm are deemed to have been acquired for the firm. Example. Chandan buys a plot in his own name using money from the firm's account. Unless the contrary intention appears, the plot is deemed acquired for the firm. Use of the firm's property (section 15) Rule. Subject to the partners' contract, the property of the firm shall be held and used by the partners exclusively for the purposes of the business. Is it the firm's property? How to read this: start at the top. Every step is subject to a contract between the partners. 1. Was it originally brought into the stock of the firm? It is firm property (section 14). 2. Was it acquired by or for the firm, or for the purposes and in the course of its business? It is firm property (section 14). 3. Was it acquired with money belonging to the firm? It is deemed acquired for the firm, unless the contrary intention appears (section 14). 4. How may it be used? Held and used by the partners exclusively for the purposes of the business (section 15).
keyPoints: Firm property: what is brought into the stock, what is acquired by or for the firm or for its business, and the goodwill (section 14). Property bought with firm money is deemed bought for the firm, unless the contrary intention appears (section 14). Held and used exclusively for the purposes of the business, subject to contract (section 15).

selfTest.q: 1. Is goodwill part of the firm's property?
selfTest.a: Yes. Section 14 says the property of the firm includes the goodwill of the business. 2. Property bought with the firm's money in a partner's name: whose is it? It is deemed acquired for the firm, unless the contrary intention appears (section 14). 3. How must the firm's property be used? Held and used by the partners exclusively for the purposes of the business, subject to contract (section 15).

law-of-contract-ii-u5-t5.subtitle: Sections 56 to 68, 70 and 71 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932

en.inOneMinute: Under section 58 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, the registration of a firm may be effected at any time by sending or delivering to the Registrar of the area a statement in the prescribed form with the prescribed fee. The statement gives the firm name, the principal place of business, other places of business, the date each partner joined, the partners' names and addresses, and the duration of the firm. When the Registrar is satisfied, he records an entry in the Register of Firms and files the statement (section 59). Later changes can be recorded (sections 60 to 63), mistakes rectified (section 64), and the Register inspected (section 66). Key points for the answer: who registers, what the statement contains, and the later steps.
en.meaning:
How a firm is registered (sections 57 to 59)

Rule. The firm sends or delivers to the Registrar of the area a statement with the prescribed fee. It states the firm name, the principal place of business, other places of business, the date each partner joined, the partners' full names and permanent addresses, and the duration of the firm. All the partners or their specially authorised agents sign it, and each signatory verifies it. When the Registrar is satisfied that section 58 is complied with, he records an entry in the Register of Firms and files the statement.

Example. Rohan, Seema and Tara run a firm called "Rohan and Company" from a shop in Pune. They send the Registrar a signed and verified statement with the fee, giving the particulars listed in section 58(1). The Registrar records an entry in the Register of Firms (section 59).

Restrictions on the firm name (section 58(3))

Rule. A firm name may not contain "Crown", "Emperor", "Empress", "Empire", "Imperial", "King", "Queen", "Royal", or words expressing or implying Government sanction, approval or patronage, unless the State Government consents in writing.

Recording later changes (sections 60 to 63)

Rule. A registered firm may have the Register updated.

Change of firm name or principal place of business: a statement with the fee, signed and verified as in section 58 (section 60). Opening or closing of a branch: intimation by any partner or agent (section 61). Change of a partner's name or address: intimation by any partner or agent (section 62). Change in the constitution of the firm or its dissolution: notice by an incoming, continuing or outgoing partner, or by a person who was a partner just before dissolution, or an authorised agent. A minor's election on attaining majority is also noticed to the Registrar (section 63).

Rectification, amendment, inspection, copies and evidence (sections 64 to 68)

Rule. The Registrar may always rectify mistakes to bring an entry into conformity with the filed documents, and may rectify a mistake in a document on the application of all who signed it (section 64). A Court may direct a consequential amendment (section 65). The Register and filed documents are open to inspection on fee (section 66). The Registrar furnishes certified copies on application and fee (section 67). A recorded statement, intimation or notice is conclusive proof against its signatories, and a certified copy proves the registration and contents (section 68).

Penalty and rules (sections 70 and 71)

Rule. A person who signs a statement or notice with a particular he knows to be false or does not believe to be true, or with particulars he knows to be incomplete, is punishable with up to three months' imprisonment, or fine, or both (section 70). The State Government makes rules under section 71.

Steps in registration How to read this: start at the top. 1. Prepare a statement with the particulars in section 58(1), signed by all partners or their authorised agents and verified. Send or deliver it with the fee to the Registrar of the area. 2. The Registrar is satisfied that section 58 is complied with. He records an entry in the Register of Firms and files the statement (section 59). 3. Later changes. Notified by statement or intimation, and recorded (sections 60 to 63). Mistakes are rectified (section 64).
keyPoints: Registration may be effected at any time by a statement with the fee to the Registrar of the area (section 58). Six particulars: name, principal place, other places, date each partner joined, partners' names and addresses, duration. Signed by all partners or their authorised agents and verified. The Registrar records an entry in the Register of Firms (section 59). Changes are recorded (sections 60 to 63). Mistakes are rectified (section 64). False particulars: up to three months' imprisonment, or fine, or both (section 70).

selfTest.q: 1. When may a firm be registered?
selfTest.a: At any time (section 58(1)). 2. Who signs the statement? All the partners, or their agents specially authorised in this behalf (section 58(1)). 3. What does the Registrar do when satisfied? Records an entry of the statement in the Register of Firms and files the statement (section 59). 4. What is the penalty for a false particular? Imprisonment up to three months, or fine, or both (section 70).

te.inOneMinute: భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 లోని సెక్షన్లు 56 నుండి 68, 70, 71 — సంస్థ నమోదు
te.meaning:
భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 సెక్షన్ 58 ప్రకారం, సంస్థ నమోదును ఎప్పుడైనా చేయవచ్చు: నిర్దేశిత ఫారంలో, నిర్దేశిత రుసుముతో ఒక ప్రకటనను ఆ ప్రాంతపు రిజిస్ట్రార్‌కు పోస్టులో పంపడం లేదా అందజేయడం ద్వారా. ప్రకటనలో సంస్థ పేరు, ప్రధాన వ్యాపార స్థలం, ఇతర వ్యాపార స్థలాలు, ప్రతి భాగస్వామి చేరిన తేదీ, భాగస్వాముల పేర్లు, చిరునామాలు, సంస్థ కాలపరిమితి ఉంటాయి.

రిజిస్ట్రార్ సంతృప్తి చెందితే, సంస్థల రిజిస్టర్‌లో ప్రకటన నమోదును రికార్డు చేసి, ప్రకటనను ఫైల్ చేస్తాడు (సెక్షన్ 59). తర్వాతి మార్పులను నమోదు చేయవచ్చు (సెక్షన్లు 60 నుండి 63), తప్పులను సరిదిద్దవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 64), రిజిస్టర్‌ను తనిఖీ చేయవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 66). సమాధానంలో ముఖ్యమైనవి: ఎవరు నమోదు చేస్తారు, ప్రకటనలో ఏముంటాయి, తర్వాతి దశలు.

ముందు ఈ పదాలు చదవండి. ఈ అంశంలో ప్రతి పదం పదే పదే వస్తుంది.

నియమం. సంస్థ నిర్దేశిత రుసుముతో ఒక ప్రకటనను ఆ ప్రాంతపు రిజిస్ట్రార్‌కు పంపుతుంది లేదా అందజేస్తుంది. అందులో సంస్థ పేరు, ప్రధాన వ్యాపార స్థలం, ఇతర వ్యాపార స్థలాలు, ప్రతి భాగస్వామి చేరిన తేదీ, భాగస్వాముల పూర్తి పేర్లు, శాశ్వత చిరునామాలు, సంస్థ కాలపరిమితి ఉంటాయి. భాగస్వాములందరూ లేదా వారి ప్రత్యేక అధికారం పొందిన ఏజెంట్లు దానిపై సంతకం చేస్తారు, ప్రతి సంతకందారు దాన్ని ధృవీకరిస్తాడు. సెక్షన్ 58 పాటించారని రిజిస్ట్రార్ సంతృప్తి చెందితే, సంస్థల రిజిస్టర్‌లో నమోదును రికార్డు చేసి, ప్రకటనను ఫైల్ చేస్తాడు.

ఉదాహరణ. రోహన్, సీమ, తార పుణెలోని ఒక దుకాణం నుండి "Rohan and Company" అనే సంస్థను నడుపుతున్నారు. సెక్షన్ 58(1) లో చెప్పిన వివరాలతో సంతకం చేసి, ధృవీకరించిన ప్రకటనను రుసుముతో రిజిస్ట్రార్‌కు పంపారు. రిజిస్ట్రార్ సంస్థల రిజిస్టర్‌లో నమోదును రికార్డు చేస్తాడు (సెక్షన్ 59).

నియమం. రాష్ట్ర ప్రభుత్వం వ్రాతపూర్వకంగా సమ్మతించకపోతే, సంస్థ పేరులో "Crown", "Emperor", "Empress", "Empire", "Imperial", "King", "Queen", "Royal" పదాలు, లేదా ప్రభుత్వ అనుమతి, ఆమోదం లేదా ప్రోత్సాహాన్ని వ్యక్తం చేసే లేదా సూచించే పదాలు ఉండకూడదు.

నియమం. నమోదైన సంస్థ రిజిస్టర్‌ను తాజాగా ఉంచవచ్చు.

selfTest.q: 1. సంస్థను ఎప్పుడు నమోదు చేయవచ్చు?
selfTest.a: ఎప్పుడైనా (సెక్షన్ 58(1)). 2. ప్రకటనపై ఎవరు సంతకం చేస్తారు? భాగస్వాములందరూ, లేదా వారి ప్రత్యేక అధికారం పొందిన ఏజెంట్లు (సెక్షన్ 58(1)). 3. సంతృప్తి చెందాక రిజిస్ట్రార్ ఏమి చేస్తాడు? సంస్థల రిజిస్టర్‌లో ప్రకటన నమోదును రికార్డు చేసి, ప్రకటనను ఫైల్ చేస్తాడు (సెక్షన్ 59). 4. తప్పుడు వివరానికి శిక్ష ఏమిటి? మూడు నెలల వరకు జైలు, లేదా జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ (సెక్షన్ 70).

hi.inOneMinute: Under section 58 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, the registration of a firm may be effected at any time by sending or delivering to the Registrar of the area a statement in the prescribed form with the prescribed fee. The statement gives the firm name, the principal place of business, other places of business, the date each partner joined, the partners' names and addresses, and the duration of the firm. When the Registrar is satisfied, he records an entry in the Register of Firms and files the statement (section 59). Later changes can be recorded (sections 60 to 63), mistakes rectified (section 64), and the Register inspected (section 66). Key points for the answer: who registers, what the statement contains, and the later steps.
hi.meaning: How a firm is registered (sections 57 to 59) Rule. The firm sends or delivers to the Registrar of the area a statement with the prescribed fee. It states the firm name, the principal place of business, other places of business, the date each partner joined, the partners' full names and permanent addresses, and the duration of the firm. All the partners or their specially authorised agents sign it, and each signatory verifies it. When the Registrar is satisfied that section 58 is complied with, he records an entry in the Register of Firms and files the statement. Example. Rohan, Seema and Tara run a firm called "Rohan and Company" from a shop in Pune. They send the Registrar a signed and verified statement with the fee, giving the particulars listed in section 58(1). The Registrar records an entry in the Register of Firms (section 59). Restrictions on the firm name (section 58(3)) Rule. A firm name may not contain "Crown", "Emperor", "Empress", "Empire", "Imperial", "King", "Queen", "Royal", or words expressing or implying Government sanction, approval or patronage, unless the State Government consents in writing. Recording later changes (sections 60 to 63) Rule. A registered firm may have the Register updated. Change of firm name or principal place of business: a statement with the fee, signed and verified as in section 58 (section 60). Opening or closing of a branch: intimation by any partner or agent (section 61). Change of a partner's name or address: intimation by any partner or agent (section 62). Change in the constitution of the firm or its dissolution: notice by an incoming, continuing or outgoing partner, or by a person who was a partner just before dissolution, or an authorised agent. A minor's election on attaining majority is also noticed to the Registrar (section 63). Rectification, amendment, inspection, copies and evidence (sections 64 to 68) Rule. The Registrar may always rectify mistakes to bring an entry into conformity with the filed documents, and may rectify a mistake in a document on the application of all who signed it (section 64). A Court may direct a consequential amendment (section 65). The Register and filed documents are open to inspection on fee (section 66). The Registrar furnishes certified copies on application and fee (section 67). A recorded statement, intimation or notice is conclusive proof against its signatories, and a certified copy proves the registration and contents (section 68). Penalty and rules (sections 70 and 71) Rule. A person who signs a statement or notice with a particular he knows to be false or does not believe to be true, or with particulars he knows to be incomplete, is punishable with up to three months' imprisonment, or fine, or both (section 70). The State Government makes rules under section 71. Steps in registration How to read this: start at the top. 1. Prepare a statement with the particulars in section 58(1), signed by all partners or their authorised agents and verified. Send or deliver it with the fee to the Registrar of the area. 2. The Registrar is satisfied that section 58 is complied with. He records an entry in the Register of Firms and files the statement (section 59). 3. Later changes. Notified by statement or intimation, and recorded (sections 60 to 63). Mistakes are rectified (section 64).
keyPoints: Registration may be effected at any time by a statement with the fee to the Registrar of the area (section 58). Six particulars: name, principal place, other places, date each partner joined, partners' names and addresses, duration. Signed by all partners or their authorised agents and verified. The Registrar records an entry in the Register of Firms (section 59). Changes are recorded (sections 60 to 63). Mistakes are rectified (section 64). False particulars: up to three months' imprisonment, or fine, or both (section 70).

selfTest.q: 1. When may a firm be registered?
selfTest.a: At any time (section 58(1)). 2. Who signs the statement? All the partners, or their agents specially authorised in this behalf (section 58(1)). 3. What does the Registrar do when satisfied? Records an entry of the statement in the Register of Firms and files the statement (section 59). 4. What is the penalty for a false particular? Imprisonment up to three months, or fine, or both (section 70).

law-of-contract-ii-u5-t7.subtitle: Sections 9 to 13, 16 and 17 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932

en.inOneMinute: The partners' mutual rights and duties may be fixed by their contract (section 11). Unless the contract says otherwise, the Act supplies these rules: every partner has a right to take part in the conduct of the business and a duty to attend to it diligently, differences on ordinary matters are decided by a majority, and no change in the nature of the business may be made without the consent of all (section 12). Unless the contract says otherwise, no partner is entitled to remuneration , the partners share profits equally and bear losses equally, and interest on a partner's advance beyond his capital is six per cent per annum (section 13). A partner must account to the firm for personal profits from the firm's transactions, property or business connection (section 16). Key points for the answer: the duties in sections 9 and 10, then sections 12, 13 and 16.
en.meaning:
General duties (section 9)

Rule. Partners must carry on the business of the firm to the greatest common advantage, be just and faithful to each other, and render true accounts and full information of all things affecting the firm to any partner or his legal representative.

Indemnity for fraud (section 10)

Rule. A partner must indemnify the firm for any loss caused to it by his fraud in the conduct of the business.

Rights and duties by contract (section 11)

Rule. The partners' mutual rights and duties are fixed by their contract, express or implied by a course of dealing, and varied by all partners' consent. The contract may bar a partner from other business while he is a partner (section 11(2)).

Conduct of the business (section 12)

Rule. Subject to contract, each partner has a right to take part in the conduct of the business and must attend diligently to his duties. Ordinary differences may be decided by a majority, after every partner has expressed his opinion. A change in the nature of the business needs the consent of all. Each partner may inspect and copy the firm's books.

Example. Of three partners in a shop, two want to stock a new brand of soap and one objects. This is an ordinary matter, so the two-partner majority may decide, after hearing the third (section 12(c)). If they wanted to change the shop into a restaurant, that is a change in the nature of the business and needs the consent of all.

Mutual rights and liabilities (section 13)

Rule. Subject to contract: no remuneration for taking part in the business; equal share in profits and equal contribution to losses; interest on capital only out of profits; six per cent per annum on payments or advances beyond agreed capital; the firm indemnifies a partner for payments and liabilities in the ordinary and proper conduct of the business and in an emergency act of ordinary prudence; a partner indemnifies the firm for loss caused by his wilful neglect.

Example. Three partners made a profit of Rs 90,000 and their contract says nothing about shares. Each is entitled to Rs 30,000 (section 13(b)). One partner lent the firm Rs 1,00,000 beyond his capital. He is entitled to interest on it at six per cent per annum (section 13(d)).

Personal profits (section 16)

Rule. Subject to contract, a partner who derives profits for himself from a transaction of the firm, or from the use of the firm's property, business connection or name, must account for and pay that profit to the firm. A partner who carries on a competing business of the same nature must account for and pay to the firm all profits made in that business.

Rights and duties after a change (section 17)

Rule. Subject to contract: after a change in the constitution of the firm, the partners' mutual rights and duties remain the same as before as far as may be; after a fixed-term firm continues past its term, they remain the same so far as consistent with a partnership at will; and for other adventures or undertakings carried out by a firm formed for particular ones, they are the same as for the original ones.

Which rule governs the partners' rights? How to read this: start at the top. 1. Is there a contract between the partners, express or implied by a course of dealing, on the point (section 11)? The contract governs. 2. If not, the Act's rules apply: conduct of business (section 12), mutual rights and liabilities (section 13), personal profits (section 16), changes (section 17). These apply "subject to contract between the partners". 3. Duties of good faith and indemnity for fraud (sections 9 and 10). Stated in the Act. Section 9 is not qualified by "subject to contract".
keyPoints: Rights and duties may be fixed by contract (section 11). Sections 12, 13, 16, 17 apply subject to it. Duties: greatest common advantage, just and faithful, true accounts (section 9). Indemnify the firm for fraud (section 10). Every partner may take part in the business. Ordinary matters by majority. Change in nature by all (section 12). No remuneration. Equal sharing of profits and losses. Interest on capital only out of profits. Six per cent on extra advances (section 13). Personal profits and competing business: account to the firm (section 16).

selfTest.q: 1. Unless the contract says otherwise, how are profits shared?
selfTest.a: Equally, and losses are borne equally (section 13(b)). 2. What interest is payable on an advance beyond a partner's capital? Six per cent per annum (section 13(d)). 3. Who decides ordinary differences about the business? A majority of the partners, after every partner has had the right to express his opinion. A change in the nature of the business needs the consent of all (section 12(c)). 4. What must a partner do with personal profits from the firm's transactions or business connection? Account for them and pay them to the firm (section 16(a)).

te.inOneMinute: భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 లోని సెక్షన్లు 9 నుండి 13, 16, 17 — భాగస్వాముల హక్కులు, విధులు
te.meaning:
భాగస్వాముల పరస్పర హక్కులు, విధులను వారి ఒప్పందం నిర్ణయించవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 11). ఒప్పందం వేరే చెప్పకపోతే, చట్టం ఈ నియమాలు ఇస్తుంది: ప్రతి భాగస్వామికి వ్యాపార నిర్వహణలో పాల్గొనే హక్కు, దానిపై శ్రద్ధగా దృష్టి పెట్టే విధి ఉన్నాయి; సాధారణ విషయాల్లో విభేదాలను మెజారిటీ నిర్ణయిస్తుంది; వ్యాపార స్వభావంలో మార్పు అందరి సమ్మతి లేకుండా చేయకూడదు (సెక్షన్ 12).

ఒప్పందం వేరే చెప్పకపోతే, ఏ భాగస్వామికీ తన పనికి వేతనం పొందే హక్కు లేదు, లాభాలను సమానంగా పంచుకుంటారు, నష్టాలను సమానంగా భరిస్తారు, భాగస్వామి మూలధనం కంటే ఎక్కువ ఇచ్చిన అడ్వాన్స్‌పై సంవత్సరానికి ఆరు శాతం వడ్డీ (సెక్షన్ 13). సంస్థ లావాదేవీలు, ఆస్తి లేదా వ్యాపార సంబంధం నుండి వచ్చిన వ్యక్తిగత లాభాలను భాగస్వామి సంస్థకు లెక్క చెప్పాలి (సెక్షన్ 16). సమాధానంలో ముఖ్యమైనవి: సెక్షన్లు 9, 10 లోని విధులు, తర్వాత సెక్షన్లు 12, 13, 16.

ముందు ఈ పదాలు చదవండి. ఈ అంశంలో ప్రతి పదం పదే పదే వస్తుంది.

నియమం. భాగస్వాములు సంస్థ వ్యాపారాన్ని గరిష్ట సమష్టి ప్రయోజనం కోసం నడపాలి, ఒకరిపట్ల ఒకరు న్యాయంగా, విశ్వాసంగా ఉండాలి, సంస్థను ప్రభావితం చేసే అన్ని విషయాలకు సంబంధించిన నిజమైన లెక్కలు, పూర్తి సమాచారం ఏ భాగస్వామికైనా లేదా అతని చట్టబద్ధ ప్రతినిధికైనా ఇవ్వాలి.

నియమం. వ్యాపార నిర్వహణలో తన మోసం వల్ల సంస్థకు కలిగిన ఏ నష్టానికైనా భాగస్వామి సంస్థకు నష్టపూరణ చేయాలి.

నియమం. భాగస్వాముల పరస్పర హక్కులు, విధులను వారి ఒప్పందం నిర్ణయిస్తుంది, అది స్పష్టంగా లేదా వ్యవహార తీరు నుండి అంతర్లీనంగా ఉండవచ్చు, భాగస్వాములందరి సమ్మతితో మార్చవచ్చు. భాగస్వామిగా ఉన్నంత కాలం వేరే వ్యాపారం చేయకూడదని ఒప్పందం నిర్దేశించవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 11(2)).

నియమం. ఒప్పందానికి లోబడి, ప్రతి భాగస్వామికి వ్యాపార నిర్వహణలో పాల్గొనే హక్కు ఉంది, తన విధులపై శ్రద్ధగా దృష్టి పెట్టాలి. ప్రతి భాగస్వామి తన అభిప్రాయం చెప్పాక, సాధారణ విభేదాలను మెజారిటీ నిర్ణయించవచ్చు. వ్యాపార స్వభావంలో మార్పుకు అందరి సమ్మతి కావాలి. ప్రతి భాగస్వామి సంస్థ పుస్తకాలను తనిఖీ చేయవచ్చు, కాపీ చేయవచ్చు.

selfTest.q: 1. ఒప్పందం వేరే చెప్పకపోతే లాభాలను ఎలా పంచుకుంటారు?
selfTest.a: సమానంగా, నష్టాలను కూడా సమానంగా భరిస్తారు (సెక్షన్ 13(b)). 2. భాగస్వామి మూలధనం కంటే ఎక్కువ అడ్వాన్స్‌పై ఏ వడ్డీ చెల్లిస్తారు? సంవత్సరానికి ఆరు శాతం (సెక్షన్ 13(d)). 3. వ్యాపారం గురించిన సాధారణ విభేదాలను ఎవరు నిర్ణయిస్తారు? ప్రతి భాగస్వామి తన అభిప్రాయం చెప్పే హక్కు ఉన్నాక భాగస్వాముల మెజారిటీ. వ్యాపార స్వభావంలో మార్పుకు అందరి సమ్మతి కావాలి (సెక్షన్ 12(c)). 4. సంస్థ లావాదేవీలు లేదా వ్యాపార సంబంధం నుండి వచ్చిన వ్యక్తిగత లాభాలను భాగస్వామి ఏమి చేయాలి? వాటికి లెక్క చెప్పి సంస్థకు చెల్లించాలి (సెక్షన్ 16(a)).

hi.inOneMinute: The partners' mutual rights and duties may be fixed by their contract (section 11). Unless the contract says otherwise, the Act supplies these rules: every partner has a right to take part in the conduct of the business and a duty to attend to it diligently, differences on ordinary matters are decided by a majority, and no change in the nature of the business may be made without the consent of all (section 12). Unless the contract says otherwise, no partner is entitled to remuneration , the partners share profits equally and bear losses equally, and interest on a partner's advance beyond his capital is six per cent per annum (section 13). A partner must account to the firm for personal profits from the firm's transactions, property or business connection (section 16). Key points for the answer: the duties in sections 9 and 10, then sections 12, 13 and 16.
hi.meaning: General duties (section 9) Rule. Partners must carry on the business of the firm to the greatest common advantage, be just and faithful to each other, and render true accounts and full information of all things affecting the firm to any partner or his legal representative. Indemnity for fraud (section 10) Rule. A partner must indemnify the firm for any loss caused to it by his fraud in the conduct of the business. Rights and duties by contract (section 11) Rule. The partners' mutual rights and duties are fixed by their contract, express or implied by a course of dealing, and varied by all partners' consent. The contract may bar a partner from other business while he is a partner (section 11(2)). Conduct of the business (section 12) Rule. Subject to contract, each partner has a right to take part in the conduct of the business and must attend diligently to his duties. Ordinary differences may be decided by a majority, after every partner has expressed his opinion. A change in the nature of the business needs the consent of all. Each partner may inspect and copy the firm's books. Example. Of three partners in a shop, two want to stock a new brand of soap and one objects. This is an ordinary matter, so the two-partner majority may decide, after hearing the third (section 12(c)). If they wanted to change the shop into a restaurant, that is a change in the nature of the business and needs the consent of all. Mutual rights and liabilities (section 13) Rule. Subject to contract: no remuneration for taking part in the business; equal share in profits and equal contribution to losses; interest on capital only out of profits; six per cent per annum on payments or advances beyond agreed capital; the firm indemnifies a partner for payments and liabilities in the ordinary and proper conduct of the business and in an emergency act of ordinary prudence; a partner indemnifies the firm for loss caused by his wilful neglect. Example. Three partners made a profit of Rs 90,000 and their contract says nothing about shares. Each is entitled to Rs 30,000 (section 13(b)). One partner lent the firm Rs 1,00,000 beyond his capital. He is entitled to interest on it at six per cent per annum (section 13(d)). Personal profits (section 16) Rule. Subject to contract, a partner who derives profits for himself from a transaction of the firm, or from the use of the firm's property, business connection or name, must account for and pay that profit to the firm. A partner who carries on a competing business of the same nature must account for and pay to the firm all profits made in that business. Rights and duties after a change (section 17) Rule. Subject to contract: after a change in the constitution of the firm, the partners' mutual rights and duties remain the same as before as far as may be; after a fixed-term firm continues past its term, they remain the same so far as consistent with a partnership at will; and for other adventures or undertakings carried out by a firm formed for particular ones, they are the same as for the original ones. Which rule governs the partners' rights? How to read this: start at the top. 1. Is there a contract between the partners, express or implied by a course of dealing, on the point (section 11)? The contract governs. 2. If not, the Act's rules apply: conduct of business (section 12), mutual rights and liabilities (section 13), personal profits (section 16), changes (section 17). These apply "subject to contract between the partners". 3. Duties of good faith and indemnity for fraud (sections 9 and 10). Stated in the Act. Section 9 is not qualified by "subject to contract".
keyPoints: Rights and duties may be fixed by contract (section 11). Sections 12, 13, 16, 17 apply subject to it. Duties: greatest common advantage, just and faithful, true accounts (section 9). Indemnify the firm for fraud (section 10). Every partner may take part in the business. Ordinary matters by majority. Change in nature by all (section 12). No remuneration. Equal sharing of profits and losses. Interest on capital only out of profits. Six per cent on extra advances (section 13). Personal profits and competing business: account to the firm (section 16).

selfTest.q: 1. Unless the contract says otherwise, how are profits shared?
selfTest.a: Equally, and losses are borne equally (section 13(b)). 2. What interest is payable on an advance beyond a partner's capital? Six per cent per annum (section 13(d)). 3. Who decides ordinary differences about the business? A majority of the partners, after every partner has had the right to express his opinion. A change in the nature of the business needs the consent of all (section 12(c)). 4. What must a partner do with personal profits from the firm's transactions or business connection? Account for them and pay them to the firm (section 16(a)).

law-of-contract-ii-u5-t10.subtitle: Sections 4, 28, 30 and 31 to 35 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932

en.inOneMinute: The Indian Partnership Act, 1932 does not divide partners into labelled classes such as active, sleeping or nominal partners. Those words do not appear in the Act. The Act does give separate rules for persons in different positions in a firm: a partner (section 4), a person who holds himself out as a partner (section 28), a minor admitted to the benefits of partnership (section 30), an incoming partner (section 31), a retiring partner (section 32), an expelled partner (section 33), an insolvent partner (section 34), and the estate of a deceased partner (section 35). This note sets out each position from the Act. A textbook classification by activity in the business is not in the Act and is not given here.
en.meaning:
Partner (section 4)

Rule. A person who has entered into partnership with another is a partner, and the partners together are the firm.

Person held out as a partner (section 28)

Rule. A person who represents himself, or knowingly permits himself to be represented, as a partner is liable as a partner to anyone who gave credit to the firm on the faith of the representation, whether or not he knows the representation reached that person.

Example. Pranav, who is not a partner, allows a firm's letterhead to list him as a partner. A supplier gives credit to the firm because of that. Pranav is liable as a partner to the supplier (section 28(1)).

Minor admitted to the benefits (section 30)

Rule. A minor is not a partner. He shares property and profits as agreed, and only his share is liable for the firm's acts. The topic on minor as partner covers this in full.

Incoming partner (section 31)

Rule. No person may be introduced as a partner without the consent of all the existing partners, subject to contract and section 30. He is not liable for acts of the firm done before he became a partner.

Retiring, expelled, insolvent and deceased partners (sections 32 to 35)

Rule. A partner retires with the consent of all, under an express agreement, or by written notice in a partnership at will. He and the partners remain liable to third parties until public notice is given, but a retired partner is not liable to a third party who did not know he was a partner. An expelled partner is treated like a retired partner for these purposes. An insolvent partner ceases to be a partner on the date of the adjudication order. Where the contract keeps the firm going after a partner's death, his estate is not liable for the firm's later acts.

Which position is the person in? How to read this: start at the top. 1. Has he entered into partnership by agreement (section 4)? He is a partner. 2. Only represented or allowed to be represented as one (section 28)? Liable as a partner to those who gave credit on the faith of it. 3. A minor admitted to the benefits (section 30)? Not a partner. His share, not he, is liable. 4. Joining, retiring, expelled, insolvent or dead (sections 31 to 35)? The rules of those sections apply.
keyPoints: The words active, sleeping and nominal partner are not in the Act. Partner (section 4). Held out as a partner (section 28). Minor admitted to benefits (section 30). Incoming partner needs everyone's consent and is not liable for earlier acts (section 31). Retired partner is liable until public notice (section 32). Expelled is treated like retired (section 33). Insolvent partner ceases to be a partner on the order (section 34). Deceased partner's estate not liable for later acts (section 35).

selfTest.q: 1. Does the Act use the terms active, sleeping and nominal partner?
selfTest.a: No. 2. When is a retired partner released from liability to third parties? Once public notice of the retirement is given, or by agreement with the third party, and he is not liable to a third party who dealt with the firm without knowing he was a partner (section 32). 3. May a person be introduced as a partner without the consent of all? No, subject to contract between the partners and section 30 (section 31(1)).

te.inOneMinute: భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 లోని సెక్షన్లు 4, 28, 30, 31 నుండి 35 — భాగస్వాముల రకాలు
te.meaning:
భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 భాగస్వాములను active, sleeping, nominal వంటి పేరున్న తరగతులుగా విభజించదు. ఆ పదాలు చట్టంలో లేవు. సంస్థలో వేర్వేరు స్థానాల్లో ఉన్న వ్యక్తులకు చట్టం వేర్వేరు నియమాలు ఇస్తుంది: భాగస్వామి (సెక్షన్ 4), తనను తాను భాగస్వామిగా చూపించుకునే వ్యక్తి (సెక్షన్ 28), భాగస్వామ్య ప్రయోజనాలకు చేర్చుకున్న మైనరు (సెక్షన్ 30), కొత్తగా చేరే భాగస్వామి (సెక్షన్ 31), విరమించే భాగస్వామి (సెక్షన్ 32), బహిష్కరించిన భాగస్వామి (సెక్షన్ 33), దివాళా తీసిన భాగస్వామి (సెక్షన్ 34), మరణించిన భాగస్వామి ఎస్టేట్ (సెక్షన్ 35).

ఈ నోట్ చట్టం నుండి ప్రతి స్థానాన్ని చెబుతుంది. వ్యాపారంలో కార్యకలాపం ఆధారంగా పాఠ్యపుస్తక వర్గీకరణ చట్టంలో లేదు, ఇక్కడ ఇవ్వలేదు.

ముందు ఈ పదాలు చదవండి. ఈ అంశంలో ప్రతి పదం పదే పదే వస్తుంది.

నియమం. మరొకరితో భాగస్వామ్యంలోకి ప్రవేశించిన వ్యక్తి భాగస్వామి, భాగస్వాములందరూ కలిసి సంస్థ.

నియమం. తనను తాను భాగస్వామిగా చూపించుకునే, లేదా అలా చూపించడానికి తెలిసి అనుమతించే వ్యక్తి, ఆ ప్రాతినిధ్యంపై నమ్మకంతో సంస్థకు అప్పు ఇచ్చిన ఎవరికైనా భాగస్వామిగా బాధ్యుడు, ఆ ప్రాతినిధ్యం ఆ వ్యక్తిని చేరిందని అతనికి తెలిసినా తెలియకపోయినా.

ఉదాహరణ. భాగస్వామి కాని ప్రణవ్, సంస్థ లెటర్‌హెడ్‌లో తనను భాగస్వామిగా జాబితా చేయడానికి అనుమతించాడు. దాని ఆధారంగా ఒక సరఫరాదారు సంస్థకు అప్పు ఇచ్చాడు. సరఫరాదారుకు ప్రణవ్ భాగస్వామిగా బాధ్యుడు (సెక్షన్ 28(1)).

నియమం. మైనరు భాగస్వామి కాడు. అంగీకరించిన మేరకు ఆస్తి, లాభాల్లో వాటా పొందుతాడు, సంస్థ పనులకు అతని వాటా మాత్రమే బాధ్యత వహిస్తుంది. minor as partner అంశం దీన్ని పూర్తిగా చెబుతుంది.

selfTest.q: 1. చట్టం active, sleeping, nominal భాగస్వామి పదాలు వాడుతుందా?
selfTest.a: వాడదు. 2. విరమించిన భాగస్వామి మూడో పక్షాలకు బాధ్యత నుండి ఎప్పుడు విముక్తి పొందుతాడు? విరమణ గురించి బహిరంగ నోటీసు ఇచ్చాక, లేదా మూడో పక్షంతో ఒప్పందం ద్వారా; అతను భాగస్వామి అని తెలియకుండా వ్యవహరించిన మూడో పక్షానికి అతను బాధ్యుడు కాడు (సెక్షన్ 32). 3. అందరి సమ్మతి లేకుండా ఎవరినైనా భాగస్వామిగా చేర్చవచ్చా? చేర్చకూడదు, భాగస్వాముల మధ్య ఒప్పందానికి, సెక్షన్ 30 కు లోబడి (సెక్షన్ 31(1)).

hi.inOneMinute: The Indian Partnership Act, 1932 does not divide partners into labelled classes such as active, sleeping or nominal partners. Those words do not appear in the Act. The Act does give separate rules for persons in different positions in a firm: a partner (section 4), a person who holds himself out as a partner (section 28), a minor admitted to the benefits of partnership (section 30), an incoming partner (section 31), a retiring partner (section 32), an expelled partner (section 33), an insolvent partner (section 34), and the estate of a deceased partner (section 35). This note sets out each position from the Act. A textbook classification by activity in the business is not in the Act and is not given here.
hi.meaning: Partner (section 4) Rule. A person who has entered into partnership with another is a partner, and the partners together are the firm. Person held out as a partner (section 28) Rule. A person who represents himself, or knowingly permits himself to be represented, as a partner is liable as a partner to anyone who gave credit to the firm on the faith of the representation, whether or not he knows the representation reached that person. Example. Pranav, who is not a partner, allows a firm's letterhead to list him as a partner. A supplier gives credit to the firm because of that. Pranav is liable as a partner to the supplier (section 28(1)). Minor admitted to the benefits (section 30) Rule. A minor is not a partner. He shares property and profits as agreed, and only his share is liable for the firm's acts. The topic on minor as partner covers this in full. Incoming partner (section 31) Rule. No person may be introduced as a partner without the consent of all the existing partners, subject to contract and section 30. He is not liable for acts of the firm done before he became a partner. Retiring, expelled, insolvent and deceased partners (sections 32 to 35) Rule. A partner retires with the consent of all, under an express agreement, or by written notice in a partnership at will. He and the partners remain liable to third parties until public notice is given, but a retired partner is not liable to a third party who did not know he was a partner. An expelled partner is treated like a retired partner for these purposes. An insolvent partner ceases to be a partner on the date of the adjudication order. Where the contract keeps the firm going after a partner's death, his estate is not liable for the firm's later acts. Which position is the person in? How to read this: start at the top. 1. Has he entered into partnership by agreement (section 4)? He is a partner. 2. Only represented or allowed to be represented as one (section 28)? Liable as a partner to those who gave credit on the faith of it. 3. A minor admitted to the benefits (section 30)? Not a partner. His share, not he, is liable. 4. Joining, retiring, expelled, insolvent or dead (sections 31 to 35)? The rules of those sections apply.
keyPoints: The words active, sleeping and nominal partner are not in the Act. Partner (section 4). Held out as a partner (section 28). Minor admitted to benefits (section 30). Incoming partner needs everyone's consent and is not liable for earlier acts (section 31). Retired partner is liable until public notice (section 32). Expelled is treated like retired (section 33). Insolvent partner ceases to be a partner on the order (section 34). Deceased partner's estate not liable for later acts (section 35).

selfTest.q: 1. Does the Act use the terms active, sleeping and nominal partner?
selfTest.a: No. 2. When is a retired partner released from liability to third parties? Once public notice of the retirement is given, or by agreement with the third party, and he is not liable to a third party who dealt with the firm without knowing he was a partner (section 32). 3. May a person be introduced as a partner without the consent of all? No, subject to contract between the partners and section 30 (section 31(1)).

law-of-contract-ii-u5-t9.subtitle: Sections 18 to 29 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932

en.inOneMinute: A partner is the agent of the firm for the purposes of the business of the firm (section 18). The act of a partner done to carry on, in the usual way, business of the kind carried on by the firm binds the firm. This authority is called his implied authority (section 19(1)). Section 19(2) lists acts that implied authority does not cover, unless a usage or custom of trade is to the contrary. The partners may extend or restrict implied authority by contract, but a restriction does not bind a third person who does not know of it or does not know or believe the partner to be a partner (section 20). Every partner is liable, jointly with all the others and also severally, for all acts of the firm done while he is a partner (section 25). Key points for the answer: sections 18 and 19, then 20 to 22 and 25.
en.meaning:
Partner as agent and implied authority (sections 18 and 19)

Rule. A partner is the agent of the firm for the purposes of its business. An act of a partner done to carry on, in the usual way, business of the kind carried on by the firm binds the firm. This is his implied authority. Unless a usage or custom of trade is to the contrary, implied authority does not cover eight acts: submitting a dispute to arbitration; opening a bank account in his own name for the firm; compromising or relinquishing a claim; withdrawing a suit; admitting liability in a suit against the firm; acquiring immovable property for the firm; transferring the firm's immovable property; and entering into partnership on behalf of the firm.

Example. Rakesh is a partner in a firm that sells groceries. He buys rice from a wholesaler for the shop. This is an act done to carry on the firm's business in the usual way, so it binds the firm (section 19(1)). If he sold the firm's shop building, that is a transfer of immovable property, which implied authority does not cover (section 19(2)).

Extension and restriction (section 20)

Rule. The partners may by contract extend or restrict a partner's implied authority. But an act within his implied authority still binds the firm unless the person dealing with him knows of the restriction or does not know or believe him to be a partner.

Emergency (section 21)

Rule. A partner may do, in an emergency, all such acts to protect the firm from loss as a person of ordinary prudence would do in his own case in similar circumstances, and such acts bind the firm.

Mode of binding the firm (section 22)

Rule. To bind a firm, an act or instrument must be done or executed in the firm name, or in another manner expressing or implying an intention to bind the firm.

Admissions and notice (sections 23 and 24)

Rule. A partner's admission or representation about the affairs of the firm, made in the ordinary course of business, is evidence against the firm (section 23). Notice to a partner who habitually acts in the business operates as notice to the firm, except in a fraud on the firm committed by or with the consent of that partner (section 24).

Liability for acts of the firm (sections 25 to 27)

Rule. Every partner is liable jointly with all the others and also severally for all acts of the firm done while he is a partner (section 25). The firm is liable to the same extent as the partner for a third party's loss or injury, or a penalty, caused by a partner's wrongful act or omission in the ordinary course of business or with his partners' authority (section 26). The firm must make good money or property misapplied by a partner acting within apparent authority, or misapplied by any partner while in the firm's custody (section 27).

Example. A firm owes a supplier Rs 1,00,000 for goods bought while Sana and Tariq were partners. The supplier may claim the whole amount from Sana alone, from Tariq alone, or from both together (section 25).

Holding out (section 28)

Rule. A person who by words or conduct represents himself, or knowingly permits himself to be represented, as a partner in a firm is liable as a partner to anyone who has on the faith of the representation given credit to the firm. It does not matter whether he knows that the representation has reached the person giving credit. Continued use of the old firm name after a partner's death does not itself make his legal representative or estate liable for later acts (section 28(2)).

Rights of a transferee of a partner's interest (section 29)

Rule. A transferee of a partner's interest, absolute or by mortgage or charge, cannot interfere in the business, require accounts or inspect the books while the firm continues. He is entitled only to the transferring partner's share of profits. On dissolution, or when the transferring partner ceases to be a partner, he is entitled against the remaining partners to the share of the assets to which the transferring partner is entitled, and to an account from the date of the dissolution.

Does the partner's act bind the firm? How to read this: start at the top. 1. Was the act done to carry on, in the usual way, business of the kind the firm carries on (section 19(1))? If yes, it binds the firm, if done in the firm name or in a manner implying an intention to bind it (section 22). 2. Is it one of the eight acts in section 19(2), with no usage or custom of trade to the contrary? Then implied authority does not cover it. 3. Did the partners restrict his authority (section 20)? The act still binds the firm unless the third person knows of the restriction or does not know or believe him to be a partner. 4. Was it an emergency act to protect the firm from loss (section 21)? Such acts bind the firm.
keyPoints: A partner is the agent of the firm (section 18). His acts in the usual course of business bind the firm: implied authority (section 19(1)). Eight acts are outside implied authority unless usage or custom says otherwise (section 19(2)). A restriction by the partners does not bind a third person who does not know of it or does not know or believe him to be a partner (section 20). Emergency acts bind the firm (section 21). Act must be in the firm name or imply an intention to bind (section 22). Partners are liable jointly and severally (section 25). The firm is liable for a partner's wrongful acts in the ordinary course (section 26). Holding out makes a person liable as a partner (section 28).

selfTest.q: 1. What is implied authority?
selfTest.a: The authority of a partner to bind the firm by an act done to carry on, in the usual way, business of the kind carried on by the firm (section 19(1)). 2. Can implied authority be used to acquire immovable property for the firm? No, unless a usage or custom of trade says otherwise (section 19(2)). 3. Are partners liable jointly or severally for the firm's acts? Both: jointly with all the others and also severally (section 25). 4. What is a transferee of a partner's interest entitled to while the firm continues? Only the transferring partner's share of profits (section 29(1)).

te.inOneMinute: భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 లోని సెక్షన్లు 18 నుండి 29 — భాగస్వాములు, మూడో పక్షాలు
te.meaning:
సంస్థ వ్యాపార ప్రయోజనాల కోసం భాగస్వామి సంస్థకు ఏజెంట్ (సెక్షన్ 18). సంస్థ నడిపే రకం వ్యాపారాన్ని సాధారణ పద్ధతిలో నడపడానికి భాగస్వామి చేసిన పని సంస్థను బంధిస్తుంది. ఈ అధికారాన్ని అతని అంతర్లీన అధికారం (implied authority) అంటారు (సెక్షన్ 19(1)).

వ్యాపార వాడుక లేదా ఆచారం వేరుగా ఉంటే తప్ప, అంతర్లీన అధికారం కవర్ చేయని పనులను సెక్షన్ 19(2) జాబితా చేస్తుంది. భాగస్వాములు ఒప్పందం ద్వారా అంతర్లీన అధికారాన్ని పెంచవచ్చు లేదా పరిమితం చేయవచ్చు, కానీ పరిమితి గురించి తెలిసిన మూడో వ్యక్తులను మాత్రమే అది బంధిస్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 20). తాను భాగస్వామిగా ఉన్నప్పుడు సంస్థ చేసిన అన్ని పనులకు ప్రతి భాగస్వామి మిగిలిన భాగస్వాములందరితో కలిసి, అలాగే విడిగా కూడా బాధ్యుడు (సెక్షన్ 25). సమాధానంలో ముఖ్యమైనవి: సెక్షన్లు 18, 19, తర్వాత 20 నుండి 22, 25.

ముందు ఈ పదాలు చదవండి. ఈ అంశంలో ప్రతి పదం పదే పదే వస్తుంది.

నియమం. సంస్థ వ్యాపార ప్రయోజనాల కోసం భాగస్వామి సంస్థకు ఏజెంట్. సంస్థ నడిపే రకం వ్యాపారాన్ని సాధారణ పద్ధతిలో నడపడానికి భాగస్వామి చేసిన పని సంస్థను బంధిస్తుంది. ఇదే అతని అంతర్లీన అధికారం. వ్యాపార వాడుక లేదా ఆచారం వేరుగా ఉంటే తప్ప, అంతర్లీన అధికారం ఎనిమిది పనులను కవర్ చేయదు: వివాదాన్ని మధ్యవర్తిత్వానికి పంపడం; సంస్థ కోసం తన సొంత పేరుతో బ్యాంక్ ఖాతా తెరవడం; క్లెయిమ్‌ను రాజీ చేయడం లేదా వదులుకోవడం; దావాను ఉపసంహరించడం; సంస్థపై దావాలో బాధ్యతను ఒప్పుకోవడం; సంస్థ కోసం స్థిరాస్తి సంపాదించడం; సంస్థ స్థిరాస్తిని బదిలీ చేయడం; సంస్థ తరఫున భాగస్వామ్యంలోకి ప్రవేశించడం.

ఉదాహరణ. కిరాణా అమ్మే సంస్థలో రాకేష్ భాగస్వామి. అతను దుకాణం కోసం హోల్‌సేలర్ నుండి బియ్యం కొన్నాడు. ఇది సంస్థ వ్యాపారాన్ని సాధారణ పద్ధతిలో నడపడానికి చేసిన పని, కాబట్టి సంస్థను బంధిస్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 19(1)). అతను సంస్థ దుకాణ భవనాన్ని అమ్మితే అది స్థిరాస్తి బదిలీ, అంతర్లీన అధికారం దాన్ని కవర్ చేయదు (సెక్షన్ 19(2)).

నియమం. భాగస్వాములు ఒప్పందం ద్వారా భాగస్వామి అంతర్లీన అధికారాన్ని పెంచవచ్చు లేదా పరిమితం చేయవచ్చు. కానీ అతనితో వ్యవహరించే వ్యక్తికి పరిమితి తెలిసినా, లేదా అతను భాగస్వామి అని తెలియకపోయినా లేదా నమ్మకపోయినా తప్ప, అతని అంతర్లీన అధికారం పరిధిలోని పని సంస్థను బంధిస్తూనే ఉంటుంది.

నియమం. అత్యవసర పరిస్థితిలో, సంస్థను నష్టం నుండి కాపాడటానికి సాధారణ వివేకం ఉన్న వ్యక్తి అలాంటి పరిస్థితుల్లో తన విషయంలో చేసే అన్ని పనులను భాగస్వామి చేయవచ్చు, ఆ పనులు సంస్థను బంధిస్తాయి.

selfTest.q: 1. అంతర్లీన అధికారం అంటే ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: సంస్థ నడిపే రకం వ్యాపారాన్ని సాధారణ పద్ధతిలో నడపడానికి చేసిన పని ద్వారా సంస్థను బంధించే భాగస్వామి అధికారం (సెక్షన్ 19(1)). 2. సంస్థ కోసం స్థిరాస్తి సంపాదించడానికి అంతర్లీన అధికారాన్ని వాడవచ్చా? వ్యాపార వాడుక లేదా ఆచారం వేరుగా ఉంటే తప్ప కాదు (సెక్షన్ 19(2)). 3. సంస్థ పనులకు భాగస్వాములు కలిసి బాధ్యులా, విడిగా బాధ్యులా? రెండూ: మిగిలిన వారందరితో కలిసి, అలాగే విడిగా కూడా (సెక్షన్ 25). 4. సంస్థ కొనసాగుతున్నప్పుడు భాగస్వామి ఆసక్తి బదిలీ పొందినవాడికి ఏ హక్కు ఉంది? బదిలీ చేసిన భాగస్వామి లాభాల వాటా మాత్రమే (సెక్షన్ 29(1)).

hi.inOneMinute: A partner is the agent of the firm for the purposes of the business of the firm (section 18). The act of a partner done to carry on, in the usual way, business of the kind carried on by the firm binds the firm. This authority is called his implied authority (section 19(1)). Section 19(2) lists acts that implied authority does not cover, unless a usage or custom of trade is to the contrary. The partners may extend or restrict implied authority by contract, but a restriction does not bind a third person who does not know of it or does not know or believe the partner to be a partner (section 20). Every partner is liable, jointly with all the others and also severally, for all acts of the firm done while he is a partner (section 25). Key points for the answer: sections 18 and 19, then 20 to 22 and 25.
hi.meaning: Partner as agent and implied authority (sections 18 and 19) Rule. A partner is the agent of the firm for the purposes of its business. An act of a partner done to carry on, in the usual way, business of the kind carried on by the firm binds the firm. This is his implied authority. Unless a usage or custom of trade is to the contrary, implied authority does not cover eight acts: submitting a dispute to arbitration; opening a bank account in his own name for the firm; compromising or relinquishing a claim; withdrawing a suit; admitting liability in a suit against the firm; acquiring immovable property for the firm; transferring the firm's immovable property; and entering into partnership on behalf of the firm. Example. Rakesh is a partner in a firm that sells groceries. He buys rice from a wholesaler for the shop. This is an act done to carry on the firm's business in the usual way, so it binds the firm (section 19(1)). If he sold the firm's shop building, that is a transfer of immovable property, which implied authority does not cover (section 19(2)). Extension and restriction (section 20) Rule. The partners may by contract extend or restrict a partner's implied authority. But an act within his implied authority still binds the firm unless the person dealing with him knows of the restriction or does not know or believe him to be a partner. Emergency (section 21) Rule. A partner may do, in an emergency, all such acts to protect the firm from loss as a person of ordinary prudence would do in his own case in similar circumstances, and such acts bind the firm. Mode of binding the firm (section 22) Rule. To bind a firm, an act or instrument must be done or executed in the firm name, or in another manner expressing or implying an intention to bind the firm. Admissions and notice (sections 23 and 24) Rule. A partner's admission or representation about the affairs of the firm, made in the ordinary course of business, is evidence against the firm (section 23). Notice to a partner who habitually acts in the business operates as notice to the firm, except in a fraud on the firm committed by or with the consent of that partner (section 24). Liability for acts of the firm (sections 25 to 27) Rule. Every partner is liable jointly with all the others and also severally for all acts of the firm done while he is a partner (section 25). The firm is liable to the same extent as the partner for a third party's loss or injury, or a penalty, caused by a partner's wrongful act or omission in the ordinary course of business or with his partners' authority (section 26). The firm must make good money or property misapplied by a partner acting within apparent authority, or misapplied by any partner while in the firm's custody (section 27). Example. A firm owes a supplier Rs 1,00,000 for goods bought while Sana and Tariq were partners. The supplier may claim the whole amount from Sana alone, from Tariq alone, or from both together (section 25). Holding out (section 28) Rule. A person who by words or conduct represents himself, or knowingly permits himself to be represented, as a partner in a firm is liable as a partner to anyone who has on the faith of the representation given credit to the firm. It does not matter whether he knows that the representation has reached the person giving credit. Continued use of the old firm name after a partner's death does not itself make his legal representative or estate liable for later acts (section 28(2)). Rights of a transferee of a partner's interest (section 29) Rule. A transferee of a partner's interest, absolute or by mortgage or charge, cannot interfere in the business, require accounts or inspect the books while the firm continues. He is entitled only to the transferring partner's share of profits. On dissolution, or when the transferring partner ceases to be a partner, he is entitled against the remaining partners to the share of the assets to which the transferring partner is entitled, and to an account from the date of the dissolution. Does the partner's act bind the firm? How to read this: start at the top. 1. Was the act done to carry on, in the usual way, business of the kind the firm carries on (section 19(1))? If yes, it binds the firm, if done in the firm name or in a manner implying an intention to bind it (section 22). 2. Is it one of the eight acts in section 19(2), with no usage or custom of trade to the contrary? Then implied authority does not cover it. 3. Did the partners restrict his authority (section 20)? The act still binds the firm unless the third person knows of the restriction or does not know or believe him to be a partner. 4. Was it an emergency act to protect the firm from loss (section 21)? Such acts bind the firm.
keyPoints: A partner is the agent of the firm (section 18). His acts in the usual course of business bind the firm: implied authority (section 19(1)). Eight acts are outside implied authority unless usage or custom says otherwise (section 19(2)). A restriction by the partners does not bind a third person who does not know of it or does not know or believe him to be a partner (section 20). Emergency acts bind the firm (section 21). Act must be in the firm name or imply an intention to bind (section 22). Partners are liable jointly and severally (section 25). The firm is liable for a partner's wrongful acts in the ordinary course (section 26). Holding out makes a person liable as a partner (section 28).

selfTest.q: 1. What is implied authority?
selfTest.a: The authority of a partner to bind the firm by an act done to carry on, in the usual way, business of the kind carried on by the firm (section 19(1)). 2. Can implied authority be used to acquire immovable property for the firm? No, unless a usage or custom of trade says otherwise (section 19(2)). 3. Are partners liable jointly or severally for the firm's acts? Both: jointly with all the others and also severally (section 25). 4. What is a transferee of a partner's interest entitled to while the firm continues? Only the transferring partner's share of profits (section 29(1)).

law-of-contract-ii-u5-t11.subtitle: Section 30 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932

en.inOneMinute: Under section 30 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, a person who is a minor according to the law to which he is subject may not be a partner in a firm. With the consent of all the partners for the time being, he may be admitted to the benefits of partnership (section 30(1)). His share is liable for the acts of the firm, but he is not personally liable (section 30(3)). Within six months of attaining majority, or of learning he had been admitted, whichever is later, he may give public notice that he has elected to become or not to become a partner. If he gives no notice, he becomes a partner when the six months expire (section 30(5)).
en.meaning:
Admission to the benefits (section 30(1) and (2))

Rule. A minor may not be a partner. With the consent of all the partners for the time being, he may be admitted to the benefits of partnership. He has a right to the share of property and profits that is agreed, and may have access to, inspect and copy the firm's accounts.

Example. Vimal, aged 16, is admitted by all the partners of a firm to the benefits of the partnership, with a 10 per cent share of profits. He is not a partner. He is entitled to the agreed share and may inspect the accounts (section 30(1) and (2)).

Liability while a minor (section 30(3))

Rule. The minor's share is liable for the acts of the firm. He is not personally liable for any such act.

No suit for accounts, except on severing (section 30(4))

Rule. The minor may not sue the partners for an account or payment of his share, except when severing his connection with the firm. His share is then valued, as far as possible, by the rules in section 48. The partners acting together, or any partner entitled to dissolve the firm on notice, may elect in the suit to dissolve the firm. The Court then proceeds as in a suit for dissolution and settlement of accounts.

Election on attaining majority (section 30(5) and (6))

Rule. Within six months of attaining majority, or of learning that he had been admitted, whichever is later, the person may give public notice that he has elected to become, or not to become, a partner. If he gives no notice, he becomes a partner on expiry of the six months. A person who asserts that he did not know of the admission until a date after those six months must prove it.

If he becomes a partner (section 30(7))

Rule. His rights and liabilities as a minor continue up to the date he becomes a partner. He also becomes personally liable to third parties for all acts of the firm done since he was admitted to the benefits. His share in the property and profits is the share he had as a minor.

If he elects not to become a partner (section 30(8))

Rule. His rights and liabilities remain those of a minor up to the date of public notice. His share is not liable for acts of the firm done after the notice. He may sue the partners for his share of the property and profits as under sub-section (4). Section 28 (holding out) is not affected (section 30(9)).

The minor's position over time How to read this: start at the top. 1. Admitted to the benefits with the consent of all the partners (section 30(1)). Not a partner. Share liable for the firm's acts, but no personal liability (section 30(3)). 2. Within six months of majority or of knowledge, whichever is later: public notice. Elects to become a partner, or not (section 30(5)). 3. No notice given. He becomes a partner on expiry of the six months (section 30(5) proviso). 4. Becomes a partner / elects not to. Personally liable for acts since admission (section 30(7)) / share not liable for acts after the notice (section 30(8)).
keyPoints: A minor may not be a partner but may be admitted to the benefits with all the partners' consent (section 30(1)). His share is liable for the firm's acts, but he is not personally liable (section 30(3)). Six months from majority or knowledge, whichever is later, to elect by public notice (section 30(5)). No notice: he becomes a partner on expiry of six months. If he becomes a partner: personally liable for acts since admission (section 30(7)). If he elects not to: his share is not liable for later acts (section 30(8)).

selfTest.q: 1. Can a minor be a partner?
selfTest.a: No. With the consent of all the partners he may be admitted to the benefits of partnership (section 30(1)). 2. Is a minor personally liable for the firm's acts? No. Only his share is liable (section 30(3)). 3. What if he gives no notice within six months of majority? He becomes a partner on the expiry of the six months (section 30(5) proviso).

te.inOneMinute: భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 లోని సెక్షన్ 30 — భాగస్వామిగా మైనరు
te.meaning:
భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 సెక్షన్ 30 ప్రకారం, తనకు వర్తించే చట్టం ప్రకారం మైనరు అయిన వ్యక్తి సంస్థలో భాగస్వామి కాకూడదు. అప్పటికి ఉన్న భాగస్వాములందరి సమ్మతితో, అతన్ని భాగస్వామ్య ప్రయోజనాలకు చేర్చుకోవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 30(1)).

అతని వాటా సంస్థ పనులకు బాధ్యత వహిస్తుంది, కానీ అతను వ్యక్తిగతంగా బాధ్యుడు కాడు (సెక్షన్ 30(3)). మెజారిటీ వచ్చిన, లేదా తనను చేర్చుకున్నట్లు తెలిసిన తేదీల్లో ఏది తర్వాతదైతే దాని నుండి ఆరు నెలల్లోపు, భాగస్వామి కావాలని లేదా కాకూడదని తాను ఎంచుకున్నట్లు బహిరంగ నోటీసు ఇవ్వవచ్చు. నోటీసు ఇవ్వకపోతే ఆరు నెలలు ముగిశాక అతను భాగస్వామి అవుతాడు (సెక్షన్ 30(5)).

ముందు ఈ పదాలు చదవండి. ఈ అంశంలో ప్రతి పదం పదే పదే వస్తుంది.

నియమం. మైనరు భాగస్వామి కాకూడదు. అప్పటికి ఉన్న భాగస్వాములందరి సమ్మతితో అతన్ని భాగస్వామ్య ప్రయోజనాలకు చేర్చుకోవచ్చు. అంగీకరించిన ఆస్తి, లాభాల వాటా పొందే హక్కు అతనికి ఉంది, సంస్థ ఖాతాలను చూడవచ్చు, తనిఖీ చేయవచ్చు, కాపీ చేయవచ్చు.

ఉదాహరణ. 16 ఏళ్ల విమల్‌ను సంస్థ భాగస్వాములందరూ 10 శాతం లాభాల వాటాతో భాగస్వామ్య ప్రయోజనాలకు చేర్చుకున్నారు. అతను భాగస్వామి కాడు. అంగీకరించిన వాటా పొందే హక్కు అతనికి ఉంది, ఖాతాలను తనిఖీ చేయవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 30(1), (2)).

నియమం. మైనరు వాటా సంస్థ పనులకు బాధ్యత వహిస్తుంది. అతను ఆ పనులకు వ్యక్తిగతంగా బాధ్యుడు కాడు.

నియమం. సంస్థతో సంబంధం తెంచుకునేటప్పుడు తప్ప, తన వాటా లెక్క లేదా చెల్లింపు కోసం మైనరు భాగస్వాములపై దావా వేయకూడదు. అప్పుడు అతని వాటాను, వీలైనంత వరకు, సెక్షన్ 48 నియమాల ప్రకారం విలువ కడతారు. భాగస్వాములందరూ కలిసి, లేదా నోటీసుతో సంస్థను రద్దు చేసే హక్కు ఉన్న ఏ భాగస్వామి అయినా, ఆ దావాలో సంస్థను రద్దు చేయాలని ఎంచుకోవచ్చు. అప్పుడు కోర్టు రద్దు, లెక్కల పరిష్కార దావాగా కొనసాగిస్తుంది.

selfTest.q: 1. మైనరు భాగస్వామి కావచ్చా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. భాగస్వాములందరి సమ్మతితో అతన్ని భాగస్వామ్య ప్రయోజనాలకు చేర్చుకోవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 30(1)). 2. సంస్థ పనులకు మైనరు వ్యక్తిగతంగా బాధ్యుడా? కాదు. అతని వాటా మాత్రమే బాధ్యత వహిస్తుంది (సెక్షన్ 30(3)). 3. మెజారిటీ వచ్చిన ఆరు నెలల్లో నోటీసు ఇవ్వకపోతే? ఆరు నెలలు ముగిశాక అతను భాగస్వామి అవుతాడు (సెక్షన్ 30(5) షరతు).

No notice: he becomes a partner on expiry of six months. If he becomes a partner: personally liable for acts since admission (section 30(7)). If he elects not to: his share is not liable for later acts (section 30(8)).

law-of-contract-ii-u5-t1.subtitle: Sections 2 to 5 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932

en.inOneMinute: Section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 defines "partnership" as the relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all. The persons are individually "partners", together "a firm", and the name under which they carry on business is the "firm name". The relation arises from contract and not from status (section 5). The Indian Contract Act, 1872 continues to apply to firms where it is not inconsistent with the Act (section 3). Key points for the answer: the elements of the definition and the rule in section 5.
en.meaning:
The definition (section 4)

Rule. A partnership has these elements, each drawn from the words of section 4.

It is a relation between persons who have agreed. There must be an agreement between persons. Section 4 says "persons" and states no number. The agreement is to share the profits of a business. The business is carried on by all or any of them acting for all.

"Business" includes every trade, occupation and profession (section 2(b)).

Example. Anu and Bala agree to run a bakery together and to share the profits equally. Either may act for both in running it. This fits the definition in section 4.

Partner, firm and firm name (section 4)

Rule. Persons who have entered into partnership are individually "partners" and collectively "a firm". The name under which their business is carried on is the "firm name".

Partnership arises from contract, not status (section 5)

Rule. The relation of partnership arises from contract and not from status. Members of a Hindu undivided family carrying on a family business as such, and a Burmese Buddhist husband and wife carrying on business as such, are not partners in that business.

Example. Brothers who are members of a Hindu undivided family run the family shop as such. They are not partners merely because of the family relationship (section 5).

Definitions used in the Act (section 2) and application of the Contract Act (section 3)

Rule. "Act of a firm", "business", "prescribed" and "third party" are defined in section 2. Words used but not defined in this Act and defined in the Contract Act have the meaning given there (section 2(e)). The unrepealed provisions of the Contract Act continue to apply to firms, so far as they are not inconsistent with the Act (section 3).

Is there a partnership? How to read this: start at the top. 1. Have persons agreed (a contract, not status: section 5)? If not, no partnership. 2. Is the agreement to share the profits of a business (section 2(b) and section 4)? If not, no partnership. 3. Is the business carried on by all or any of them acting for all? If yes, it is a partnership under section 4. The persons are partners and the group is a firm.
keyPoints: Partnership: relation between persons who have agreed to share profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all (section 4). Persons are partners, collectively a firm, and the business name is the firm name (section 4). Business includes every trade, occupation and profession (section 2(b)). Partnership arises from contract, not status. A Hindu undivided family running a family business is not a partnership (section 5). The Contract Act applies unless inconsistent (section 3).

selfTest.a: As the relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all. 2. What is a firm? The partners collectively. The name under which their business is carried on is the firm name (section 4). 3. Does partnership arise from status? No. It arises from contract and not from status (section 5). 4. What does "business" include? Every trade, occupation and profession (section 2(b)).

te.inOneMinute: భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 లోని సెక్షన్లు 2 నుండి 5 — భాగస్వామ్య ఒప్పందం, నిర్వచనం, స్వభావం
te.meaning:
భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 సెక్షన్ 4 "partnership" ను, అందరి తరఫున అందరూ లేదా వారిలో ఎవరైనా నడిపే వ్యాపార లాభాలను పంచుకోవడానికి అంగీకరించిన వ్యక్తుల మధ్య సంబంధంగా నిర్వచిస్తుంది. ఆ వ్యక్తులు విడివిడిగా "partners", కలిసి "a firm", వారు వ్యాపారం నడిపే పేరు "firm name".

ఈ సంబంధం ఒప్పందం నుండి ఏర్పడుతుంది, హోదా (status) నుండి కాదు (సెక్షన్ 5). భారతీయ ఒప్పంద చట్టం, 1872, ఈ చట్టానికి విరుద్ధం కానంత వరకు సంస్థలకు వర్తిస్తూనే ఉంటుంది (సెక్షన్ 3). సమాధానంలో ముఖ్యమైనవి: నిర్వచనంలోని అంశాలు, సెక్షన్ 5 లోని నియమం.

ముందు ఈ పదాలు చదవండి. ఈ అంశంలో ప్రతి పదం పదే పదే వస్తుంది.

నియమం. భాగస్వామ్యానికి ఈ అంశాలు ఉంటాయి, ప్రతిదీ సెక్షన్ 4 పదాల నుండి వచ్చినదే.

"Business" లో ప్రతి వాణిజ్యం, వృత్తి, వ్యాపారం ఉంటాయి (సెక్షన్ 2(b)).

ఉదాహరణ. అను, బాల కలిసి ఒక బేకరీ నడపడానికి, లాభాలను సమానంగా పంచుకోవడానికి అంగీకరించారు. ఇద్దరిలో ఎవరైనా ఇద్దరి తరఫున నడపవచ్చు. ఇది సెక్షన్ 4 నిర్వచనానికి సరిపోతుంది.

నియమం. భాగస్వామ్యంలోకి ప్రవేశించిన వ్యక్తులు విడివిడిగా "partners", కలిసి "a firm". వారి వ్యాపారం నడిచే పేరు "firm name".

selfTest.q: 1. సెక్షన్ 4 భాగస్వామ్యాన్ని ఎలా నిర్వచిస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: అందరి తరఫున అందరూ లేదా వారిలో ఎవరైనా నడిపే వ్యాపార లాభాలను పంచుకోవడానికి అంగీకరించిన వ్యక్తుల మధ్య సంబంధంగా. 2. సంస్థ అంటే ఏమిటి? భాగస్వాములందరూ కలిసి. వారి వ్యాపారం నడిచే పేరు సంస్థ పేరు (సెక్షన్ 4). 3. భాగస్వామ్యం హోదా నుండి ఏర్పడుతుందా? లేదు. అది ఒప్పందం నుండి ఏర్పడుతుంది, హోదా నుండి కాదు (సెక్షన్ 5). 4. "Business" లో ఏవి ఉంటాయి? ప్రతి వాణిజ్యం, వృత్తి, వ్యాపారం (సెక్షన్ 2(b)).

law-of-contract-ii-u5-t12.subtitle: Sections 17 and 31 to 38 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932

en.inOneMinute: Yes, a firm can be reconstituted. The Act deals with changes in the constitution of a firm: a person may be introduced as a partner with the consent of all the existing partners (section 31), a partner may retire (section 32), a partner may be expelled only in good faith under a power in the partners' contract (section 33), and a partner ceases to be a partner on being adjudicated an insolvent (section 34). Where the contract keeps the firm going after a partner's death, the estate is not liable for later acts (section 35). After such a change, the mutual rights and duties of the partners in the reconstituted firm remain the same as before, as far as may be (section 17(a)). Sections 36 and 37 give the rights of an outgoing partner. Section 38 says a continuing guarantee given to a firm is revoked as to future transactions by a change in the firm, unless otherwise agreed.
en.meaning:
Can a firm be reconstituted?

Rule. Yes. A firm is reconstituted when a person is introduced as a partner (section 31), a partner retires (section 32), is expelled (section 33), is adjudicated an insolvent (section 34), or dies where the contract keeps the firm going (section 35). Subject to contract, the partners' mutual rights and duties in the reconstituted firm stay the same as far as may be (section 17(a)).

Example. A, B and C run a firm. C retires with the consent of A and B. The firm continues as a firm of A and B, and the mutual rights and duties of A and B remain as before so far as may be (section 17(a)).

Introducing a partner (section 31)

Rule. No person may be introduced without the consent of all the existing partners, subject to contract and section 30. He is not liable for acts of the firm done before he became a partner.

Retirement (section 32)

Rule. A partner may retire with everyone's consent, under an express agreement, or by written notice in a partnership at will. He may be discharged by agreement with the third party and the partners of the reconstituted firm, and that agreement may be implied from a course of dealing. Until public notice is given, he and the partners remain liable to third parties as partners. He is not liable to a third party who dealt with the firm without knowing he was a partner.

Expulsion (section 33)

Rule. No majority may expel a partner, except in the good-faith exercise of powers given by the partners' contract. Section 32(2), (3) and (4) apply to him as if he had retired.

Insolvency and death (sections 34 and 35)

Rule. A partner adjudicated an insolvent ceases to be a partner on the date of the order, whether or not the firm is dissolved. If the contract keeps the firm going, the insolvent's estate is not liable for the firm's acts after that date, and the firm is not liable for the insolvent's acts. Where the contract keeps the firm going after a death, the deceased's estate is not liable for acts after his death.

Rights of an outgoing partner (sections 36 and 37)

Rule. An outgoing partner may carry on and advertise a competing business, but, subject to contrary contract, may not use the firm name, represent himself as carrying on the firm's business, or solicit the firm's former customers. A reasonable agreement restraining him within a specified period or place is valid despite section 27 of the Contract Act (section 36). If the continuing partners carry on the business with the firm's property without a final settlement, the outgoing partner or his estate may choose a share of profits attributable to the use of his share of the property, or interest at six per cent per annum on his share (section 37).

Guarantees (section 38)

Rule. A continuing guarantee given to a firm, or to a third party about the firm's transactions, is revoked as to future transactions from the date of a change in the firm's constitution, unless agreed otherwise.

Change in the firm: what follows? How to read this: start at the top. 1. A partner joins (section 31), retires (section 32), is expelled (section 33), is adjudicated insolvent (section 34), or dies (section 35)? The firm is reconstituted. Mutual rights and duties continue as far as may be (section 17(a)). 2. Third parties dealing with the firm. The outgoing partner stays liable until public notice (section 32(3)), unless the third party did not know he was a partner. 3. The outgoing partner's claims. Share of profits or six per cent interest if the business continues with the firm's property without settlement (section 37). 4. A continuing guarantee. Revoked as to future transactions, unless agreed otherwise (section 38).
keyPoints: A firm can be reconstituted. Rights and duties continue as far as may be (section 17(a)). New partner: consent of all existing partners (section 31). Retirement: consent of all, agreement, or written notice if at will. Liability continues until public notice (section 32). Expulsion only in good faith under a contractual power (section 33). Outgoing partner: competing business allowed, with limits (section 36). Profits or six per cent interest (section 37). Continuing guarantee revoked as to future transactions (section 38).

selfTest.q: 1. How may a partner be introduced into a firm?
selfTest.a: With the consent of all the existing partners, subject to contract and section 30 (section 31(1)). 2. Can a majority expel a partner? Only in the good-faith exercise of powers conferred by the partners' contract (section 33(1)). 3. What may an outgoing partner not do after leaving? Subject to contrary contract, use the firm name, represent himself as carrying on the firm's business, or solicit the firm's former customers (section 36(1)). 4. What happens to a continuing guarantee when the firm changes? It is revoked as to future transactions from the date of the change, unless agreed otherwise (section 38).

te.inOneMinute: భారతీయ భాగస్వామ్య చట్టం, 1932 లోని సెక్షన్లు 17, 31 నుండి 38 — సంస్థ పునర్నిర్మాణం
te.meaning:
అవును, సంస్థను పునర్నిర్మించవచ్చు. సంస్థ స్వరూపంలో మార్పులను చట్టం చెబుతుంది: ఇప్పటికే ఉన్న భాగస్వాములందరి సమ్మతితో ఒక వ్యక్తిని భాగస్వామిగా చేర్చుకోవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 31), భాగస్వామి విరమించవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 32), భాగస్వాముల ఒప్పందంలోని అధికారం కింద మంచి విశ్వాసంతో మాత్రమే భాగస్వామిని బహిష్కరించవచ్చు (సెక్షన్ 33), దివాళా తీసినట్లు ప్రకటించగానే భాగస్వామి భాగస్వామి కాకుండా పోతాడు (సెక్షన్ 34). భాగస్వామి మరణం తర్వాత ఒప్పందం సంస్థను కొనసాగిస్తే, ఎస్టేట్ తర్వాతి పనులకు బాధ్యత వహించదు (సెక్షన్ 35).

అలాంటి మార్పు తర్వాత, పునర్నిర్మించిన సంస్థలో భాగస్వాముల పరస్పర హక్కులు, విధులు, వీలైనంత వరకు, ముందు ఉన్నట్లే ఉంటాయి (సెక్షన్ 17(a)). సెక్షన్లు 36, 37 వైదొలగిన భాగస్వామి హక్కులు ఇస్తాయి. విరుద్ధ ఒప్పందం లేకపోతే సంస్థ స్వరూపంలో మార్పు వల్ల సంస్థకు ఇచ్చిన కొనసాగే హామీ భవిష్యత్ లావాదేవీలకు రద్దవుతుందని సెక్షన్ 38 చెబుతుంది.

ముందు ఈ పదాలు చదవండి. ఈ అంశంలో ప్రతి పదం పదే పదే వస్తుంది.

నియమం. అవును. ఒక వ్యక్తిని భాగస్వామిగా చేర్చినప్పుడు (సెక్షన్ 31), భాగస్వామి విరమించినప్పుడు (సెక్షన్ 32), బహిష్కరించినప్పుడు (సెక్షన్ 33), దివాళా తీసినట్లు ప్రకటించినప్పుడు (సెక్షన్ 34), లేదా ఒప్పందం సంస్థను కొనసాగిస్తూ మరణించినప్పుడు (సెక్షన్ 35) సంస్థ పునర్నిర్మితమవుతుంది. ఒప్పందానికి లోబడి, పునర్నిర్మించిన సంస్థలో భాగస్వాముల పరస్పర హక్కులు, విధులు, వీలైనంత వరకు, అలాగే ఉంటాయి (సెక్షన్ 17(a)).

ఉదాహరణ. A, B, C ఒక సంస్థ నడుపుతున్నారు. A, B ల సమ్మతితో C విరమించాడు. సంస్థ A, B ల సంస్థగా కొనసాగుతుంది, A, B ల పరస్పర హక్కులు, విధులు వీలైనంత వరకు ముందులాగే ఉంటాయి (సెక్షన్ 17(a)).

నియమం. ఒప్పందానికి, సెక్షన్ 30 కు లోబడి, ఇప్పటికే ఉన్న భాగస్వాములందరి సమ్మతి లేకుండా ఎవరినీ చేర్చకూడదు. భాగస్వామి కాక ముందు సంస్థ చేసిన పనులకు అతను బాధ్యుడు కాడు.

నియమం. భాగస్వామి అందరి సమ్మతితో, స్పష్టమైన ఒప్పందం ప్రకారం, లేదా ఇష్టానుసారం భాగస్వామ్యంలో వ్రాతపూర్వక నోటీసుతో విరమించవచ్చు. మూడో పక్షంతో, పునర్నిర్మించిన సంస్థ భాగస్వాములతో ఒప్పందం ద్వారా అతనికి విముక్తి దొరకవచ్చు, ఆ ఒప్పందం వ్యవహార తీరు నుండి అంతర్లీనంగా ఏర్పడవచ్చు. బహిరంగ నోటీసు ఇచ్చే వరకు అతను, భాగస్వాములు మూడో పక్షాలకు భాగస్వాములుగా బాధ్యులు. అతను భాగస్వామి అని తెలియకుండా సంస్థతో వ్యవహరించిన మూడో పక్షానికి అతను బాధ్యుడు కాడు.

selfTest.q: 1. సంస్థలో భాగస్వామిని ఎలా చేర్చవచ్చు?
selfTest.a: ఒప్పందానికి, సెక్షన్ 30 కు లోబడి, ఇప్పటికే ఉన్న భాగస్వాములందరి సమ్మతితో (సెక్షన్ 31(1)). 2. మెజారిటీ భాగస్వామిని బహిష్కరించగలదా? భాగస్వాముల ఒప్పందం ఇచ్చిన అధికారాలను మంచి విశ్వాసంతో వినియోగిస్తేనే (సెక్షన్ 33(1)). 3. వైదొలగిన భాగస్వామి ఆ తర్వాత ఏమి చేయకూడదు? విరుద్ధ ఒప్పందానికి లోబడి, సంస్థ పేరు వాడకూడదు, సంస్థ వ్యాపారం నడుపుతున్నట్లు చూపించుకోకూడదు, సంస్థ పూర్వపు కస్టమర్ల ఆదరణను కోరకూడదు (సెక్షన్ 36(1)). 4. సంస్థ మారినప్పుడు కొనసాగే హామీకి ఏమవుతుంది? వేరుగా అంగీకరించకపోతే, మార్పు తేదీ నుండి భవిష్యత్ లావాదేవీలకు రద్దవుతుంది (సెక్షన్ 38).
